The Saeima has adopted and the President of the State proclaims the following law:

Civil Procedure Law

Part A

General Provisions

First Section

Fundamental Provisions of Civil Proceedings

Chapter 1

Principles of Civil Procedure

#### Article 1. Right of a Person to Court Protection

(1) Every natural and legal person (hereinafter — person) has the right to protection in court of their violated or disputed civil rights or interests protected by law.

(2) A person who has applied to a court has the right to have their case examined in court in the procedural order established by law.

#### Article 2. Court Adjudication in Civil Cases

Civil cases are adjudicated by a court in the order established in this Law and in the Law "On Judicial Power".

#### 3.pants. Force of Legal Norms Regulating Civil Proceedings in Time

Civil proceedings are governed by the civil procedural legal norms that are in force at the time of examination of the case, performance of individual procedural acts or enforcement of a court judgment.

(In the wording of the Law of 07.04.2004., which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

#### 4.pants. Court Instances in Civil Cases

(1) A civil case is examined on the merits by a first instance court, but upon appeal by the parties to the case against the judgment of this court — also by a second instance court in the procedure of appeal, unless otherwise provided by law.

(2) A civil case shall not be examined on the merits in a higher court instance before it has been examined in a lower court instance, unless otherwise provided by this Law.

(3) The parties to the case may appeal the judgment of the second instance court in the procedure of cassation.

(With amendments made by the Law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

#### 5.pants. Application of Legal Norms

(1) The court adjudicates civil cases in accordance with laws and other regulatory enactments, international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia and European Union law.

(2) If an international agreement approved by the Saeima provides for different provisions than a Latvian law, the provisions of the international agreement shall apply.

(3) If the relevant legal issue is governed by European Union law that is directly applicable in Latvia, Latvian law shall apply insofar as permitted by European Union law.

(4) In cases provided for by law or agreement, the court shall also apply the laws of other states and norms of international law.

(5) If there is no law governing the disputed relationship, the court shall apply the law that governs similar legal relationships, but if there is no such law — shall be guided by the general principles and spirit of law.

(6) In applying legal norms, the court shall take into account case law.

(In the wording of the Law of 07.04.2004., which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

5.1 pants. Referring a Question to the Court of Justice of the European Union

The court, in accordance with European Union law, shall refer a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union regarding the interpretation or validity of European Union law for the adoption of a preliminary ruling.

(In the wording of the Law of 07.04.2004. with amendments made by the Law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

#### 6.pants. Initiation of Civil Cases in Court

(1) A judge shall initiate a civil case on the basis of an application by the persons to whom the case relates.

(2) A judge shall also initiate a civil case on the basis of an application by state or local government institutions and persons who have been granted by law the right to defend in court the rights or legally protected interests of other persons.

(3) In proceedings on claims, claim applications shall be submitted, but in cases of special procedure — applications.

#### 7.pants. Civil Claim in Criminal Case

(Deleted by the Law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 8.pants. Establishment of Circumstances in Civil Case

(1) The court shall establish the circumstances of the case by examining evidence obtained in the procedure prescribed by law.

(2) The court shall explain to the parties to the case their rights and duties, as well as the consequences of performing or not performing procedural acts.

(With amendments made by the Law of 25.05.2006., which enters into force on 28.06.2006.)

#### 9.pants. Equality of the Parties in Civil Procedure

(1) The parties have equal procedural rights.

(2) The court shall ensure equal opportunities for the parties to exercise the rights granted to them in defence of their interests. 9.1 pants. Duty to State the Truth

The parties, third parties and representatives on behalf of those represented shall provide the court with truthful information about facts and circumstances of the case.

(In the wording of the Law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

#### 10.pants. Adversarial Principle in Civil Procedure

(1) The parties exercise their procedural rights in adversarial form.

(2) The adversarial process takes place by the parties giving explanations, submitting evidence, applications addressed to the court, participating in the questioning of witnesses and experts, examination and evaluation of other evidence, participating in court debates and performing other procedural acts in the procedure prescribed by this Law.

#### 11.pants. Publicity of Civil Case Hearings

(1) Civil cases in courts are heard publicly, except for cases concerning:

- 1) determination of a child's origin;
- 2) approval and revocation of adoption;
- 3) dissolution or non-existence of marriage;
- 4) restriction of a person's legal capacity due to mental or other health disorders;
- 41) establishment of temporary guardianship;
- 42) suspension of a future representative's rights;
- 5) unlawful removal of a child across the border to a foreign country or retention abroad and unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia;
- 6) custody and contact rights;
- 7) temporary protection against violence.
  - (2) Persons who are younger than 15 years of age and who are not parties to the case or witnesses may be present at the court session only with the permission of the court.
  - (3) Upon a motivated request of a party to the case or at the discretion of the court, a court session or part thereof may be declared closed:
- 1) if it is necessary to protect state secrets or trade secrets;
- 2) if it is necessary to protect the private life and secrecy of correspondence of persons;
- 3) in the interests of minors;
- 4) if it is necessary to question a person who has not reached 15 years of age;
- 5) in the interests of the administration of justice;
- 6) if it is necessary to protect information of limited access in cases concerning compensation for damage caused by infringements of competition law.
  - (31) The court shall warn in writing persons who participate in the examination of a case whose materials include a state secret object or trade secret and who have the right to acquaint themselves with the case materials, of the duty to preserve state secrets or trade secrets and of the liability provided for disclosure of state secrets or trade secrets. Production of copies of documents containing state secrets or trade secrets is not permitted.
  - (32) If the court needs to verify information that is a state secret object for the establishment of objective truth, persons whose rights to acquaint themselves with case materials containing state secrets have not been restricted by the court, and, if necessary, other persons who have a special permit for access to state secrets shall participate in the verification of this information.
  - (4) The parties to the case participate in the closed court session and, if necessary — also experts and interpreters.
  - (5) If no party to the case objects, with the permission of the presiding judge of the court session, persons who have a special reason to do so may participate in the closed court session.
  - (6) A case in a closed court session is examined in compliance with all procedural rules.
  - (7) Court decisions in cases examined publicly shall be announced publicly.
  - (8) In cases examined in a closed session, the operative part of the court decision shall be announced publicly. In cases concerning approval or revocation of adoption, the decision shall be announced in a closed court session.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012., 13.02.2014., 23.04.2015., 19.10.2017., 28.02.2019. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 12.pants. Individual and Collegial Examination of Civil Cases

(1) In the first instance court, a civil case is examined by a judge individually.

(2) In the court of appeal and cassation instance, a civil case is examined collegially.

#### 13.pants. Language of Proceedings

(1) Proceedings are conducted in the state language.

(2) Parties submit documents in foreign languages with a certified translation in the state language attached in the prescribed manner.

(3) The court may allow individual procedural actions in another language if requested by one of the parties and if all parties agree. The court session protocol and court decisions shall be written in the state language.

(4) For parties who receive state-provided legal aid in the case or are exempt from payment of court costs, the court ensures the right to familiarize themselves with case materials and participate in procedural actions using the assistance of an interpreter if they do not speak the language of proceedings.

(With amendments made by the law of 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016. The amendment related to interpreters in the fourth paragraph enters into force on 31.07.2016. See transitional provision 114.)

#### 14.pants. Immutability of the Composition of the Court

(1) Examination of a case on the merits proceeds with an immutable composition of the court.

(2) Replacement of a judge during trial is permissible only if, due to transfer to another job, illness or other objective reasons, he cannot complete the examination of the case.

(3) If during trial, before drafting the judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment set out in Article 193 of this law, one of the judges is replaced by another judge, the trial must be started anew. The decision on replacement of a judge is made by the president of the court in the manner prescribed in the law "On Judicial Power".

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002, with amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The new wording of the first sentence of the third paragraph enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provision 137.)

#### 15.pants. Directness and Orality of Civil Case Examination

(1) The court of first instance and the court of appeal, when examining a civil case, itself examines the evidence in the case.

(2) Persons invited and summoned to court give explanations and testimonies orally. The testimonies of previously questioned witnesses, written evidence and other materials are read out at the request of the parties. The court may not read out documents in the case if the parties agree.

(3) In cases provided for in this law or in European Union legal norms, the court examines applications, complaints and questions in written proceedings without holding a court session. If the court deems it necessary to clarify additional circumstances that could be significant in deciding the application, complaint and question, the court may examine it in a court session, notifying the parties in advance of its time and place. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application, complaint and question.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002, with amendments made by the laws of 25.05.2006, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

2.nodaļa

Composition of the Court

#### 16.pants. Judges

Cases in court are examined by judges appointed or confirmed in the manner prescribed in the law "On Judicial Power".

#### 17.pants. Decision of Questions in Court

(1) All questions that arise when examining a case collegially are decided by judges by a majority of votes. No judge has the right to abstain from voting.

(2) In cases provided for in this law, questions are decided by the judge individually.

#### 18.pants. Inadmissibility of a Judge's Participation in Repeated Examination of a Case

(1) A judge who participated in the examination of a case in a court of first instance may not participate in the examination of this case in a court of appeal or cassation, as well as in a new examination of the case in a court of first instance, if a judgment or decision on termination of proceedings or leaving an action without examination that was drafted with his participation has been annulled.

(2) A judge who participated in the examination of a case in a court of appeal or cassation may not participate in the examination of this case in a court of first instance or a court of appeal.

#### 19.pants. Withdrawal or Challenge of a Judge

(1) A judge is not entitled to participate in the examination of a case if he:

- 1) in the previous examination of this case was a party, witness, expert, interpreter or court session secretary;
- 2) is in a relationship of kinship up to the third degree or affinity up to the second degree with any of the parties;
- 3) is in a relationship of kinship up to the third degree or affinity up to the second degree with any of the judges who are in the composition of the court examining the case;
- 4) is personally directly or indirectly interested in the outcome of the case or there are other circumstances that give rise to justified doubts about his objectivity.
  - (2) If the circumstances mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article or in Article 18 of this law exist, the judge withdraws before the commencement of the trial.
  - (3) If the judge discovers the circumstances mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article during trial, the withdrawal must be made in a court session, indicating the reasons for withdrawal. In this case, the court postpones the examination of the case.
  - (4) If the judge has not withdrawn, any party may, on the grounds mentioned in this Article, submit a challenge to a judge or several judges simultaneously, indicating the reasons for the withdrawal of each judge.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 20.pants. Submission of a Challenge

(1) A party may submit a challenge in writing or orally, and an entry shall be made thereof in the court session protocol.

(2) A challenge must be submitted before the examination of the case on the merits has commenced. Later, a challenge may be submitted if its grounds became known during the trial.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 21.pants. Procedure for Examining a Submitted Challenge

(1) If a challenge is submitted, the court hears the opinion of other parties and listens to the judge against whom the challenge is submitted.

(2) The challenge submitted in the court session is decided by the court in deliberation.

(3) In a case that a judge examines individually, the submitted challenge is decided by the judge himself.

(4) In a case examined collegially, the submitted challenge is decided in the following manner:

- 1) if the challenge is submitted against one judge, it is decided by the remaining composition of the court. If the votes are equally divided, the judge is challenged;
- 2) if the challenge is submitted against several judges, it is decided by the same court in full composition by a majority of votes.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 22.pants. Consequences of Satisfying a Challenge

(1) If a judge or several judges are challenged, the case is examined by the same court in a different composition.

(2) If it is not possible to form a new composition of the court in the respective court, the case is sent to another district (city) court or another regional court.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

3.nodaļa

Jurisdiction and Venue of Civil Disputes

#### 23.pants. Jurisdiction

(1) All civil disputes are subject to the court unless otherwise provided by law. This does not deprive the parties of the right, by mutual agreement, to resort to arbitration for dispute resolution or to use mediation.

(2) The question of jurisdiction over a dispute is decided by the court or the judge. If the court or judge recognizes that the dispute is not subject to the court, the decision must indicate the institution within whose competence the resolution of this dispute falls.

(3) The court also examines applications of natural and legal persons that do not have the character of a civil dispute, if this is provided for by law.

(With amendments made by the law of 22.05.2014, which enters into force on 18.06.2014.)

#### 24.pants. Jurisdiction

(1) A district (city) court examines civil cases as a court of first instance. Riga City Court examines cases whose materials include a state secret object, and cases on patent rights, plant varieties, semiconductor product topographies, designs, trademarks, certification marks and geographical indications protection, cases on copyright and related rights, database creators' rights (sui generis) protection and cases on trade secret protection against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure. If the case under consideration includes a claim that is related to a claim in a case that has jurisdiction both to Riga City Court and to a district (city) court, or if a counterclaim that has jurisdiction to Riga City Court has been received in a district (city) court, the case is examined by Riga City Court.

(11) The Court of Economic Affairs as a court of first instance examines:

- 1) claims arising from reinsurance contracts;
- 2) claims arising from investment services or investment ancillary services contracts;
- 3) claims by European Union Member State investors against the State of Latvia on investment protection;
- 4) claims arising from group legal relationships;
- 5) claims arising from mutual legal relationships between members (shareholders) of a capital company;
- 6) claims arising from financial collateral contracts;
- 7) claims arising from capital company transactions with related parties within the meaning of the Commercial Law and the Financial Instrument Market Law;
- 8) claims arising from business transfers and company reorganization, excluding employee claims;
- 9) claims arising from contractual obligations between construction process participants, including with subcontractors, in relation to the construction of such second and third group buildings for which a building permit is required, excluding the construction of a separate one-apartment or two-apartment residential building and functionally related buildings;
- 10) claims regarding competition law violations;
- 11) claims regarding decisions of a capital company's members' (shareholders') meeting;
- 12) applications regarding liquidation and insolvency of credit institutions.
  - (12) If the case under consideration includes a claim that is mutually related to a claim in a case that has jurisdiction to the Court of Economic Affairs, or if a counterclaim that has jurisdiction to the Court of Economic Affairs has been received in a district (city) court, the case is examined by the Court of Economic Affairs.
  - (13) If the case under consideration includes a claim that is mutually related to a claim in a case that has jurisdiction both to the Court of Economic Affairs and to Riga City Court in accordance with the jurisdiction established in the third sentence of the first paragraph of this Article, or if a counterclaim that has jurisdiction to the other court has been received in one of these courts, the case is examined by Riga City Court.
  - (2) A regional court as an appellate instance examines cases in the appellate procedure.
  - (21) A decision of the Court of Economic Affairs appealed in the appellate procedure is examined by the Riga Regional Court.
  - (3) The Supreme Court as a cassation instance examines cases in the cassation procedure.

(As worded by the Law of 30.10.2014., with amendments made by the Laws of 31.05.2018., 25.10.2018., 28.02.2019., 01.10.2020., 21.01.2021., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 01.08.2022.)

#### 25.pants. Jurisdiction of Regional Court

(Deleted by the Law of 30.10.2014., which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

#### 26.pants. Bringing a Claim According to Defendant's Declared Place of Residence or Registered Address

(1) A claim against a natural person is brought in court according to its declared place of residence.

(2) A claim against a legal person is brought in court according to its registered address.

(With amendments made by the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 27.pants. Bringing a Claim if Defendant Has No Declared Place of Residence

(1) A claim against a defendant who has no declared place of residence is to be brought according to his or her place of residence.

(2) A claim against a defendant whose place of residence is not known or who has no permanent place of residence in Latvia is to be brought according to the location of his or her immovable property or according to his or her last known place of residence.

(With amendments made by the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 28.pants. Jurisdiction by Claimant's Choice

(1) A claim arising in connection with the activities of a branch or representative office of a legal person may also be brought in court according to the registered address of the branch or representative office.

(11) A claim regarding fulfilment of obligations against a commercial company that has been reorganized by way of cross-border conversion to another Member State may, within two years after the entry into force of the reorganization, also be brought according to the last registered address of the commercial company in Latvia.

(2) A claim regarding recovery of maintenance for a child or parent or establishment of paternity may be brought by the claimant also according to his or her own declared place of residence.

(3) A claim arising from personal offences (Articles 1635, 2347–2353 of the Civil Law), the claimant may bring also according to his or her own declared place of residence or according to the place where the offence was committed.

(4) A claim regarding losses caused to the property of a natural or legal person may also be brought according to the place where they were caused.

(5) A claim regarding return of property or compensation for its value may be brought by the claimant also according to his or her own declared place of residence.

(6) A maritime claim may also be brought according to the place of arrest of the defendant's vessel.

(7) A claim against several defendants who live or are located in different places may be brought according to the declared place of residence or registered address of one defendant.

(8) A claim regarding divorce or non-existence of marriage may be brought in court by the claimant's choice in accordance with the provisions of Article 234 of this Law.

(9) A claim arising from employment legal relationships may be brought by the claimant also according to his or her own declared place of residence or place of work.

(10) If in the cases referred to in this Article the claimant has no declared place of residence, he or she may bring the claim according to his or her own place of residence.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 19.06.2003., 07.04.2004., 28.10.2010., 09.06.2011., 29.11.2012. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 29.pants. Exclusive Jurisdiction

(1) A claim regarding property rights and regarding any other right in rem to immovable property or its accessories, as well as a claim regarding registration of the said rights in the Land Register or regarding deletion of these rights and regarding exclusion of property from a description deed is to be brought according to the location of the property.

(2) A creditor's claims against the estate, when the heirs confirmed by succession rights or who have accepted the inheritance are not known, have jurisdiction to the court according to the testator's declared place of residence or place of residence, but if his or her declared place of residence or place of residence has not been in Latvia or if it is not known, — to the court according to the location of the inherited property or its parts.

(3) Exclusive jurisdiction may also be established in other laws.

(With amendments made by the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 30.pants. Contractual Jurisdiction

(1) When concluding a contract, the parties may determine the court of first instance in which disputes that may arise between them regarding this contract or its performance are to be decided.

(2) The exclusive jurisdiction established by law cannot be altered by agreement of the parties.

#### 31.pants. Jurisdiction of Several Mutually Related Cases

(1) A counterclaim regardless of its jurisdiction is to be brought in court according to the place of examination of the initial claim.

(2) (Deleted by the Law of 11.11.2021.)

(With amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 31.1 pants. Bringing a Claim in Accordance with International Treaties Binding on the Republic of Latvia and European Union Legal Norms if the Case Has Jurisdiction to a Court of Latvia

If in accordance with international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia and European Union legal norms the case has jurisdiction to a court of Latvia, but the jurisdiction provisions of this Law do not provide in which court the claim is to be brought, the claimant may bring the claim in any court of Latvia by his or her own choice, observing the provisions of Articles 23 and 24 of this Law.

(As worded by the Law of 29.11.2012., with amendments made by the Law of 30.10.2014., which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

#### 32.pants. Transfer of cases accepted in proceedings to another court

(1) A case that a court has accepted in its proceedings, observing the rules of jurisdiction, must be examined by the court on the merits, even if its jurisdiction has changed during the course of the case.

(2) The court may transfer a case for examination to another court if:

- 1) when examining the case in court, it is discovered that it was accepted in violation of the rules of jurisdiction;
- 2) after the removal or recusal of one or more judges, their replacement in the same court is not possible;
- 3) (deleted by the law of 29.11.2012.).
  - (3) (Deleted by the law of 30.10.2014.)
  - (4) The decision on the transfer of a case for examination to another court may be appealed by the parties to the case in the manner prescribed by this law.
  - (5) The case is transferred for examination to another court when the time limit for appealing this decision has expired, but if the decision has been appealed — after the dismissal of the appeal.
  - (6) A case that has been sent from one court to another court shall be accepted for examination by the court to which the case has been sent.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 29.11.2012. and 30.10.2014., which enter into force on 01.01.2015.)

Article 32.1 Transfer of cases accepted in proceedings to another court to ensure faster examination of the case

(1) A court of first instance may initiate the transfer for examination to another court of the same instance of a claim proceedings case pending before it, except for a case whose jurisdiction is determined in accordance with Article 30 of this law, if the examination of the case on the merits has not been commenced and, by transferring the case to another court, it is possible to achieve its faster examination. When initiating the transfer of a case for examination to another court of the same instance, preference is given to the transfer of a case to be examined in written proceedings.

(2) A regional court may initiate the transfer for examination to another regional court of an appellate case pending before it, which has been initiated regarding a judgment (supplementary judgment) of a court of first instance, if the examination of the case on the merits has not been commenced and, by transferring the case to another court, it is possible to achieve its faster examination.

(3) A case whose jurisdiction is determined in accordance with Article 28 or 29 of this law may be initiated for transfer for examination to another court of the same instance by the instance court before which the case is pending only upon a written request of the plaintiff.

(4) The decision on the transfer of a case from one court to another court, upon the proposal of the president of the court to which the case is subject to jurisdiction, shall be taken by the president of a court one level higher. If a case pending in a district (city) court is to be transferred to a court located in another court district, the question shall be decided by the president of the regional court in whose territory of operation the court initiating the transfer of the case to another court is located. The decision is taken in the form of a resolution and is not subject to appeal.

(5) The court that has initiated the transfer of the case to another court shall inform the parties to the case about the adoption of the decision referred to in paragraph four of this Article.

(6) If a case has been transferred for examination to another court in any of the judicial instances to ensure its faster examination, repeated transfer of the case in the manner prescribed by this Article is not permissible.

(In the wording of the law of 23.04.2015. with amendments made by the law of 21.01.2021., which enters into force on 01.03.2021.)

Litigation costs

#### Article 33. Litigation costs

(1) Litigation costs are court costs, security deposit and costs related to conducting the case.

(2) Court costs are:

- 1) state fee;
- 2) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);
- 3) costs related to the examination of the case.
  - (3) Costs related to conducting the case are:
- 1) costs for legal assistance;
- 2) costs related to appearance at court sessions;
- 3) costs related to the collection of evidence;
- 4) costs for state-provided legal aid;
- 5) costs for interpreter assistance at court sessions.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 10.12.2015., 04.02.2016., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 34.pants. State Fee

(1) For each statement of claim — an initial claim or counterclaim, a third party application with an independent claim regarding the subject matter of the dispute submitted in proceedings already commenced, an application in special proceedings cases, as well as other applications provided for in this Article that are submitted to court — a state fee is payable in the following amount:

- 1) for a claim that can be valued in a monetary sum:

  - c) from 7115 euro to 28 457 euro, — 520 euro plus 3.2 percent of the claim amount exceeding 7114 euro,

  - f) more than 711 435 euro, — 8715 euro plus 0.6 percent of the claim amount exceeding 711 435 euro;

- 3) for an application in special proceedings cases — 45 euro, for an insolvency proceedings application submitted by a creditor regarding a legal person or natural person who is simultaneously a sole trader, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, farm, fishery or performer of economic activity — 355 euro, for an insolvency proceedings application submitted by a debtor regarding a legal person or natural person — 70 euro, for a legal protection proceedings application — 145 euro, for a credit institution insolvency or liquidation application — 355 euro;
- 4) for other claims that are not of a pecuniary nature or are not to be valued, — 70 euro;
- 41) for a statement of claim for recognition of an arbitration agreement as invalid — 500 euro;
- 5) for an application concerning copyright and related rights, database protection (sui generis), trademarks, certification marks and geographical indications, patents, designs, plant varieties, topographies of semiconductor products (hereinafter — intellectual property rights) infringements and protection, for an application in cases concerning protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure, as well as for an application in cases where the dispute was examined in the Industrial Property Appeals Board, — 215 euro;
- 6) for a statement of claim in a case concerning recognition of decisions of meetings of members (shareholders) of capital companies as invalid (Chapter 30.4) — 145 euro;
- 7) for an application for securing a claim or an application for interim protection — 70 euro;
- 71) for an application for a European Account Preservation Order in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014 establishing a European Account Preservation Order procedure to facilitate cross-border debt recovery in civil and commercial matters (hereinafter — Regulation No. 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council) — 0.5 percent of the claim amount, but not less than 70 euro;

8) for an application for preservation of evidence, if it is submitted before filing a claim, — 30 euro;

9) for an application for a European order for payment in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 December 2006 creating a European order for payment procedure (hereinafter — Regulation No. 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council), or for voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings — 2 percent of the debt amount or the value of property to be returned or sold at voluntary auction, but not more than 500 euro;

91) for an application for enforcement of obligations through warning procedure — 2 percent of the debt amount;

92) for an application for undisputed enforcement — 2 percent of the debt amount or the value of property to be returned, but not more than 500 euro, but if undisputed enforcement is permitted for obligations that are not of a pecuniary nature or are not to be valued, — 45 euro;

11) for an application for reopening of proceedings and new examination of a case in which a judgment in absentia was made, — in the same amount as for a statement of claim;

12) for a statement of claim for division of joint property — in the same amount as for a statement of claim in the general procedure;

13) for complaints in legal protection proceedings cases, for complaints in insolvency proceedings cases in connection with creditors' meeting decisions, for complaints concerning decisions of the Insolvency Control Service, as well as for performance of actions provided for in Articles 46 and 51 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 May 2015 on insolvency proceedings (hereinafter — Regulation No. 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council) — 25 euro;

14) (deleted by the Law of 25.03.2021);

15) for an application for registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer — 70 euro;

17) for an application for cancellation of a natural person's release from debt obligations in cases specified in the Law on Release of Natural Persons from Debt Obligations — 70 euro;

18) for an application for issuing a duplicate writ of execution — 15 euro;

#### 35.pants. Claim Amount

(1) The claim amount is:

- 1) in claims for recovery of money — the amount to be recovered;
- 2) in claims for recovery of property — the value of the property to be recovered;
- 3) in claims for recovery of maintenance — the total amount of payments for one year;
- 4) in claims for fixed-term payments and contributions — the total amount of all payments or contributions, but not more than for three years;
- 5) in claims for indefinite or lifetime payments and contributions — the total amount of all payments and contributions for three years;
- 6) in claims for reduction or increase of payments or contributions — the amount by which the payments or contributions are reduced or increased, but not more than for one year;
- 7) in claims for termination of payments or contributions — the total amount of remaining payments or contributions, but not more than for one year;
- 8) in claims for early termination of lease and rent agreements — the total amount of payments for the remaining term of the agreement, but not more than for three years;
- 9) in claims for property rights to immovable property — its value, but not less than its cadastral value;
- 10) in claims consisting of several independent proprietary claims — the total amount of all claims;
- 11) in claims for termination or invalidation of a transaction — the amount of the disputed transaction.
  - (2) The claim amount is indicated by the claimant. If the indicated claim amount manifestly does not correspond to the actual value of the property to be recovered, the claim amount is determined by the court.

(With amendments made by the law of 02.09.2004., which comes into force on 07.10.2004.)

#### 36.pants. Additional State Fee

(1) For a claim that is difficult to assess at the time of submission, the judge determines the amount of state fee in advance. The final amount of state fee is determined by the court when examining the case.

(2) If the claim amount is increased, except for the addition of interest and increments, the state fee is to be paid accordingly.

36.1 pants. Crediting of State Fee

The fee paid for an application for a European payment order in accordance with Regulation No. 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be credited to the state fee for the claim if the defendant has notified an objection to the European payment order and the claim proceedings are continued.

(In the wording of the law of 08.09.2011., which comes into force on 30.09.2011.)

#### 37.pants. Refund of State Fee

(1) The paid state fee shall be refunded in full or in part in the following cases:

- 1) if a higher fee has been paid than required by law;
- 2) if the court refuses to accept the application;
- 3) if proceedings in the case are terminated on the ground that the examination of the case is not subject to the court;
- 4) if the claim is left without examination on the ground that the interested person who has applied to the court has not observed the procedure for out-of-court examination of the case established for the relevant category of cases, or the application has been submitted by a person with no civil procedural capacity;
- 5) if the court has approved a settlement — in the amount of 50 percent of the state fee paid for proceedings in the court of the relevant instance;
- 6) if the court refuses to initiate appellate proceedings in accordance with the seventh part of Article 440.8 of this Law — in the amount of 50 percent of the state fee paid;
- 7) if the ground for termination of proceedings is the claimant's renunciation of the claim because a mediation agreement has been reached, which is certified by a written confirmation of the mediation result issued by the mediator — in the amount of 50 percent of the state fee paid.
  - (2) (Declared invalid by the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 02.11.2020.)
  - (3) The court or judge, on its own initiative or upon an application by a person, adopts a decision on refund of the state fee if any of the cases mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article is established. An application for refund of the state fee may be submitted to the court where the case is located within one year from the day when the ground for refund of the state fee arose.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 20.12.2010., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 20.03.2014., 22.05.2014., 29.10.2015., the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 02.11.2020. and the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 39.pants. Costs Related to the Examination of a Case

(1) Costs related to the examination of a case are:

- 1) amounts to be paid to witnesses and experts;
- 2) costs related to the examination of witnesses or on-site inspections;
- 3) costs related to the search for the defendant or a witness;
- 4) costs related to the enforcement of a court judgment;
- 5) costs related to the preparation, delivery, issuance, translation of copies of court summons and other court documents and the return of written evidence;
- 6) costs related to the preparation and issuance of the text of an announcement;
- 7) costs related to securing the claim or interim protection;
- 8) (deleted from 01.01.2012. by the law of 31.10.2002.).
  - (2) The amount and procedure for calculating the amounts to be paid to witnesses and experts, as well as costs related to the examination of witnesses or on-site inspections, search for the defendant or a witness, preparation, delivery, issuance, translation of copies of court summons and other court documents, return of written evidence, preparation and issuance of the text of an announcement, and securing the claim or interim protection shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 40.pants. Procedure for Payment of Costs Related to the Examination of a Case

(1) The amounts of costs to be paid to witnesses and experts, or the amounts necessary for payment of costs for the examination of witnesses or on-site inspections, translation of court summons and other court documents, preparation and issuance of the text of an announcement, and securing the claim or interim protection shall be paid by the party that has made the relevant request. The amounts necessary for payment of costs for the preparation, delivery, issuance of copies of court summons and other court documents, and the return of written evidence shall be paid by the state.

(2) If, following a request from Latvia, evidence is obtained or court documents are issued to a person abroad, the amounts of costs that the competent foreign authority requests to be paid before or reimbursed after the execution of the request shall be paid by the party that has made the relevant request.

(3) If both parties have submitted the request referred to in the first or second paragraph of this Article, they shall pay the requested amounts in equal measure.

(4) If the request referred to in the first or second paragraph of this Article has been submitted by the court or judge on its own initiative in the cases provided for in this Law, the necessary amount shall be paid by the state.

(5) The amounts referred to in this Article shall not be paid by a party exempted from payment of court costs.

(In the wording of the law of 05.02.2009. with amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force

#### Article 41. Reimbursement of Court Costs

(1) To the party in whose favor the judgment is made, the court awards from the other party all court costs paid by it. If the claim is satisfied partially, the sums specified in this article are awarded to the plaintiff proportionally to the amount of claims satisfied by the court, but to the defendant — proportionally to that part of the claims in which the claim was rejected. The state fee for an application for resumption of proceedings and new examination of a case in which a default judgment was made is not reimbursed.

(2) If the plaintiff withdraws from the claim, he or she reimburses the defendant for the court costs incurred. The court costs paid by the plaintiff in this case are not reimbursed by the defendant. However, if the plaintiff does not maintain his or her claims because the defendant has voluntarily satisfied them after filing the claim, the court, upon the plaintiff's request, awards from the defendant the court costs paid by the plaintiff.

(3) If the claim is left without examination, the court, upon the defendant's request, awards from the plaintiff the court costs paid by the defendant, except for the case specified in point 2 of the first part of Article 219 of this law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002, 08.09.2011 and 14.12.2017, which enter into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment in the first part regarding the deletion of the words "ancillary complaint about court decision" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provisions points 139 and 140)

#### Article 42. Reimbursement of Court Costs to the State

(1) Court costs, if the plaintiff has been exempted from their payment, are to be awarded from the defendant to state revenue proportionally to the satisfied part of the claim.

(2) If the claim is rejected, left without examination, or if the plaintiff withdraws from the claim, the court costs that have not been paid previously are to be awarded from the plaintiff to state revenue. However, if the plaintiff does not maintain his or her claims because the defendant has voluntarily satisfied them after filing the claim, the court costs are collected to state revenue from the defendant.

(3) If the claim is satisfied partially but the defendant is exempted from payment of court costs, they are to be collected to state revenue from the plaintiff who is not exempted from payment of court costs, proportionally to that part of the claim which was rejected.

(4) If both parties are exempted from payment of court costs, the court costs are assumed by the state.

(5) If the court approves a settlement and terminates the proceedings in the case, the court costs that have not been paid previously are to be awarded from both parties to state revenue in equal amounts, unless otherwise specified in the settlement.

(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 23.04.2015, which enter into force on 26.05.2015.)

- 11) plaintiffs — in claims arising from an agreement on performance of work if the plaintiff is a person serving a sentence in a place of imprisonment;

- 31) applicants — for recognition or recognition and enforcement of a foreign decision on recovery of maintenance for a child or parent;
- 4) plaintiffs — in claims for compensation for damage and non-pecuniary harm resulting from a criminal offence or administrative offence;
- 5) prosecutors, those state or municipal institutions which have been granted by law the rights to defend in court the rights and legally protected interests of other persons;
- 6) applicants — for restriction of a person's legal capacity due to mental disorder or other health impairments, review of restriction of legal capacity or restoration of legal capacity;
- 61) applicants — for establishment and termination of temporary guardianship;
- 7) applicants — for restriction of a person's legal capacity and establishment of guardianship due to a profligate or extravagant lifestyle, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances;
- 8) defendants — in cases concerning reduction of court-ordered maintenance for a child or parent and reduction of those payments which the court has ordered in claims arising from personal injuries resulting in mutilation or other damage to health or death of a person;
- 9) (deleted as of 01.01.2012. by the Law of 31.10.2002.);
- 91) applicants — in cases concerning unlawful removal of a child across a border or retention;
- 10) administrators — in claims brought on behalf of persons for whom insolvency proceedings of a legal person and insolvency proceedings of a natural person have been declared, if such persons are participants in or victims of the relevant legal transaction or unlawful action in connection with which the claim is brought;
- 11) creditors — in enforcement matters concerning recoveries to state revenues;
- 111) creditors — in enforcement matters when recovery is to be made in accordance with a uniform instrument permitting enforcement in the requested Member State;
- 12) the tax (duty) administration — in applications in insolvency proceedings of legal persons;
- 13) the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs — in cases concerning deprivation of Latvian citizenship;
- 14) the State Social Insurance Agency — in cases concerning recovery of financial resources to the state budget in respect of overpayment of social insurance services or state social benefits and payment of social insurance services or state social benefits in connection with road traffic accidents;
- 15) applicants — for temporary protection against violence;
- 16) a party receiving state-provided legal aid in a case;
- 161) a party recognized as a whistleblower or who is his or her relative or related person within the meaning of the Whistleblowing Law;
- 17) applicants — for confirmation of adoption;
- 18) a sworn notary — in cases concerning cancellation of a natural person's discharge from debt obligations if the sworn notary has drawn up a notarial deed on a natural person's discharge from debt obligations;
- 19) complainants — concerning a sworn notary's refusal to certify an application for a natural person's discharge from debt obligations, as well as concerning refusal to discharge a natural person from debt obligations;
- 20) plaintiffs — in consumer collective actions.
  - (2) If a prosecutor, those state or municipal institutions which have been granted by law the rights to defend in court the rights and legally protected interests of other persons, withdraw an application submitted on behalf of another person, but that person requests examination of the case on the merits, court costs must be paid in accordance with general rules.
  - (3) Parties shall also be exempt from payment of court costs to state revenues in other cases provided for by law.
  - (4) The court or judge, taking into account the financial situation of a natural person, fully or partially exempts the person from payment of court costs to state revenues, and also postpones payment of court costs awarded to state revenues or divides it into instalments.
  - (5) In claims for divorce, at the request of the plaintiff, the judge postpones payment of the state fee or divides it into instalments if the plaintiff has care of a minor child.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 20.06.2001., 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 07.09.2006., 01.11.2007., 05.02.2009., 01.06.2017., 22.06.2017., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018., 28.02.2019., 11.11.2021., 15.06.2021., 16.03.2023. and 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023. Security deposit

(1) A security deposit is payable in the following amount:

- 1) for an appeal, except an appeal against a decision refusing to exempt from a security deposit or payment of court costs to state revenues — 70 euros;
- 2) for a cassation appeal — 300 euros;
- 3) for a complaint against actions of an insolvency administrator (hereinafter — administrator) or a sworn bailiff, or a sworn notary — 70 euros;
- 4) for an application for reopening of a case due to newly discovered circumstances — 300 euros.
  - (2) A security deposit need not be paid by persons who are exempt from the state fee in accordance with law. The court or judge, taking into account the financial situation of a natural person, may fully or partially exempt a person from payment of a security deposit.

(In the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021. 43.2 pants. Refund of security deposit

(1) If the court fully or in any part thereof annuls or amends the appealed or contested court decision or fully or partially grants a complaint against actions of an insolvency administrator, sworn bailiff or sworn notary, the security deposit shall be refunded. If the appeal or application is rejected, the security deposit shall not be refunded.

(2) A security deposit shall also be refunded or not refunded in other cases provided for in this Law.

(3) A security deposit shall be refunded from state budget resources on the basis of a decision of the court or judge.

(In the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

43.3 pants. Payment of court costs and security deposit into an incorrect state budget account

If court costs or a security deposit has been paid into an incorrect account of the Court Administration, the State Revenue Service or the Supreme Court in the State Treasury, then these court costs and security deposit shall be transferred by the Court Administration, the State Revenue Service or the Supreme Court to the appropriate account on the basis of a decision in the form of a resolution by the judge who has established it.

(In the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 44.pants. Litigation Costs and Their Reimbursement

(1) Litigation costs are reimbursable in the following amounts:

- 1) expenses for payment of legal assistance:
  - a) reimbursable expenses for payment of legal assistance in claims of a proprietary nature where the claim amount does not exceed 8500 euros — in their actual amount, but not more than 30 percent of the satisfied part of the claims,
  - b) reimbursable expenses for payment of legal assistance in claims of a proprietary nature where the claim amount is from 8501 euros to 57 000 euros — in their actual amount, but not more than 2850 euros,
  - c) reimbursable expenses for payment of legal assistance in claims of a proprietary nature where the claim amount exceeds 57 001 euros — in their actual amount, but not more than 5 percent of the satisfied part of the claims,
  - d) reimbursable expenses for payment of legal assistance in claims of a non-proprietary nature — in their actual amount, but not more than 2850 euros,
  - e) reimbursable expenses for payment of legal assistance in claims of a non-proprietary nature and in cases which the court has recognised as complex — in their actual amount, but not more than 4275 euros;
- 2) travel and subsistence expenses in connection with attendance at a court hearing, as well as in connection with the presence or participation of parties or their representatives in obtaining evidence, when evidence is obtained abroad at the request of Latvia — according to the rates established by the Cabinet of Ministers for reimbursement of business trip expenses;
- 3) expenses in connection with obtaining written evidence — in the actual amount of expenses;
- 4) interpreter expenses in connection with the presence or participation of parties or their representatives in obtaining evidence, when evidence is obtained abroad at the request of Latvia — in the actual amount of expenses, but not more than the rates established by the Cabinet of Ministers;
- 5) interpreter expenses in connection with the participation of parties in a court hearing — in the actual amount of expenses, but not more than the rates established by the Cabinet of Ministers.
  - (11) The actual amount of reimbursable expenses referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of this Article shall be considered to include both expenses that have already been paid and expenses for which an invoice has been issued in accordance with the agreement between the lawyer and the party on the provision of legal assistance.
  - (2) Litigation costs shall be awarded from the defendant in favour of the plaintiff if his or her claim has been satisfied in full or in part, as well as where the plaintiff does not maintain his or her claims because the defendant has voluntarily satisfied them after the submission of the claim.
  - (3) If the claim is rejected, litigation costs shall be awarded from the plaintiff in favour of the defendant.
  - (4) If the claim has been heard only by a court of first instance, reimbursable expenses for payment of legal assistance may not exceed 50 percent of the maximum reimbursement amount established in the first paragraph of this Article.
  - (5) The court may determine a lower amount of reimbursable expenses for payment of legal assistance, observing the principles of fairness and proportionality, as well as evaluating the objective circumstances related to the case, in particular — the degree of complexity and volume of the case, the number of court hearings during the consideration of the case and the court instance in which the claim is being heard.
  - (6) The court may refuse to reimburse interpreter expenses if the party in whose favour these expenses are to be awarded has command of the language of the proceedings.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 20.06.2001., 05.02.2009., 29.11.2012., 12.09.2013., 04.02.2016. and 22.06.2017., which enters into force on 01.08.2017.)

44.1 pants. Expenses for State-Provided Legal Aid and Their Reimbursement to the State

(1) Expenses for state-provided legal aid are:

- 1) expenses for the provision of state-provided legal aid;
- 2) reimbursable expenses related to the provision of state-provided legal aid.
  - (2) The court, when issuing a decision, shall recover expenses for state-provided legal aid in accordance with the conditions specified in Article 42 of this Law.
  - (3) The court shall obtain information on the amount of state-provided legal aid expenses from the state-provided legal aid register and from the notification submitted by the state-provided legal aid provider on the provision of state-provided legal aid in civil cases, if such information is not included in the state-provided legal aid register.
  - (4) If a party from whom expenses for state-provided legal aid would have to be recovered in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article is exempt from payment of court costs, then expenses related to the provision of state-provided legal aid shall be borne by the state.

(As worded by the Law of 10.12.2015., which enters into force on 01.01.2016. See point 112 of the transitional provisions)

#### 45.pants. Appeal of Decisions on Litigation Costs

A decision on the question of litigation costs may be appealed by a person to whom it applies.

(As worded by the Law of 19.06.2003., which enters into force on 24.07.2003.)

5.nodaļa

Procedural Time Limits

#### 46.pants. Determination of Procedural Time Limits

(1) Procedural actions shall be performed within the time limits established by law. If procedural time limits are not established by law, they shall be determined by the court or judge. The length of the time limit determined by the court or judge must be such that the procedural action can be performed.

(2) For the performance of procedural actions, a specific date or a time limit until a specific date, or a period of time (in years, months, days or hours) shall be determined. If a procedural action need not be performed on a specific date, it may be performed throughout the entire established time limit.

(3) A time limit may be determined by also indicating an event which must occur in any case.

(4) If the law establishes time limits for the court or judge for the hearing of cases or the performance of other procedural actions and the participant in the case is notified of the performance of the relevant procedural action in accordance with Article 56.2 of this Law, but the performance of the relevant procedural action within the time limit established by law is not possible, the court or judge is entitled to determine a more reasonable and longer time limit.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002. and 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### 47.pants. Commencement of Calculation of Procedural Time Limits

(1) A time limit calculated in years, months or days shall commence on the next day after the date or after the event that determines its commencement.

(2) A time limit calculated in hours shall commence in the next hour after the event that determines its commencement.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

#### 48.pants. Expiry of Procedural Time Limits

(1) A time limit calculated in years shall expire in the relevant month and on the relevant date of the last year of the time limit. A time limit calculated in months shall expire on the relevant date of the last month of the time limit. If a time limit calculated in months ends in a month which does not have the relevant date, it shall expire on the last day of that month. A time limit established until a specific date shall expire on that date.

(2) If the last day of the time limit is a Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday established by law, the next working day shall be considered as the last day of the time limit.

(3) A procedural action for which the time limit expires may be performed on the last day of the time limit until twenty-four o'clock.

(4) If the procedural action is to be performed in court, the time limit shall expire at the hour when the court finishes work. If a statement of claim, complaint or other postal items have been submitted to a communications institution on the last day of the time limit before twenty-four o'clock, they shall be deemed to have been submitted within the time limit.

(With amendments made by the Law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 49.pants. Consequences of Failure to Observe Procedural Time Limits

The right to perform procedural actions shall be lost upon expiry of the time limit established by law or by the court. Complaints and documents submitted after the expiry of the procedural time limit shall not be accepted.

(As worded by the Law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 50.pants. Suspension of Procedural Time Limits

When proceedings in a case are suspended, the calculation of the time limit shall be suspended. The calculation of the time limit shall stop at the moment when a circumstance has arisen which is grounds for suspending the proceedings. The calculation of the procedural time limit shall continue from the day when proceedings in the case are resumed.

(With amendments made by the Law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### Article 51. Renewal of Procedural Time Limits

(1) Missed procedural time limits shall be renewed by the court upon application of a party to the case if it considers the reasons for missing them to be justified.

(2) When renewing a missed time limit, the court shall simultaneously allow the missed procedural action to be performed.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### Article 52. Extension of Procedural Time Limits

Time limits set by the court or judge may be extended upon application of a party to the case.

#### Article 53. Procedure for Extension and Renewal of Procedural Time Limits

(1) An application for extension of a time limit or renewal of a missed time limit shall be submitted to the court in which the missed action was to be performed, and it shall be examined in written proceedings. The parties to the case shall be notified in advance of the examination of the application in written proceedings, simultaneously sending them the application for extension of the time limit or renewal of the missed time limit.

(2) The application for renewal of a procedural time limit shall be accompanied by documents necessary for performance of the procedural action and justification for renewal of the time limit.

(3) A time limit set by a judge may be extended by the judge individually .

(4) An appeal may be filed against the refusal of the court or judge to extend or renew a time limit.

(With amendments made by the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

Chapter 6

Court Notifications, Summons and Delivery and Issuance of Court Documents

(Chapter title in the wording of the law of 05.02.2009, which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### Article 54. Summoning to Court

(1) Parties to a case shall be summoned to court by timely notification of the time and place of the court session or separate procedural action.

(2) Parties to a case shall be summoned to court with a court summons. In cases provided for in this Law, the defendant may be summoned to court by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(3) Witnesses and experts shall be summoned to court with court summons.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016. The amendment related to interpreters made in the third part enters into force on 31.07.2016. See transitional provision 114)

Article 54.1 Determination of Defendant's Place of Residence

(1) If the defendant does not have a declared place of residence address in Latvia, the claimant has the duty to indicate to the court the defendant's place of residence address if it is known to him or her.

(2) If the claimant has not been able to determine the defendant's place of residence, which is not in Latvia, due to objective reasons, the court, upon a reasoned request of the claimant, may use procedures provided for in international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia or in European Union legal acts for determining the defendant's address.

(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### Article 55. Court Summons

A summons shall indicate:

- 1) the name, surname, address of the natural person being summoned or the name and registered address of the legal person;
- 2) the name and address of the court;
- 3) the time and place of appearance;
- 4) the name of the case in connection with which the person is summoned;
- 5) an indication in what connection the addressee is summoned;
- 51) an indication that videoconference will be used;
- 6) an indication that a person who has received the summons due to the absence of the addressee has the duty to deliver it to the addressee;
- 7) consequences of non-appearance;
- 8) an indication that proceedings are conducted in the state language and that a party to the case who does not speak the state language has the duty to ensure interpreter assistance himself or herself, except in cases provided for in this Law. A party to the case has the duty to ensure interpreter assistance also for experts or witnesses summoned at his or her request if the expert or witness does not speak the language of the proceedings.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 29.11.2012 and 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016. The amendment related to interpreters, supplementing the article with point 8, enters into force on 31.07.2016. See transitional provision 114)

#### 56.pants. Service and Delivery of Summons and Other Court Documents

(1) (Deleted by the law of 23.11.2016)

(2) Court-prepared documents (decisions, notices, summons, etc.), as well as documents (application in special proceedings, appeals, cassation complaints, written explanations, etc.) submitted to the court by the parties to the case but which are further served by the court, shall be sent electronically, by simple mail or delivered by a messenger.

(21) Court documents shall be sent electronically, observing the following sequence:

- 1) in the online system, if the addressee has notified the court that they consent to communication with the court using the online system;

- 3) to the addressee's official electronic address.

If the defendant does not have a declared place of residence and has not indicated another address for communication with the court, court documents shall be delivered to the address indicated by the party to the case in accordance with the first part of Section 54.1 of this law. Court documents may also be sent to the person's place of work.
  - (23) A natural person has an obligation to be reachable in the online system, at their specified electronic mail address or official electronic address, if the natural person has consented to electronic communication with the court, at the declared place of residence address, at the additional address indicated in the declaration, or at another address specified by that person for communication with the court.
  - (24) If it is not possible to send court documents to a legal person electronically in accordance with Section 2.1 of this Article, they shall be sent to its legal address.
  - (25) A legal person has an obligation to be reachable in the online system, at its specified electronic mail address or official electronic address, if the legal person has consented to electronic communication with the court.
  - (26) When executing a foreign request for service of documents (Sections 672 and 681), documents shall be delivered to the addressee at the address indicated in the request, but if the addressee is not found at that address, they may be delivered in the manner prescribed in this Article.
  - (3) Court documents may be served to the addressee personally against signature, if necessary, by summoning the addressee by summons to appear at the court for the documents to be served.
  - (4) A party to the case may, with the consent of the judge, receive court documents for delivery to another addressee in the case.
  - (5) Court documents delivered by a messenger or a party to the case shall be served to the addressee personally against signature.

In the signature part, the time and date of service of the document shall be noted and the signature part shall be returned to the court. If court documents are delivered by a bailiff or their assistant, an act drawn up by the bailiff or their assistant shall be submitted to the court.
