56.1 pants. Date of Delivery and Service of Court Documents

(1) If court documents have been delivered in the manner prescribed in Section 56 of this law, except for the case provided for in its ninth part, it shall be considered that the person has been notified of the time and place of the court session or procedural action or of the content of the relevant document and the court documents have been served:

- 1) on the date when the addressee or another person received them in accordance with the third, seventh or eighth part of Section 56 of this law;
- 2) on the date when the person refused to receive them (Section 57);
- 3) on the seventh day from the date of sending, if the documents were sent by mail;
- 4) on the third day from the date of sending, if the documents were sent electronically;
- 5) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021).
  - (2) The fact that court documents have been delivered to the address of the natural person's declared place of residence, the additional address indicated in the declaration, the address indicated by the natural person for communication with the court or the legal address of the legal person and a certificate of service of the consignment has been received from the post office or the documents are sent back, does not in itself affect the fact of notification of the documents. The addressee may rebut the presumption that the documents have been served on the seventh day from the date of their sending, if the documents were sent by mail, or on the third day from the date of sending, if the documents were sent electronically, by pointing to objective circumstances that, independent of their will, have been an obstacle to receiving the documents at the indicated address.

(As worded by the law of 05.02.2009, with amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011, 29.11.2012, 23.11.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

56.2 pants. Delivery and Service of Court Documents to a Person Whose Place of Residence or Location is Not in Latvia

(1) To a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, court documents shall be delivered:

- 1) in the manner prescribed in Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2020 on the service in the Member States of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters (service of documents) (hereinafter — Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council) (Chapter 81);
- 2) in the manner prescribed in Article 13 of Regulation (EC) No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 July 2007 establishing a European Small Claims Procedure (hereinafter — Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council);
- 3) in the manner prescribed in international agreements binding on Latvia (Chapter 82);
- 4) in the manner prescribed in Chapter 83 of this law;
- 5) in the manner prescribed in the Hague Convention of 15 November 1965 on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters (hereinafter — the Hague Convention of 1965) (Chapter 81.1).
  - (2) If court documents have been delivered to a person in the manner prescribed in the first part of this Article, it shall be considered that the person has been notified of the time and place of the court session or procedural action or of the content of the relevant document only if a confirmation of service of the document has been received. The documents shall be considered served on the date indicated in the confirmation of service of documents.
  - (21) If court documents have been delivered to a person in the manner prescribed in the first part of this Article and a confirmation of non-service has been received, the court shall evaluate the reasons for non-service of documents and determine the impact of non-service of documents on the proceedings in accordance with the provisions of this law. After evaluating the reasons for non-service of documents, the court may deliver the documents again or use another method for service of documents. If the documents cannot be served again, Section 59 of this law shall apply.
  - (3) This Article shall not apply if a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia conducts the case through an authorised representative in Latvia. In such a case, court documents shall be served in the general procedure only to the representative.
  - (4) This Article shall not apply if the representative's declared place of residence or indicated address is outside Latvia. To a representative whose declared place of residence or indicated address is outside Latvia, summons, court-prepared documents, as well as other electronically prepared documents shall be sent by electronic mail, unless the representative has notified the court of the registration of their participation in the online system.

(As worded by the law of 05.02.2009, with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and

16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### 57.pants. Consequences of Refusal to Accept Court Documents

(1) If the addressee refuses to accept court documents, the document deliverer shall make an appropriate note in the document, also indicating the reasons for refusal, date and time.

(2) Refusal to accept court documents is not an obstacle to the hearing of the case.

(In the wording of the law of 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### 58.pants. Change of Address During Case Proceedings

(1) A party to the case shall notify the court of a change of email address, if they have agreed to electronic communication with the court, or of a change of their address during the proceedings of the case. If such notification has not been made, summonses and other court documents shall be sent to the last email address known to the court, if the party has agreed to electronic communication with the court, or address. In this case, it shall be deemed that the content of the document has been communicated to the party.

(2) If a party fails to notify the court of a change of their email address or address during the proceedings, the court or judge may impose a fine of up to 50 euros.

(With amendments made by the laws of 30.09.2010., 12.09.2013. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 59. pants. Summons to Court by Publication

(1) A defendant whose address could not be established in accordance with Article 54.1 of this law or to whom documents could not be delivered at the address indicated by a party in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 54.1 of this law, or to whom court documents could not be delivered in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law, shall be summoned to court by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(2) Regardless of the publication of the summons in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis", the plaintiff is entitled to publish the text of the court summons at their own expense in other newspapers.

(3) The publication shall indicate the text of the summons corresponding to the content of the summons.

(4) The court may hear the case without the participation of the defendant if at least one month has passed from the day of publication of the summons in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(5) In addition to summoning the defendant by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis", the summons shall also be sent to the location of their immovable property, if indicated by the plaintiff.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 60.pants. Search for Defendant if Their Whereabouts are Unknown

If the whereabouts of the defendant are unknown, the court is entitled to declare a search for the defendant at the request of the plaintiff.

7.nodaļa

Minutes

#### 61.pants. Recording the Course of the Court Session

(1) Minutes of the court session shall be written for each court session. The course of the court session shall be recorded in full using technical means.

(2) Materials obtained as a result of using audio recording or other technical means shall be attached to the case and stored together with it or entered and stored in the court information system.

(3) In cases provided for in this law, minutes shall also be written for individual procedural actions performed outside the court session.

(4) The course of the court session shall not be recorded using technical means if none of the parties to the case has appeared at the court session or if the court needs to verify information that is the subject of a state secret or commercial secret in order to establish the objective truth.

(5) If the course of the court session has been recorded using audio recording, the respective audio recording shall be available to persons who have the right to familiarize themselves with the case materials on the next working day after the day of the court session.

(In the wording of the law of 19.12.2013. with amendments made by the laws of 22.05.2014. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force

#### 62.pants. Content of the Minutes

(1) If the course of the court session is not recorded using technical means, the minutes of the court session shall indicate:

- 1) the year, date, month and place of the court session;
- 2) the name of the court hearing the case, the composition of the court, the secretary of the court session, the lawyer and prosecutor participating in the case;
- 3) that the course of the court session is being recorded using technical means;
- 4) the time of opening of the court session;
- 5) the name of the case;
- 6) information about the appearance of parties to the case, witnesses, experts and interpreters;
- 7) information that the procedural rights and obligations have been explained to the parties to the case;
- 8) information that witnesses, experts and interpreters have been warned of criminal liability;
- 9) information about the examination of material and written evidence;
- 10) court orders and decisions that have not been adopted in the form of separate procedural documents;
- 11) information about the court's withdrawal to adopt a decision or render a judgment;
- 12) information about the announcement of a judgment or decision adopted in the form of a separate procedural document;
- 13) information about the explanation of the content of the judgment or decision, the procedure for appeal and the time limit;
- 14) information about when the parties to the case may familiarize themselves with the minutes of the court session, audio recording and the text of the judgment;
- 15) the time of closing of the court session;
- 16) the time of signing of the minutes of the court session.
  - (2) A note shall be made in the minutes of the court session about the plaintiff's withdrawal from the claim, as well as about the fact that the defendant has acknowledged the claim and the parties to the case have acknowledged legal facts.
  - (3) The minutes of the court session shall be signed by the presiding judge of the court session and the secretary of the court session.
  - (4) The minutes of individual procedural actions performed outside the court session must comply with the requirements of this Article.

(In the wording of the law of 19.12.2013. with amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 64.pants. Notes on Minutes

(Deleted by the law of 19.12.2013., which enters into force on 04.01.2014.)

8.nodaļa

Procedural Sanctions

#### 65.pants. Types of Procedural Sanctions

In cases specified in this law, the court may impose the following procedural sanctions:

- 1) warning;
- 2) expulsion from the courtroom;
- 3) fine;
- 4) compulsory bringing to court.

#### 66.pants. Warning

A person who disturbs the order during the hearing of the case shall be given a warning by the presiding judge of the court session, and a note about this shall be made in the minutes of the court session.

#### 67.pants. Expulsion from the Courtroom

If parties to the case, witnesses, experts or interpreters repeatedly disturb the order during the hearing of the case, they may be expelled from the courtroom by a court decision, but other persons present may be expelled by order of the presiding judge of the court session also without prior warning.

#### 68.pants. Fine

(1) The court shall impose a fine in cases and amounts specified in this law. If the court imposes a fine at the court session, the decision shall be recorded in the minutes of the court session.

(2) The court decision on the imposition of a fine shall be sent to the person on whom the fine has been imposed.

(3) A person on whom a fine has been imposed may, within 10 days after the issuance of the court decision, request the court that imposed it to release this person from the fine or reduce its amount. This application shall be examined at a court session, having previously notified the person on whom the fine has been imposed of the session. The non-appearance of this person is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(4) Fines imposed on officials shall be recovered from their personal funds.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 19.12.2013. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 69.pants. Compulsory Bringing

(1) In cases specified in this law, the court may adopt a decision on the compulsory bringing of a person to court.

(2) This decision shall be executed by the police institution indicated by the court.

#### 70.pants. Administrative and Criminal Liability of Parties to the Case and Other Persons

Parties to the case and other persons who, by their action or inaction, interfere with the work of the court, in addition to the procedural sanctions provided for by law, may be held administratively or criminally liable in cases specified by law.

Otrā sadaļa

Parties to the Case

### 9. nodaļa

Civil Procedural Legal Capacity and Active Capacity

#### 71.pants. Civil Procedural Legal Capacity

(1) Civil procedural legal capacity is the ability to be vested with civil procedural rights and duties.

(2) Civil procedural legal capacity is recognized equally for all natural and legal persons.

#### 72.pants. Civil Procedural Capacity to Act

(1) The ability to exercise civil procedural rights and perform duties (civil procedural capacity to act) belongs to adults to the extent that it has not been restricted by a court, and to legal persons.

(2) For natural persons aged from 15 to 18, cases in court are conducted by their legal representatives. For adults whose capacity to act has been restricted by a court, cases in court are conducted by their representatives or — in cases provided for by law — representatives together with these persons. In cases conducted by the representatives of the aforementioned persons, the court invites these persons themselves to participate.

(3) For natural persons who have not reached the age of 15, cases in court are conducted by their legal representatives.

(4) In cases provided for by law, minors are entitled to independently exercise their civil procedural rights and perform duties. In such cases, at the discretion of the court, the legal representatives of these persons may be invited to assist them in conducting the case.

(5) However, adults whose capacity to act has been restricted by a court have full civil procedural capacity to act in cases examining restrictions on their actions and freedom, as well as disputes between such person and their guardian. In such cases, the court invites a prosecutor and a representative of the orphan's court.

(As amended by the Law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 73.pants. Concept of Participant in a Case

(1) Participants in a case are the parties, third parties, representatives of the parties and third parties, the prosecutor and those state or municipal institutions and persons that have been granted rights by law to defend the rights of other persons in court and legally protected interests, institutions that are invited to give opinions in cases provided for by law, as well as representatives of these persons.

(2) A participant in a case may be a person who has civil procedural legal capacity and capacity to act. State and municipal institutions that have been granted rights by law to defend the rights of other persons in court and legally protected interests may be participants in a case regardless of whether they are legal persons.

(As amended by the Law of 07.04.2004., which comes into force on 01.05.2004.)

73.1 pants. Dishonest Use of Rights and Duties or Contempt of Court

(1) If a participant in a case dishonestly uses their rights or dishonestly performs their duties, including providing the court with knowingly false information about facts and circumstances of the case or knowingly by action or inaction delays the examination of the case or matter, the judge issues a warning to the participant in the case or imposes a fine of up to 800 euros.

(2) For contempt of court — any conduct that indicates a blatant disregard for the rules existing in the court session or in the court — the court may impose a fine of up to 1000 euros on the participant in the case.

(3) For the submission of a knowingly false application, statement of claim or complaint, except for an ancillary complaint, appeal or cassation complaint, with the purpose of achieving an unlawful objective or hindering the protection of rights or legitimate interests, the court may impose a fine of up to 1200 euros on the party.

(4) The court imposes the fine referred to in paragraph three of this Article by a decision with which the case is decided on the merits or with which the application, claim or complaint is left without examination, or the proceedings are terminated. A person on whom a fine has been imposed may express objections to the imposition of the fine by submitting an appeal, a cassation complaint or an ancillary complaint if the decision is appealable to a higher court instance. The imposition of a fine is not appealable separately from the appeal of the decision with which it was imposed.

(In the wording of the Law of 23.04.2015. as amended by the Law of 25.10.2018., which comes into force on 28.11.2018.)

73.2 pants. Restriction of the Rights of Participants in a Case in Protecting State Secrets

The court, by a reasoned decision, in the interests of protecting state secrets, may restrict the rights of participants in a case who do not have appropriate special permission to access state secrets to familiarize themselves with the volume containing state secret objects, insofar as it does not affect the establishment of objective truth.

(In the wording of the Law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

10.nodaļa

Parties

#### 74.pants. Parties, Their Rights and Duties

(1) In civil proceedings, any natural or legal person may be a party — claimant and defendant.

(2) Parties have the following civil procedural rights:

- 1) to familiarize themselves with the case materials and make copies thereof;
- 2) to participate in the court session;
- 3) to file challenges;
- 4) to submit evidence;
- 5) to participate in the examination of evidence;
- 6) to file requests;
- 7) to give oral and written explanations to the court;
- 8) to express their arguments and considerations;
- 9) to raise objections against the requests, arguments and considerations of other participants in the case;
- 10) to appeal court judgments and decisions;
- 11) to receive the judgment, decision and other documents in the case or copies thereof, as well as to exercise other procedural rights granted to them by this Law.
  - (3) The claimant is furthermore entitled to:
- 1) wholly or partially waive the claim;
- 2) reduce the amount of the claim;
- 3) amend in writing the basis or subject of the claim or increase the amount of the claim before the examination of the case on the merits has begun (Article 163 of this Law).
  - (4) The defendant is entitled to wholly or partially acknowledge the claim, raise objections against the claim or file a counterclaim.
  - (5) The parties may agree on the use of mediation, as well as conclude a settlement or agree on the referral of the case for examination to an arbitration court.
  - (6) Parties must exercise their rights and perform their duties in good faith.
  - (7) Parties have the duty to:
- 1) appear in court upon the court's summons;
- 2) notify in writing in a timely manner of the reasons for which they cannot appear at the court session, submitting evidence thereof;
- 21) provide the assistance of an interpreter if they do not have command of the language of the proceedings, except in cases provided for in this Law, including providing the assistance of an interpreter also to experts or witnesses summoned at the request of the parties if the expert or witness does not have command of the language of the proceedings;
- 3) perform other procedural duties imposed on them in accordance with this Law.

(As amended by the Laws of 04.08.2011., 22.05.2014., 04.02.2016. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on

#### 75.pants. Procedural Co-participation

(1) A claim may be brought by several claimants against one defendant, one claimant against several defendants or several claimants against several defendants.

(2) Each co-claimant and co-defendant acts independently in relation to the other party and other co-participants.

(3) Co-participants may entrust the conduct of the case to one of them or to one common representative.

#### 76.pants. Claimant in Cases Initiated at the Initiative of Other Persons

A person in whose interests a case has been initiated upon the application of a prosecutor, as well as a state or municipal institution or person that has been granted rights by law to defend the rights of other persons in court and legally protected interests, participates in the case as a claimant.

#### 77.pants. Succession to Procedural Rights of a Party

(1) If one of the parties to the case withdraws (death of a natural person, cessation of a legal person, assignment of claim, debt transfer and other circumstances), the court permits the replacement of this party by its successor in rights.

(11) An application for succession to procedural rights shall be examined in written proceedings, except in cases where the court considers it necessary to examine the application in a court session.

(12) Before making a decision on succession to procedural rights, the court shall verify in the Court Information System whether the party that has assigned the claim is registered in the Register of Applicants and Debtors of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund. If it is established that the party is a maintenance debtor, the court shall adopt a decision rejecting the application for succession to the party's procedural rights.

(2) Succession to rights is possible at any stage of the proceedings.

(21) An interlocutory appeal may be filed against the court's decision.

(3) All actions performed in the proceedings until the moment the successor enters are as binding on the successor as they were on the person whose rights have been succeeded.

(As amended by the Laws of 08.09.2011, 22.06.2017 and 05.10.2023, which enters into force on 02.11.2023. Part 1.2 enters into force on 01.12.2023. See transitional provision 182.)

11.nodaļa

Third Parties

#### 78.pants. Participation of Third Parties in Civil Proceedings

(1) A third party in civil proceedings may be a natural or legal person whose rights or obligations towards one of the parties may be affected by the judgment in the case.

(2) The provisions on procedural legal capacity and legal capacity of parties apply to third parties, they have the procedural rights and obligations of parties with the exceptions set out in Article 80 of this Law.

(3) Third parties may enter the case before the examination of the case on the merits in the court of first instance is completed. They may also be invited to participate in the case at the request of the parties or the prosecutor.

#### 79.pants. Third Parties with Independent Claims

(1) Third parties who assert independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute may enter the case by filing a statement of claim.

(2) Third parties with independent claims have the rights and obligations of a plaintiff.

#### 80.pants. Third Parties without Independent Claims

(1) Third parties who do not assert independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute may enter the case on the side of the plaintiff or defendant if the judgment in the case may affect these persons' rights or obligations towards one of the parties.

(2) Third parties who do not assert independent claims have the procedural rights and obligations of a party, except for the right to amend the basis or subject matter of the claim, increase or decrease the amount of the claim, withdraw from the claim, acknowledge the claim or conclude a settlement, as well as demand enforcement of the court judgment.

(3) Submissions concerning the invitation of third parties and submissions of third parties concerning entry into the case on the side of the plaintiff or defendant shall indicate the grounds for which the third parties are to be invited or permitted to participate in the case.

#### 81.pants. Court Decision on Inviting or Permitting a Third Party to Participate in a Case

A third party shall be invited or permitted to participate in the case in accordance with a court decision. A decision granting or refusing a request to invite or allow a third party to enter the case is not subject to appeal. The decision shall be sent to the third party to the official electronic address or by registered mail. (In the wording of the Law of 29.11.2012, as amended by the Laws of 23.11.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 

12.nodaļa

Representatives

#### 82.pants. Right to Representation in Civil Proceedings

(1) Natural persons may conduct their cases in court themselves or through authorized representatives.

(2) Cases of legal persons in court shall be conducted by their officials acting within the powers granted by law, statutes or regulations, or by other authorized representatives of legal persons.

(3) Cases of a state or local government institution that has been granted by law the right to defend the rights of other persons or interests protected by law shall be conducted in court by the head of the institution or his authorized representative.

(4) Participation of the participants in the case referred to in paragraphs one, two and three of this Article in civil proceedings does not deprive them of the right to invite a lawyer to provide legal assistance in their case. In this case, the scope of the lawyer's powers is determined by Article 86 of this Law, and he does not provide explanations on the merits of the case.

(5) (Deleted by the Law of 12.02.2004)

(6) (Deleted as of 01.01.2019 by the Law of 14.12.2017. See transitional provision 132)

(7) (Deleted as of 01.01.2019 by the Law of 14.12.2017. See transitional provision 132)

(As amended by the Laws of 20.06.2001, 31.10.2002, the Constitutional Court judgment of 27.06.2003, the Laws of 12.02.2004, 19.12.2013 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018.)

82.1 pants. Exceptions to General Rules on the Right to Representation

(1) Natural persons and legal persons in the court of first instance and the court of appeal shall conduct their cases themselves or through a lawyer:

- 1) in cases within the jurisdiction of the Economic Court;
- 2) in cases arising from the law of obligations if the amount of the claim exceeds 150,000 euros;
- 3) in cases concerning the protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure (Chapter 30.8).
  - (11) Cases concerning the protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure (Chapter 30.8) may also be conducted through a professional patent attorney.
  - (2) In the cases referred to in paragraph one of this Article, the case shall be conducted by the legal person itself if it is conducted by its officials acting within the powers granted by law, statutes or regulations, as well as persons who are in employment or civil service relations with the respective legal person and are authorized thereto in the manner prescribed in this Law. If a legal person is a controlling or subsidiary company of a group, the officials mentioned in this paragraph, as well as persons who are in employment relations with the respective legal person, may also conduct the cases of the controlling or subsidiary company.
  - (3) Natural persons shall conduct their cases in the court of cassation themselves or through a lawyer.
  - (4) Cases of legal persons in the court of cassation shall be conducted by their officials acting within the powers granted by law, statutes or regulations, or shall be conducted through a lawyer.
  - (5) Cases of natural and legal persons concerning violations and protection of industrial property rights and the cases referred to in paragraph 1, point 3 of this Article in the court of cassation may also be conducted through a professional patent attorney.

(In the wording of the Law of 14.12.2017, as amended by the Laws of 28.02.2019, 01.10.2020, 21.01.2021 and 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 83.pants. Person Who May Be an Authorized Representative in Civil Proceedings

Any natural person may be an authorized representative in civil proceedings, subject to the restrictions set out in Articles 82.1 and 84 of this Law.

(In the wording of the Law of 12.02.2004, as amended by the Laws of 19.12.2013 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment to the Article replacing the number and words "in paragraphs six and seven of Article 82" with the number and word "in Article 82.1" enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision 132.)

#### 84.pants. Persons Who Cannot Be Representatives in Civil Proceedings

(1) The following cannot be representatives in civil proceedings:

- 1) a person who has not reached the age of majority;
- 2) a person for whom guardianship has been established;
- 3) a person whose right to conduct the cases of other persons has been removed by court judgment;
- 4) a person who is related by consanguinity up to the third degree or by affinity up to the second degree with the judge who must adjudicate the case;
- 5) a person who has provided legal assistance to the other party to the dispute in this or in another related case;
- 6) a mediator who has participated in mediation in this or in another related case.
  - (2) Upon establishing the circumstances mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article, the court shall not admit such person to participation in the examination of the case.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 22.05.2014, which enter into force on 18.06.2014.)

#### 85.pants. Formalization of Representation

(1) The representation of natural persons shall be formalized by a notarized power of attorney. The represented person may express the authorization of the representative orally in court, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.

(2) The representation of legal persons shall be formalized by a written power of attorney or by documents certifying the official's right to represent the legal person without special authorization.

(3) An advocate's authorization to provide legal assistance is certified by a warrant. If an advocate acts as an authorized representative of a party, this authorization is certified by a written power of attorney.

(31) The authorization of a state-provided legal aid provider to provide legal assistance is certified by an assignment for the provision of legal assistance issued by the responsible state institution.

(32) The representation of a professional patent attorney shall be formalized by a written power of attorney and a document certifying the status of the patent attorney.

(4) Parents, adopters, guardians and curators shall present to the court documents certifying their rights.

(5) If the authorized representative is one of the procedural participants acting on behalf of other participants, the represented person may express his or her authorization orally in court, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001, 12.02.2004, 17.02.2005, 10.12.2015 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 86.pants. Scope of Representatives' Powers of Attorney

(1) A representative has the right to perform all procedural acts on behalf of the represented person, except those for which special authorization is required. If a natural person conducts a case through an authorized representative, court notices and documents shall be sent only to the representative. If the authorized representative of a natural person, whose declared place of residence or indicated address is outside Latvia, does not indicate an e-mail address or does not notify of the registration of his or her participation in the online system, court notices and documents may be sent only to the represented person.

(2) Full or partial renunciation of a claim, amendment of the subject of the claim, filing of a counterclaim, full or partial acknowledgment of a claim, conclusion of a settlement, referral of a case to arbitration, appeal of court decisions by way of appeal or cassation, submission of enforcement documents for recovery, receipt of adjudged property or money, termination of enforcement proceedings must be specifically indicated in the power of attorney issued by the represented person.

(3) All procedural acts performed by a representative in accordance with the power of attorney issued to him or her are binding on the represented person.

(With amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003 and 01.06.2017, which enter into force on 01.07.2017.)

#### 87.pants. Early Termination of Representation

(1) The represented person may at any time revoke the authorization given to the representative, immediately notifying the court thereof in writing. An oral notification of the revocation of the authorization may be given at a court session, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.

(2) A representative has the right to refuse to conduct a case, notifying the represented person and the court thereof in writing in a timely manner.

(With amendments made by the law of 23.11.2016, which enters into force on 01.01.2017.)

13.nodaļa

Institutions and Persons Participating in Proceedings Pursuant to Law

(Chapter title as worded by the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

#### 88.pants. Participation of State or Local Government Institutions and Individual Persons in Proceedings, Protecting the Rights of Other Persons

(1) In cases provided for by law, international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia or European Union legal acts, state or local government institutions and persons may submit an application to a court to protect the rights and legally protected interests of other persons.

(2) The institutions and persons referred to in this Article may familiarize themselves with the case materials, file challenges, give explanations, submit evidence, participate in the examination of evidence, submit petitions, appeal court judgments and decisions.

(3) The refusal of the indicated institutions and persons to withdraw from an application they have submitted pursuant to the first paragraph of this Article does not deprive the person for whose interests the application has been submitted of the right to demand that the court examine the case on its merits.

(With amendments made by the law of 09.06.2011, which enters into force on 18.06.2011.)

#### 89.pants. Participation of Institutions in Proceedings to Give Opinions

(1) The court, in cases provided for by law, invites institutions to participate in proceedings so that they may, within their competence, give an opinion in the case and protect the rights and legally protected interests of persons.

(2) The invited institutions have the right to familiarize themselves with the case materials, participate in the examination of evidence, file petitions and give an opinion.

(As worded by the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

14.nodaļa

Prosecutor

#### 90.pants. Participation of a Prosecutor in Civil Proceedings

(1) A prosecutor is entitled to participate in the examination of a case if he or she has filed a claim, submitted an application, or his or her participation is mandatory.

(2) A prosecutor has the right to file a claim or submit an application to a court if:

- 1) it is necessary for the protection of state or local government rights and interests established by law;
- 2) the rights or legitimate interests of minors, persons under guardianship, persons with disabilities, prisoners or other such persons who have limited opportunities to defend their rights have been violated;
- 3) a violation of law has been established during a prosecutor's inspection.
  - (3) The participation of a prosecutor in the examination of a case is mandatory if it is established by law or the court has deemed it necessary.
  - (4) A prosecutor participating in the examination of a case has the right to familiarize himself or herself with the case materials, file challenges, submit evidence, participate in the examination of evidence, file petitions, give an opinion on issues that have arisen during the adjudication of the case and on the merits of the case as a whole, submit a protest against a court judgment or decision, receive a judgment, decision or other document in the case or a copy thereof, as well as perform other procedural acts established by law.
  - (5) If a prosecutor is a party to a case, he or she has the right to submit a protest against a court judgment or decision in all cases when other parties to the case have the right to appeal the judgment or decision.
  - (6) A prosecutor's withdrawal from a claim or application he or she has submitted to a court does not deprive the person for whose interests the prosecutor has submitted the claim or application of the right to demand that the court examine the case on its merits.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 91.pants. Recusal or Rejection of Prosecutor

(1) A prosecutor cannot give their opinion in a case if they have previously been in the examination of this case a judge, party, third person, representative, witness, expert, interpreter or court session secretary, as well as in the cases specified in Section 19, Paragraph 1, Points 2,

3 and 4 of this law.

(2) If the mentioned circumstances exist, the prosecutor must recuse themselves before the start of the trial of the case.

(3) If the prosecutor has not recused themselves, the participants in the case are entitled to file a rejection of the prosecutor on the grounds mentioned in this Section.

(4) A rejection of the prosecutor is filed and the court decides it in the procedure established in Sections 20 and 21 of this law.

Third Part

Evidence

15.nodaļa

General Provisions on Evidence

#### 92.pants. Evidence

Evidence is information on the basis of which the court determines the existence or non-existence of such facts that are significant in deciding the case.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

#### 93.pants. Duty to Prove and Submit Evidence

(1) Each party must prove the facts on which it bases its claims or objections. The plaintiff must prove the validity of their claims. The defendant must prove the validity of their objections.

(2) Evidence is submitted by the parties and other participants in the case. If it is not possible for the parties or other participants in the case to submit evidence, the court requests it upon their reasoned request.

(21) If the parties submit evidence or the court requests evidence containing a state secret object, the court requests from the competent institution that has classified the information as a state secret object an opinion on the rights of the participant in the case to become acquainted with it.

(3) Evidence is submitted to the court no later than 14 days before the court session, unless the judge has set another time limit for the submission of evidence. The second sentence of Section 48, Paragraph 4 of this law does not apply to this time limit.

(31) During the trial of a case, evidence may be submitted upon a reasoned request by a party or other participants in the case if it does not delay the trial of the case, or the court has recognised the reasons for not submitting evidence in a timely manner as justified, or the evidence concerns facts that became known during the trial of the case.

(32) If a participant in the case submits evidence after the time limit has expired and the court does not recognise the reasons for not submitting in a timely manner as justified, it imposes a fine of up to 750 euros on the participant in the case.

(33) A court decision to refuse to accept evidence is not appealable, but objections to it may be expressed in an appeal or cassation complaint.

(4) If the court finds that no evidence has been submitted regarding any of the facts on which the party's claims or objections are based, it notifies the parties thereof and, if necessary, sets a time limit for the submission of evidence. (31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003., 07.09.2006., 29.11.2012., 12.09.2013. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 94.pants. Relevance of Evidence

The court accepts only such evidence that is significant in the case.

#### 95.pants. Admissibility of Evidence

(1) The court admits only the means of proof established by law.

(2) Facts that according to law can be proved only by specific means of proof cannot be proved by any other means of proof.

#### 96.pants. Grounds for Exemption from Proving

(1) If the court recognises a fact as commonly known, it need not be proved.

(2) Facts that have been established by a judgment that has entered into legal force in one civil case need not be proved again when trying other civil cases in which the same parties participate.

(3) A court judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force, a prosecutor's prescription for punishment, as well as a decision to terminate criminal proceedings on a non-rehabilitative ground is binding on the court examining the case concerning the civil liability of the person regarding whom the relevant decision has been made, only in the question of whether the criminal act or omission occurred or was committed or permitted by the same person.

(4) Facts that according to law are deemed established need not be proved. Such presumptions may be challenged in the general procedure.

(5) A party need not prove facts that have not been contested by the other party in the procedure established by this law.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.10.2002. un 05.02.2009. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.03.2009.)

#### 97.pants. Evaluation of Evidence

(1) The court evaluates evidence according to its internal conviction, which is based on evidence comprehensively, fully and objectively examined in the court session, guided by legal consciousness based on the laws of logic, scientific findings and observations gained in life.

(2) No evidence has predetermined force that would bind the court.

(3) The court must indicate in the judgment why it gave preference to one piece of evidence compared to another piece of evidence and recognised some facts as proved and others as not proved.

16.nodaļa

Securing of Evidence

#### 98.pants. Admissibility of Securing Evidence

(1) If a person has grounds to believe that the submission of evidence necessary for them may later be impossible or difficult, they may request that this evidence be secured.

(2) Applications for securing evidence may be submitted at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before filing a claim in court.

(3) Evidence before the initiation of a case in court is secured by the district (city) court in which the claim is to be filed. Evidence after the initiation of a case in court is secured by the court examining the case.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 14.12.2006. un 16.03.2023. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 29.03.2023.)

#### 99.pants. Application for Securing Evidence

The application for securing evidence shall indicate:

- 1) the first name, surname of the applicant, the case for the examination of which it is necessary to secure evidence, or its potential participants;
- 2) the evidence that needs to be secured;
- 3) the facts for the proving of which this evidence is necessary;
- 4) the reasons for which the applicant requests to secure evidence.

#### 100.pants. Procedure for deciding on an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim

(1) The court or judge decides on an application for preservation of evidence within 10 days from the day of its receipt.

(2) If the application for preservation of evidence is decided by the court, the applicant and possible parties to the case are invited to the court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the submitted application.

(3) By decision of the judge, evidence may be preserved without inviting possible parties to the case only in urgent cases, including urgent cases of intellectual property rights violations or possible violations or in cases where it is not possible to determine who will be the parties to the case.

(4) If the decision on preservation of evidence has been made without the presence of the possible defendant or other party to the case, he or she shall be notified of this decision no later than the moment of execution of the said decision.

(5) The examination of witnesses, as well as on-site inspections and expert examinations, shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of this law.

(6) When granting an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for submitting the statement of claim, not exceeding 30 days.

(7) When granting an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim, the judge may request that the potential claimant, by paying a specified sum of money into the bailiff's deposit account or by providing an equivalent guarantee, ensure coverage of the losses that may be incurred by the defendant in connection with the preservation of evidence.

(8) The court session protocol and materials collected in preserving evidence shall be kept until they are requested by the court examining the case.

(9) An ancillary complaint may be submitted against the judge's decision to refuse to accept an application for preservation of evidence or the decision referred to in paragraph three of this Article. If the decision on preservation of evidence has been made without the presence of a party to the case, the time limit for submitting an ancillary complaint shall be counted from the day of issuance or dispatch of the decision.

(14.12.2006. law version with amendments made by 20.12.2010. law, which enters into force on 01.01.2011.)

#### 101.pants. Procedure for examining an application for preservation of evidence after initiation of a case in court

(1) An application for preservation of evidence shall be examined at a court session in accordance with the relevant provisions of this law.

(2) The submitter of the application and other parties to the case shall be notified of the time and place of the session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application for preservation of evidence.

#### 102.pants. Court commissions

(1) If the court examining the case is unable to collect evidence located in another city or district, the court or judge shall instruct the relevant court to perform certain procedural actions.

(2) The decision on the court commission shall briefly set out the substance of the case to be examined and indicate the circumstances to be clarified and the evidence to be collected by the court executing the commission. This decision is binding on the court to which it is addressed and must be executed within 15 days.

(With amendments made by 31.10.2002. law, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 103.pants. Procedure for execution of court commissions

(1) Court commissions shall be executed at a court session in the procedure established by this law. The parties to the case shall be notified of the time and place of the session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the execution of the commission.

(2) Protocols and other case materials collected in executing the commission shall be sent to the court examining the case within three days.

103.1 pants. Termination of preservation of evidence

If the decision on preservation of evidence has been made before filing a claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge, upon receipt of an application from the potential claimant or defendant, shall make a decision to revoke the preservation of evidence.

(14.12.2006. law version, which enters into force on 01.03.2007.)

103.2 pants. Compensation for losses caused by preservation of evidence

The defendant is entitled to claim compensation for losses incurred in connection with the preservation of evidence if the preservation of evidence has been revoked in the case specified in Article 103.1 of this law, if the claim filed against him or her has been rejected, left without examination, or the proceedings have been terminated in the cases specified in Points 2 and 4 of Article 223 of this law.

(14.12.2006. law version, which enters into force on 01.03.2007.)

17.nodaļa

Means of proof

#### 104.pants. Explanations of parties and third persons

(1) Explanations of parties and third persons that contain information about facts on which their claims or objections are based shall be recognized as evidence if they are confirmed by other evidence examined and evaluated at the court session.

(2) If one party acknowledges facts on which the other party bases its claims or objections, the court may recognize such facts as proven if it has no doubt that the acknowledgment has not occurred under the influence of fraud, violence, threats or mistake or in order to conceal the truth.

#### 105.pants. Witness testimony

(1) A witness is a person who knows facts relating to the case and who has been summoned by the court to a court session.

(2) A party to the case, when requesting to examine a witness, must indicate what circumstances relevant to the case the witness can confirm.

(3) No person summoned to court as a witness has the right to refuse to give testimony, except in the cases provided for in Articles 106 and 107 of this law.

(4) A witness may be examined only about facts to be clarified in this case.

(5) Witness testimony based on information whose source is not known or on information provided by other persons if these persons have not been examined cannot be evidence.

#### 106.pants. Persons who cannot be witnesses

The following cannot be summoned and examined as witnesses:

- 1) clergy — about circumstances that have become known to them while hearing confession, and persons who by virtue of their office or profession have no right to disclose information entrusted to them — about such information;
- 2) minors — about circumstances that testify against their parents, grandparents, brothers and sisters;
- 3) persons who, due to their physical or mental deficiencies, are unable to correctly perceive circumstances that are relevant to the case;
- 4) children under seven years of age;
- 5) persons who have participated in mediation in this case or in another case related to it.

(With amendments made by 22.05.2014. law, which enters into force on 18.06.2014.)

#### 107.pants. Persons who may refuse to testify

(1) The following may refuse to testify:

- 1) relatives of the parties in direct line and in the first and second degree of the collateral line, spouse and first-degree in-laws, as well as family members of the parties;
- 2) guardians and trustees of the parties, as well as persons who are under the guardianship or trusteeship of the parties;
- 3) persons who are in litigation with one of the parties in another case.
  - (2) The court must explain to the said persons their right to refuse to testify.

#### 108.pants. Obligations of a witness

(1) A person summoned as a witness must appear in court and give truthful testimony about circumstances known to him or her. A witness may also be examined using videoconference in court at the place where the witness is located or in a place specially equipped for this purpose.

(2) A witness must answer questions from the court and parties to the case.

(3) The court may examine a witness at his or her location if he or she is unable to appear in response to the court summons due to illness, age, disability or other excusable reason.

(With amendments made by 08.09.2011. law, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

#### 109.pants. Liability of a witness

(1) For refusing to testify for reasons that the court has recognized as inexcusable, and for knowingly giving false testimony, a witness is liable in accordance with criminal law.

(2) If a witness fails to appear in response to a court or judge summons without an excusable reason, the court may impose a fine of up to 60 euros on him or her or bring him or her to court by force.

(With amendments made by 12.09.2013. law, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

#### 110.pants. Written Evidence

Written evidence is information about facts that are significant in a case, and this information is recorded in documents, other writings, as well as in the respective recording systems with the aid of letters, numbers and other written signs or technical means

(audio, video tapes, computer diskettes, etc.).

#### 111.pants. Procedure for Submission of Written Evidence

(1) When submitting written evidence to the court or requesting it to be obtained, the parties shall indicate what circumstances significant to the case this evidence may confirm.

(2) Written evidence shall be submitted in the original or in a copy certified in the prescribed manner. If, for the determination of facts significant to the case, a part of a written document or other writing is sufficient, an extract thereof may be submitted to the court.

(3) Original documents, as well as written evidence certified in the prescribed manner, shall be submitted if laws or international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia provide that specific facts may be proven only with original documents or copies certified in the prescribed manner.

(4) If written evidence is submitted to the court in the form of a copy, the court, upon a reasoned request of the parties or on its own initiative, shall be entitled to request that the original be submitted or produced, if it is necessary for determining the circumstances of the case.

(As amended by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 112.pants. Procedure for Requesting Written Evidence

(1) The court or judge, upon a reasoned request of a party, shall be entitled to request written evidence from state and municipal institutions, other natural and legal persons.

(2) A party who requests the court to obtain written evidence shall describe this evidence and give reasons why he or she considers that it is held by the said person.

(3) State and municipal institutions, other natural and legal persons who are unable to submit the requested written evidence or to submit it within the time limit set by the court or judge shall notify the court thereof in writing, indicating the reasons.

(4) If a party refuses to submit the written evidence requested by the court to the court, without denying that this evidence is held by that party, the court may recognise as proven the facts in confirmation of which the opposing party has referred to this written evidence.

(As amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 113. pants. Return of Written Evidence in the Case

The court shall return the originals of written evidence to the submitter after converting them into electronic form and attaching them to the case materials. If it is not possible to convert the originals of written evidence into electronic form, the court shall return them to the submitter after the court judgment has entered into legal force.

(Wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 114.pants. Inspection of Written Evidence at Their Storage Location

If submission of written evidence to the court is impossible or difficult due to their number, volume or other reasons, the court may carry out an inspection and examination of the written evidence at their storage location.

(As amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 115.pants. Material Evidence

Material evidence is physical objects which, by their characteristics, features or very existence, may be useful for the determination of facts that are significant in the case.

#### 116.pants. Submission and Requesting of Material Evidence

(1) A party who submits material evidence to the court or requests it to be obtained shall indicate what circumstances significant to the case this evidence may confirm.

(2) A party who requests the court to obtain material evidence shall describe this evidence and give reasons why he or she considers that it is held by the said person.

(3) The court or judge, upon a reasoned request of a party, shall be entitled to request material evidence from state and municipal institutions, other natural and legal persons.

(4) State and municipal institutions, other natural and legal persons who are unable to submit the requested material evidence or to submit it within the time limit set by the court or judge shall notify the court thereof in writing, indicating the reasons.

(As amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 117.pants. Inspection of Material Evidence at Their Storage Location

If submission of material evidence to the court is impossible or difficult due to their number, volume or other reasons, the court may carry out an inspection and examination of the material evidence at their storage location or commission a bailiff to do so.

(As amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 118.pants. Storage of Material Evidence

(1) Material evidence shall be attached to the case or stored in the court's material evidence repository.

(2) Objects which cannot be brought to the court shall be stored at their location. They shall be described and, if necessary, photographed or filmed. The descriptions and images shall be attached to the case.

(3) Perishable material evidence shall be examined by the court immediately, with notice to the parties. After the examination, this material evidence shall be returned to the persons from whom it was received.

#### 119.pants. Return of Material Evidence

(1) Material evidence, after the court judgment has entered into legal force, shall be returned to the persons from whom it was received or transferred to the persons to whom the court has recognised rights to these objects.

(2) Material evidence which, by law or by court judgment, may not be returned to the parties or the persons from whom it was received, shall be transferred by the court to the relevant state institutions.

(3) In individual cases, material evidence may be returned before the judgment has entered into legal force, if it does not prejudice the examination of the case.

#### 120.pants. Liability for Failure to Submit Written and Material Evidence

If the court has not been notified that it is not possible to submit the requested written or material evidence, or if it has not been submitted for reasons which the court has found to be unjustified, the court may impose a fine of up to 40 euros on the guilty person. Payment of the fine shall not release this person from the obligation to submit the evidence requested by the court.

(As amended by the law of 12.09.2013, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

#### 121.pants. Expert Examination

(1) The court shall order an expert examination in a case upon a party's request in cases where special knowledge in science, technology, art or other fields is necessary for the determination of facts significant to the case. If necessary, the court shall order several expert examinations.

(2) The expert examination shall be carried out by persons specified in the Law on Forensic Experts. The expert shall be chosen by the parties by mutual agreement, but if such agreement is not reached within the time limit set by the court, the expert shall be chosen by the court. If necessary, several experts may be chosen.

(3) The parties shall be entitled to submit to the court questions which, in their opinion, the expert should answer. The questions to be answered by the expert shall be determined by the court. The court shall give reasons for the rejection of questions posed by the parties.

(4) The court's decision on ordering an expert examination shall indicate the questions to be answered by the expert and who is commissioned to carry out the expert examination.

(5) The expert examination shall be carried out in court or outside court if carrying it out in court is not possible or is difficult.

(As amended by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

#### 122.pants. Duties and Rights of an Expert

(1) A person appointed as an expert must appear upon summons by the court. An expert may be examined also by using videoconference in court at the expert's location or in a place specially equipped for this purpose.

(2) If the summoned expert does not appear at a court session for reasons which the court has deemed unjustified, the court may impose on him or her a fine of up to 60 euros.

(3) An expert has the right to familiarise himself or herself with the case materials, ask questions to parties and witnesses, as well as request the court to obtain additional materials.

(4) An expert gives an objective opinion in his or her own name and is personally responsible for it.

(5) An expert may refuse to give an opinion if the materials provided to him or her for examination are insufficient or if the questions posed exceed the limits of his or her special knowledge. In these cases, the expert shall notify the court in writing that it is not possible to give an opinion.

(6) For refusal without justified reason to perform his or her duties or for knowingly giving a false opinion, an expert is liable in accordance with criminal law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011. and 12.09.2013., which enter into force on 01.01.2014.)

#### 123.pants. Recusal or Challenge of an Expert

(1) An expert may not participate in the examination of a case if he or she has previously been a judge or a party in the examination of this case, as well as in the cases provided for in clauses 2, 3 and 4 of the first part of Article 19 of this Law.

(2) An expert may not participate in the examination of a case also if:

- 1) he or she is or has been dependent, by virtue of official position or otherwise, on a party or other participant in the case;
- 2) one of the parties in the case under examination has been connected with the performance of this expert's professional duties prior to the institution of proceedings in court;
- 3) it has been ascertained that he or she is not competent.
  - (3) In the presence of the mentioned circumstances, the expert must recuse himself or herself before the commencement of the trial.
  - (4) If the expert has not recused himself or herself, the parties to the case are entitled to submit a challenge to him or her on the grounds mentioned in this Article.
  - (5) A challenge to an expert is submitted and the court decides it in the procedure established in Articles 20 and 21 of this Law.

#### 124.pants. Expert Opinion

(1) An expert opinion must be reasoned and substantiated.

(2) The opinion is expressed in writing and submitted to the court. An expert opinion must contain a precise description of the examinations performed, the conclusions drawn as a result thereof, and reasoned answers to the questions posed by the court. If, in conducting the examination, the expert ascertains circumstances which are significant for the case and regarding which questions have not been posed to him or her, he or she is entitled to indicate these circumstances in his or her opinion.

(3) If several experts are appointed, they are entitled to consult among themselves. If the experts reach a common opinion, it is signed by all experts. If the opinions of the experts differ, each expert writes a separate opinion.

#### 125.pants. Evaluation of an Expert Opinion

(1) The court evaluates an expert opinion in accordance with the provisions of Article 97 of this Law.

(2) If the expert opinion is not sufficiently clear or is incomplete, the court may order an additional examination, assigning its performance to the same expert.

(3) If the expert opinion is not substantiated, as well as in the case where the opinions of several experts are contradictory, the court may order a repeated examination, assigning its performance to another expert or experts.

#### 126.pants. Opinion of an Institution

The court evaluates the opinion of an institution invited in the procedure established in Article 89 of this Law as evidence. The court's non-adherence to the opinion must be reasoned in the decision adopted in the case.

(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2004., which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

Part B

Proceedings in a Court of First Instance

Fourth Section

Claim Proceedings

Chapter 18

Institution of a Claim

#### 127.pants. Persons Who May Institute a Claim in Court

(1) The right to institute a claim in court to defend his or her infringed or contested civil rights belongs to persons who have civil procedural capacity.

(2) In the interests of minors, a claim is instituted by the legal representatives of these persons, but in the cases provided for in the fourth part of Article 72 of this Law, a claim may be instituted by the minor himself or herself. In the interests of persons under guardianship, a claim is instituted by the representatives of these persons together with the person under guardianship or by themselves alone in place of the respective person if the court has so determined, except in the case provided for in the fifth part of Article 72.

(3) A prosecutor, state or municipal institutions or persons who have been granted the right by law to defend the rights of other persons or interests protected by law in court may institute a claim to defend the infringed or contested civil rights of these persons.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 128.pants. Statement of Claim

(1) A claim is filed by submitting a written statement of claim to the court.

(2) The statement of claim must specify:

- 1) the name of the court to which the application is submitted;
- 11) the claimant's name, surname, personal identification code, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant consents to electronic communication with the court, also indicates the email address and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also includes an indication of registration;
- 12) the defendant's, third party's name, surname, personal identification code, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. The defendant's personal identification code or registration number is indicated if it is known;
- 13) the claimant's representative's (if the claim is filed by a representative) name, surname, personal identification code and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant's representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, consents to electronic communication with the court, also indicates the email address and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also includes an indication of registration. If the claimant's representative's address is outside Latvia, additionally indicates the email address or notifies of registration of their participation in the online system;
- 2) (deleted by law of 29.11.2012);
- 21) the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment of the amount to be recovered or litigation costs to be reimbursed is to be made;
- 3) the subject matter of the claim;
- 4) the amount of the claim, if the claim is assessable in monetary terms, as well as the calculation of the amount to be recovered or contested;
- 5) the circumstances on which the claimant bases their claim, and the evidence that confirms them;
- 51) information on the use of mediation to resolve the dispute before applying to court;
- 6) the law on which the claim is based;
- 7) the claimant's claims;
- 8) the list of documents attached to the statement of claim;
- 9) the time of preparation of the statement of claim and other information, if it is necessary for consideration of the case. The claimant may indicate their telephone number if they consent to use the telephone for communication with the court.
  - (3) The statement of claim is signed by the claimant or their representative, or the claimant together with the representative, if so determined by the court, except in the case specified in the fifth paragraph of Article 72 of this Law. If the claim is filed on behalf of the claimant by their representative, a power of attorney or other document confirming the representative's authority to file a claim must be attached to the statement of claim.
  - (4) In cases concerning maintenance in the cases provided for in European Union legal acts and international treaties, using the forms specified in the respective legal acts, the statement of claim may be submitted or forwarded through the intermediary of the Latvian central authorities designated to ensure cooperation.
  - (5) In the statement of claim in cases concerning debt recovery, claims for payments for management activities in a multi-apartment residential building (management expenses), claims for payments for services necessary for maintenance of the building (utility services) and claims for payments to the reserve fund of the apartment owners' community (reserves) are indicated separately.
  - (6) In the statement of claim in cases concerning the non-existence or dissolution of marriage, in claims for personal injury, in claims for recovery of maintenance, in claims for division of the parties' common dwelling in which they live in one household, or for determination of the order of use of the dwelling in which the parties live in one household, and in cases arising from custody and contact rights, if a decision on temporary protection against violence has been made before filing the claim, the court that made the decision on temporary protection against violence and the date of adoption of the decision are indicated.
  - (7) If the claim is related to a state secret object, then the statement of claim does not indicate information containing state secrets. Information containing state secrets must be indicated in a separate document.

(As amended by the laws of 09.06.2011, 08.09.2011, 29.11.2012, 22.05.2014, 29.10.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017, 22.06.2017, 21.01.2021, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 129.pants. Documents to Be Attached to the Statement of Claim

(1) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(2) The following documents confirming must be attached to the statement of claim:

- 1) payment of state duty and other court costs in the procedure and amount established by law, except in cases where the statement of claim has been submitted and payment made in the online system;
- 2) compliance with the procedure for prior out-of-court consideration of the case, if established by law;
- 3) the circumstances on which the claim is based.
  - (3) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)
  - (4) In cases provided for by law, a translation certified in the prescribed manner must be attached to the statement of claim and the documents attached thereto, if the documents are intended for delivery to a person in accordance with Article 56.2 of this Law.

A person who is exempted from payment of court costs does not attach a translation.

(As amended by the laws of 05.02.2009 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 130.pants. Submission of the Statement of Claim to the Court

(1) The statement of claim must be submitted to a court of first instance in accordance with the rules on jurisdiction.

(2) (Deleted by the law of 23.04.2015)

(3) (Deleted by the law of 23.04.2015)

(4) An unsigned statement of claim is considered not submitted and is sent back to the submitter.

(As amended by the law of 23.04.2015, which entered into force on 26.05.2015.)

#### 131.pants. Decision on Acceptance of the Statement of Claim and Institution of Civil Proceedings

(1) Upon receipt of the statement of claim by the court, the judge within ten days, but upon receipt of the application referred to in Article 644.7 or 644.17 of this Law no later than the next day, makes a decision:

- 1) on acceptance of the statement of claim and institution of the case;
- 2) to refuse to accept the statement of claim;
- 3) to leave the statement of claim without action.
  - (2) If consideration of the case is not possible in accordance with Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council or Regulation No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council, in the cases provided for in the said legal acts, the judge makes one of the decisions provided for in the first paragraph of this Article regarding the progress of the statement of claim.

(As amended by the laws of 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 04.08.2011 and 25.10.2018, which entered into force on

#### 132.pants. Grounds for Refusing to Accept a Statement of Claim

(1) A judge refuses to accept a statement of claim if:

- 1) the dispute is not subject to the court's jurisdiction;
- 2) the claim has been brought by a person who has no right to bring a claim;
- 3) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to submit the dispute to arbitration, except in cases where a statement of claim has been submitted to the court for declaring the arbitration agreement invalid;
- 31) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to resolve the dispute using mediation, and no evidence has been submitted that the proposal to resolve the dispute using mediation has been rejected or that a mediation agreement has not been concluded, or that mediation has been terminated without reaching an agreement in the manner prescribed by the Mediation Law;
- 4) the same or another court has proceedings concerning a dispute between the same parties, concerning the same subject matter and on the same grounds;
- 5) in a dispute between the same parties, concerning the same subject matter and on the same grounds, there is a court judgment that has entered into legal force or a decision to terminate proceedings due to the plaintiff's withdrawal of the claim or approval of a settlement between the parties;
- 6) the case does not fall within the jurisdiction of this court;
- 7) the plaintiff has not complied with the pre-trial out-of-court procedure established for the relevant category of cases or has not taken the measures prescribed by law to settle the dispute with the defendant before bringing the claim;
- 8) the statement of claim has been submitted by a person who lacks capacity to conduct civil proceedings;
- 9) the power of attorney or other document attached to the statement of claim does not show authorization for the representative to bring such a claim;
- 10) no power of attorney or other document confirming the representative's authorization to bring a claim is attached to the statement of claim.
  - (2) Concerning the refusal to accept a statement of claim, the judge shall adopt a reasoned decision. The decision together with the submitted statement of claim shall be issued to the plaintiff.
  - (3) The decision may be appealed in the manner prescribed by this law, except for a decision to refuse to accept a statement of claim on the grounds of point 10 of paragraph (1) of this Article.
  - (4) A judge's refusal to accept a statement of claim on the grounds of points 6 to 10 of paragraph (1) of this Article is not an obstacle to the submission of the same application to the court once the deficiencies have been remedied.

(As amended by the laws of 29.11.2012., 22.05.2014., 23.04.2015. and 28.05.2015., which enter into force

#### 133.pants. Leaving a Statement of Claim Without Movement

(1) A judge shall leave a statement of claim without movement if:

- 1) the statement of claim does not contain all the particulars specified in paragraph two, four or five of Article 128 of this law;
- 2) the documents specified in Article 129 of this law are not attached to the statement of claim;
- 3) the statement of claim in simplified procedure cases is not drawn up in accordance with Article 250.20 of this law.
  - (2) Concerning leaving a statement of claim without movement, the judge shall adopt a reasoned decision, send it to the plaintiff and set a time limit for remedying the deficiencies. This time limit may not be shorter than 20 days from the date of sending the decision. The judge's decision may be appealed in the manner prescribed by this law. The time limit for appeal shall be calculated from the date the decision is issued to the plaintiff.
  - (3) If the plaintiff remedies the deficiencies within the specified time limit, the statement of claim shall be deemed to have been submitted on the date it was first submitted to the court.
  - (4) If the plaintiff does not remedy the deficiencies within the specified time limit, the statement of claim shall be deemed not to have been submitted and shall be returned to the plaintiff.
  - (5) The return of a statement of claim to the plaintiff is not an obstacle to its re-submission to the court, subject to the general procedure for submitting statements of claim prescribed by this law.

(As amended by the laws of 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 23.04.2015., 14.12.2017. and 21.01.2021., which enter into force 01.03.2021.)

#### 134.pants. Joinder of Claims and Civil Cases

(1) A plaintiff is entitled to join several interrelated claims in one statement of claim.
