(2) If the court has several similar cases in which the same parties are involved, or cases in which one plaintiff brings a claim against several defendants or several plaintiffs against one and the same defendant, the court is entitled to join these cases in one proceeding if such joinder will facilitate faster and more correct examination of the cases.

(As amended by the law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force 30.09.2011.)

#### 135.pants. Separation of Claims and Civil Cases

(1) A judge may order the plaintiff to separate one claim or several claims from the joined claims into a separate claim if it is considered appropriate to examine the claims separately.

(2) The court examining the case may, by decision, separate one claim or several claims from the joined claims into a separate case if their examination in one proceeding has become difficult or impossible.

#### 136.pants. Filing a Counterclaim

(1) A defendant is entitled to file a counterclaim against the plaintiff in the court of first instance until the examination of the case on the merits is completed.

(2) A counterclaim shall be filed in accordance with the general rules for filing a claim.

(3) The court or judge shall accept a counterclaim if:

- 1) a set-off is possible between the original claim and the counterclaim;
- 2) satisfaction of the counterclaim completely or partially precludes satisfaction of the original claim;
- 3) the counterclaim and the original claim are interrelated and their joint examination will facilitate faster and more correct adjudication of the case.
  - (4) The counterclaim shall be examined together with the original claim.

(As amended by the laws of 19.06.2003. and 05.02.2009., which enter into force 01.03.2009.)

### 19. nodaļa

Securing of Claims and Interim Protection

(Chapter title as amended by the law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force 20.04.2021.)

#### 137. pants. Basis for securing claims and interim protection and content of application

(1) Securing of a claim may be applied in claims of a proprietary nature if there is a basis to believe that the execution of the court judgment in the case could become difficult or impossible.

(2) Interim protection may be applied in claims of a proprietary or non-proprietary nature if there is a basis to believe that the claimant's rights are being violated or could be violated until the moment the decision enters into force, and if the application of interim protection is necessary to prevent possible significant harm. Interim protection is also applied in cases where a temporary regulation of disputed relations must be established until the moment the decision enters into force, if this is necessary for the claimant to prevent possible significant harm.

(3) The court or judge may, upon a reasoned application of the claimant, adopt a decision on the application of securing a claim or interim protection. Securing of a claim and interim protection may also be applied simultaneously.

(4) The application shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the application is submitted;
- 2) the claimant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, or, if there is none, — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant consents to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if the claimant has registered in the online system for communication with the court, an indication of the registration shall also be included;
- 3) the defendant's, third party's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, or, if there is none, — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. The defendant's personal identity number or registration number shall be indicated if it is known;
- 4) the claimant's representative's (if the claim is brought by a representative) name, surname, personal identity number and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant's representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, consents to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if the representative has registered in the online system for communication with the court, an indication of the registration shall also be included. If the claimant's representative's address is outside Latvia, the email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of their participation in the online system shall be provided;
- 5) the subject matter of the claim;
- 6) in claims of a proprietary nature — the claim amount;
- 7) the means of securing the claim or interim protection that the claimant requests to be applied;
- 8) the circumstances on which the claimant bases the necessity of securing the claim or interim protection.
  - (5) Evidence confirming the circumstances on which the necessity of securing the claim or interim protection is based shall be attached to the application.
  - (6) The question of securing a claim or interim protection may be examined at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before bringing the claim to court.

(As worded by the Law of 25.03.2021 with amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 138.pants. Means of securing claims

(1) The means of securing a claim are:

- 1) pledge of movable property and cash belonging to the defendant;
- 2) entry of a prohibition note in the relevant movable property register or other public register;
- 3) entry of a claim securing note in the Land Register or ship register;
- 4) arrest of a ship;
- 5) prohibition on the defendant to perform certain actions or obligation of the defendant to perform certain actions within a specified period;
- 6) pledge of payments due from third parties, including funds in credit institutions and other financial institutions;
- 7) suspension of enforcement actions (also prohibition on the bailiff to transfer money or property to the creditor or debtor or suspension of the sale of property).
  - (2) When securing a claim by entering a prohibition note in the relevant movable property register or other public register, the decision shall indicate the type of prohibition to be entered.
  - (3) If the subject matter of the claim is ownership right to movable property or immovable property or the claim is directed towards the execution of a registration of a right, the securing of the claim shall be made by pledging the movable property in dispute or by entering a prohibition note in the relevant immovable property section in the Land Register.
  - (4) If the subject matter of the claim is a property right to immovable property, the securing of the claim shall be made by entering an encumbrance note in the relevant immovable property section in the Land Register.
  - (5) If the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim, its securing with immovable property shall be made by entering a pledge right note in the relevant immovable property section in the Land Register, indicating the amount of the claim to be secured.
  - (6) Arrest of a ship shall be applied only in maritime claims.
  - (7) Suspension of the sale of property is not permissible in cases where the claim is brought for recovery of money.
  - (71) Pledge of payments due from third parties, including funds in credit institutions and other financial institutions, is not permissible in claims where the claim is compensation to be determined at the court's discretion.
  - (8) When granting an application for securing a claim, the decision shall indicate the amount up to which the security extends, but it may not be greater than the claim amount.
  - (9) It is permissible to apply several means of securing a claim simultaneously, observing the provisions of paragraph eight of this Section.

(As worded by the Law of 07.09.2006 with amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009, 04.08.2011, 11.09.2014 and 25.03.2021, which entered into force on 20.04.2021.)

138.1 pants. Means of interim protection

(1) The means of interim protection are:

- 1) pledge of movable property belonging to the defendant;
- 2) entry of a prohibition note or other note in the Land Register, relevant movable property register or other public register;
- 3) prohibition on the defendant to perform certain actions or obligation of the defendant to perform certain actions within a specified period;
- 4) suspension of enforcement actions (also prohibition on the bailiff to transfer money or property to the creditor or debtor or suspension of the sale of property);
- 5) temporary regulation of disputed relations.
  - (2) When applying a means of interim protection — entry of a prohibition note or other note in the Land Register, relevant movable property register or other public register —, the decision shall indicate the type of prohibition or note to be entered.

(As worded by the Law of 25.03.2021, which entered into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 139. pants. Security for Claim and Interim Protection Before Filing a Claim

(1) A prospective plaintiff may request security for a claim before filing it in court and even before the expiry of the obligation period, if the debtor, avoiding the performance of the obligation, removes or alienates his property, leaves the declared place of residence or place of residence without informing the creditor, or performs other actions indicating that he is not acting in good faith. When submitting an application for security for a claim before filing a claim, the prospective plaintiff shall provide evidence confirming his right to the claim and the necessity to secure the claim.

(11) A prospective plaintiff may request interim protection before filing a claim if interim protection must be applied immediately to prevent substantial harm. In the application for interim protection, the prospective plaintiff shall substantiate the urgency of its application. Evidence confirming his right to the claim and the necessity to apply interim protection shall be attached to the application.

(2) An application for security for a claim or interim protection before filing a claim shall be submitted to the court in which the claim is to be filed. If the parties have agreed to refer the dispute to a permanent arbitral tribunal, the application shall be submitted to the court according to the location of the debtor or his property.

(3) When granting an application for security for a claim or interim protection before filing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for the plaintiff of no longer than 30 days for submitting the statement of claim to the court or permanent arbitral tribunal. (As amended by the law of 07.09.2006., with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 11.09.2014. and 25.03.2021., which entered into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 140.pants. Examination of Issues of Security for a Claim

(1) An application for security for a claim shall be decided by the court or judge, without prior notice to the participants in the case, no later than the next day after its receipt or, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the statement of claim, after initiation of the case. In the appellate instance, the application shall be decided by three judges collegially. When deciding the issue of security for a claim, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim and the proportionality between the legal interests of the parties.

(2) Upon granting an application for security for a claim, the court or judge may require the claimant to secure damages that may be incurred by the defendant in connection with the security for the claim by paying a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff.

(21) In cases where the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim and the security measure for the claim specified in points 1, 2, 4 or 6 of the first paragraph of Section 138 of this Law is applied, the claimant shall secure possible damages to the defendant by paying five percent of the claim amount into the deposit account of a bailiff. The court or judge, when adopting a decision on security for a claim, may impose an obligation on the claimant to secure possible damages in a greater amount. The court shall set a time limit for securing damages, which may not be longer than 20 days from the day of adoption of the decision. The court or judge may fully or partially release from securing damages if, taking into account the circumstances of the case, securing damages is not fair or is disproportionate to the claimant's financial situation. Securing damages does not apply to persons who are exempt from state fees pursuant to law.

(22) If the obligation imposed by the court or judge in accordance with the second and 2.1 paragraphs of this Section has not been fulfilled and the claimant has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff regarding the payment of the sum of money into their deposit account within the time limit set by the court or judge, the court or judge shall adopt a decision on the cancellation of the security measure for the claim.

(3) The court may, upon application of a participant in the case, replace the specified security measures for the claim with other measures.

(31) Upon granting an application for replacement of security measures for a claim with other measures, the court may decide again on the obligation imposed on the claimant in accordance with the second and 5.1 paragraphs of this Section.

(4) In cases where the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim, the defendant may pay the amount of the secured claim into the deposit account of a bailiff. In the application to the bailiff, the defendant shall indicate in which case this amount is being paid for the replacement of the applied security measure for the claim, and shall also submit to the bailiff the relevant decision on the security for the claim. The court or judge, on the basis of a certificate issued by the bailiff regarding the payment of the amount into the deposit account, shall replace the adopted security measure for the claim with a pledge of the paid monetary funds. The replacement of pledged movable property with money by paying the amount of the secured claim into the deposit account of a bailiff shall be deemed to be a replacement of the security measure for the claim.

(5) Security for a claim may be cancelled, upon a reasoned application of a party, by the same court that secured the claim or by the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits. When deciding the issue of cancellation of security for a claim, the court shall evaluate the conditions specified in the first paragraph of this Section, taking into account the evidence and substantiation submitted by the party. The defendant may include in the application substantiation regarding damages that have been incurred by them due to the applied security measure for the claim or could be incurred if the security measure for the claim is not cancelled.

(51) Upon rejecting an application for cancellation of security for a claim, the court or judge may simultaneously impose an obligation on the claimant to secure the damages referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Section by paying a sum of money determined by the court into the deposit account of a bailiff within 20 days from the day of adoption of the decision.

(6) Upon rejecting the claim, the court shall cancel the security for the claim in the judgment. Security for the claim shall remain in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.

(61) If the claimant has been obliged to secure compensation for damages to the defendant that may be incurred in connection with security for the claim, the court, in the judgment or decision by which the claim is left without examination or the case is terminated, shall simultaneously decide the issue of payment of the amount paid to secure compensation for damages from the account of a sworn bailiff. Upon rejecting or granting the claim in part, the court shall decide the issue of full or partial payment of the secured damages to the defendant upon the defendant's request, if the defendant has submitted evidence to the court regarding the amount of actual damages. If the request and evidence regarding the amount of actual damages have not been submitted to the court, the secured damages shall be reimbursed to the claimant. The defendant has the right to claim compensation for damages not recovered in accordance with the procedure of Section 143 of this Law.

(7) If the claim is left without examination or the proceedings are terminated, the court shall cancel the security for the claim in the decision. Security for the claim shall remain in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.

(8) If a decision on security for a claim was adopted before the filing of the claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge shall, upon receipt of an application from the potential claimant or defendant, adopt a decision on the cancellation of the security.

(9) The applications referred to in the third and fifth paragraphs of this Section shall be decided at a court session, with prior notice to the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application. The date of the court session shall be set no later than 30 days after receipt of the application.

(10) If in a decision adopted on a party's application for cancellation of security for a claim the claimant has been required to fulfil the obligation imposed in paragraph 5.1 of this Section, but it has not been fulfilled and the claimant has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff regarding the payment of the amount into their deposit account, the court or judge shall adopt a decision on the cancellation of the security measure for the claim.

(07.09.2006. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 04.08.2011., 11.09.2014., 23.04.2015., 28.05.2015., 25.03.2021. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 140.1 pants. Examination of Issues of Interim Protection

(1) When deciding the issue of interim protection, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie

formal legal basis of the claim and the proportionality between the legal interests of the parties.

(2) An application for interim protection shall be decided by the court or judge, without holding a court session and without prior notice to the participants in the case, within 10 days after its receipt or, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the statement of claim, after initiation of the case. In the appellate instance, the application shall be decided by three judges collegially. If the court or judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided at a court session within 15 days after its receipt or, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the statement of claim, after initiation of the case, summoning the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(3) If delay could cause irreparable harm and it is not necessary to request additional evidence, an application for interim protection shall be decided by the court or judge no later than the next day after initiation of the case or, if the case has already been initiated, no later than the next day after receipt of the application, without prior notice to the defendant and other participants in the case.

(4) Upon granting an application for interim protection, the court or judge may require the claimant to secure damages that may be incurred by the defendant in connection with the application of interim protection, and to pay a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or to submit to the court an equivalent guarantee. If the claimant has not fulfilled the imposed obligation or has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff regarding the payment of the sum of money into their deposit account within the time limit set by the court or judge, the court or judge shall adopt a decision on the cancellation of the interim protection measure.

(5) The court may, upon application of a participant in the case, replace the applied interim protection measure with another measure or amend it.

(6) Upon granting an application for replacement of an interim protection measure with another measure, the court may decide again on the obligation imposed on the claimant in accordance with the fourth and eighth paragraphs of this Section.

(7) Interim protection may be cancelled, upon a reasoned application of a party, by the same court that applied the interim protection or by the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits. When deciding the issue of cancellation of interim protection, the court or judge shall evaluate the conditions specified in the first paragraph of this Section, taking into account the evidence and substantiation submitted by the party. The defendant may include in the application substantiation regarding damages that have been incurred by them due to the applied interim protection measure or could be incurred if the interim protection measure is not cancelled.

(8) Upon rejecting an application for cancellation of interim protection, the court or judge may simultaneously impose an obligation on the claimant to secure the damages referred to in the seventh paragraph of this Section by paying a sum of money determined by the court into the deposit account of a bailiff within 20 days from the day of adoption of the decision.

(9) Upon rejecting the claim, leaving the claim without examination or terminating the proceedings, the court shall cancel the interim protection in the respective ruling. Interim protection shall be in force until the day the ruling enters into legal force.

(10) Upon granting the claim, the court shall decide on the cancellation or continuation of the applied interim protection until enforcement of the judgment.

(11) If a decision on interim protection was adopted before the filing of the claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the court or judge shall, upon receipt of an application from the potential claimant or potential participant in the case, adopt a decision on the cancellation of the interim protection.

(12) An application for cancellation or replacement of an interim protection measure shall be decided at a court session, with prior notice to the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(25.03.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

#### 141. pants. Notification and appeal of decisions adopted in matters of security for a claim and interim protection

(1) An ancillary complaint may be lodged against the decision referred to in the third paragraph of Section 140 and the fifth paragraph of Section 140.1 of this Law, a decision rejecting an application for security for a claim or an application for interim protection, and a decision rejecting an application for cancellation of security for a claim or interim protection, as well as a court decision on security for damages that might be incurred by the defendant in connection with security for a claim or interim protection (Section 140, paragraphs two, 3.1 and 5.1 and Section 140.1, paragraphs four, six and eight).

(11) A decision adopted on security for damages that might be incurred by the defendant in connection with security for a claim or interim protection shall be notified to the defendant after the claimant has paid the amount determined by the court or judge into the bailiff's deposit account.

(2) If a decision on security for a claim or interim protection has been adopted without the presence of a party to the case, the time limit for lodging a complaint shall be calculated from the date of issue of the decision.

(3) If a decision on security for a claim has been adopted without the presence of the defendant or other parties to the case, the court shall notify the defendant and the other parties to the case of this decision no earlier than on the third day after its adoption.

(4) If a decision on the application of interim protection has been adopted without the presence of the defendant or other parties to the case, the court shall notify the defendant and the other parties to the case of this decision simultaneously with the notification of the decision to the claimant.

(07.09.2006. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 14.12.2006., 05.02.2009. likumu, Satversmes tiesas 30.03.2010. spriedumu, 04.08.2011., 23.04.2015., 25.03.2021. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 142. pants. Execution of decisions adopted in matters of security for a claim and interim protection

(1) A decision on security for a claim (Section 140, paragraph one) and application of interim protection

(Section 140.1, paragraph one) and a decision on cancellation of security for a claim (Section 140, paragraphs five and ten) and cancellation of interim protection (Section 140.1, paragraph seven) shall be executable immediately after its adoption.

(2) A decision on security for a claim and application of interim protection, adopted with the condition specified in the second paragraph, paragraph 2.1 of Section 140 or the fourth paragraph of Section 140.1 of this Law, shall be executable after the claimant has paid the amount determined by the court or judge into the bailiff's deposit account or — in the case referred to in the fourth paragraph of Section 140.1 — has submitted an equivalent guarantee. A writ of execution or the decision referred to in the third paragraph of this Section shall be issued after payment of the amount determined by the court or receipt of the equivalent guarantee.

(3) If a claim has been secured by or interim protection has been applied in relation to immovable property or a ship or by entry of a prohibition note or other note in the Land Register, movable property register or other public register, the court shall issue to the claimant the respective decision with an inscription that this decision has been issued for entry of a note in the Land Register, movable property register or other relevant public register, but in the case of arrest of a ship — for detention of the ship in port.

(4) A decision on security for a claim or application of interim protection by pledging movable property or cash belonging to the defendant which is in the possession of the defendant or third parties shall be executed in accordance with the procedure specified in Chapter 71 of this Law.

(5) When pledging payments that are due to the defendant from third parties under a contract (except funds in credit institutions or with other payment service providers), the bailiff, on the basis of a writ of execution, shall send a request to these persons to notify whether they have an obligation to pay any amounts to the defendant, in what amount and time limit, and shall also notify that these amounts are being pledged in the amount of the claim, observing the restriction specified in paragraph 3 of Annex 1 of this Law in relation to debtors, and shall give an order to pay the payments (including demand deposits) for which the time limit has arrived into the bailiff's deposit account. The bailiff shall pledge funds in credit institutions or with other payment service providers in accordance with the procedure specified in Section 599.1 of this Law. Pledged payments may be paid to other persons only in accordance with the calculation of the bailiff who first pledged the payments.

(6) A decision on security for a claim or application of interim protection by establishing a prohibition on the defendant to perform certain acts or an obligation of the defendant to perform certain acts shall be executed by the bailiff and the court decision shall be notified to the defendant or the relevant third party in accordance with the procedure specified in Section

555 of this Law.

(7) If in cases where the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim, the defendant has paid the amount of the claim into the bailiff's deposit account, the bailiff shall release the pledged movable property from the pledge.

(8) If the applied security for a claim or interim protection has been cancelled, then the decision on cancellation shall be executed on the order of the bailiff who executed the decision on security for a claim or interim protection.

(9) A decision on replacement of a security for a claim or interim protection measure shall be executed by the bailiff, first securing the claim with the replacement measure and then cancelling the replaced measure. An amount that has been paid into the bailiff's deposit account as a security for a claim measure may be refunded by the bailiff only on the basis of a court decision.

(07.09.2006. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 25.03.2021. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

142.1 pants. Treatment of pledged movable property that is perishable in the context of security for a claim or interim protection

(1) The bailiff shall not pledge property that is perishable and the sale of which during its shelf life may not be possible.

(2) If the bailiff has pledged property that is perishable, but which could be possible to sell during its shelf life, upon request of the bailiff, the court that adopted the decision on security for a claim or interim protection, or the court in which the case is at that time, shall decide on permission to sell the pledged property, but pledge the money obtained from the sale, from which sales expenses have been deducted, for security for a claim or interim protection. The court shall resolve the bailiff's request in written proceedings no later than the next day after its receipt. A decision permitting the sale of pledged property shall be drawn up in the form of a resolution. The court decision is not subject to appeal.

(3) After receipt of the court decision permitting the sale of the pledged property and the pledging of the monetary funds obtained from the sale, the bailiff shall sell the pledged property in accordance with the procedure provided for in the second paragraph of Section 581 of this Law, but shall deposit and keep the money obtained from the sale, from which sales expenses have been deducted, in the bailiff's deposit account. In such a case, the monetary funds obtained from the sale shall serve in the case as a security for a claim or interim protection measure. The bailiff shall notify the court, the claimant and the defendant of the sale of movable property pledged for security for a claim or interim protection and the results of the sale.

(4) If the court rejects the bailiff's request to allow the sale of the pledged property, it shall simultaneously assess the need to cancel the applied security for a claim or interim protection in relation to the specific property.

(01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 25.03.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

#### 143. Article. Compensation for Damages Caused by Security for a Claim and Interim Protection

The defendant has the right to claim compensation for damages caused to them in connection with the security for a claim or the application of interim protection, if the security for a claim or interim protection is revoked in the case specified in Part Eight of Section 140 or Part Eleven of Section 140.1 of this Law, or if the claim filed against them is dismissed or left without examination, or the proceedings in the case are terminated in the cases specified in Clauses 2 and 4 of Section 223 of this Law.

(In the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021., which comes into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 144. Article. Revocation of Security for a Claim

(Deleted by the Law of 07.09.2006., which comes into force on 11.10.2006.)

#### 145. Article. Termination of Security for a Claim

(Deleted by the Law of 07.09.2006., which comes into force on 11.10.2006.)

#### 146. Article. Appeal of a Decision

(Deleted by the Law of 07.09.2006., which comes into force on 11.10.2006.)

Chapter 20

Preparation of Civil Cases for Trial

(Chapter in the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002., which comes into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 147. Article. Preparation of Civil Cases for Trial

(1) To ensure the timely examination of a case, the judge prepares the case for trial after receiving the statement of claim.

(2) The obligation of the parties to the case is to participate in the preparation of the case for trial: to respond to the judge's requests within the time limits set by them, to submit written explanations, necessary evidence, and to appear in court at the judge's invitation.

#### 148. Article. Sending the Statement of Claim and Accompanying Documents to the Defendant

(1) After the initiation of a case, the statement of claim is immediately sent to the defendant to their official electronic address or by registered mail and a time limit is set for the submission of written explanations — 15 to 30 days from the date of sending the statement of claim, but in cases concerning children — not longer than 15 days from the date of sending the statement of claim. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the statement of claim may also be sent to the defendant.

(11) If the statement of claim and the documents attached to it (Part Four of Section 129) after the initiation of the case are to be sent to the defendant in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law, the time limit for submitting written explanations is 30 days, counted from the day when the statement of claim is issued to the defendant.

(12) The claimant is notified of the sending of the statement of claim and the accompanying documents to the defendant.

(13) The court sends information to the claimant and the defendant about the possibility of resolving the dispute by using mediation and about the obligation to notify the court within the specified time limit if they agree to use mediation.

(14) The court sends information to the claimant and the defendant about the court's proposal to transfer the case for examination to another court in accordance with Section 32.1 of this Law and about the obligation to notify the court within the specified time limit if the transfer of the case for examination to another court will create significant obstacles for the claimant or defendant to appear at the court hearing.

(2) In the explanation, the defendant indicates:

- 1) whether they acknowledge the claim in full or in any part thereof;
- 2) their objections to the claim and the grounds thereof;
- 3) evidence confirming their objections to the claim and the grounds thereof, as well as the law on which they are based;
- 4) requests for the admission of evidence or its collection;
- 5) other circumstances that they consider significant in the examination of the case, and may also indicate their telephone number if they agree to use the telephone for communication with the court;
- 51) email address for communication with the court and, if they have registered their participation in the online system, also include an indication of registration, if the defendant (or their representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia) agrees to electronic communication with the court. If the address of the defendant's representative is outside Latvia, additionally indicate the email address or notify about the registration of their participation in the online system;
- 52) the name of the credit institution and the account number to which litigation costs are to be reimbursed;
- 6) whether they agree to use mediation.
  - (3) Evidence confirming the circumstances on which the objections are based is attached to the explanation.
  - (31) The defendant does not indicate information containing state secrets in the explanations. Information containing state secrets must be indicated in a separate document.
  - (4) After receiving the explanation, it is immediately sent to the claimant and third parties. If the judge considers it necessary, they have the right to request a reply from the claimant regarding the explanation.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009., 22.05.2014., 29.10.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017., 22.06.2017., 21.01.2021., 11.11.2021., and 22.12.2021., which comes into force on 24.12.2021.)

#### 149.pants. Judge's Actions in Preparing a Case for Trial

(1) After receiving an explanation or upon expiry of the time limit set for its submission, the judge decides on the preparatory actions for the case so that it can be examined in a court session.

(2) In preparing the case for trial, the judge attempts to reconcile the parties and also offers to resolve the dispute using mediation.

(3) In preparing the case for trial, the judge decides on the requests of the participants in the case regarding:

- 1) involvement or admission of third parties;
- 2) securing of evidence;
- 3) summoning of witnesses;
- 4) appointment of expert examination;
- 5) acceptance or request of written and material evidence;
- 6) participation of persons in the trial of the case using videoconference.
  - (4) The judge is entitled to request written explanations from the participants in the case in order to clarify the circumstances and evidence of the case. Explanations and evidence shall be submitted within the time limit set by the judge.
  - (41) If the claimant and the defendant agree to the use of mediation, the judge, when adopting a decision on the use of mediation, shall set a time limit for the use of mediation, which shall not exceed six months, and the obligation of the parties to submit to the court evidence of the mediation result no later than seven days after the termination of mediation.

The judge's decision on the use of mediation is not subject to appeal.

(5) The judge decides on questions regarding the participation of representatives of state and local government institutions and the prosecutor in the case in the cases provided for by law, on the sending of court orders to other courts, on the participation of persons in the trial of the case using videoconference, and also performs other necessary procedural actions.

(6) For the performance of the actions specified in this Article, the judge may set a preparatory session to which the parties and third parties are invited.

(7) If a preparatory session is not necessary, the judge sets the date and time of the court session, and the persons to be invited and summoned to the court. When setting the time limit for the use of mediation, the judge shall simultaneously set the date of the court session no earlier than after the time limit referred to in Paragraph 4.1 of this Article.

(8) In cases concerning the reinstatement of an employee at work and in cases concerning the recognition of an employer's termination as invalid, the date of the court session shall be set no later than within 15 days after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission, or after the preparatory session, or after the expiry of the mediation time limit. If evidence of the mediation result is received by the court before the time limit set by the judge, the judge may set a new date for the court session.

(9) In cases concerning claims arising from the alienation of immovable property for the needs of society, the court session shall be set within 15 days after receipt of the explanations or expiry of the time limit for their submission, or after the preparatory session, or after the expiry of the mediation time limit. If evidence of the mediation result is received by the court before the time limit set by the judge, the judge may set a new date for the court session.

(10) In cases concerning administrator's claims on behalf of insolvent debtors in the cases provided for in Chapter XVII of the Insolvency Law and concerning the recovery of damages from members of management institutions of a legal person and participants (shareholders) of a capital company, based on their obligation to be liable for damages caused, as well as from personally liable members of a partnership, based on their obligation to be liable for the obligations of the partnership, the court session shall be set no later than within three months after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission, or after the preparatory session, or after the expiry of the mediation time limit. If evidence of the mediation result is received by the court before the time limit set by the judge, the judge may set a new date for the court session.

(As amended by the Laws of 07.04.2004., 09.06.2005., 30.09.2010., 08.09.2011., 22.05.2014. and 11.11.2021., which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 149.1 pants. Preparatory Session

(1) In a preparatory session, the judge questions the participants in the case about the substance of the case in order to clarify the subject matter and limits of the dispute, explains to the participants in the case their procedural rights and obligations, the consequences of performing or not performing procedural actions, decides on the questions provided for in Paragraphs three, four and five of Article 149 of this Law, attempts to reconcile the parties, and also offers to resolve the dispute using mediation, if necessary, sets a time limit within which individual procedural actions are to be performed.

(2) If the court session has not been set previously, in the preparatory session the judge sets the date and time of the court session and notifies the participants in the case who are present, and also determines the persons to be invited and summoned to the court session.

(3) The preparatory session shall be recorded. The course of the preparatory session shall be recorded in full using technical means. The record shall contain information about the course of the session, the substance of the explanations of the participants in the case and the decisions adopted by the judge.

(As amended by the Laws of 19.12.2013., 22.05.2014. and 11.11.2021., which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 150.pants. Liability of Participants in the Case

(1) If a participant in the case fails to submit an explanation within the time limit set by the judge without valid reason, fails to respond to a request from the judge, the judge may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on him or her.

(2) If a participant in the case fails to appear at the preparatory session without valid reason, the judge may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on him or her.

(3) If the defendant has not submitted an explanation, has not appeared at the preparatory session and has not notified the reason for his or her non-appearance, the court may render a default judgment at the preparatory session.

(As amended by the Laws of 30.09.2010., 29.11.2012., 12.09.2013. and 11.11.2021., which entered into force Chapter 21

Trial of Civil Cases

#### 151.pants. Court Session

(1) A case shall be tried in a court session, which is presided over by a judge.

(2) The judge shall conduct the trial of the case in such a way as to ensure that all participants in the case have equal opportunities to participate in the clarification of the circumstances of the case.

(3) During the trial of the case, the judge attempts to reconcile the parties and also offers to resolve the dispute using mediation.

(As amended by the Law of 22.05.2014., which entered into force on 18.06.2014.)

#### 152.pants. Order in the Court Session

(1) Participants in the case, witnesses, experts, interpreters shall observe the order established in this Law in the court session and shall comply without objection with the instructions of the judge and the decisions of the court.

(2) Persons present in the courtroom shall behave in such a way as not to disturb the course of the court session.

(3) The course of the trial may be recorded or otherwise documented without disturbing the proceedings of the court session. The use of photographic, cinema and video equipment in the court session shall be permitted only with the permission of the court. Before deciding this question, the court shall hear the opinion of the participants in the case.

(4) The number of persons admitted to the courtroom shall be determined by the court in accordance with the number of seats in the room. Relatives of the parties and representatives of mass media shall have preferential rights to be present at the trial.

(5) When the court enters the courtroom and leaves it, all persons present in the courtroom shall rise.

(6) Participants in the case, witnesses and experts shall provide the court with explanations and opinions, submit requests and give testimony, while standing. Derogation from this provision shall be permitted only with the permission of the judge.

(7) All persons present in the courtroom shall listen to the court judgment while standing.

(As amended by the Law of 19.06.2003., which entered into force on 24.07.2003.)

#### 153.pants. Maintenance of order in court session

(1) To a person who disturbs order during the hearing of a case, the judge issues a warning.

(2) If parties to the case, witnesses, experts or interpreters repeatedly disturb order, the court may impose a fine of up to 80 euros on these persons.

(3) If a prosecutor or advocate repeatedly disturbs order, this is reported to a higher-ranking prosecutor or to the Latvian Council of Sworn Advocates.

(4) If a person who is not a party to the case repeatedly disturbs order, the judge expels them from the courtroom. This person may also be held liable under the law for contempt of court.

(As amended by the law of 12.09.2013, which came into force on 01.01.2014.)

#### 154. pants. Commencement of court session

At the time set for the hearing of the case, the court enters the courtroom, the presiding officer opens the court session and announces:

- 1) the year, date, month and place of the court session;
- 2) the name of the court hearing the case, the composition of the court, the secretary of the court session, the interpreter, the court-appointed representative for the videoconference proceedings if a party to the case participates in the court session using videoconference in court at the location of the party to the case or in a specially equipped place for this purpose, the advocate and prosecutor participating in the case;
- 3) the time of opening of the court session;
- 4) the name of the case.

(In the wording of the law of 08.09.2011, as amended by the law of 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 155.pants. Verification of the attendance of participants in proceedings

(1) The secretary of the court session reports to the court which of the persons invited and summoned in this case have attended, as well as whether the court session has been notified to persons who have not attended and what information has been received about the reasons for the non-attendance of these persons.

(2) The court verifies the identity of persons who have attended, the identity of persons who participate in the court session using videoconference in an online system, and the powers of representatives. A court-appointed representative verifies the identity of persons who participate in the court session using videoconference in court at the person's location or in a specially equipped place for this purpose.

(As amended by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 156.pants. Consequences of the non-attendance of a party to the case, witness, expert or interpreter

(1) If one of the parties to the case, a witness, an expert or an interpreter has not attended the court session, the court commences the examination of the case unless there is a ground to postpone it pursuant to Article 209 or 210 of this Law.

(2) If a party to the case who has not attended the court session has not notified the court in time of the reason for their non-attendance, the court may impose a fine of up to 80 euros on this person.

(3) If one of the parties to the case does not attend court for reasons which the court considers unjustified, the court may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on this person.

(4) The procedural sanctions provided for in Articles 109 and 122 of this Law are applicable to a witness and an expert who have not attended the court session.

(As amended by the law of 12.09.2013, which came into force on 01.01.2014.)

#### 157.pants. Explanation of duties to the interpreter

(1) The court explains to the interpreter their duty to interpret the explanations, questions, testimony, applications and requests of those persons who do not have command of the language of proceedings, and to these persons — the explanations, questions, testimony, applications, requests of other parties to the case, the content of documents read out, the judge's orders and court decisions.

(2) The court warns the interpreter that they are liable under the Criminal Law for refusal to interpret or for deliberately incorrect interpretation.

#### 158.pants. Expulsion of witnesses from the courtroom

Witnesses are expelled from the courtroom until the commencement of their examination. The presiding officer of the session ensures that witnesses examined by the court do not communicate with witnesses who have not been examined.

#### 159.pants. Explanation of rights and duties to the parties to the case

(1) The court explains to the parties to the case their procedural rights and duties.

(2) During the examination of the case, the court explains to the parties and third persons the consequences of performing or failing to perform procedural acts.

#### 160.pants. Decision on challenges

(1) The court ascertains whether the parties to the case have challenges to the judge, prosecutor, secretary of the court session, expert or interpreter.

(2) The court decides on challenges filed in the procedure set out in Article 21 of this Law.

#### 161.pants. Explanation of rights and duties to the expert

If the person chosen as an expert is not a court expert certified in the procedure set out in the Law on Court Experts, the court explains to the expert their rights and duties and warns that the expert is liable under the Criminal Law for refusal to provide an opinion or for deliberately providing a false opinion.

(As amended by the law of 29.10.2015, which came into force on 03.12.2015.)

#### 162.pants. Decision on requests filed by parties to the case

The court ascertains whether the parties to the case have requests related to the hearing of the case and decides on them after hearing the opinion of the other parties to the case.

#### 163.pants. Commencement of the examination of the case on the merits

(1) The examination of the case on the merits begins with the judge's report on the circumstances of the case.

(2) After the judge's report, the court ascertains whether the plaintiff maintains the claim, whether the defendant admits the claim and whether the parties wish to conclude a settlement or submit the case for examination to an arbitration court.

#### 164.pants.

Waiver of claim, admission of claim, settlement, agreement to submit the case to an arbitration court or to use mediation

(1) A waiver of claim or admission of claim may be expressed orally at a court session.

(2) If a waiver of claim or admission of claim is expressed in written applications addressed to the court, they are appended to the case.

(3) A settlement is to be submitted to the court in writing and is appended to the case.

(4) An agreement to submit the case to an arbitration court is drawn up in writing and appended to the case.

(5) On the plaintiff's waiver of claim, on the parties' agreement to submit the case for examination to an arbitration court, as well as on the parties' settlement, the court adopts a decision by which it simultaneously terminates proceedings in the case. The decision on the approval of the settlement must indicate the terms of the settlement.

(6) On the refusal to approve a settlement, the court adopts a reasoned decision and continues to examine the case on the merits.

(7) Before the examination of the case on the merits is completed, it is possible to waive the claim, admit the claim, conclude a settlement or an agreement to submit the dispute for examination to an arbitration court, as well as to agree on the use of mediation.

(As amended by the laws of 19.12.2013, 22.05.2014 and 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 165.pants. Explanations of parties to the case

(1) Parties to the case provide explanations at a court session in the following order: the plaintiff, the third person with independent claims and the defendant.

(2) If a third person without independent claims participates in the case, they provide explanations after the plaintiff or the defendant depending on which side this third person participates in the case.

(3) If the claim has been brought by a prosecutor, a state or local government institution or a person who has been granted the right by law to defend in court the rights and legally protected interests of other persons, they provide explanations first at the court session.

(4) Representatives of parties to the case provide explanations on behalf of the persons they represent.

(5) Parties to the case indicate in their explanations all circumstances on which their claims or objections are based.

(As amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which came into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 166.pants. Written explanations of parties to the case

(1) Parties to the case are entitled to submit their explanations to the court in writing.

(2) Written explanations of parties to the case are read out at the court session, observing the order set out in Article 165 of this Law, and are appended to the case.

#### 167.pants. Order of asking questions

(1) With the court's permission, parties to the case may ask each other questions. The court may reject questions that do not relate to the case.

(2) A judge may ask a question to a party to the case if they express themselves unclearly or indefinitely, as well as when it is not apparent from the explanations that the party acknowledges or denies the circumstances on which the opposing party's claims or objections are based.

(3) If a party refuses to answer a question about disputed circumstances or avoids giving explanations about them, the court may assume that the party does not dispute these circumstances.

#### 168.pants. Determination of the order of examination of evidence

The court, having heard the explanations of the parties to the case and listened to their opinion, determines the order of examination of witnesses and experts and examination of other evidence.

#### 169.pants. Warning of a witness

(1) Before examining a witness, the court establishes their identity and warns about liability for refusing to testify or for giving deliberately false testimony, as well as explains the content of Article 107 of this law.

(2) Before examination, the witness gives orally the following affirmation:

"I, . . . (witness's name and surname), undertake to testify to the court about everything known to me in the case in which I am summoned as a witness. I have been informed that for refusing to testify or for giving deliberately false testimony I face criminal liability in accordance with the criminal law."

(3) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(4) To a witness who has not reached 14 years of age, the judge explains their duty to testify truthfully, to tell everything known to them in this case, but does not warn this witness about liability for refusing to testify or for giving deliberately false testimony.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 170.pants. Examination of witnesses

(1) Each witness is examined separately.

(2) First, the witnesses indicated by the plaintiff are examined, then — the witnesses indicated by the defendant. The order of examination of witnesses indicated by one party is determined by the court, taking into account the opinion of that party.

(3) A witness gives their testimony and answers questions orally.

(4) The court establishes the witness's relationship with the parties and third parties and invites them to tell the court everything that is personally known to the witness in the case, avoiding providing information whose source they cannot indicate, as well as from expressing their assumptions and conclusions. The court may interrupt the witness's statement if they speak about circumstances that do not relate to the case.

(5) With the court's permission, parties to the case may ask questions to the witness. The first to ask questions is the party at whose request the witness was summoned, then — other parties to the case.

(6) The judge may ask questions to the witness at any moment of their examination. During the examination of a witness, questions may also be asked to the parties to the case.

(7) The court may examine a witness a second time in the same or another court session, and also confront witnesses.

(8) If the circumstances for the clarification of which witnesses were summoned have been clarified, the court with the consent of the parties may not examine the witnesses who have arrived, adopting an appropriate decision on this.

(With amendments made by the laws of 19.12.2013 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 171.pants. Right of a witness to use written notes

During testimony, a witness may use written notes if their testimony is related to calculations or other data that are difficult to remember. These notes must be shown to the court and the parties to the case, and they may be attached to the case by decision of the court.

#### 172.pants. Examination of a minor witness

(1) Examination of a minor witness shall be conducted, at the court's discretion, in the presence of a legal representative or teacher. These persons may ask questions to the minor witness.

(2) In cases where it is necessary for clarifying the circumstances of the case, during the examination of a minor witness, by decision of the court, any party to the case and persons present in the courtroom may be removed from the courtroom. After the party's return to the courtroom, they are acquainted with the testimony of the minor witness and given the opportunity to ask questions to the witness.

(3) A witness who has not reached 15 years of age must be removed from the courtroom after examination, except in cases where the court considers the presence of this witness in the courtroom necessary.

#### 173.pants. Reading of a witness's testimony

A witness's testimony obtained in the course of securing evidence or by court commission or in a previous court session shall be read or played back, if it was recorded using audio recording, in the court session in which the case is heard.

(With amendments made by the law of 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016.)

#### 174.pants. Obligation of an examined witness

An examined witness must remain in the courtroom until the end of the hearing of the case. They may leave the courtroom before the end of the hearing of the case only pursuant to a court decision, adopted after hearing the opinions of the parties to the case.

#### 175.pants. Examination of an expert opinion and examination of an expert

(1) An expert opinion is read in a court session.

(2) The court and parties to the case may ask questions to an expert in the same manner as to witnesses.

(3) In the cases referred to in Article 125 of this law, the court may order a supplementary or repeated expert examination.

#### 176.pants. Attachment of written evidence to the case

(1) The question of attaching written evidence to the case is decided by the court after it has acquainted the parties to the case with the content of this evidence and heard their opinion.

(2) State secret items are compiled in a separate volume.

(3) Evidence containing commercial secrets is compiled in a separate volume upon a reasoned request of a party.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009 and 28.02.2019, which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

#### 177.pants. Examination of written evidence

(1) Written evidence or their inspection protocols are read in a court session or shown to the parties to the case, but, if necessary, — also to experts and witnesses.

(2) Personal correspondence may be read in an open court session only with the consent of the persons involved in the correspondence. If there is no such consent or the persons are deceased, the said evidence is read and examined in a closed court session.

#### 178.pants. Challenging written evidence

(1) Parties to the case may challenge the authenticity of written evidence.

(2) A person who has signed written evidence themselves cannot object to its authenticity. This person may challenge this evidence by bringing a separate claim if the signature was given under the influence of violence, threats or fraud.

(3) The authenticity of land register, notarial and other documents certified in the manner prescribed by law cannot be doubted. They may be challenged by bringing a separate claim.

(4) The submitter of challenged written evidence must give explanations in the same court session on whether they wish to use this written evidence or request its exclusion from evidence.

(5) If a party to the case wishes to use the challenged evidence, the court, having compared this evidence with other evidence in the case, decides on the admissibility of its use.

#### 179.pants. Application concerning forgery of written evidence

(1) A party to the case may submit a reasoned application concerning forgery of written evidence.

(2) The person who submitted this evidence may request the court to exclude it.

(3) To verify an application concerning forgery of written evidence, the court may order an expert examination or request other evidence.

(4) If the court finds that written evidence is forged, it excludes this evidence and reports the fact of forgery to the prosecutor.

(5) If the court finds that a party to the case has deliberately unreasonably initiated a dispute about the forgery of written evidence, it may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on this party to the case.

(With amendments made by the law of 12.09.2013, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

#### 180.pants. Examination of Physical Evidence

(1) Physical evidence is examined at a court hearing and shown to the parties, but if necessary — also to experts and witnesses.

(2) Parties may provide explanations regarding physical evidence and express their opinion and requests.

(3) The protocol of examination of physical evidence, which has been prepared in the course of securing evidence or pursuant to a court commission, is read out at the court hearing.

#### 181.pants. Inspection and Examination of Evidence on Site

(1) If written or physical evidence cannot be brought to court, upon the request of a party the court adopts a decision to inspect and examine such evidence at the location where it is situated.

(2) The court notifies the parties about the on-site inspection. Failure of these persons to appear is not an obstacle to conducting the inspection.

(3) When conducting an on-site inspection, the court may summon experts and witnesses.

(4) The course of the inspection is recorded in the court hearing protocol, to which the plans, drawings and images of physical evidence prepared and examined during the inspection are attached.

#### 182.pants. Opinion of Institution

(1) After examination of evidence, the court hears the opinion of the institution participating in the proceedings pursuant to law or a court decision.

(2) The judge and the parties may pose questions to the representative of this institution in connection with the opinion.

(07.04.2004. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.05.2004.)

#### 183.pants. Completion of Examination of the Case on the Merits

(1) After all submitted evidence has been examined, the court ascertains the opinion of the parties regarding the possibility of completing the examination of the case on the merits.

(2) If it is not necessary to examine additional evidence, the court ascertains whether the plaintiff maintains the claim and whether the parties wish to conclude a settlement.

(3) If the plaintiff does not withdraw the claim and the parties do not wish to conclude a settlement, the court declares the examination of the case on the merits completed and proceeds to court debates.

#### 184.pants. Court Debates

(1) In court debates, the plaintiff or their representative speaks first, followed by the defendant or their representative. A prosecutor, a representative of state or local government institutions, and a person who has applied to court to defend the rights and legally protected interests of other persons, speak first in court debates.

(2) If a third party with independent claims to the subject matter of the dispute participates in the case, such person or their representative speaks after the parties.

(3) A third party without independent claims to the subject matter of the dispute, or their representative, speaks after the plaintiff or defendant on whose side this third party participates in the case.

(4) A participant in court debates is not entitled to refer in their speech to circumstances and evidence that have not been examined at the court hearing.

(5) The court may interrupt a debate participant if they speak about circumstances that are not relevant to the case.

#### 185.pants. Replies

(1) After the parties referred to in Section 184 of this Law have spoken in debates, each of them is entitled to one reply.

(2) The court may limit the duration of replies.

#### 186.pants. Opinion of Prosecutor

If a prosecutor who has not brought the claim participates in the case, they give an opinion on the merits of the claim after court debates and replies.

#### 187.pants. Court Deliberation

(1) After court debates, as well as replies and the opinion of the prosecutor, the court withdraws to deliberation to render a judgment, having announced this beforehand to those present in the courtroom.

(2) If the court finds that it is not possible to render a judgment at this court hearing, it determines the date when the judgment will be prepared and available in the online system.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003., 14.12.2017. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 188.pants. Resumption of Examination of the Case on the Merits

(1) If during deliberation the court finds it necessary to ascertain new circumstances that are relevant to the case, or to additionally examine existing or new evidence, it resumes examination of the case on the merits.

(2) In such case, the court hearing continues in the procedure provided for in this Chapter.

22.nodaļa

Judgment

#### 189.pants. General Provisions

(1) A court decision by which a case is adjudicated on the merits is rendered by the court in the form of a judgment and announced in the name of the Republic of Latvia.

(2) A judgment is rendered and announced after examination of the case.

(3) A judgment must be lawful and substantiated.

(4) No direct or indirect interference in the rendering of a judgment or influencing of the court is permissible.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 24.07.2003.)

#### 190.pants. Lawfulness and Substantiation of Judgment

(1) When rendering a judgment, the court is guided by norms of substantive and procedural law.

(2) The court bases the judgment on circumstances established by evidence in the case. In the judgment, the court does not reflect information that is a state secret or commercial secret, but indicates that it has reviewed and evaluated such information.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009. un 28.02.2019. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.04.2019.)

#### 191.pants. Procedure for Rendering Judgment

(1) (Izslēgta ar 19.06.2003. likumu.)

(2) Only the judges who are in the composition of the court in the case being examined may be present in the deliberation of judges.

(3) If the judgment is rendered collegially, the presiding judge of the court hearing expresses their opinion last.

(4) The court, when rendering a judgment, adopts all decisions by majority vote. The judgment is signed by all judges.

(5) In a case which a judge examines individually, the judgment is signed by the judge.

(6) After the judgment has been signed, it is not permitted to amend or change it.

(7) (Izslēgta ar 11.11.2021. likumu)

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 192.pants. Observance of the Limits of the Claim

The court renders a judgment on the subject of the claim specified in the claim and on the basis indicated in the claim, without exceeding the limits of the claim.

#### 193.pants. Form and Content of Judgment

(1) A judgment is prepared in writing.

(2) A judgment consists of an introductory part, a descriptive part, a reasoning part, and an operative part.

(3) The introductory part indicates that the judgment is rendered in the name of the Republic of Latvia, as well as the time of rendering the judgment, the name of the court that rendered the judgment, the composition of the court, the secretary of the court hearing, the parties, and the subject matter of the dispute.

(4) The descriptive part indicates the claims of the plaintiff, the counterclaim of the defendant, objections, as well as the essence of the explanations provided by the parties.

(5) The reasoning part indicates the facts established in the case, the evidence on which the court's conclusions are based, and the arguments with which certain evidence is rejected. This part also indicates the regulatory enactments by which the court was guided, and the legal evaluation of the established circumstances of the case, as well as the court's conclusions regarding whether the claim is well-founded or ill-founded.

(6) The operative part indicates the court's decision on full or partial satisfaction of the claim or on its full or partial rejection, separately indicating the claims that are satisfied and those that are rejected, and the essence of the judgment. Furthermore, it indicates to whom and in what amount litigation costs are payable, also indicating the name of the credit institution and the account number to which payment is to be made, the time limit for voluntary execution of the judgment if the court has determined such, the time limit and procedure for appealing the judgment, as well as the date of preparation of the judgment, observing the exceptions provided for in this Law.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 17.02.2005., 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009., 28.05.2015., 22.06.2017. un 14.12.2017. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 15.01.2018. Grozījums par piektās daļas pēdējā teikuma izslēgšanu, kā arī grozījums sestās daļas pēdējā teikumā par vārda "pilna" izslēgšanu un teikuma papildināšanu ar vārdiem "ievērojot šajā likumā paredzētos izņēmumus" stājas spēkā 01.03.2018. Sk. pārejas noteikumu 137. punktu)
