#### 194. pants. Abbreviated Judgment, Its Form and Content

(1) The court shall prepare an abbreviated judgment:

- 1) if the defendant has fully acknowledged the claim and the court grants the claim;
- 2) in the case of a default judgment, if the court grants the claim in full;
- 3) in simplified procedure cases;
- 4) (deleted by the law of 25.10.2018.).
  - (2) The abbreviated judgment shall be prepared in accordance with the requirements of Article 193 of this Law, except for the descriptive part, which shall indicate only the subject matter of the claim, the legal acts followed by the party, as well as the claim, and the reasoning part, which shall indicate only the legal acts followed by the court.
  - (3) The court shall prepare the abbreviated judgment within 14 days.

(As worded by the law of 14.12.2017., with amendments made by the law of 25.10.2018., which enters into force on 28.11.2018.)

#### 195.pants. Judgment on Recovery of a Sum of Money

(1) When rendering a judgment on the recovery of a sum of money, the court shall indicate in the operative part the type of claim and the amount to be recovered, showing separately the principal debt and interest, the time for which interest is awarded, the claimant's right to receive interest for the time until execution of the judgment (date of completion of auction), also indicating the amount thereof, as well as the name of the credit institution and the account number to which payment is to be made, if such is indicated in the statement of claim.

(2) When rendering a judgment on the recovery of a sum of money for payments for management activities in a multi-apartment residential building (management expenses), for payments for services necessary for the maintenance of the building (utility services) or payments to the reserve fund of the apartment owners' community (reserves), the court, in addition to what is mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article, shall separately indicate in the operative part of the judgment these claims and the amount to be recovered separately for each claim, as well as the time period for which each claim is to be satisfied. (As worded by the law of 08.09.2011., with amendments made by the laws of 28.05.2015. and 21.01.2021., which enters into force on 01.03.2021. See points 162 and 163 of the transitional provisions)

#### 196.pants. Judgment on Return of Property in Kind

When rendering a judgment on the return of property in kind, the court shall indicate in the operative part the specific property, and shall also determine that in the event of the absence of the property, its value is to be recovered from the defendant, indicating a specific sum.

#### 197.pants. Judgment Imposing an Obligation to Perform Specific Actions

(1) In a judgment imposing an obligation to perform specific actions, the court shall determine specifically for whom, what actions and within what time limit are to be performed.

(2) When rendering a judgment that imposes on the defendant an obligation to perform specific actions that are not related to the transfer of property or a sum of money, the court may indicate in the judgment that if the defendant does not execute the judgment within the specified time limit, the claimant is entitled to perform these actions at the defendant's expense, subsequently recovering from him the necessary expenses.

#### 198.pants. Judgment in Favour of Several Claimants or Against Several Defendants

(1) In a judgment in favour of several claimants, the court shall indicate what part of the judgment applies to each of them, or that the rights of recovery are joint and several.

(2) In a judgment against several defendants, the court shall indicate what part of the judgment is to be executed by each of them, or that their liability is joint and several.

#### 199. pants. Pronouncement of Judgment

(1) A judgment shall be pronounced at a court hearing by reading out its introductory part and operative part, but in the case referred to in the second paragraph of Article 187 of this Law, the court shall set a date within the next 30 days when the judgment will be available in the online system. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be deemed to be the date of pronouncement of the judgment.

(2) If the judgment is pronounced at a court hearing, the judge shall explain the procedure and time limits for appealing it.

(3) If the case is heard at a court hearing, the abbreviated judgment shall be pronounced at the court hearing after its preparation by reading out its introductory part and operative part, but in the case referred to in the second paragraph of Article 187 of this Law, the court shall set a date within the next 14 days when the abbreviated judgment will be available in the online system. The date when the abbreviated judgment is available in the online system shall be deemed to be the date of pronouncement of the judgment.

(4) If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach to the online system on the date of pronouncement of the judgment, the judgment shall be available at the court office on the same date. In such a case, the date when the judgment is available at the court office shall be deemed to be the date of pronouncement of the judgment.

(As worded by the law of 14.12.2017., with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 200.pants. Correction of Clerical and Mathematical Calculation Errors

(1) The court may, on its own initiative or upon application by a party, correct clerical and mathematical calculation errors in the judgment. The issue of error correction shall be examined in written proceedings. The parties shall be notified in advance of the examination of the said issue in written proceedings. If the application has been submitted by a party, simultaneously with sending the notification, the court shall send to the parties the application for correction of clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment.

(2) Clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment shall be corrected by a court decision, which shall be sent to the parties within three days of its adoption.

(3) A party may file an ancillary complaint against the decision to make a correction of errors in the judgment.

(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 201.pants. Supplementary Judgment

(1) The court that has rendered a judgment in the case is entitled, on its own initiative or upon application by a party, to render a supplementary judgment if:

- 1) no judgment has been rendered on any of the claims on which the parties have submitted evidence and given explanations;
- 2) the court has not determined the amount awarded, the property to be transferred, the actions to be performed, or compensation for legal costs.
  - (2) The rendering of a supplementary judgment may be initiated within the time limit for appealing the judgment as provided by law.
  - (3) The court shall notify the parties of the time and place of examination of this issue. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to deciding the issue of rendering a supplementary judgment.
  - (4) An ancillary complaint may be filed against the court's decision to refuse to render a supplementary judgment.

#### 202.pants. Clarification of Judgment

(1) The court that has rendered the judgment may, upon application by a party, clarify it by its decision without changing the content of the judgment.

(2) Clarification of the judgment is permissible if it has not yet been executed and the time limit for its enforcement has not expired.

(3) The issue of clarification of the judgment shall be examined in written proceedings, with advance notification to the parties. Simultaneously with the notification, the court shall send to the parties the application for clarification of the judgment.

(4) An ancillary complaint may be filed against the court's decision on the issue of clarification of the judgment.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

#### 203.pants. Entry of a Judgment into Legal Force

(1) A court judgment shall enter into legal force after the time period for appealing it has expired and no appeal has been filed. If the court of appeal has left the appeal without consideration or terminated the appeal proceedings, the judgment shall enter into force from the moment of announcement of the respective decision.

(2) If the judgment is appealed in part, in the non-appealed part the judgment shall enter into force when the time period for appealing it has expired.

(21) If for at least one party the time period for filing an appeal against a first instance court judgment is determined in accordance with Section 415, Paragraph 2.2 of this law, the court judgment shall enter into legal force after the time period for appealing it has expired, counting the time period from the later date of issuance of the judgment, if no appeal has been filed.

(22) If in the cases mentioned in Paragraph 2.1 of this Section no relevant confirmation of issuance of the judgment has been received (Section 56.2), the judgment shall enter into legal force six months after its announcement.

(3) After the judgment has entered into legal force, the parties, as well as their successors in law, are not entitled in another proceeding to contest the facts established by the court, or to bring a new action to court regarding the same subject matter on the same basis, except in cases specified in this law.

(4) If after a judgment has entered into legal force by which periodic payments have been awarded from the defendant, circumstances change that affect the determination of the amount or duration of payments, each party is entitled, by filing a new claim, to request modification of the amount or time period of payments.

(5) A judgment that has entered into legal force has the force of law, it is binding and enforceable throughout the entire territory of the state, and it may be revoked only in cases and in the manner specified by law.

(With amendments made by laws of 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 204.pants. Execution of a Judgment

A judgment shall be executed after it has entered into legal force, except in cases where the judgment is immediately enforceable. 204.1 pants. Voluntary Execution of a Judgment

(1) When rendering a judgment on recovery of a sum of money, on return of property in kind, on eviction of persons and property from premises, and on recovery of litigation costs, the court shall set a time period for voluntary execution of the judgment, except in cases where the judgment is immediately enforceable.

(2) The time period for voluntary execution of a judgment may not be longer than 10 days from the date the judgment enters into force.

(17.02.2005. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 10.03.2005.)

#### 205.pants. Immediately Enforceable Judgments

(1) At the request of a party, the court in the judgment may determine that immediately enforceable, in whole or in a specified part, are judgments:

- 1) on recovery of maintenance for a child or parent;
- 2) on recovery of wages;
- 3) on reinstatement to work;
- 4) on compensation for mutilation or other injury to health;
- 5) on recovery of maintenance in connection with the death of a person who had an obligation to support someone;
- 6) in cases where the defendant has acknowledged the claim;
- 7) in cases where, due to special circumstances, delay in execution of the judgment may cause substantial losses to the creditor or the recovery itself may become impossible;
- 8) in cases arising from guardianship and contact rights.
  - (2) Immediate execution of a judgment in the case provided for in Point 7 of Paragraph one of this Section is permissible only if requiring from the creditor adequate security in case the court of appeal modifies the judgment.
  - (3) In the cases provided for in Points 1 and 8 of Paragraph one of this Section, the court may also on its own initiative determine that the judgment is to be executed immediately, in whole or in a specified part.

(With amendments made by laws of 09.06.2011., 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 206.pants. Postponement of Execution of a Judgment, Division into Installments, Modification of Its Manner or Procedure of Execution

(1) The court that has rendered the judgment in the case is entitled, at the application of a party, taking into account the financial situation of the parties, the rights of children, or other circumstances, to adopt a decision on postponement of execution of the judgment or division into installments, as well as on modification of its manner and procedure of execution. A decision on postponement of execution of a judgment, division into installments, or modification of the manner and procedure of execution is immediately enforceable.

(2) The application shall be examined in written proceedings, with prior notification to the parties. Simultaneously with the notification, the court, setting a time period for submission of an explanation, sends to the parties the application on postponement of execution of the judgment, division into installments, modification of its manner or procedure of execution.

(3) An interlocutory appeal may be filed against the court's decision to postpone execution of a judgment or to divide it into installments, as well as to modify its manner and procedure of execution. Filing of an interlocutory appeal does not suspend execution of the decision.

(With amendments made by laws of 14.12.2006., 08.09.2011. and 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

206.1 pants. Issues of Execution of a Judgment Rendered in the Procedure Provided for in European Parliament and Council Regulation No. 861/2007 and a European Payment Order Rendered in the Procedure Provided for in European Parliament and Council Regulation No. 1896/2006

(1) The court that has rendered a judgment in the procedure provided for in European Parliament and Council Regulation No. 861/2007 or a European payment order in the procedure provided for in European Parliament and Council Regulation No. 1896/2006 is entitled, at the application of the debtor, in the cases provided for in Article 15, Paragraph 2 of European Parliament and Council Regulation No. 861/2007 or Article 23 of European Parliament and Council Regulation No. 1896/2006:

- 1) to substitute execution of the judgment or European payment order with the measures provided for in Section 138 of this law for securing execution of this judgment or European payment order;
- 2) to modify the manner or procedure of execution of the judgment or European payment order;
- 3) to suspend execution of the judgment or European payment order.
  - (2) The application mentioned in Paragraph one of this Section shall be examined in written proceedings, with prior notification to the parties. Simultaneously with the notification, the court, setting a time period for submission of an explanation, sends the application to the parties.
  - (3) An interlocutory appeal may be filed against the court's decision.

(05.02.2009. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 08.09.2011. un 29.10.2015. likumu, kas stājas spēkā

#### 207.pants. Security for Execution of a Judgment

At the application of the parties, the court in the judgment may determine the measures provided for in Section 138 or Chapter 77.3 of this law for securing execution of the judgment.

(With amendments made by laws of 07.09.2006. and 08.12.2016., which enters into force on 04.01.2017. Amendments to the Section in connection with the European Account Preservation Order enter into force on 18.01.2017. See Point 121 of transitional provisions)

#### 208.pants. Sending of a Judgment to the Parties

(1) To a party who has not participated in the court session, the judgment shall be sent not later than within three days after announcement of the judgment.

(2) (Deleted as of 01.03.2018. by the law of 14.12.2017. See Point 137 of transitional provisions)

(3) If in the cases mentioned in Paragraph one of this Section the judgment is to be sent to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law and in cases provided for in this law a translation is to be attached to the judgment, the court shall send the judgment together with the translation immediately after preparation of the translation.

(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force

### 22. nodaļa

Default judgment

(Chapter in the version of 31.10.2002. law, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

208.1 pants. Default judgment

(1) A default judgment is a judgment made by a first instance court in a case where the defendant has not provided an explanation regarding the claim and has not appeared upon the court's summons without notifying the reason for non-appearance.

(2) The court makes a default judgment based on the plaintiff's explanations and the materials in the case, if the court considers them sufficient for resolving the dispute.

(3) A default judgment cannot be made in cases:

- 1) which cannot be terminated by settlement;
- 2) where the defendant's declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is not in the Republic of Latvia;
- 3) where the defendant is summoned to court by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis";
- 4) where there are several defendants and at least one participates in the proceedings.
  - (4) The provisions on default judgment do not apply to special trial proceedings.

(With amendments made by 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

208.2 pants. Form and content of a default judgment

(1) The court makes and prepares a default judgment in the procedure specified in Articles 189-198 of this law, observing the particularities set out in this Article.

(2) The fact that the judgment is a default judgment is indicated in its title.

(3) The descriptive part of a default judgment indicates the plaintiff's claims, the essence of the plaintiff's explanation, the procedural basis for making this judgment, except in cases where the descriptive part of the default judgment is made in accordance with the requirements of paragraph 2 of the first part and the second part of Article 194 of this law.

(4) In the operative part of a default judgment, in addition to what is mentioned in the sixth part of Article 193 of this law, the court indicates that the plaintiff is entitled to appeal the judgment in appellate proceedings, but the defendant within 20 days from the date of sending the default judgment is entitled to submit to the court that made the default judgment an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case.

(With amendments made by 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

208.3 pants. Sending a default judgment to the defendant

A default judgment is sent to the defendant to the official electronic address or by registered mail.

(In the version of 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

208.4 pants. Appeal of a default judgment

(1) The plaintiff is entitled to appeal a default judgment in appellate proceedings.

(2) The defendant is not entitled to appeal a default judgment in appellate proceedings.

208.5 pants. Restoration of proceedings and re-examination of a case

(1) The defendant is entitled within 20 days from the date of sending the default judgment to submit to the court that made the default judgment an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case.

(2) The application indicates:

- 1) the name of the court that made the default judgment;
- 2) the defendant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the defendant agrees to electronic communication with the court, it also indicates the e-mail address and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also includes an indication of registration;
- 21) the name of the credit institution and account number to which litigation costs are to be reimbursed;
- 3) the date and essence of the making of the default judgment;
- 4) the reasons why the defendant has not taken part in the case;
- 5) the defendant's objections to the claim and judgment, justification of objections;
- 6) evidence confirming the objections and their justification, the law on which they are based;
- 7) requests for admission of evidence or its requesting;
- 8) request to restore proceedings in the case and re-examine the case.
  - (3) The following documents are attached to the application confirming:
- 1) payment of state fee and other court costs in the procedure and amount prescribed by law, except in cases where the application is submitted and payment is made in the online system;
- 2) justification of objections.
  - (4) Evidence confirming the circumstances on which the application is based is attached to the application.
  - (5) An unsigned application is considered not submitted and is sent back to the submitter.

(With amendments made by 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 22.06.2017. and 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

208.6 pants. Leaving an application without movement

(1) The judge leaves the application without movement if:

- 1) the application does not contain all the requisites specified in the second part of Article 208.5 of this law;
- 2) the documents specified in the third and fourth parts of Article 208.5 of this law are not attached to the application.
  - (2) Regarding leaving the application without movement, the judge adopts a reasoned decision, which is sent to the defendant, and sets a deadline, not shorter than 20 days, for remedying the deficiencies. The deadline is counted from the date of issue of the decision.

The judge's decision is appealable in the procedure prescribed in this law. The appeal deadline is counted from the date of issue of the decision.

(3) If the defendant has not remedied the deficiencies within the deadline set by the judge, the application is considered not submitted and is returned to the defendant. The decision to return the application is not appealable.

(4) If the application is returned to the defendant, he has no right to re-submit the application to the court.

(With amendments made by 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021. law, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

208.7 pants. Judge's action after acceptance of application

(1) Having found that the application complies with the requirements of Article 208.5 of this law, the judge notifies the plaintiff and third parties of the application and sends them the application. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, documents attached to the claim may also be sent to the plaintiff and third parties.

(2) The judge examines the application within seven days of its receipt and adopts one of the following decisions:

- 1) on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case, if it is found that the examination of the case without the defendant's participation and verification of the evidence submitted by him has led or could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case;
- 2) on rejection of the application, if it is found that there is no basis specified in paragraph 1 of the second part of this Article for re-examination of the case.
  - (3) In the decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case, the judge sets the day and time of the court session and the persons to be summoned and called to court.
  - (4) If a decision has been made on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case and the plaintiff has submitted an appeal against a default judgment, the complaint is returned to the plaintiff.
  - (5) An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding a decision rejecting an application. A decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of a case is not appealable.

(With amendments made by 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022. law, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

208.8 pants. Entry into legal force of a default judgment

(1) A default judgment enters into legal force if an appeal has not been submitted within the period prescribed by law and an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case has not been submitted.

(2) If an application for restoration of proceedings has been rejected and an appeal against the court judgment has not been submitted, the default judgment enters into force after the deadline for appealing the judge's decision has expired.

(3) If the judge's decision on rejection of the application has been appealed and the appellate court has left it unchanged, the default judgment enters into force from the moment of announcement of the appellate court's decision. 208.9 pants. Re-examination of a case

If a decision has been made on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case, the default judgment does not enter into force and the case is re-examined in full in the procedure provided for in Chapter 21 of this law. The restriction prescribed by law for a judge to participate in the re-examination of a case does not apply to this case. 23.nodaļa

Postponement of examination of a case

#### 209.pants. Court's Duty to Postpone Examination of a Case

The court shall postpone the examination of the case:

- 1) if one of the parties to the case does not appear at the court session and he/she has not been notified of the time and place of the court session;
- 2) if one of the parties to the case, who has been notified of the time and place of the court session, does not appear at the court session for a reason which the court recognizes as justifiable;
- 3) if the statement of claim has not been served on the defendant and therefore he/she requests postponement of the examination of the case;
- 4) if it is necessary to invite as a party to the case a person whose rights or interests protected by law may be affected by the court judgment;
- 5) in the case provided for in Article 240 of this Law;
- 6) if the defendant does not appear at the court session, to whom in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 56.2 of this Law a notification of the time and place of the court session has been sent and confirmation of service of the documents has been received (second paragraph of Article 56.2), but the defendant has not received the notification in time;
- 7) if the defendant does not appear at the court session, to whom in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 56.2 of this Law a notification of the time and place of the court session or the statement of claim has been sent, and no confirmation of service of the documents (second paragraph of Article 56.2) or non-service of the documents has been received;
- 8) if the parties' consent to mediation has been received.

(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 22.05.2014. and 11.11.2021., which come into force

#### 210.pants. Court's Right to Postpone Examination of a Case

(1) The court may postpone the examination of the case:

- 1) if the plaintiff, who has been notified of the time and place of the court session, does not appear at the court session for an unknown reason;
- 2) if the defendant, who has been notified of the time and place of the court session, does not appear at the court session for an unknown reason;
- 3) if it recognizes that it is not possible to examine the case because a party to the case whose participation in the examination of the case is mandatory according to law, as well as a witness, expert or interpreter provided by the court, has not appeared;
- 4) at the request of a party to the case, to give him/her the opportunity to submit additional evidence;
- 5) if a person is unable to participate in the court session by videoconference due to technical or other reasons beyond the court's control;
- 6) if the interpreter does not appear at the court session for a reason which the court recognizes as justifiable.
  - (2) For the reason specified in point 1 or 2 of the first paragraph of this Article, the court may postpone the examination of the case no more than once.

(With amendments made by laws of 08.09.2011. and 04.02.2016., which come into force on 29.02.2016. In connection with interpreters, the amendment to point 3 of the first paragraph and the amendment supplementing the first paragraph with point 6 come into force on 31.07.2016. See point 114 of transitional provisions)

#### 211.pants. Decision on Postponement of Examination of a Case

(1) The decision on postponement of the examination of the case shall be recorded in the court session protocol.

(2) When postponing the examination of the case, the court shall indicate all the procedural actions to be carried out before the next court session, as well as determine the day of the next court session. If the court postpones the examination of the case in the case provided for in point 7 of Article 209 of this Law, the next court session shall be determined only after the conditions referred to in Article 22(2) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council or in the second paragraph of Article 15 of the 1965 Hague Convention have been complied with or, if the legal acts referred to in this Article are not applicable, equivalent measures have been taken.

(21) When postponing the examination of the case in the case referred to in point 8 of Article 209 of this Law, the court shall, in the decision on postponement of the examination of the case, set a time limit for the use of mediation, which is not longer than six months, and the parties' obligation to submit evidence to the court on the result of the mediation no later than seven days after the termination of the mediation. The court's decision on postponement of the examination of the case for the use of mediation is not subject to appeal.

(3) The court shall notify the persons who appeared at the court session of the day of the next court session. Persons present shall not be summoned or invited to the court session again.

(4) The decision on postponement of the examination of the case is not subject to appeal, except for a decision in which the day of the next court session has not been determined.

(With amendments made by laws of 08.09.2011., 22.05.2014., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which come into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### 212.pants. Examination of Witnesses When Postponing Examination of a Case

(1) If all parties to the case are present at the court session, the court, when postponing the examination of the case, may examine the witnesses who have appeared.

(2) If necessary, the examined witnesses may be summoned to the next court session.

#### 213.pants. Resumption of Examination of a Case

(Deleted by law of 07.09.2006., which comes into force on 11.10.2006.)

24.nodaļa

Suspension of Proceedings in a Civil Case

#### 214.pants. Court's Duty to Suspend Proceedings

The court shall suspend proceedings if:

- 1) a natural person has died or a legal person who is a party or third person with independent claims in the case has ceased to exist, and if the disputed legal relationship permits succession of rights;
- 2) the court has imposed such a restriction on the legal capacity of a party or third person that does not allow it to independently exercise civil procedural rights and obligations;
- 3) a party or third person is completely unable to participate in the examination of the case due to serious illness, age or disability;
- 4) it adopts a decision on the submission of an application to the Constitutional Court or the Constitutional Court has initiated a case in connection with a constitutional complaint submitted by a party or third person;
- 41) it adopts a decision to refer a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union for a preliminary ruling;
- 5) the examination of the case is not possible until another case to be examined in accordance with the civil procedure, criminal procedure, administrative procedure or administrative offence procedure has been decided;
- 6) (deleted by law of 08.09.2011.);
- 7) the Competition Council is examining a case concerning a competition law infringement related to a claim for damages;
- 8) the Consumer Rights Protection Centre is examining a case concerning consumer rights infringement related to a collective consumer action.

(With amendments made by laws of 20.06.2001., 07.04.2004., 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 19.10.2017., 11.11.2021. and 14.09.2023., which come into force on 15.10.2023.)

#### 215.pants. Court's Right to Suspend Proceedings

The court, at the initiative of a party to the case or on its own initiative, may suspend proceedings if:

- 1) a party or third person with independent claims is outside the borders of Latvia in connection with a long-term business trip or performance of state duties;
- 2) a search for the defendant has been announced;
- 3) a party or third person with independent claims is unable to participate in the examination of the case due to illness;
- 4) the court orders an expert examination;
- 5) there is a mutual agreement between the parties on the suspension of proceedings and the third person with independent claims does not object thereto;
- 6) in claims of a proprietary nature, legal person insolvency proceedings or natural person insolvency proceedings have been declared for the defendant.

(With amendments made by law of 18.04.2013., which comes into force on 22.05.2013.)

#### 216.pants. Periods for Suspension of Proceedings

Proceedings shall be suspended:

- 1) in the cases provided for in Paragraph 1 of Article 214 of this law — until the determination of a successor in title or the appointment of a legal representative;
- 2) in the cases provided for in Paragraph 2 of Article 214 of this law — until the appointment of a legal representative;
- 3) in the cases provided for in Paragraph 3 of Article 214 of this law — until the time limit set by the court for formalisation of representation;
- 4) in the cases provided for in Paragraphs 4, 4.1 and 5 of Article 214 of this law — until a judgment of the Constitutional Court or the Court of Justice of the European Union or a judgment in civil proceedings, criminal proceedings, administrative proceedings or administrative violation proceedings enters into legal force;
- 5) in the cases provided for in Paragraphs 1 to 4 of Article 215 of this law — until the moment when the circumstances mentioned in these paragraphs have ceased;
- 6) in the cases provided for in Paragraph 5 of Article 215 of this law — until the time limit set in the court decision;
- 7) (deleted by law of 08.09.2011);
- 8) in the cases provided for in Paragraph 6 of Article 215 of this law — until the termination of insolvency proceedings of a legal person or insolvency proceedings of a natural person;
- 9) in the case provided for in Paragraph 7 of Article 214 of this law — until the competition authority has adopted a decision or otherwise terminated the examination of the case;
- 10) in the case provided for in Paragraph 8 of Article 214 of this law — until the Consumer Rights Protection Centre has adopted a decision or otherwise terminated the examination of the case.

(With amendments made by laws of 20.06.2001, 07.04.2004, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 18.04.2013, 19.10.2017, 11.11.2021 and 14.09.2023, which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

#### 217.pants. Decision on Suspension of Proceedings

(1) Regarding the suspension of proceedings, the court shall adopt a reasoned decision, which shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document.

(2) The decision shall indicate the circumstances until the occurrence or cessation of which the proceedings are suspended, or the time limit for which the proceedings are suspended.

(3) An appeal may be lodged against the court decision to suspend proceedings.

#### 218.pants. Resumption of Proceedings

(1) Proceedings shall be resumed by the court with a decision on its own initiative or at the request of the participants in the case.

(2) If insolvency proceedings of a legal person or insolvency proceedings of a natural person have been declared against the defendant in claims of a proprietary nature, the court shall resume the suspended proceedings:

- 1) at the request of the creditor, if the insolvency administrator has adopted a decision not to recognise or to recognise in part the creditor's claim, on the ground that there is a dispute over rights;
- 2) if, when examining an appeal against a decision of the insolvency administrator, it has been established that there is a dispute over rights, and within the time limit set by the court a request has been made to resume proceedings.

(With amendments made by law of 18.04.2013, which enters into force on 22.05.2013.)

25.nodaļa

Leaving a Claim Without Consideration

#### 219.pants. Duty of the Court to Leave a Claim Without Consideration

(1) The court shall leave a claim without consideration if:

- 1) the claimant has not complied with the procedure for prior out-of-court examination of the case established for the relevant category of cases or has not taken the measures provided for in law to settle its dispute with the defendant before bringing the claim;
- 2) the claim has been filed by a person who does not have civil procedural capacity;
- 3) the claim has been brought in the name of the claimant by a person who is not authorised to do so in the procedure established by law;
- 4) a dispute in the claim between the same parties, on the same subject-matter and on the same grounds is pending before the same or another court;
- 5) in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia and European Union law, the case does not fall within the jurisdiction of a Latvian court;
- 6) the parties have agreed, in the procedure established by law, on the resolution of the dispute using mediation, except for an employee's claim arising from employment legal relations, and no evidence has been submitted that the proposal to resolve the dispute using mediation has been rejected or that a mediation agreement has not been concluded, or that mediation has ended without reaching an agreement.
  - (2) The court shall leave a claim without consideration in the part for which a European payment order is not issued in the case provided for in Article 10(2) of European Parliament and Council Regulation No 1896/2006.

(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009, 29.11.2012 and 22.05.2014, which enters into force on 18.06.2014.)

#### 220. pants. Right of the Court to Leave a Claim Without Consideration

The court may leave a claim without consideration if:

- 1) the claimant or his or her representative repeatedly fails to appear in court and has not requested that the case be examined in his or her absence;
- 2) a person who is one of the parties to the case has died and within one year from the suspension of proceedings no succession case for that person has been initiated.

(In the version of law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 221.pants. Decision on Leaving a Claim Without Consideration

(1) Regarding leaving a claim without consideration, the court shall adopt a reasoned decision in the form of a separate procedural document.

(2) An appeal may be lodged against a court decision to leave a claim without consideration.

#### 222.pants. Consequences of Leaving a Claim Without Consideration

If a claim has been left without consideration, the claimant is entitled to submit a new claim to the court, observing the procedure established by law.

26.nodaļa

Termination of Proceedings

#### 223.pants. Grounds for Termination of Proceedings

The court shall terminate proceedings in a case if:

- 1) the examination of the case is not subject to the court;
- 2) the claim has been brought by a person who does not have the right to bring a claim;
- 3) a judgment that has entered into legal force has been issued in a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject-matter and on the same grounds, or a court decision by which proceedings have been terminated;
- 4) the claimant has renounced the claim;
- 5) the parties have concluded a settlement and the court has approved it;
- 6) the parties have agreed, in the procedure established by law, on the referral of the dispute for examination to an arbitral tribunal;
- 7) a natural person who is one of the parties to the case has died and the disputed legal relationship does not allow succession of rights;
- 8) a legal person who is one of the parties to the case has ceased to exist and there is no successor to its rights;
- 9) insolvency proceedings of a natural person have been terminated and, in accordance with Article 164 of the Insolvency Law, the natural person has been released from the respective obligations;
- 10) an administrator of insolvency proceedings of a debtor has submitted a request in a claim for the exclusion of that debtor from another company, which has been brought in accordance with Articles 136.1 and 195 of the Commercial Law.

(With amendments made by laws of 18.04.2013 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. Paragraph 10 in the part regarding termination of proceedings in a case if an administrator of insolvency proceedings of a debtor has submitted a request in a claim for the exclusion of that debtor from another company, which has been brought in accordance with Article 136.1 of the Commercial Law, enters into force on 01.07.2023. See transitional provision, Paragraph 180)

#### 224.pants. Decision on Termination of Proceedings

(1) Proceedings shall be terminated by a reasoned court decision, which shall be adopted in the form of a separate procedural document.

(2) An appeal may be lodged against a court decision to terminate proceedings.

#### 225.pants. Consequences of Termination of Proceedings

If proceedings have been terminated, a repeated application to the court in a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject-matter and on the same grounds is not admissible.

27.nodaļa

Settlement

#### 226.pants. Agreement on Settlement

(1) A settlement is admissible at any stage of the proceedings.

(2) A settlement is admissible in any civil dispute, except in the cases provided for in this law.

(3) A settlement is not admissible:

- 1) in disputes relating to amendments to civil status records;
- 2) in disputes relating to proprietary rights of persons under guardianship or curatorship;
- 3) in disputes concerning immovable property, if among the participants there are persons whose rights to acquire immovable property in ownership or possession are restricted in the procedure established by law;
- 4) if the terms of the settlement affect the rights or legally protected interests of other persons.

#### 227.pants. Conclusion of Settlement

(1) The parties conclude the settlement in writing and submit it to the court.

(2) The settlement shall specify:

- 1) the plaintiff's name, surname, personal identification number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; if the plaintiff is a legal entity — its name, registration number and legal address;
- 2) the defendant's name, surname, personal identification number, declared place of residence, additional address (addresses) indicated in the declaration and place of residence, if known, but if the defendant is a legal entity — its name, registration number and legal address;
- 3) the subject matter of the dispute;
- 4) the obligations of each party that it voluntarily undertakes to perform.
  - (3) The court may approve the settlement without the presence of a party at the court session or in written proceedings if the settlement has been made before a notary in the form of a notarial act and it contains a statement by the parties that they are aware of the procedural consequences of approving the settlement.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015. and 04.02.2016., which came into force on 29.02.2016.)

#### 228.pants. Court decision on approval of settlement

(1) Upon receiving the parties' settlement, the court shall ascertain whether the parties have voluntarily agreed on the settlement, whether it complies with the requirements of Articles 226 and 227 of this Law and whether the parties are aware of the procedural consequences of approving the settlement.

(2) If the court acknowledges that the settlement complies with the requirements of this Law, it shall adopt a decision approving the settlement and terminating the proceedings in the case.

(3) A settlement approved by a court decision shall be enforceable in accordance with the rules for the enforcement of court judgments. 28.nodaļa

Court Decision

#### 229.pants. Adoption of decision

(1) A court ruling by which a case is not adjudicated on the merits shall be adopted in the form of a decision.

(2) A decision shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document or entered in the record of the court session and announced after its adoption. In cases provided for in this Law, a decision may be drawn up in the form of a resolution. In such case, only the time and place of adoption of the decision, the name and composition of the court, as well as the court's or judge's ruling shall be indicated.

(3) A court decision shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document in cases provided for in this Law.

(4) A decision on a judge's procedural action outside a court session shall be adopted, which shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document.

(With amendments made by the laws of 15.03.2012., 29.10.2015. and 25.10.2018., which came into force on 28.11.2018.)

#### 230.pants. Form and content of decision

(1) A decision shall consist of an introductory part, a descriptive part, a reasoning part and an operative part.

(2) The introductory part shall indicate the time and place of adoption of the decision, the name and composition of the court, the parties to the case and the subject matter of the dispute.

(3) The descriptive part shall indicate the issues on which the decision has been adopted.

(4) The reasoning part shall indicate the established facts, evidence on which the conclusions and arguments of the court or judge are based, as well as the regulatory enactments by which the court has been guided.

(5) The operative part shall indicate the court's or judge's ruling and the procedure and time limits for appealing the decision.

(6) In decisions that are necessary for the bailiff, additional information shall be provided about the parties to the case [for a natural person

— the plaintiff or applicant — name, surname, personal identification number (if known) and declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a natural person — the defendant — name, surname, personal identification number (if known), declared place of residence, additional address (addresses) indicated in the declaration and place of residence, if known; for a legal entity — name, legal address and registration number].

(In the wording of the law of 29.10.2015., which came into force on 03.12.2015.)

230.1 pants. Abbreviated decision

(1) The court shall draw up an abbreviated decision:

- 1) on granting an application for undisputed enforcement of obligations;
- 2) on granting or partially granting an application for enforcement of obligations in warning procedure
  - with respect to the granted part;
- 3) on approval of a settlement concluded by the parties.
  - (2) An abbreviated decision shall be drawn up in accordance with the requirements of Article 230 of this Law, except for the reasoning part, which shall only indicate the regulatory enactments by which the court has been guided.
  - (3) The abbreviated decision referred to in paragraph 3 of the first part of this Article shall be announced and sent in accordance with Article
    - 231 of this Law.

(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 231.pants. Announcement and sending of decision

(1) The court shall announce the decision at the court session by reading out its introductory part and operative part or by setting a date within the next 14 days when the decision will be available in the online system. The date when the decision is available in the online system shall be deemed to be the date of announcement of the decision. A decision adopted in written proceedings shall be deemed to be drawn up on the date when it is available in the online system. If for technical reasons it is not possible to add to the online system on the date of announcement or drawing up of the decision, the decision shall be available at the court office on the same date. The date of announcement or drawing up of the decision in such case shall be deemed to be the date when the decision is available at the court office.

(2) The court decision shall be sent within three days of the announcement of the decision to a party to the case who has not participated in the court session and to a person to whom it relates. A decision adopted in written proceedings shall be sent within three days of the drawing up of the decision.

(3) If the court decision in the cases referred to in the first and second parts of this Article has been sent to a person in accordance with Article 56.2 of this Law and in cases provided for in this Law a translation is to be attached to the court decision, the court shall send the decision together with the translation immediately after the preparation of the translation.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 29.10.2015., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 232.pants. Ancillary court decision

(1) If, when examining a case, circumstances are established that indicate a possible violation of law, the court shall be entitled to adopt an ancillary decision, which shall be sent to the relevant institution.

(2) An ancillary court decision is not subject to appeal.

### 28. nodaļa

Appeal of Actions of a Sworn Notary

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which came into force on 01.01.2022.)

232.1 pants. Jurisdiction of court over complaints against actions of a sworn notary and procedure for submission

A complaint against the actions of a sworn notary in performing official duties, as well as a complaint against refusal to perform these duties, shall be submitted by a person whose rights have been affected to the district (city) court at the address of the sworn notary's place of practice within 30 days from the day when the sworn notary performed the action against which the complaint has been submitted or when he or she refused to perform such action.

(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which came into force on 01.01.2022.)

232.2 pants. Procedure for examining complaints

(1) The court shall examine the complaint within 30 days from the day of receipt of the complaint.

(2) The court shall examine the complaint in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where it deems it necessary to examine the case at a court session or when the complainant, sworn notary or other interested persons request the case to be examined at a court session, substantiating their request. The complainant, sworn notary and other interested persons shall be invited to the court session. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the matter.

(3) A copy of the decision adopted by the court after examining the complaint shall be sent to the complainant, sworn notary and other interested persons.

(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which came into force on 01.01.2022.)

232.3 pants. Appeal of decisions adopted on complaints

(1) An ancillary complaint may be submitted against a court decision within the time limit and in the procedure established by this Law.

(2) A court decision by which a complaint against the actions of a sworn notary in performing official duties in a case concerning the discharge of a natural person from debt obligations has been examined is not subject to appeal.

(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which came into force on 01.01.2022.)

Piektā sadaļa

Specifics of Examination of Certain Categories of Cases

29.nodaļa

Cases Concerning Non-existence or Dissolution of Marriage

#### 233.pants. Procedure for Examining Cases

Cases on non-existence of marriage or divorce shall be examined by the court in the order of claims according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

#### 234.pants. Jurisdiction of Cases

A claim for non-existence of marriage or divorce may also be filed in court according to the plaintiff's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the plaintiff's place of residence, if:

- 1) the plaintiff has minor children;
- 2) (deleted by the Law of 29.11.2012);
- 3) the marriage is to be dissolved with a person serving a sentence in a place of deprivation of liberty;
- 4) the marriage is to be dissolved with a person who has no declared place of residence and whose place of residence is not known or who lives abroad.

(With amendments made by the Law of 29.11.2012, which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 235.pants. Cases on Divorce by Application of Both Spouses

(Deleted by the Law of 28.10.2010, which comes into force on 01.02.2011.)

235.1 pants. Claim for Divorce In the claim for divorce, in addition to that specified in Article 128 of this Law, the following shall be indicated:

- 1) since when the parties have lived separately;
- 2) whether the other spouse agrees to the divorce;
- 3) whether the parties have agreed on the custody of the child, the procedure for exercising the other parent's contact rights, maintenance and the division of property acquired during the marriage, or file respective claims.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the Law of 19.06.2003, which comes into force on 24.07.2003.)

#### 236.pants. Participation of Parties in Court Session

(1) A divorce case shall be examined with the participation of both parties.

(11) At the request of one spouse, the court may hear each spouse in a separate court session if the divorce is related to violence against the spouse who requests the divorce, or against his or her child, or the spouses' common child.

(2) If the defendant does not appear upon the court's invitation without justifiable reason, if it was sent to the official electronic address or by registered mail, he or she may be brought to court by force.

(3) If one of the parties lives far away or for another reason cannot appear upon the court's invitation, the court may recognize that written explanations of this party or the participation of its representative is sufficient for examining the case.

(4) If the defendant's place of residence is not known or it is not located in Latvia, the case may be examined without the defendant's participation if he or she has been invited to court in the manner prescribed by law.

(5) In a case on divorce or non-existence of marriage, the representative of a party must be specially authorized to conduct this case. The authorization for representation in a divorce or non-existence of marriage case also applies to all other claims related thereto.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the Laws of 19.06.2003, 29.11.2012, 23.11.2016 and 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 237.pants. Filing a Claim for Non-Existence of Marriage

A claim for non-existence of marriage may be filed by interested persons and the prosecutor.

#### 238.pants. Prohibition of Claim Separation

(1) In a case on divorce or non-existence of marriage, claims arising from family legal relations shall be adjudicated simultaneously. Such claims are disputes on:

- 1) determination of custody;
- 2) exercise of contact rights;
- 3) maintenance for a child, including maintenance in the minimum amount determined by the Cabinet of Ministers;
- 4) means for ensuring the previous standard of living of a spouse;
- 5) the common family dwelling and household or personal use items;
- 6) division of spouses' property (also if it affects third parties).
  - (2) (Deleted by the Law of 29.10.2015)
  - (3) (Deleted by the Law of 29.10.2015)
  - (4) (Deleted by the Law of 29.10.2015)
  - (5) (Deleted by the Law of 29.10.2015) (In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the Laws of 07.09.2006, 04.08.2011, 29.11.2012, 29.10.2015 and 08.12.2016, which comes into force on 04.01.2017.)

238.1 pants. Interim Decision on Certain Claims

(1) At the request of a party, the court or judge may adopt a decision temporarily establishing, until the adoption of a judgment on divorce or non-existence of marriage, the child's place of residence, the procedure for child care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, maintenance for the child, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country, means for ensuring the other spouse's previous standard of living, the procedure for using the spouses' common dwelling, or ordering one party to give the other party household and personal use items.

(2) A request for maintenance for a child and means for ensuring the spouse's previous standard of living shall be examined in written proceedings.

(3) A request for the child's place of residence, the procedure for child care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country, the procedure for using the spouses' common dwelling, or an order for one party to give the other party household and personal use items shall be examined in a court session.

(4) The representative of the orphan's court in claims concerning a child (on the child's place of residence, the procedure for child care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country), at the request of the court, shall provide any information that is relevant in the case on:

- 1) the living conditions of the parties;
- 2) the child's opinion, if the child is able to formulate it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity;
- 3) the child's contact with the parties and other persons who live or are known to live with the child in one household;
- 4) the child's health care and education;
- 5) the cooperation of the parties with the social service;
- 6) persons who live or are known to live with the child in one household;
- 7) violence by the parties against the child or the child's parent.
  - (5) The parties shall be notified of the court session, but in claims concerning a child — the representative of the orphan's court shall be invited to the court session.

If the court considers it necessary to clarify the information provided by the orphan's court, it shall ascertain the child's opinion if the child is able to formulate it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity. The non-appearance of the other spouse is not an obstacle to examining the claim.

(6) If in claims on the procedure for exercising contact rights the court, at the request of a participant in the case or on its own initiative, determines that contact rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, the court shall invite the contact person to participate in the court session. The court shall ascertain whether the contact person agrees that contact rights be exercised in its presence.

(7) The court or judge shall examine the request of the party and adopt a decision within one month from the date of receipt of the request. The decision shall be enforceable immediately. The decision shall cease to be valid when the judgment in the case enters into force or when another decision is adopted, except when the ruling is enforceable immediately.

(8) The judge's decision on the claims mentioned in the second part of this Article is not subject to appeal. A collateral complaint may be filed against the court's decision in the case on the claims mentioned in the third part of this Article.

(9) The court, at a reasoned request of a party, may review the decision on the request mentioned in the third part of this Article if circumstances have substantially changed and it is in the interests of the child. Such a court decision is not subject to appeal.

(10) If the court does not determine grounds for reviewing the decision or adopting a new decision, or considers that examination of the case on the merits may be initiated, it shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application. The court shall adopt the decision to refuse to accept the application in the form of a resolution, and it is not subject to appeal.

(In the wording of the Law of 29.10.2015 with amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)
