#### 239.pants. Preparation and hearing of divorce cases

(1) In a divorce or invalidity case, the court on its own initiative requests evidence, especially for deciding questions that concern the child's interests.

(2) In questions regarding the granting of custody rights, child care and the procedure for exercising contact rights, the court requests the opinion of the orphan's court and invites its representative to participate in the court session, and also ascertains the child's opinion if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account their age and degree of maturity.

(3) Divorce cases shall be heard and judgment shall be announced in closed court session. Copies of documents (full text of documents) shall be issued to third parties only if it directly relates to these persons. (In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 04.08.2011. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 240.pants. Postponement of hearing of divorce cases

(1) The court on its own initiative postpones the hearing of the case for the purpose of restoring the spouses' cohabitation or facilitating a peaceful resolution of the case.

(2) The court may not postpone the hearing of the case if the parties have lived separately for more than a year, if both parties object to the postponement of the hearing, or if the divorce is related to violence against the spouse who requests the divorce, or against their child, or the spouses' common child.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force

#### 241.pants. Settlement and reconciliation of parties

(1) In cases of divorce or invalidity, a settlement between the parties is permissible only in disputes related to family legal relations (first part of Article 238).

(2) Withdrawal of a divorce claim or termination of proceedings on divorce is not an obstacle to the examination of other claims on the merits.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 242.pants. Court judgment in divorce cases

When making a judgment in a divorce case, the court:

- 1) decides all claims that arise from family legal relations and for which actions have been brought;
- 2) determines whether the party who changed their surname upon entering marriage is to be granted their premarital surname;
- 3) distributes between the parties the litigation costs, excluding the security deposit, taking into account their financial situation.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 243.pants. Court judgment in cases of invalidity of marriage

When making a judgment on the invalidity of marriage, the court indicates in the judgment:

- 1) the basis for the invalidity of marriage in accordance with Articles 60. — 67. of the Civil Law;
- 2) whether the party who changed their surname upon entering marriage is to be granted their premarital surname or is to retain the marital surname;
- 3) with which parent and which children remain, if there is a dispute about this;
- 4) from which parent and in what amount funds are to be collected for the child's maintenance, if there is a dispute about this.

#### 244. pants. Sending and issuing of judgment

(1) After the judgment regarding the invalidity or dissolution of marriage has entered into legal force, the judgment or an extract from such judgment is sent to the civil registry office where the relevant civil status register is kept, but if the marriage was concluded before a clergyman, — to the respective church (parish clergyman) and to the civil registry office in whose territorial jurisdiction the church (parish) is located.

(2) In a case where the defendant has no declared place of residence and their place of residence is unknown, the court announces the invalidity of marriage in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(3) The court issues to the former spouses the judgment by which the marriage has been dissolved or declared invalid. (With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force

### 29. nodaļa

Cases arising from custody and access rights

(Chapter in the version of the law of 07.09.2006, which enters into force on 11.10.2006.)

Article 244.1 Procedure for hearing cases

The court hears cases arising from custody and access rights in claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

Article 244.2 Filing of a claim

(1) A claim in cases arising from custody rights may be filed by the child's parents, guardians, the orphan's court or the prosecutor.

(2) A claim in cases arising from access rights may be filed by the persons specified in Article 181 of the Civil Law, as well as the prosecutor or the orphan's court.

(3) In cases arising from access rights, the claimant in the statement of claim indicates, in addition to what is mentioned in Article 128 of this law:

- 1) the procedure, time and place for exercising access rights;
- 2) if the claimant requests that access rights be exercised in the presence of a contact person — information about the relevant contact person (for natural persons — name, surname, personal identity number and address, for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number).
  - (4) If a claim in a case arising from custody rights is filed in accordance with point 5 of Article 29 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 of 25 June 2019 on jurisdiction, the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial matters and matters of parental responsibility, and on international child abduction (hereinafter — Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111), the claimant shall attach to the statement of claim, in addition to the documents mentioned in Article 129 of this law, the documents mentioned in point 5 of Article 29 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022. Part four enters into force on 01.08.2022. See point 177 of transitional provisions)

Article 244.3 Jurisdiction over cases

(1) A claim in cases arising from custody and access rights is filed in the court according to the child's place of residence.

(11) The child's place of residence in cases arising from custody and access rights is considered to be the declared place of residence of his or her parents. If the declared places of residence of the child's parents are located in different administrative territories, the child's place of residence is considered to be the declared place of residence of the parent with whom he or she lives. If the child's parents or the child do not have a declared place of residence, the child's place of residence is considered to be the place of residence of his or her parents.

(2) If cases arising from custody or access rights are to be heard together with a case on divorce or nullity of marriage, the provisions of Chapter 29 of this law apply.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

Article 244.4 Participation of parties in court hearing

(1) A case arising from custody or access rights is to be heard with the participation of the parties.

(11) If the claim for deprivation of custody rights has been filed by the orphan's court, the case may be heard without the participation of the defendant if he or she has been summoned to court in the manner prescribed by law.

(2) If the defendant fails to appear following the court's summons without justifiable reason, he or she may be brought to court by force.

(3) If one of the parties lives far away or for another reason cannot appear following the court's summons, the court may consider that a written explanation of this party or the participation of its representative is sufficient for hearing the case.

(4) If the defendant's place of residence is not known or is not located in Latvia, the case may be heard without the participation of the defendant if he or she has been summoned to court in the manner prescribed by law.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

Article 244.6 Settlement of parties

(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

Article 244.7 Consequences of court judgment

(Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

Article 244.8 Contact person

(1) A contact person is a participant in the case in cases arising from access rights. A contact person has the following procedural rights and obligations:

- 1) the right to familiarize oneself with the request for the involvement of a contact person to participate in the case;
- 2) the right to participate in a court hearing;
- 3) the right to express consent or objections to being imposed obligations by a ruling;
- 4) the right to receive a court judgment or decision;
- 5) the obligation to appear in court upon the court's summons;
- 6) the obligation to notify in writing in a timely manner of the reasons for which he or she cannot appear at the court hearing, submitting evidence thereof;
- 7) to appeal the court judgment and decision in the part relating to the contact person.
  - (2) A contact person is invited to participate in the case at the initiative of a participant in the case or the court.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

(1) In a case arising from custody or access rights, the court requests evidence on its own initiative or at the request of a participant in the case.

(2) In a case arising from custody or access rights, the court on its own initiative or at the request of a participant in the case requests an opinion from the relevant orphan's court and invites its representative to participate in the court hearing, as well as ascertains the child's view if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity.

(3) If in a case arising from access rights the court at the request of a participant in the case or on its own initiative finds that access rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, the court invites the contact person to participate in the court hearing. The court ascertains whether the contact person consents to access rights being exercised in his or her presence.

(4) Upon commencing the hearing of the case on the merits, the court hears the contact person. The contact person does not participate in the further hearing of the case on the merits.

(5) When hearing cases arising from custody or access rights, the court takes into account, in addition to other circumstances, all instances where the person who wishes to exercise custody or access rights has used violence against the child or the child's parent. When hearing cases arising from custody rights, the court takes into account, in addition to other circumstances, violations of the procedure for exercising access rights established by it.

(6) The court in cases provided for in international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia or in European Union law, on its own initiative or at the request of a participant in the case, may adopt a decision on taking over a case for hearing in Latvia or transferring a case for hearing to a court in another country if the court of the relevant country has consented to transfer or take over international jurisdiction in the respective case.

(7) (Deleted by the law of 16.06.2022)

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015 with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

Article 244.10 Interim decision

(1) At the request of a party, the court or judge shall adopt a decision establishing, temporarily until the judgment is issued, the child's place of residence, the procedure for caring for the child, the procedure for exercising access rights, maintenance for the child, a prohibition on taking the child out of the country.

(2) A request for maintenance for the child shall be examined in written proceedings.

(3) A request for the child's place of residence, the procedure for caring for the child, the procedure for exercising access rights, a prohibition on taking the child out of the country shall be examined at a court hearing.

(4) A representative of the orphan's court at the court's request shall provide any information relevant to the case on:

- 1) the living conditions of the parties;
- 2) the child's view, if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity;
- 3) the child's contact with the parties and other persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;
- 4) the child's health care and education;
- 5) the cooperation of the parties with the social service;
- 6) persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;
- 7) violence by the parties against the child or the child's parent.
  - (5) The parties are notified of the court hearing and a representative of the orphan's court is invited to the court hearing. If the court considers it necessary to clarify the information provided by the orphan's court, it ascertains the child's view if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity. The failure of the other party to appear is not an obstacle to hearing the matter.
  - (6) If in claims concerning the procedure for exercising access rights the court at the request of a participant in the case or on its own initiative finds that access rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, it invites the contact person to participate in the court hearing. The court ascertains whether the contact person consents to access rights being exercised in his or her presence.
  - (7) The court or judge shall examine the party's request and adopt a decision within one month from the date of receipt of the request.

The decision is enforceable immediately. The decision loses force when the judgment in the case enters into force or when another decision is adopted, except in cases where the ruling is enforceable immediately.

(8) A judge's decision on the claim mentioned in part two of this article is not subject to appeal. An interlocutory appeal may be filed against a court decision in a case concerning the claims mentioned in part three of this article.

(9) The court at the reasoned request of a party may review the decision on the request mentioned in part three of this article if circumstances have changed significantly and it is in the interests of the child. Such court decision is not subject to appeal.

(10) If the court does not find grounds for reviewing the decision or adopting a new decision or considers that it may commence hearing the case on the merits, it adopts a decision refusing to accept the application. The court adopts the decision refusing to accept the application in the form of an endorsement, and it is not subject to appeal.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 244.11 Settlement of parties

(1) In cases arising from custody and access rights, the parties are entitled to conclude a settlement.

(2) The settlement is to be approved by the court requesting on its own initiative an opinion from the relevant orphan's court or inviting its representative to participate in the court hearing.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

Article 244.12 Court ruling in cases arising from custody and access rights

(1) In cases arising from access rights, in addition to what is specified in Article 193 or Article 230 of this law, the court ruling indicates:

- 1) information about the child — name, surname, personal identity number and place of residence;
- 2) the procedure, time and place for exercising access rights;
- 3) if necessary, the obligations of the parties and the division of expenses between the parties for exercising access rights;
- 4) if necessary, the restrictions mentioned in Article 182 of the Civil Law;
- 5) if necessary, other obligations of the parties.
  - (2) In cases arising from custody rights, in addition to what is specified in Article 193 or Article 230 of this law, the court ruling indicates information about the child — name, surname, personal identity number and place of residence.
  - (3) In cases arising from custody and access rights, the court in the ruling warns the parties that if the judgment is not complied with voluntarily, a fine will be imposed in accordance with this law, the matter of suspension or deprivation of custody rights will be decided and the party will be liable under the Criminal Law for malicious non-compliance with the ruling.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

Article 244.13 Claims arising from the impossibility of enforcement of a ruling on the exercise of access rights

(1) If the bailiff in accordance with Article 620.27 of this law establishes that enforcement of the ruling is not possible, the judgment creditor may request the court to review the time and place for exercising access rights established in the ruling.

(2) The request mentioned in part one of this article is submitted to the court that issued the ruling in the case arising from access rights, or in whose area of operation the ruling is to be enforced, if enforcement of a foreign court ruling is not possible.

(3) The court requests from the orphan's court, which in accordance with Article 620.26 of this law has assessed the debtor's conduct, information about the child's daily routine.

(4) The court, having received information that it is not possible for the orphan's court to ascertain the child's daily routine because the child's whereabouts are not known, adopts a decision on searching for the child or the debtor and the child with the assistance of the police.

(5) The request for review of the time and place for exercising access rights shall be examined at a court hearing, notifying the participants in the case in advance thereof. The failure of the other party to appear is not an obstacle to examining the application.

(6) The court on its own initiative or at the request of interested persons shall request that the bailiff who in accordance with Article 620.27 of this law has established that enforcement of the ruling is not possible provide information about the circumstances established in the enforcement case, including obstacles to enforcing the ruling.

(7) The court invites a representative of the orphan's court to participate in the court hearing, as well as a psychologist if the orphan's court has involved one or if the court considers it necessary.

(8) If the court at the request of a participant in the case or on its own initiative finds that access rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, it invites the contact person to participate in the court hearing. The court ascertains whether the contact person consents to access rights being exercised in his or her presence.

(9) The court adopts a ruling on review of the time and place for exercising access rights within one month, unless exceptional circumstances make it impossible. The decision is enforceable immediately.

(10) The court, having found that there are circumstances that hinder the enforcement of the ruling or make it impossible, in the ruling on review of the time and place for exercising access rights may establish a different procedure for exercising access rights in the interests of the child.

(11) If the exercise of access rights is not possible otherwise than by entering premises and it is foreseeable that the bailiff will not be admitted to premises about which there is information that the child is located therein, the court in the ruling on review of the time and place for exercising access rights may indicate in the interests of the child that the premises are to be opened by force. In such case, the court in the ruling indicates the address of the relevant premises and the time period during which the premises may be opened by force.

(12) If the court in the ruling on review of the time and place for exercising access rights has indicated in the interests of the child that the premises are to be opened by force, the ruling shall be pronounced in the absence of the defendant, and the ruling shall be sent to the defendant after the time period indicated in the ruling for opening the premises by force has passed.

(13) If the court finds that circumstances have changed so significantly that it is not possible to adopt a ruling on review of the time and place for access rights established in the judgment, the court shall reject the judgment creditor's request and inform the judgment creditor of his or her right to file a new claim in court in the general procedure. A change in the time and place for exercising access rights shall not be considered a significant change of circumstances if access rights are maintained in the previous scope.

(14) A ruling on review of the time and place for exercising access rights is not subject to appeal. An interlocutory appeal may be filed against a court decision rejecting the judgment creditor's request for review of the time and place for exercising access rights established in an interim decision.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015 with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

Article 244.14 Consequences of court judgment

If after a judgment in a case arising from custody or access rights has entered into legal force circumstances change, each party is entitled to file a new claim in court in the general procedure.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 30. Chapter

Cases on Determination of Child's Origin

(Chapter in the version of the law of 19.06.2003., which enters into force on 24.07.2003.)

#### 245. Section. Procedure for Hearing Cases

Cases on determination of child's origin or challenging of paternity are heard by the court according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

#### 246. Section. Persons Who May Challenge the Presumption of Paternity

(1) The presumption of paternity may be challenged in court by the child's mother, the child's mother's husband, and the child himself/herself after reaching the age of majority.

(2) After the death of the child's mother's husband, such a claim may be brought by the husband's parents if the husband had not known about the child's birth until the moment of death.

(3) After the death of the child's mother's husband, his legal heirs may enter into the proceedings initiated by him as successors of rights.

(4) If the presumption of paternity has been challenged by a person for whom guardianship has been established, a representative of the orphan's court is invited to participate in the case.

(5) The claim referred to in this Section may be brought in accordance with the provisions of Section 149 of the Civil Law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006. and 29.11.2012., which enter into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 247. Section. Persons Who May Challenge the Acknowledgment of Paternity

(1) Paternity that has been acknowledged and registered in the civil registry office may be challenged by the person who acknowledged paternity, the child's mother, or a person who considers himself to be the child's father.

(2) The child himself/herself may bring such a claim after reaching the age of majority.

(3) After the death of the child's father, his legal heirs may enter into the proceedings initiated by him as successors of rights.

(4) Paternity that has been determined by a court judgment that has entered into legal force cannot be challenged.

(5) The claim referred to in this Section may be brought in accordance with the provisions of Section 156 of the Civil Law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 22.05.2014., which enter into force on 18.06.2014.)

#### 248. Section. Persons Who May Bring a Claim for Determination of Paternity

(1) A claim to determine the child's paternity in court may be brought by the child's mother or the child's guardian, as well as the child's biological father.

(2) The child himself/herself may bring such a claim after reaching the age of majority.

(3) The claim referred to in this Section may be brought in accordance with the provisions of the first part of Section 158 of the Civil Law.

#### 249. Section. Procedure for Bringing a Claim for Determination of Child's Paternity

(1) The child's mother, the child himself/herself, or his/her guardian may bring a claim for determination of paternity against the person from whom the child originates.

(2) The person from whom the child originates may bring a claim for determination of paternity against the child's mother in the case where she does not consent to the determination of paternity or there exist other obstacles specified in the law for making a paternity entry in the birth register.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 07.09.2006.)

(4) Claims for challenging the presumption of paternity and for determination of paternity may be joined.

(With amendments made by the law of 07.09.2006., which enters into force on 11.10.2006.)

249.1 Section. Expert Examination

(1) The court, at the request of a party to the case, appoints an expert examination for determination of the child's biological origin.

(2) If any of the parties to the case evades the expert examination, the court adopts a decision on the forced delivery of this person for carrying out the forensic expert examination.

249.2 Section. Establishment of the Fact of Paternity

If the person from whom the child originates has died, the fact of paternity may be established in special court proceedings.

249.3 Section. Interim Decision

(1) At the request of a party, the court or judge adopts a decision prohibiting the removal of the child from the country for a period until the judgment is issued in the case on determination of the child's origin.

(2) The request for prohibition of removal of the child from the country is heard at a court session.

(3) The representative of the orphan's court, upon the court's request, provides information on the child's opinion if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his/her age and degree of maturity, and other evidence that is relevant to the case.

(4) Notice of the court session is given to the parties and a representative of the orphan's court is invited to the court session. If the court considers it necessary to clarify the information provided by the orphan's court, it ascertains the child's opinion if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his/her age and degree of maturity. The non-appearance of the other party is not an obstacle to hearing the matter.

(5) The court or judge hears the party's request and adopts a decision within one month from the date of receipt of the request. The decision is enforceable immediately. The decision loses force if another decision or judgment is adopted in the relevant claim.

(6) An appeal may be filed against the court's decision in the mentioned claim.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

249.4 Section. Opinion of the Orphan's Court

In a case on challenging the acknowledgment of paternity, the court, on its own initiative or at the request of interested persons, requests the opinion of the relevant orphan's court and may invite its representative to participate in the court session.

(In the version of the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

#### 250. Section. Sending and Issuing of Court Judgment

The court judgment on determination of paternity, establishment of the fact of paternity, and recognition of the paternity entry as invalid is sent by the court for amendment of the entry to the civil registry office where the child's birth was registered.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 30. nodaļa

Cases concerning the division of inheritance

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 31.10.2002, which comes into force on 01.01.2003.)

250.1 pants. Jurisdiction

(1) An application for a claim concerning the division of inheritance, if the heirs do not agree on it at home or with a notary, shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of one heir, but if there is none — according to the place of residence, but if the inheritance includes immovable property — according to its location.

(2) In an application concerning the division of inheritance, it shall be indicated which property included in the inheritance is subject to division and which heirs claim it.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

250.2 pants. Actions of the judge in the preparation of the case

(1) The judge sets a preparatory hearing, of which the parties are notified.

(2) According to the judge's decision, a notation of securing the claim or interim protection shall be made in the Land Register in accordance with the provisions on securing the claim or interim protection.

(3) The judge may instruct the notary who issued the certificate of inheritance or the European Certificate of Succession, or another notary practicing in the court district, to supervise the course of preparation of the inheritance division project.

(With amendments made by the laws of 28.05.2015 and 25.03.2021, which comes into force on 20.04.2021.)

250.3 pants. Preparation of the inheritance division project

(1) The notary who has received the task to supervise the course of preparation of the inheritance division project, if necessary, invites the bailiff to prepare an inventory act of the inherited property and to carry out the valuation of the property.

(2) The inventory of inherited property takes place in accordance with the provisions of this law. The inventory act also indicates known debts, obligations and entries in the Land Register that encumber the inheritance.

(3) The notary carries out actions to bring the parties' views closer together and to reach an agreement.

(4) The persons who prepare the inheritance division project, in their opinion, indicate what reasoning they have taken into account.

(5) The notary submits the property inventory act, the property valuation and the inheritance division project to the judge.

250.4 pants. Actions of the judge after receiving the inheritance division project

(1) The court sends the documents submitted by the notary to the co-heirs and sets a deadline for providing explanations.

(2) In addition to written explanations, the judge may invite all co-heirs to verify the calculations and to clarify the inheritance division project.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.5 pants. Sale of divisible property at auction

(1) Property is valued and sold at auction according to the general provisions of this law. If all heirs and, in relevant cases, also the orphan's court (Articles 280—283 of the Civil Law) agree to it, the property may be sold at a free price.

(2) The sale of immovable property to determine its true value shall be carried out according to the provisions on voluntary sale at auction through judicial procedure, observing the provisions of Articles 737 and 738 of the Civil Law, moreover, immovable property is inventoried and valued only if any of the co-heirs requests it.

(With amendments made by the law of 07.09.2006, which comes into force on 11.10.2006. See transitional provisions.)

250.6 pants. State fee in property division cases

In property division cases, the state fee is divided among the heirs, taking into account the value of the property allocated to each.

250.7 pants. Division of common property

The provisions of this chapter also apply to the division of all kinds of common property, observing the provisions of the relevant laws in such division.

### 30. nodaļa

Cases on Intellectual Property Rights Violations and Protection

(Chapter in the version of the law of 14.12.2006, which enters into force on 01.03.2007.)

250.8 pants. Procedure for Examination of Cases

Cases on intellectual property rights violations and protection shall be examined by the court in proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

250.9 pants. Persons Who May Submit an Application Regarding Intellectual Property Rights Violations and Protection

An application regarding intellectual property rights violations and protection may be submitted by persons specified in law.

250.10 pants. Basis and Means for Establishing Provisional Protection

(1) If there is reason to believe that the rights of an intellectual property rights holder are being violated or could be violated, the court, upon a reasoned application of the plaintiff, may adopt a decision on establishing a provisional protection measure. The application for establishing a provisional protection measure shall specify the provisional protection measure.

(2) It is permissible to examine the question of establishing a provisional protection measure at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before filing a claim in court.

(3) Provisional protection measures are:

- 1) seizure of movable property with which intellectual property rights are possibly being violated;
- 2) obligation to recall goods with which intellectual property rights are possibly being violated;
- 3) prohibition to perform certain actions both for the defendant and for persons whose services are used to violate intellectual property rights, or persons who make such a violation possible.

250.11 pants. Establishment of a Provisional Protection Measure Before Filing a Claim

(1) Within three months from the day when the prospective plaintiff learned of the violation or possible violation, he or she may request that a provisional protection measure be established before filing a claim in court.

(2) When submitting an application for establishing a provisional protection measure before filing a claim, the prospective plaintiff shall provide evidence confirming his or her intellectual property rights that are being violated, and evidence that they are being violated or could be violated.

(3) The application for establishing a provisional protection measure before filing a claim shall be submitted to the court where the claim is to be filed.

(4) When granting the application for establishing a provisional protection measure before filing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for the plaintiff to file the statement of claim in court, not longer than 30 days.

250.12 pants. Examination of the Question of Establishing a Provisional Protection Measure

(1) The application for establishing a provisional protection measure shall be decided by the court or judge within 10 days after receiving the application or initiating the case, if the application is submitted simultaneously with filing the claim.

(2) If delay could cause irreversible harm to the intellectual property rights holder, then the application for establishing a provisional protection measure shall be decided by the court or judge no later than the next day after receiving the application, without prior notice to the defendant and other participants in the case. If the decision on establishing a provisional protection measure is adopted without the presence of the defendant or other participants in the case, the defendant and other participants in the case shall be notified of this decision no earlier than on the third day after adoption of the decision.

(3) When granting the application for establishing a provisional protection measure before filing a claim, the court or judge may require the plaintiff to secure the losses that could arise for the defendant or other persons mentioned in paragraph 3 of Section 250.10(3) of this law in connection with establishing the provisional protection measure, by depositing a specified sum of money in the bailiff's deposit account or providing an equivalent guarantee.

(4) The court, upon the plaintiff's application, may replace the established provisional protection measures with other measures.

(5) Provisional protection measures may be revoked by the same court upon application of a participant in the case.

(6) When dismissing the claim, the court shall revoke the provisional protection measure in the judgment. The provisional protection measure shall be in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.

(7) If the claim is left without examination or the proceedings are terminated, the court shall revoke the provisional protection measure in the decision. The provisional protection measure shall be in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.

(8) If the decision on establishing a provisional protection measure is adopted before filing a claim and the claim is not filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge, upon receiving the application of the prospective plaintiff or other prospective participant in the case or the defendant, shall adopt a decision on revoking the provisional protection measure.

(9) The applications mentioned in paragraphs one, four and five of this Section shall be decided at a court hearing, with prior notice to the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.13 pants. Appeal of Decisions Adopted Regarding Establishing Provisional Protection Measures

(1) An interlocutory complaint may be submitted regarding the decisions mentioned in Section 250.12(4) of this law, a decision by which an application for establishing a provisional protection measure has been rejected, and a decision by which an application for revoking a provisional protection measure has been rejected.

(2) If the decision on establishing a provisional protection measure is adopted without the presence of a participant in the case, the time limit for submitting an interlocutory complaint shall be calculated from the day of issuance of the decision.

(With amendments made by the law of 04.08.2011, which enters into force on 01.10.2011.)

250.14 pants. Enforcement of the Decision on Establishing a Provisional Protection Measure

(1) The decision on establishing a provisional protection measure (Section 250.12(1) and (2)) and the decision on revoking a provisional protection measure (Section 250.12(5)) shall be enforceable immediately after its adoption.

(2) The decision on establishing a provisional protection measure that is adopted with the condition mentioned in Section 250.12(3) of this law shall be enforceable after the plaintiff has deposited the sum specified by the court or judge in the bailiff's deposit account or has submitted an equivalent guarantee. The enforcement document shall be issued after payment of the sum specified by the court or receipt of the equivalent guarantee.

(3) The decision on establishing a provisional protection measure by seizing movable property with which intellectual property rights are possibly being violated shall be enforced in the procedure specified in Chapter 71 of this law.

(4) The decision on establishing a provisional protection measure by establishing a prohibition to perform specific actions or an obligation to recall goods with which intellectual property rights are possibly being violated shall be enforced by the bailiff and shall notify the defendant or the relevant third party of the court decision in the procedure specified in Section 555 of this law.

(5) The revocation of the applied provisional protection measure shall be enforceable pursuant to the order of the bailiff who enforced the decision on establishing the provisional protection measure.

(6) The decision on replacement of a provisional protection measure shall be enforced by the bailiff, first by applying the replacement provisional protection measure and then by revoking the replaced provisional protection measure.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.15 pants. Compensation for Losses Caused by a Provisional Protection Measure

The defendant is entitled to claim compensation for losses incurred in connection with establishing a provisional protection measure if the provisional protection measure has been revoked in the case specified in Section 250.12(8) of this law, if the claim filed against him or her has been dismissed, left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated in the cases specified in paragraphs 2 and 4 of Section 223 of this law.

250.16 pants. Right to Information

(1) In cases on intellectual property rights violations, upon a reasoned request of the plaintiff, the court, observing the rights of the participants in the case to protection of trade secrets, may request that information about the origin and distribution of goods or services be provided by the defendant or a person:

- 1) who possesses infringing goods (counterfeit copies) on a commercial scale;
- 2) who has provided or used services on a commercial scale in connection with unlawful use of intellectual property objects;
- 3) about whom the persons mentioned in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this paragraph have provided information that he or she is involved in the production, distribution or offering of infringing goods (counterfeit copies) or in the provision or offering of services related to the unlawful use of intellectual property objects.
  - (2) The information mentioned in paragraph one of this Section shall specify information about the manufacturer, distributor, supplier, wholesaler and retailer of the relevant goods or the provider and distributor of the relevant services [for a natural person - name, surname, personal identity number (if known) and declared place of residence and place of residence if it differs, for a legal person - name, legal address and registration number (if known)], information about the quantity of goods produced, distributed, received or ordered or services provided or ordered, as well as the price paid for them.
  - (3) If there is clear evidence of an intellectual property violation and the intellectual property rights holder has requested the application of securing of evidence, securing of the claim or establishing a provisional protection measure provided for in this law, then the intellectual property rights holder is entitled to request that the information mentioned in paragraphs one and two of this Section also be secured before filing a claim in court within the framework of the procedure for securing evidence provided for in this law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011 and 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

250.17 pants. Court Judgment in Intellectual Property Rights Violation and Protection Cases

(1) If the fact of violation is proven, the court may establish one or more of the following measures in the judgment:

- 1) cease and prohibit unlawful use of the intellectual property object;
- 2) cease and prohibit measures that are considered to be preparation for unlawful use of intellectual property objects;
- 3) cease and prohibit the provision of services that are used for unlawful actions with intellectual property objects, to persons:
  - a) whose services are used to violate the rights of intellectual property holders,
  - b) who make such a violation possible;
- 4) compensate for the losses and non-pecuniary harm caused in connection with the unlawful use of the intellectual property object in the procedure specified by law.
  - (2) The court, upon the plaintiff's application, regardless of the harm caused to the plaintiff and compensation for harm, may establish one or more of the following measures, which shall be carried out at the infringer's expense:
- 1) recall or completely withdraw from commerce the infringing goods (counterfeit copies);
- 2) destroy the infringing goods (counterfeit copies);
- 3) recall or completely withdraw from commerce or destroy devices and materials that were used or intended for the production of infringing goods (counterfeit copies), if their owner knew or from the circumstances of the case should have known that these devices and materials were used or intended for the performance of unlawful actions;
- 4) publish information about the judgment, including publishing the court judgment in full or in part in mass media.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 30. Chapter

Consideration of certain categories of cases in written proceedings

### (Chapter 08.

As worded by the law of 09.2011, which came into force on 30.09.2011. Title of the chapter as worded by the law of 10.12.2015, which came into force on 01.01.2016.)

Section 250.18. Procedure for Hearing Cases

(1) The court shall hear simplified procedure cases and cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board in claim proceedings according to the general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(2) The provisions of this chapter shall not affect the application of Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council, except in the case specified in the second paragraph of Section 250.27 of this Law.

(3) Cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall be heard by Riga City Court.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.03.2014, 10.12.2015, 14.12.2017 and 16.06.2022, which came into force on Section 250.19. Initiation of Cases

(1) Initiation and hearing of simplified procedure cases in the procedure provided for in this chapter shall be permitted only in claims for recovery of money and recovery of maintenance (clauses 1 and 3 of the first paragraph of Section 35).

(2) The judge shall initiate a simplified procedure case on the basis of a written claim, if the principal debt or — in a claim for recovery of maintenance — the total sum of payments on the day of submission of the claim does not exceed 2500 euros. The total sum of payments in claims for recovery of maintenance shall apply to each child separately.

(21) The court shall initiate a case for recovery of maintenance for a child if:

- 1) the amount of the claim does not exceed the amount in which maintenance is paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, and there exist the obstacles referred to in the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Law which prevent a person from receiving maintenance from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund;
- 2) the amount of the claim exceeds the amount in which maintenance is paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund.
  - (3) Cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall be initiated on the basis of a written claim.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.09.2013, 10.12.2015, 08.12.2016, 14.12.2017 and 10.12.2020, which came into force on 31.12.2020. Amendments to the second paragraph and paragraph 2.1 came into force on 01.01.2021. See transitional provision 160)

Section 250.20. Content of the Claim

(1) The claim in the simplified procedure shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) In the claim, in addition to what is specified in Section 128 of this Law, it shall be indicated whether the claimant requests a hearing of the case in a court session, substantiating his or her request.

(3) In the claim in cases in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board, it shall be indicated how the incorrectness of the decision of the Industrial Property Appeal Board manifests itself.

(4) The respective decision of the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall be attached to the claim in cases in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board. Evidence submitted to the Industrial Property Appeal Board need not be attached to the claim.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015, 10.12.2015, 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which came into force on Section 250.21. Sending the Claim and Documents Attached Thereto to the Defendant

(1) Simultaneously with sending the claim in the simplified procedure to the defendant, an explanation form shall be sent, setting a time limit of 30 days for submitting a written explanation, calculated from the day when the claim in the simplified procedure was sent to the defendant. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the claim may also be sent to the defendant.

(2) The court shall additionally inform the defendant that failure to submit an explanation is not an obstacle to rendering a judgment in the case, as well as that the defendant may request a hearing of the case in a court session.

(With amendments made by the laws of 10.12.2015, 14.12.2017, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which came into force on Section 250.22. Explanation of Procedural Rights to the Parties

(1) Simultaneously with sending documents to the parties (Section 148), the court shall explain to them the procedural rights, inform them of the composition of the court that will hear the case, and explain the right to challenge a judge.

(2) The civil procedural rights referred to in this Law which are related to the preparation of a case for hearing may be exercised by the parties no later than seven days before the notified time for hearing the case (first paragraph of Section 250.25). Section 250.23. Defendant's Explanation

(1) The explanation concerning the claim in the simplified procedure shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) In the explanation, the defendant shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the explanation has been submitted;
- 11) the claimant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and, if there is none, place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;
- 12) the defendant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration and, if there is none, place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;
- 13) an e-mail address for communication with the court and, if he or she has registered his or her participation in the online system, also includes an indication of the registration, if the defendant (or his or her representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia) agrees to electronic communication with the court. If the defendant's representative's address is outside Latvia, an e-mail address shall additionally be indicated or notification given of the registration of his or her participation in the online system;
- 14) the name of the credit institution and account number to which litigation costs are to be reimbursed;
- 2) (deleted by the law of 29.11.2012);
- 3) the case number and subject-matter of the claim;
- 4) whether he or she acknowledges the claim in full or in part;
- 5) his or her objections to the claim and the grounds therefor, as well as the legal act on which they are based;
- 6) evidence confirming his or her objections to the claim;
- 7) requests for obtaining evidence;
- 8) whether he or she requests reimbursement of court costs;
- 9) whether he or she requests reimbursement of costs related to the conduct of the case, indicating the amount thereof and attaching documents substantiating the amount;
- 10) whether he or she requests a hearing of the case in a court session, substantiating his or her request;
- 11) other circumstances which he or she considers important in the hearing of the case;
- 12) other requests;
- 13) a list of documents attached to the explanation;
- 14) the time and place of drawing up the explanation.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 29.10.2015, 10.12.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017, 22.06.2017, 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 250.24. Filing of a Counterclaim

(1) The defendant shall have the right to file a counterclaim within the time limit set for providing an explanation.

(2) The court shall accept the counterclaim (third paragraph of Section 136) and hear the case in the procedure specified in Chapter 30.3 of this Law, if the counterclaim complies with the claim amount specified in Section 250.19 of this Law and is drawn up in accordance with the provisions of Section 250.20 of this Law.

(3) The court shall accept the counterclaim (third paragraph of Section 136), but shall continue to hear the case in claim proceedings according to the general rules, if the claim amount indicated in the counterclaim exceeds the claim amount specified in Section 250.19 of this Law or it is not a claim for recovery of money or recovery of maintenance (clauses 1 and 3 of the first paragraph of Section 35).

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 250.25. Hearing Cases in Written Proceedings, Drawing Up, Sending of Judgment and Request for Drawing Up Judgment

(1) If the court does not hear a simplified procedure case in a court session in accordance with Section 250.26 of this Law, the case shall be heard in written proceedings, notifying the parties in due time of the date when the summary judgment will be available in the online system, as well as informing them of the composition of the court that will hear the case and explaining the right to challenge a judge. The date when the summary judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up the judgment.

(11) If the court does not hear a case in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board in a court session in accordance with Section 250.26 of this Law, the case shall be heard in written proceedings, notifying the parties in due time of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system, as well as informing them of the composition of the court that will hear the case and explaining the right to challenge a judge. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up the judgment.

(2) (Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015)

(21) The court shall draw up a judgment in a simplified procedure case in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law, if a party submits a request in writing for drawing up a judgment. The request shall be submitted to the court within 10 days from the date of drawing up the summary judgment, and the provision of the second sentence of the fourth paragraph of Section 48 of this Law shall not apply to this time limit. The court may also, on its own initiative, in the procedure specified in paragraph 2.3 of this Section, draw up a judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law.

(22) An unsigned request for drawing up a judgment in a simplified procedure case shall be considered not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter. A request for drawing up a judgment submitted after expiry of the time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter. A decision on refusal to accept a request for drawing up a judgment shall not be subject to appeal.

(23) In the case referred to in paragraph 2.1 of this Section, the judgment shall be drawn up within 20 days after expiry of the time limit for submitting a request for drawing up a judgment. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up the judgment.

(3) At a party's written request, the summary judgment or the judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law shall be sent to the party without delay.

(4) (Deleted from 01.03.2018 by the law of 14.12.2017. See transitional provision 137)

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015, 10.12.2015, 14.12.2017, 25.10.2018, 28.02.2019 and 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 250.26. Hearing Cases in a Court Session, Drawing Up, Sending of Judgment and Request for Drawing Up Judgment

(1) The court, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter, shall hear a case in a court session if a substantiated request has been received from a party and the court considers it necessary to hear the case in a court session. The court may also hear a case in a court session on its own initiative. If the court refuses a request to hear a case in a court session, this shall be indicated in the judgment.

(2) When scheduling a simplified procedure case for hearing in a court session, simultaneously with the summons, the court shall notify that in the event that one of the parties fails to appear at the court session, the court shall complete the hearing of the case in that party's absence and shall set a date within the nearest 14 days after the notified court session date when the summary judgment will be available in the online system, and shall also explain the parties' right to submit a request for drawing up a judgment.

(3) In a court session in a simplified procedure case, the court shall set a date for drawing up the summary judgment within the nearest 14 days when the summary judgment will be available in the online system. The date when the summary judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up the summary judgment. The summary judgment shall also indicate the date when the judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law will be available in the online system, if a party has submitted a request for drawing up a judgment.

(4) The court shall draw up a judgment in a simplified procedure case in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law, if a party submits a request in writing for drawing up a judgment. The request shall be submitted to the court within 10 days from the date of drawing up the summary judgment, and the provision of the second sentence of the fourth paragraph of Section 48 of this Law shall not apply to this time limit. The court may also, on its own initiative, in the procedure specified in the sixth paragraph of this Section, draw up a judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law.

(5) An unsigned request for drawing up a judgment in a simplified procedure case shall be considered not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter. A request for drawing up a judgment submitted after expiry of the time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter. A decision on refusal to accept a request for drawing up a judgment shall not be subject to appeal.

(6) If a request for drawing up a judgment in a simplified procedure case has been received, the judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section

193 of this Law shall be drawn up by the court within 20 days after expiry of the time limit specified in the fourth paragraph of this Section. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered the date of drawing up the judgment.

(7) At a party's written request, the summary judgment or the judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law shall be sent to the party without delay.

(As worded by the law of 14.12.2017 with amendments made by the laws of 25.10.2018 and 11.11.2021, which came into force on Section 250.27. Content of the Summary Judgment and Entry into Legal Force of Judgment

(1) In the operative part of the summary judgment, in addition to what is specified in Section 194 of this Law, the court shall indicate that a request for drawing up a judgment may be submitted within 10 days from the date of drawing up the summary judgment, and shall also indicate the date when the judgment will be available in the online system, if a party has submitted a request for drawing up a judgment.

(2) A summary judgment in a simplified procedure case shall enter into legal force after expiry of the time limit for submitting a request for drawing up a judgment and none of the parties has submitted a request for drawing up a judgment. If, following a request for drawing up a judgment, the court draws up a judgment, it shall enter into force in the procedure specified in Section 203 of this Law.

(21) A court judgment in a case in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board shall enter into force in the procedure specified in Section 203 of this Law.

(3) Participants in the case may appeal against a court judgment drawn up in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law by way of appeal within 20 days from the date of drawing up the judgment, if one of the grounds for initiating appeal proceedings specified in Section 440.2 of this Law exists.

(4) A participant in the case to whom the judgment has been sent in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law may appeal against the judgment by way of appeal within 20 days from the date of issue of a copy of the judgment.

(5) In cases concerning rights in respect of which a dispute has been examined by the Industrial Property Appeal Board, the operative part of the judgment shall indicate, in addition to what is specified in the sixth paragraph of Section 193 of this Law, the rights granted, confirmed or denied to a person, or amendments to registration information in accordance with the provisions of legal acts. (As worded by the law of 14.12.2017 with amendments made by the laws of 25.10.2018 and 11.11.2021, which came into force on Section 250.27A. Exception Regarding Availability of Judgment

If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of drawing up the judgment, the judgment shall be available at the court registry on the same date. In such a case, the date when the judgment is available at the court registry shall be considered the date of drawing up the judgment.

(As worded by the law of 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 30. Chapter

Cases on Declaring Invalid Resolutions of General Meetings of Members (Shareholders) of Capital Companies


This excerpt sits under: Issuer: Saeima Published:

### (Chapter 18.

Version of 04.2013. law, which enters into force on 22.05.2013. The provisions of the chapter are not applicable to the examination of claim applications received by the court until 30.06.2013. See transitional provision paragraph 68) Article 250.28. Jurisdiction and procedure for examination

Cases concerning the recognition of capital company members' (shareholders') meeting decisions as invalid are examined by the Commercial Court in the procedure for claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(With amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017 and 01.10.2020, which enter into force on 01.01.2021.)

Article 250.29. Persons who may submit a claim application

A claim application for the recognition of capital company members' (shareholders') meeting decisions as invalid may be submitted by persons specified in law.

Article 250.30. Initiation of a case

Initiation and examination of a case in the procedure provided for in this chapter is admissible in claims against a capital company for the recognition of the following decisions of its members' (shareholders') meeting as invalid:

- 1) decision on changes in the composition of the capital company officials (board, council, liquidator) or in the representation rights of board members;
- 2) decision on changes in the amount of share capital;
- 3) decision on making amendments to the statutes;
- 4) decision on termination of the capital company's activities, reorganisation or conclusion, amendment or termination of a group agreement.

Article 250.31. Content of the claim application

(1) In the claim application, in addition to that specified in Article 128 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

- 1) whether the claimant requests the trial of the case in a court session;
- 2) an address in Latvia for communication with the court to receive court documents, if the claimant's place of residence or location is not in Latvia and the claimant has not agreed to electronic communication with the court.
  - (2) In the application, the claimant may request the establishment of a provisional protective measure (Article 250.35).

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.32. Sending of the claim application and attached documents to the defendant

(1) The time limit for submission of an explanatory statement is 15 days, counted from the day when the claim application was sent to the defendant.

(2) The court informs the defendant that failure to submit an explanatory statement is not an obstacle to making a judgment in the case, and also that the defendant may submit evidence and request the trial of the case in a court session only in the explanatory statement and within the time limit set for its submission.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.33. Explanation of procedural rights to participants in the case

(1) Simultaneously with sending documents to participants in the case (Article 148), the court explains to them their procedural rights, informs them about the composition of the court that will examine the case, and explains the right to challenge a judge.

(2) The civil procedural rights mentioned in this law that are related to the preparation of a case for trial, except for the right to request the trial of a case in a court session, may be exercised by participants in the case no later than seven days before the announced time for examination of the case (Article 250.36, first paragraph).

Article 250.34. Requesting a reply

(1) If the judge deems it necessary, he or she has the right to request a reply from the claimant regarding the explanatory statement, setting a time limit of 15 days for submission of the reply, which is counted from the day when the explanatory statement was sent to the claimant.

(2) In the reply and within the time limit set for its submission, the claimant may request the trial of the case in a court session if such a request was not expressed in the claim application. If the defendant submits an explanatory statement and a reply is not requested, then the claimant may request the trial of the case in a court session no later than seven days before the announced time for examination of the case, if such a request was not expressed in the claim application.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.35. Provisional protective measures

(1) If there is a basis to believe that the claimant's rights are being violated or could be violated, the court or judge, upon a reasoned application by the claimant, may adopt a decision on establishing a provisional protective measure. The application for establishing a provisional protective measure shall indicate the provisional protective measure.

(2) The question of establishing a provisional protective measure cannot be examined before filing a claim in court.

(3) Provisional protective measures are:

- 1) entry of a prohibition note in the Commercial Register;
- 2) prohibition for the defendant to perform certain actions.
  - (4) The court or judge shall decide on the application for establishing a provisional protective measure without prior notice to the defendant and other participants in the case, within 15 days after receipt of the application or simultaneously with the initiation of the case, if the application is submitted simultaneously with filing the claim.
  - (5) The court or judge shall notify the defendant of the decision on application of the provisional protective measure specified in paragraph 1 of the third part of this article no earlier than the third day after adoption of the decision, but shall notify the defendant of the decision on application of the provisional protective measure specified in paragraph 2 of the third part of this article simultaneously with notification of the decision to the claimant. The defendant is responsible for observing the prohibition on performing certain actions from the moment when this decision is notified to him or her. The court or judge shall notify the Commercial Register institution about the entry of a prohibition note in the Commercial Register.
  - (6) Upon the claimant's application, the court may replace the established provisional protective measure with another provisional protective measure.
  - (7) Upon a party's application, the court may revoke the provisional protective measure.
  - (8) By rejecting the claim, the court shall revoke the provisional protective measure in the judgment. The provisional protective measure is in force until the day when the judgment enters into legal force.
  - (9) If the claim is left without examination or the proceedings are terminated, the court shall revoke the provisional protective measure in the decision.

The provisional protective measure is in force until the day when the decision enters into legal force.

(10) An ancillary complaint cannot be submitted regarding a decision by which a provisional protective measure is established, replaced or revoked.

(11) The defendant has the right to claim compensation for losses caused to him or her in connection with the establishment of a provisional protective measure if the claim filed against him or her is rejected, left without examination or proceedings are terminated in the cases specified in paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 223 of this law.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.36. Examination of a case in written proceedings and drafting and pronouncement of the judgment

(1) If the parties do not request the trial of the case in a court session or the court does not deem it necessary to try the case in a court session, the court shall examine the case in written proceedings no later than within one month after receipt of the explanatory statement or expiry of its submission time limit or after receipt of the reply or expiry of its submission time limit, timely notifying the participants in the case of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system. This date shall be considered the date of drafting the judgment. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of drafting the judgment, the judgment on the same date shall be available in the court office. In such case, the date when the judgment is available in the court office shall be considered the date of drafting the judgment.

(2) The court judgment shall be pronounced by immediately issuing the judgment to participants in the case after drafting the judgment.

(3) Upon written request of a participant in the case, the judgment shall be sent immediately after the date of drafting the judgment. Receipt of the judgment does not affect the counting of time limits.

(4) A decision on leaving the claim without examination, on termination of proceedings or on transfer of the case for examination in a court session may also be adopted in written proceedings.

(With amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.37. Trial of a case in a court session

(1) The court shall try a case in a court session in the procedure for claim proceedings if requested by one of the parties or if the court deems it necessary to try the case in a court session.

(2) The judge shall set the date of the court session no later than within 15 days after receipt of the explanatory statement or expiry of its submission time limit or after receipt of the reply or expiry of its submission time limit.

(3) If the court postpones the examination of the case, then the date of the next court session shall be set no later than within 15 days, except in cases where there is an objective basis for a longer time limit. Postponement of the case is not admissible in the case provided for in paragraph 4 of the first part of Article 210.

Article 250.38. Entry of the judgment into legal force

(1) The court judgment cannot be appealed in appellate procedure.

(2) Participants in the case may appeal the court judgment in cassation procedure (tenth division). In this case, the actions of the appellate court judge mentioned in the tenth division of this law shall be performed by the first instance court judge.

(3) The court judgment enters into legal force after the time limit for its appeal in cassation procedure has expired and a cassation complaint has not been submitted.

(4) If a cassation complaint has been submitted, the court judgment enters into legal force simultaneously with:

- 1) the decision of the Supreme Court panel session, if initiation of cassation proceedings has been refused (third part of Article 464 and Article 464.1);
- 2) the judgment of the cassation instance court, if the court judgment has not been revoked or the said judgment or a part thereof has been revoked and the application has been left without examination or proceedings have been terminated (Article 474).
  - (5) The provisions of the second, third, fourth and fifth parts of Article 203 of this law shall apply to the legal force of the court judgment.
  - (6) If in relation to any participant in the case the time limit for submission of a cassation complaint regarding the court judgment is set in accordance with part 2.1 of Article 454 of this law, the court judgment shall enter into legal force after the time limit for its appeal has expired, counting the time limit from the later date of issuance of the judgment, if a cassation complaint has not been submitted.
  - (7) If in the cases mentioned in the sixth part of this article the respective confirmation of issuance of the judgment has not been received (Article 56.2), the judgment shall enter into legal force six months after its pronouncement.
  - (8) The court judgment shall be executed in accordance with the provisions of Articles 204, 204.1 and the first part of Article 205 of this law. Immediate execution of the judgment in the case provided for in paragraph 7 of the first part of Article 205 is admissible only by requiring from the claimant adequate security for the case when the cassation instance court adopts the judgment mentioned in paragraphs 2, 3 or 4 of Article 474.

(With amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.39. Submission of an ancillary complaint

(1) An ancillary complaint may be submitted within 10 days from the day of adoption of the court or judge decision to the Supreme Court regarding the following decisions:

- 1) on refusal to accept the claim application;
- 2) on a decision by which the claim application is returned to the claimant;
- 3) on leaving the claim without examination;
- 4) on termination of proceedings.
  - (2) Regarding a decision adopted in written proceedings, the time limit for submission of an ancillary complaint shall be counted from the day of receipt of the decision.
  - (3) An ancillary complaint cannot be submitted regarding other court and judge decisions, but objections against these decisions may be expressed in a cassation complaint.

(With amendments made by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

Article 250.40. Content of the cassation complaint

If the claimant's place of residence or location is not in Latvia and the claimant has not agreed to electronic communication with the court, the cassation complaint shall, in addition to that specified in Article 453 of this law, indicate the address of the complaint submitter in Latvia for communication with the court to receive court documents.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.41. Supreme Court panel session

The Supreme Court panel session shall take place no later than within one month after the expiry of the time limit for submission of explanatory statements specified in the first part of Article 460 and the third part of Article 463.

(With amendments made by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

Article 250.42. Time limits for examination of a case at the Supreme Court

(1) The case shall be examined in written proceedings and the judgment shall be drafted no later than within two months after the respective Supreme Court panel session.

(2) The case shall be examined in a Supreme Court session no later than within two months after the respective Supreme Court panel session or after a decision on transfer of the case for examination in a court session has been adopted in written proceedings.
(With amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment in the first part regarding deletion of the word "full" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provision paragraph 137)
