### Chapter 30

Temporary protection against violence

(Chapter in the wording of 13.02.2014. law, which enters into force 31.03.2014.)

Article 250.43 Admissibility of temporary protection against violence in claims

Temporary protection against violence is admissible in claims for the non-existence or dissolution of marriage, in claims for personal injuries, in claims for the recovery of maintenance, in claims for the division of the parties' joint dwelling in which they live in one household, or for determining the procedure for using the dwelling in which the parties live in one household, and in cases arising from guardianship and contact rights. Article 250.44 Persons who may submit an application for temporary protection against violence

An application for temporary protection against violence may be submitted by spouses or former spouses; persons between whom there exists a parent-child relationship, there exists or has existed a guardianship or other out-of-family care relationship; persons between whom there exists a relationship of kinship or affinity; persons who live or have lived in one household; persons who have or are expecting a common child, regardless of whether these persons have ever been married or have ever lived together; persons between whom there exists or has existed a close personal or intimate relationship. Article 250.45 Basis for temporary protection against violence

(1) If a person is subject to any physical, sexual, psychological or economic violence that occurs between former or current spouses or other mutually related persons regardless of whether the offender lives or has lived in one household with the injured person, the court or judge upon a reasoned application of the person or an application submitted through the intermediary of the police may adopt a decision on temporary protection against violence. (2) The first paragraph of this Article shall also apply in cases where a person is subject to coercive control — such action or set of actions that includes injury, sexual coercion, threats, humiliation, intimidation or other violent actions whose purpose is to harm, punish or intimidate the injured person. (3) It is permissible to examine the issue of temporary protection against violence at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before bringing a claim to court. Article 250.46 Content of the application for temporary protection against violence

(1) The application for temporary protection against violence shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers. (2) The application for temporary protection against violence shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the application is submitted; - 2) the claimant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence. If the claimant consents to electronic communication with the court, the e-mail address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include a reference to the registration. The claimant may additionally also indicate another address for communication with the court; - 3) the respondent's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence. The respondent's personal identity number shall be indicated if it is known; - 4) the claimant's representative's (if the application is submitted by a representative) name, surname, personal identity number and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and registered address. If the claimant's representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, consents to electronic communication with the court, the e-mail address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include a reference to the registration. If the claimant's representative's address is outside Latvia, an e-mail address shall be additionally indicated or notification shall be given of the registration of their participation in the online system; - 5) the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law and how these circumstances manifest themselves; - 6) evidence confirming the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law, if such is at the claimant's disposal and if the person from whom the said evidence can be demanded is known, but it is not at the claimant's disposal or the claimant cannot demand it themselves for objective reasons; - 7) the applicable temporary protection against violence measure or measures; - 8) a list of documents attached to the application; - 9) a confirmation that true information about facts has been provided to the court and the claimant or the claimant and representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed about liability in accordance with the Criminal Law for submitting a false application; - 10) the time of drawing up the application and other information, if it is necessary for examining the case. - (3) If the applicable temporary protection measure is the obligation of the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and stay in it, an annex shall be attached to the application indicating the claimant's contact information (telephone, e-mail address, address) so that the State Police, by contacting the claimant, can carry out control of the execution of the respective decision. This annex is information of limited access, which in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Article 250.62 of this Law is sent to the State Police and is not attached to the case materials. - (31) In the application, the claimant may request the court to send the decision on temporary protection against violence to the social service at the claimant's place of residence. - (4) If the application does not contain the confirmation referred to in point 9 of the second paragraph of this Article, the application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter. (With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.47 Temporary protection against violence measures

(1) Temporary protection against violence measures are:

- 1) the obligation of the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and stay in it; - 2) a prohibition on the respondent from being closer to the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides than the distance specified in the court decision on temporary protection against violence; - 3) a prohibition on the respondent from staying in specified places; - 4) a prohibition on the respondent from meeting the claimant and maintaining physical or visual contact with them; - 5) a prohibition on the respondent from communicating with the claimant in any way; - 6) a prohibition on the respondent from, using the intermediary of another person, organising a meeting or any kind of communication with the claimant; - 7) a prohibition on the respondent from using the claimant's personal data; - 71) the obligation of the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour, the scope, procedure for receipt, payment, execution, interruption and termination of which shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers; - 8) other prohibitions and obligations that the court or judge has imposed on the respondent and whose purpose is to ensure the claimant's temporary protection against violence. - (2) The temporary protection against violence measure referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of this Article shall be determined if the respondent has reached the age of majority. - (3) It is permissible to simultaneously impose several temporary protection against violence measures. (With amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force 20.04.2021. Point 7.1 of the first paragraph enters into force 01.07.2021. See transitional provision 164)

Article 250.48 Obligation of the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and stay in it

(1) The obligation of the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and stay in it is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision on the respondent to remain and stay in this dwelling regardless of whether the respondent is the owner, possessor or user of this dwelling. (2) If the respondent is imposed the restriction referred to in this Article, the respondent shall be ensured the right to take or shall be issued the necessary clothing, footwear, linen, books, instruments, tools, things necessary for health care and other items that the respondent needs on a daily basis, which are in the dwelling. Article 250.49 Prohibition on the respondent from being closer to the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides than the distance specified in the court decision on temporary protection against violence

A prohibition on the respondent from being closer to the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides than the distance specified in the court or judge's decision on temporary protection against violence is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision on the respondent from visiting the respective dwelling and being closer to it than the distance specified in the decision. Article 250.50 Prohibition on the respondent from staying in specified places

(1) A prohibition on the respondent from staying in specified places is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision on the respondent from visiting the respective place, which is not a dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, or being closer to this place than the distance specified in the decision. (2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition on the respondent from staying in specified places applies to the address of a specific place or places that meet certain characteristics, or to public or other specified events. The court or judge shall as far as possible take into account the respondent's obligations to arrive at the workplace and other obligations of the respondent related to arriving at specified places. Article 250.51 Prohibition on the respondent from meeting the claimant and maintaining physical or visual contact with them

(1) A prohibition on the respondent from meeting the claimant and maintaining physical or visual contact with them is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision on the respondent from deliberately approaching or being closer to the claimant than the distance specified in the decision and avoiding physical or visual contact with the claimant. (2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition on the respondent from meeting the claimant and maintaining physical or visual contact with them also applies to persons who are closely connected with the claimant or dependent on the claimant. Article 250.52 Prohibition on the respondent from communicating with the claimant in any way

(1) A prohibition on the respondent from communicating with the claimant in any way is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision on the respondent from using means of communication, including electronic means of communication, or any other methods of transmitting information to contact the claimant. (2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition on the respondent from communicating with the claimant in any way also applies to persons who are closely connected with the claimant or dependent on the claimant. Article 250.53 Prohibition on the respondent from, using the intermediary of another person, organising a meeting or any kind of communication with the claimant

A prohibition on the respondent from, using the intermediary of another person, organising a meeting or any kind of communication with the claimant is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision on the respondent from using the intermediary of another person to approach the claimant or organise physical or visual contact with the claimant or to contact the claimant using any means of communication or any other methods of transmitting information. Article 250.54 Prohibition on the respondent from using the claimant's personal data

A prohibition on the respondent from using the claimant's personal data is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision on the respondent from processing, publishing, making known or otherwise using the claimant's personal data in any way, except in procedural actions related to legal proceedings. Article 250.54A Obligation of the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour

(1) The obligation of the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour is an obligation imposed by a court or judge's decision on the respondent to complete this course in order to prevent or reduce further risks of violence. (2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the obligation referred to in this Article, shall impose on the respondent also the obligation to partially cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour in the amount of 10 percent if the respondent begins to complete the course within six months, and in full if the respondent begins to complete the course after six months. (In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force 01.07.2021. The Article enters into force 01.07.2021. See transitional provision 164)

Article 250.55 Temporary protection against violence before bringing a claim

(1) A potential claimant may submit a reasoned application with a request to the court to ensure temporary protection against violence before bringing a claim to court if the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law exist. (2) If the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law relate to a child, the application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article may be submitted in the child's interests by one of the child's parents, a guardian, an orphan's court or a prosecutor. (3) An application for temporary protection against violence before bringing a claim shall be submitted to the court at the place where the injury was caused or the applicant's location. (With amendments made by the law of 01.10.2020., which enters into force 01.01.2021.)

Article 250.56 Temporary protection against violence before bringing a claim upon an application submitted through the intermediary of the police

(1) If before bringing a claim the police has adopted a decision that imposes an obligation on the potential respondent who poses a threat to leave the dwelling, not to return and not to stay in it or near it, or prohibits the potential respondent from contacting the potential claimant (police decision on separation), the police, upon the potential claimant's request, shall send to the court a copy of the police decision, the potential claimant's application stating that the potential claimant wishes the court to examine the issue of temporary protection against violence, as well as other information that is at the police's disposal and relates to the issue of temporary protection against violence. (2) The application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers. (3) The application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, as well as other information, shall be sent by the police to the court at the place where the injury was caused or the applicant's location. (4) The potential claimant's application submitted through the intermediary of the police need not contain an authorisation to the police to submit the application on behalf of the applicant. (5) The issue of temporary protection against violence, based on the potential claimant's application submitted through the intermediary of the police, shall be examined by the judge in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 250.58 of this Law. (With amendments made by the law of 01.10.2020., which enters into force 01.01.2021.)

Article 250.57 Evidence in cases of temporary protection against violence

(1) In cases of temporary protection against violence, a party to the case shall confirm with a confirmation the circumstances significant for the case indicated in the application. (2) If there is no other evidence or it is insufficient, the court on its own initiative at a court hearing may request a party to the case to confirm their explanations containing information about facts and circumstances on which their claims or objections are based. (3) Before giving the explanation, the party to the case shall give orally a confirmation of the following content:

"I, (name, surname), confirm that in good conscience I will tell only the truth and will conceal nothing. I confirm that the information I have provided to the court about facts and circumstances of the case is exhaustive and true. I have been warned that for giving deliberately false explanations and deliberately concealing facts and circumstances of the case known to me I may be held criminally liable in accordance with the Criminal Law."

(4) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)

(5) For giving a confirmed deliberately false explanation or application to the court, a party to the case may be held criminally liable in accordance with the Criminal Law. (6) A confirmation of an explanation and application as evidence is not admissible in respect of such circumstances that have been established by a judgment that has entered into force, as well as for confirming or refuting generally known facts. (With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.58 Examination of the issue of temporary protection against violence

(1) An application for temporary protection against violence shall be decided by the court or judge no later than the next day after receiving the application if it is not necessary to request additional evidence or the delay could cause a substantial infringement of the claimant's rights. The court or judge shall decide this application without prior notification to the parties to the case. (2) If the evidence is insufficient or it must be requested from the state or local government institutions or other natural or legal persons indicated in the application, the court or judge upon the request of a party to the case or on their own initiative shall request the evidence or invite the institutions to provide an opinion and shall decide the application for temporary protection against violence within 20 days after receiving it. (3) The court or judge shall decide the application for temporary protection against violence even if the application does not indicate all the information referred to in Article 250.46 of this Law or documents are attached, provided that the lack of documents or necessary information does not substantially affect the possibility of deciding the application. (4) The court or judge, when deciding the application for temporary protection against violence, shall take into account the proportionality between the infringement of rights or potential infringement and the applicable temporary protection against violence measure. The court or judge at their own discretion may also impose another temporary protection against violence measure that is not indicated in the application. (5) If prima facie it appears from the application for temporary protection against violence that a delay could cause a substantial infringement of the claimant's rights, the court or judge in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article shall decide this application and may grant it, based on the confirmation contained in the application also in cases where there is no other evidence or it is insufficient. (6) If prima facie it does not appear from the application for temporary protection against violence that a delay could cause a substantial infringement of the claimant's rights, and it has not been possible to obtain other evidence in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article, the court or judge in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article shall decide this application and may grant it, based on the confirmation contained in the application and the confirmation of the explanation given in accordance with the second and third paragraphs of Article 250.57 of this Law. (7) Upon granting the application for temporary protection against violence before bringing a claim, the court or judge shall set a time limit for the claimant to submit a statement of claim to the court, not longer than one year, but, when imposing temporary protection against violence measures referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law on a respondent who permanently resides in the dwelling together with the claimant — not longer than 30 days. (71) When examining a claim, the court or judge on their own initiative may apply the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law. (8) Upon granting the claim, the temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day when the judgment enters into legal force, except for the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law, which shall be in force until its execution. (9) In individual cases, the court may determine in the judgment that the temporary protection against violence shall be in force also after the judgment enters into legal force, but not longer than one year after the judgment enters into legal force. If a temporary protection against violence measure referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been imposed on a respondent who permanently resides in the dwelling together with the claimant, the court may determine that the temporary protection against violence shall be in force not longer than 30 days after the judgment enters into legal force. (10) Upon rejecting the claim, the court shall revoke the temporary protection against violence in the judgment. The temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day when the judgment enters into legal force. (11) If the claim is left without examination or the proceedings are terminated, the court shall revoke the temporary protection against violence by a decision. The temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day when the decision enters into legal force. (12) If a decision on temporary protection against violence has been adopted before bringing a claim and a claim has not been brought within the time limit set by the court, the judge, upon receiving a reasoned application from the potential claimant or respondent, shall adopt a decision on revoking the temporary protection against violence. In this case, litigation expenses shall not be reimbursed. (13) The application referred to in the second paragraph of this Article shall be examined in written proceedings. If the court considers it necessary, the application may be examined in a closed court hearing, with prior notification to the parties to the case. The court, upon the request of one party, may hear each party in a separate court hearing. The respondent's non-appearance shall not be an obstacle to examining the application. (With amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.59 Decision on temporary protection against violence

(1) In addition to that provided for in Article 230 of this Law, the court or judge shall indicate in the decision information about the parties to the case [name, surname, personal identity number (if it is known), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence]. (2) The court or judge in the decision on imposing the temporary protection against violence measure — the obligation of the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides — shall, if necessary, indicate the time limit for voluntary execution of the decision. (3) The court or judge in the decision on temporary protection against violence shall warn the respondent that the police will carry out control of the execution of the decision and, if the decision is not executed voluntarily, the respondent will be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law. (4) The court or judge in the decision on imposing the temporary protection against violence measure — the obligation of the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides — shall indicate that:

- 1) the respondent has the obligation to notify the court of their future address for communication with the court if this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration and the respondent has not consented to electronic communication with the court; - 11) the respondent is prohibited from alienating or transferring the dwelling, hindering or obstructing the use of the dwelling or deteriorating the condition of the dwelling regardless of whether the respondent is the owner, possessor or user of the dwelling; - 2) the respondent has the right to submit an application to the court for replacement or revocation of the temporary protection against violence measure; - 3) the date when the State Police acquaints the respondent with the decision shall be considered as the date when the said decision is notified to the respondent, and that the respondent's refusal to acquaint themselves with the decision does not affect its legal consequences; - 4) the decision is available in the online system. - (41) The court or judge in the decision on imposing the temporary protection against violence measure — the obligation of the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour — shall indicate:
- 1) the contact information of the violent behaviour reduction service provider and the respondent's obligation within 10 days from the day of receiving the decision to contact the violent behaviour reduction service provider; - 2) the respondent's obligation within one year from the day of receiving the decision to complete the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour and a warning to the respondent that if this course is not completed within one year, they will be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law; - 3) the respondent's obligation to partially cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour in the amount of 10 percent until completing the course if the respondent has begun to complete this course within six months from the day of receiving the decision, and in full if the respondent has begun to complete the course after six months from the day of receiving the decision, as well as that if the respondent does not cover these costs voluntarily, they will be recovered in the procedure established in this Law; - 4) a warning to the respondent that covering the costs of the rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour does not release them from the obligation to complete the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour and liability in accordance with the Criminal Law. - (5) A decision on temporary protection against violence (first and second paragraphs of Article 250.58) shall be executed immediately after its adoption, except for the part of the decision on covering the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour in accordance with that provided for in the second paragraph of Article 250.54A of this Law. (With amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.60 Revocation or replacement of ensuring temporary protection against violence

(1) Temporary protection against violence measures, except for the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law, upon a reasoned application of a party may be replaced with other measures by the same court that imposed the temporary protection against violence measures, or the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits. (2) Temporary protection against violence measures, upon a reasoned application of a party, may be revoked by the same court that imposed the temporary protection against violence measures, or the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits. (3) The application referred to in the first and second paragraphs of this Article shall be decided in a closed court hearing, with prior notification to the parties to the case. The court, upon the request of one party, may hear each party in a separate court hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the application. (4) A decision on replacing or revoking a temporary protection against violence measure shall be executed immediately after its adoption. (With amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force 20.04.2021. The amendment to the first paragraph enters into force 01.07.2021. See transitional provision 164)

Article 250.61 Appeal of decisions adopted on temporary protection against violence

(1) An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of Article 250.60 of this Law, a decision by which an application for temporary protection against violence has been rejected, and a decision by which an application for revoking temporary protection against violence has been rejected. (2) The submission of an ancillary complaint regarding the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall not suspend their execution. (3) If the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of this Article have been adopted without the presence of a party to the case, the time limit for submitting an ancillary complaint shall be counted from the day of issuing the respective decision. Article 250.62 Notification of the decision on temporary protection against violence

(1) The decision on temporary protection against violence, the decision on replacing or revoking a temporary protection against violence measure shall be notified to the parties by the court by issuing it against signature or by sending it to the official electronic address, or in a registered mail shipment. A decision by which an application for temporary protection against violence has been rejected, unless it has been examined with the participation of the parties, shall be notified only to the claimant. (2) The court shall send the decision on temporary protection against violence, the decision on replacing or revoking a temporary protection against violence measure immediately after their adoption to the State Police for execution control to the e-mail address indicated by it and also to the State Police structural unit at the claimant's place of residence. (3) If the decision on the issue of temporary protection against violence has been adopted upon an application submitted through the intermediary of the police (Article 250.56), the decision shall be available to the potential respondent and potential claimant in the online system on the next day after the court has received the application and police information. This date shall be considered as the date when the said decision is notified to the potential respondent, and the non-delivery of the decision to the respondent does not affect its legal consequences. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the decision to the online system on the specified date, the decision on the same date shall be available at the court office. In such case, the date when the decision is available at the court office shall be considered as the date of notification of the decision. (4) If a temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been applied to the respondent upon a reasoned application of the claimant submitted without the intermediary of the police, the court shall not send the decision to the respondent. The court shall send this decision and the claimant's contact information referred to in the third paragraph of Article 250.46 of this Law to the State Police in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article. The State Police, when commencing control of the execution of this decision, shall acquaint the respondent with the decision. The date when the State Police has acquainted the respondent with the decision shall be considered as the date when the decision is notified to the respondent, and the non-delivery of the decision to the respondent does not affect its legal consequences. Only after the notification of the decision shall the decision be available to the respondent in the online system. (5) If it appears from the materials of the case of temporary protection against violence that the interests of a minor child or a person with limited legal capacity are affected, the court shall additionally send the decision on temporary protection against violence or the decision on replacing or revoking a temporary protection against violence measure to the orphan's court and the social service at the child's or person's place of residence. In other cases, the court shall send the decision on temporary protection against violence or the decision on replacing or revoking a temporary protection against violence measure to the social service at the claimant's place of residence if the claimant has requested it. (6) If the temporary protection against violence measure provided for in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been applied to the respondent, the court shall send the decision on temporary protection against violence or the decision on revoking the temporary protection against violence measure immediately after its adoption additionally also to the violent behaviour reduction service provider to the e-mail address indicated by it. The information referred to in point 3 of the second paragraph of Article 250.46 of this Law shall also be sent to the service provider. The court shall also inform the service provider about the day when the decision was notified to the respondent, except in cases where the decision is notified in accordance with the fourth paragraph of this Article. If the decision is notified in accordance with the fourth paragraph of this Article, the State Police shall inform the service provider about the day when the decision was notified to the respondent. (With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.62A Conditions of execution and execution control if the respondent has been imposed the obligation to complete a social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour

(1) The court or judge, upon receiving from the violent behaviour reduction service provider a certificate that the respondent has not completed the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour within one year, shall send this certificate and the decision by which the obligation to complete the said course has been imposed on the respondent to the State Police for execution control to the e-mail address indicated by it and also to the State Police structural unit at the claimant's place of residence, so that it decides the issue of initiating criminal proceedings against the respondent for malicious non-execution of the decision on protection against violence. (2) The court or judge, upon receiving from the violent behaviour reduction service provider a certificate that the respondent has not covered the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour until completing the course, shall send a writ of execution to the bailiff at the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — at the debtor's place of residence. (3) The part of the decision by which the obligation to cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reducing violent behaviour has been imposed on the respondent shall be executed, if the respondent has not covered these costs voluntarily, in the procedure established in Part E of this Law. (In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021., which enters into force 20.04.2021.)

Article 250.63Article 250.63. Special conditions for the respondent's communication with the court if the respondent has been subject to a prohibition to return to and remain in the dwelling that is the respondent's declared place of residence

(1) If a temporary protection measure against violence has been applied that imposes an obligation on the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the applicant permanently resides, and establishes a prohibition to return to and remain in it, and this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration, further decisions on temporary protection against violence, decisions on the replacement or revocation of this temporary protection measure against violence shall be communicated by the court to the respondent electronically in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 56 of this law, but if that is not possible, to the address indicated by him for communication with the court.

(2) If a temporary protection measure against violence has been applied that imposes an obligation on the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the applicant permanently resides, and establishes a prohibition to return to and remain in it, and this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration, and if the applicant has brought an action within the time limit specified in the court decision on temporary protection against violence, summonses and other court documents related to this action shall be communicated to the respondent electronically in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 56 of this law, but if that is not possible, to the address indicated by him for communication with the court.

(3) If in the cases referred to in paragraphs one and two of this Article it is not possible to notify the respondent electronically or the respondent has not indicated his address for communication with the court, the respondent shall be summoned to court and other court documents shall be delivered and issued by summoning the respondent with a summons that is published in accordance with Article 59.

(As amended by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.64. Requesting the file and hearing the action in cases of temporary protection against violence following an application submitted before bringing an action

(1) If the applicant brings an action within the time limit specified in the decision on temporary protection against violence following an application submitted before bringing an action, in the competent court that is not the court that established the temporary protection measure against violence, the court having jurisdiction to hear the case on the merits shall request the relevant file from the court that established the temporary protection measure against violence and attach it to the action case materials.

(2) When examining the application, the court or judge shall, with regard to temporary protection against violence, at the request of a party to the case or on its own initiative, request evidence or invite institutions to provide an opinion.

(As amended by the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### Chapter 30

Cases on damages for infringements of competition law

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

Section 250.65. Procedure for hearing cases

(1) Cases on damages for infringements of competition law shall be heard by the Court of Economic Affairs in the procedure for claims according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(2) Cases on damages for infringements of competition law within the meaning of this chapter are cases related to such infringements of competition law which are defined in Article 101 or 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union or in the legal acts of Latvia or a Member State of the European Union whose main objective is the same as that of Articles 101 and 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017 with amendments made by the law of 31.05.2018 and 01.10.2020, which enters into force Section 250.66. Disclosure of evidence in cases on damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The court, following a reasoned request by the parties to the case, which is substantiated by reasonably available information, may in cases on damages for infringements of competition law request the disclosure of evidence, observing:

- 1) the extent to which the request or the respondent's objections to the request are substantiated by available information that justifies the request to disclose evidence;
- 2) the status of the evidence and the costs of obtaining it, especially in relation to persons who are not parties to the case;
- 3) whether the evidence that is being requested contains confidential information, especially concerning other persons who are not parties to the case, and the procedure provided for the protection of such confidential information.
  - (2) A person from whom evidence is requested has the right to notify the court in writing of the status and costs of submitting the requested information, substantiating them.
  - (3) The court may reject the request for disclosure of evidence if it considers that the scope of the evidence to be disclosed or the costs associated with the disclosure of evidence are not proportionate to the amount of the claim filed.
  - (4) The court, observing the person's rights to protection of confidential information, requires that a person whose information provided has been granted the status of confidential information submits the relevant derivative of written evidence without indicating the confidential information.
  - (5) The court may restrict the rights of an authorised representative of a party to a case to examine such evidence in the case which contains confidential information but has been submitted in an unredacted form, and the disclosure of this information may cause substantial harm to a party to the case or another person.
  - (6) The court, when requesting evidence that has been submitted to a competition authority or is in the case materials of a competition authority, shall assess whether the request specifies the evidence as precisely as possible, based on the information provided by the party, and whether the submission of evidence to the court will not create obstacles to the effective application of competition law.
  - (7) In order to assess whether the submission of evidence to the court will not create obstacles to the effective application of competition law, the court shall request the opinion of the competition authority. After evaluating the opinion of the competition authority, the court shall decide on the disclosure of evidence.

(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

Section 250.67. Restrictions on disclosure of evidence in cases on damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The court shall not request from the parties or other persons:

- 1) statements provided to a competition authority within the framework of a leniency programme;
- 2) settlement submissions for the conclusion of an administrative settlement with a competition authority.
  - (2) The court shall request evidence from the case materials of a competition authority if it is not possible to obtain this evidence from the parties to the case or other persons.
  - (3) Following a substantiated request by the claimant, the court, in order to verify that the materials submitted to the Competition Council comply with the provisions of paragraph one of this Section, shall request an opinion from the Competition Council and the view of the person who submitted these materials to the Competition Council.
  - (4) Having received the opinions referred to in paragraph three of this Section, the court may verify the information indicated in the opinions by requesting the submission of the authority's case materials, which shall not be attached to the civil case.
  - (5) The court shall adopt a decision on attaching the materials submitted to the Competition Council to the case materials if the requirements laid down in paragraph one of this Section do not apply to the materials submitted by the competition authority.

(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017 with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

Section 250.68. Admissibility of evidence in cases on damages for infringements of competition law

(1) Evidence referred to in paragraph one of Section 250.67 of this Law shall not be admissible if a person has obtained it by using access to the case materials of a competition authority.

(2) Information which a person has obtained by using access to the case materials of a competition authority may be used as evidence only by the said person or a person who is a successor to the rights and obligations of the said person.

(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

Section 250.69. Grounds for exemption from proof in cases on damages for infringements of competition law

(1) An infringement of competition law established by a decision of the Competition Council that has entered into force or by a court judgment that has entered into legal force shall not be proved anew when hearing a claim for damages filed in accordance with Article 101 or 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union or the Competition Law.

(2) An infringement of competition law established by a decision of the competition authority of another Member State that has entered into force shall be considered proven unless a party to the case submits to the court evidence of the non-existence of the infringement of competition law.

(3) If one party refers to evidence that is in the possession of the other party, and the latter, following a request by the court, refuses to submit the relevant evidence to the court or has destroyed it, without denying that this evidence is or has been in its possession, the court may recognise as proven those facts to confirm which the opposing party referred to this evidence.

(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

Section 250.70. Liability for failure to submit, destruction or unauthorised use of evidence in cases on damages for infringements of competition law

If the court does not establish objective circumstances for failure to submit evidence or a person has violated the restrictions on admissibility of evidence specified in Section

250.68 of this Law, or the court has established that evidence has been destroyed, the court may impose a fine on a natural person of up to 14,000 euros, but on a legal person — up to 140,000 euros.

(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

### Chapter 30

Cases on disputes concerning rights and interim protection for claims in insolvency proceedings

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. See point 144 of the transitional provisions)

Section 250.71. Jurisdiction of cases and the procedure for examination

(1) Cases on disputes concerning rights in insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court in which the respective insolvency proceedings have been declared, in the case provided for in the fourth part of Section 363.17 of this Law and in the first part of Section 80 of the Insolvency Law. Cases shall be examined in the procedure of claims according to general provisions, observing the exceptions provided for in this Chapter.

(2) Cases on disputes concerning rights in insolvency proceedings within the meaning of this Chapter shall also include cases on creditor claims in accordance with the provisions of the second and third parts of Section 80 of the Insolvency Law.

(3) If a case for examination of a dispute concerning rights has been initiated before the commencement of insolvency proceedings in a court and the examination of this case on the merits has not commenced, the court shall transfer this case for examination to the court in which the respective insolvency proceedings have been declared, if there is no procedural co-participation on the defendant's side among the parties to the case.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Section 250.72. Content of a statement of claim

In a statement of claim, in addition to what is provided for in Section 128 of this Law, the following shall be indicated:

- 1) an address in Latvia for communication with the court to receive court documents, if the claimant's place of residence or location is not in Latvia and the claimant has not consented to electronic communication with the court;
- 2) whether the claimant requests the hearing of the case in a court session, substantiating their request.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 250.73. Leaving a statement of claim without progress

(1) The court shall leave a statement of claim without progress if:

- 1) the statement of claim does not contain all the requisites provided for in the second or third part of Section 128 and Section 250.72 of this Law;
- 2) the documents provided for in Section 129 of this Law are not attached to the statement of claim.
  - (2) The judge shall adopt a reasoned decision on leaving a statement of claim without progress, send it to the claimant and set a time limit of up to 20 days for remedying the deficiencies, counting from the day of sending the decision. The judge's decision may be appealed in the procedure provided for in this Law. The appeal period shall be counted from the day when the decision is issued to the claimant.
  - (3) If the claimant remedies the deficiencies within the set time limit, the statement of claim shall be deemed to have been submitted on the day when it was first submitted to the court.
  - (4) If the claimant does not remedy the deficiencies within the set time limit, the statement of claim shall be considered as not submitted and returned to the claimant. The decision on returning the statement of claim to the claimant is not subject to appeal.
  - (5) The return of the statement of claim to the claimant is an obstacle to its repeated submission to the court.
  - (6) The court shall simultaneously with the decision on returning the statement of claim to the claimant adopt a decision on the complaint against the administrator's decision in the case and revoke the interim protection measure.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Section 250.74. Grounds for granting interim protection and applicable measures in insolvency proceedings

(1) Upon a reasoned application of the complainant, the court may adopt a decision on granting an interim protection measure if there is a reason to believe that the administrator's decision could violate the creditor's rights provided for in the Insolvency Law. The granting of an interim protection measure is permissible when considering the question of accepting a complaint against the administrator's decision in the cases provided for in part 1.1 and the fourth part of Section 363.17 of this Law, if the administrator's decision has been appealed by the person provided for in the second or third part of Section 80 of the Insolvency Law.

(2) When considering the question of granting an interim protection measure, the court shall take into account, in addition to the circumstances indicated in the complaint against the administrator's decision, also other materials of the insolvency proceedings case.

(3) The application for granting an interim protection measure shall indicate the interim protection measure which the court is requested to grant until the adoption of the judgment.

(4) The complainant has the right to request the court to grant the following interim protection measures:

- 1) a prohibition for the creditor, regarding whose acknowledged claim a complaint has been submitted, to participate in the creditors' meeting with voting rights;
- 2) a prohibition for the creditor, regarding whose acknowledged claim a complaint has been submitted, to submit objections to the information received as provided for in the first and second parts of Section 81 of the Insolvency Law.
  - (5) The court shall decide on the application for granting an interim protection measure no later than the next day after the complaint against the administrator's decision has been received, without prior notice to the administrator and creditors.
  - (6) The administrator is responsible for compliance with the prohibition on performing certain actions from the moment when this decision is notified to him. The court shall notify the responsible authority that makes entries in the insolvency register of the application of the interim protection measure.
  - (7) Upon a reasoned application of the complainant or interested person, the court may replace the granted interim protection measure with another interim protection measure.
  - (8) Upon a reasoned application of an interested person, the court may revoke the interim protection measure.
  - (9) If an interim protection measure has been granted but a claim for examination of a dispute concerning rights has not been filed and the court has not set a time limit for filing the claim, then when adopting a decision on the complaint against the administrator's decision in the case, the court shall simultaneously revoke the interim protection measure.
  - (10) If an interim protection measure has been granted before filing a claim for examination of a dispute concerning rights and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint against the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint against the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.
  - (11) When rejecting the claim for examination of a dispute concerning rights, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint against the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint against the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.
  - (12) If the claim for examination of a dispute concerning rights has been left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint against the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint against the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.
  - (13) A supplementary complaint cannot be submitted against a decision by which an interim protection measure has been granted, replaced or revoked.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Section 250.75. Examination of a case in written proceedings and preparation of a judgment

(1) The examination of a case in written proceedings shall be commenced no later than within 30 days after receipt of an explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission, timely notifying the parties to the case of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system. The court shall inform about the composition of the court that will examine the case and explain the right to challenge the judge. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered as the date of preparation of the judgment. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of preparation of the judgment, the judgment shall be available at the court office on the same date. In such case, the date when the judgment is available at the court office shall be considered as the date of preparation of the judgment.

(2) Upon a written request of a party to the case, the judgment shall be sent immediately after the date of preparation of the judgment. Receipt of the judgment does not affect the counting of the time limit.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 250.76. Hearing of a case in a court session

(1) The court shall hear the case in a court session if a reasoned request of a party to the case has been received and if the court considers it necessary to hear the case in a court session.

(2) The court shall set the date of the court session no later than within 30 days after receipt of an explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission.

(3) If the court postpones the examination of the case, the next date of the court session shall be set no later than within 15 days, except in cases where there is an objective reason for a longer time limit.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Section 250.77. Appeal of a judgment, entry into force and entry into force of a decision on examination of a complaint

(1) Parties to the case may appeal the court judgment by way of appeal if there is one of the grounds for instituting appeal proceedings provided for in Section 440.2 of this Law.

(2) The judgment shall enter into force after the time limit for submitting an appeal has expired.

(3) If the judgment has been appealed and the court of appeal refuses to institute appeal proceedings, the judgment of the court of first instance and the decision on the complaint against the administrator's decision shall enter into force simultaneously with the decision by which the institution of appeal proceedings has been refused.

(4) The court decision on the complaint against the administrator's decision in the case provided for in the fourth part of Section 363.17 of this Law shall enter into force if an appeal has not been submitted within the time limit provided for by law.

(5) After the entry into force of the rulings mentioned in this Section, they shall also be sent to the administrator and the Insolvency Control Service.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 30. nodaļa

Cases on the protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure

(Chapter in the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.78. Procedure for consideration of cases

Cases concerning occurred or reasonably foreseeable unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure of trade secrets (hereinafter – infringement) shall be examined by a court in claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this Chapter.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.79. Protection of information containing trade secrets

(1) If, following a reasoned request of a party, the court recognises that the case contains a document containing trade secrets, which has been submitted in an undisclosed form, and the disclosure of this information may cause substantial harm to a participant in the case or another person, the court may restrict the right of a person participating in the examination of the case to become acquainted with this part of the case materials, by including the relevant evidence in a separate volume.

(2) The court, observing the right of a person to protection of trade secrets, requests that the person whose information submitted has the status of a trade secret submits a derivative of the relevant written evidence, without indicating information containing trade secrets or by submitting it in a redacted form.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.80. Basis for the application of interim measures and general provisions

(1) The court, following a reasoned application of the claimant, may adopt a decision on the application of interim measures if there is a basis to consider that:

- 1) a trade secret exists and the claimant is its holder;
- 2) the rights to the protection of a trade secret against unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure are being infringed or could be infringed.
  - (2) The court, when deciding on the satisfaction or rejection of the application or assessing the proportionality of the application of interim measures, takes into account that set out in Section 250.88 of this Law.
  - (3) It is permissible to consider the question of the application of interim measures at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before bringing an action to court.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.81. Interim measures

(1) The application for the application of interim measures shall indicate the relevant interim measure.

(2) Interim measures are:

- 1) a prohibition on the defendant or a specified person who makes possible the commission of the infringement from using or disclosing a trade secret, manufacturing, offering, placing on the market or using infringing goods for the mentioned purposes;
- 2) the attachment of movable property with which the rights to the protection of a trade secret against unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure are possibly being infringed.
  - (3) The court, when deciding on an application that is not related to the disclosure of a trade secret, may not apply the interim measures set out in paragraph two of this Section, but impose an obligation on the defendant to pay a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or to submit an equivalent security to the court, in order to ensure compensation to the holder of the trade secret.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.82. Application of interim measures before bringing an action

(1) A potential claimant may request that an interim measure be applied before bringing an action within three months from the day when they learned or should have learned of the infringement of rights or possible infringement.

(2) When submitting an application, the potential claimant shall provide evidence confirming the infringement of rights or possible infringement.

(3) The application for the application of interim measures before bringing an action shall be submitted to the court in which the action is to be brought.

(4) When satisfying an application for the application of interim measures before bringing an action, the judge shall set a time limit for the claimant to submit a statement of claim to the court, not longer than 30 days.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.83. Examination of the question of the application of interim measures

(1) The application for the application of interim measures before bringing an action, as well as in cases when it is not possible to determine who will be the participants in the case, shall be decided by the court or judge within 10 days of receiving the application, without holding a court hearing and without prior notice to the participants in the case. If the judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided within 15 days of receiving it, inviting the applicant and potential participants in the case to a court hearing. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(2) The application for the application of interim measures, if the application is submitted simultaneously with bringing an action, shall be decided by the court or judge within 10 days of initiating the case, without holding a court hearing and without prior notice to the participants in the case, or within 10 days of receiving the application if the case has already been initiated. If the judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided within 15 days of initiating the case or, if the case has already been initiated, within 15 days of receiving it, inviting the applicant and potential participants in the case to a court hearing. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(3) If delay could cause irreversible harm to the holder of the trade secret and if it is not necessary to request additional evidence, the application for the application of interim measures shall be decided by the judge not later than the next day after initiating the case or, if the case has already been initiated, not later than the next day after receiving the application, without prior notice to the defendant and other participants in the case.

(4) If a decision on the application of interim measures has been adopted without the presence of the defendant or other participants in the case, the court shall notify the defendant and other participants in the case of this decision not earlier than the third day after the adoption of the decision.

(5) When satisfying an application for the application of interim measures, the court or judge may instruct the claimant to secure losses that could arise for the defendant or other persons mentioned in point 1 of paragraph two of Section 250.81 of this Law in connection with the application of interim measures, by paying a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or by submitting an equivalent security to the court. If the claimant has not fulfilled the imposed obligation or has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff confirming the payment of the sum of money into their deposit account within the time limit set by the court or judge, the court or judge shall adopt a decision to revoke the interim measure. The decision on securing losses shall be notified to the defendant after the claimant has paid the sum of money set by the court or judge into the deposit account of a bailiff.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 250.84. Replacement or revocation of interim measures

(1) The court, following an application of the claimant, may replace the set interim measure with another measure.

(2) An interim measure may be revoked by the same court following an application of a participant in the case.

(3) The court, following receipt of an application from the claimant, another potential participant in the case or a person to whom the applied interim measure relates, shall adopt a decision to revoke the interim measure if:

- 1) a decision on the application of interim measures has been adopted before bringing an action and the action has not been brought within the time limit set by the court;
- 2) the relevant information that was considered to be a trade secret no longer meets the requirements for a trade secret set out in the Trade Secret Protection Law for reasons that cannot be related to the defendant.
  - (4) When rejecting the claim, the court shall revoke the interim measure in the judgment. The interim measure shall be in force until the day when the judgment enters into legal force.
  - (5) If the claim has been left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated, the court shall revoke the interim measure in the decision.

The interim measure shall be in force until the day when the decision enters into legal force.

(6) The applications mentioned in paragraphs one, two and three of this Section shall be decided at a court hearing, with prior notice to the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.85. Appeal of decisions adopted regarding the application of interim measures

(1) A subsidiary complaint may be submitted regarding a decision by which the set interim measure has been replaced, a decision by which an application for the application of interim measures has been rejected, and a decision by which an application for the revocation of an interim measure has been rejected.

(2) If a decision on the application of interim measures has been adopted without the presence of a participant in the case, the time limit for submitting a subsidiary complaint shall be calculated from the day of issuing the decision.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.86. Execution of a decision on the application of interim measures

(1) A decision on the application of interim measures and a decision on the revocation of an interim measure shall be enforceable immediately after its adoption.

(2) A decision on the application of interim measures adopted with the condition mentioned in paragraph five of Section 250.83 of this Law shall be enforceable after the claimant has paid the sum of money set by the court or judge into the deposit account of a bailiff or has submitted an equivalent security to the court. The enforcement document shall be issued after the payment of the sum of money set by the court or receipt of the equivalent security.

(3) A decision on the application of interim measures by attaching movable property with which an infringement has possibly been committed shall be executed in the procedure set out in Chapter 71 of this Law.

(4) A decision on the application of interim measures, by setting a prohibition to carry out specified actions with which an infringement has possibly been committed, shall be executed by a bailiff and the court decision shall be notified to the defendant or the relevant third party in the procedure set out in Section 555 of this Law.

(5) The revocation of an applied interim measure shall be enforceable following an order of the bailiff who executed the decision on the application of the interim measure.

(6) A decision on the replacement of an interim measure shall be executed by a bailiff by first applying the replacing interim measure and then revoking the replaced interim measure.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 250.87. Compensation for harm caused by an interim measure

The defendant is entitled to claim compensation for harm caused to them in connection with the setting of an interim measure if the interim measure has been revoked in the case set out in point 1 of paragraph three of Section 250.84 of this Law, if the claim brought against them has been rejected, left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated in the cases set out in points

2 and 4 of Section 223 of this Law.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

Section 250.88. General provisions for the examination of the statement of claim and the application of legal remedies

The court, when deciding on the full or partial satisfaction of the claim or on its full or partial rejection or assessing the proportionality of the application of a legal remedy, takes into account the circumstances of the relevant case, including where possible:

- 1) the value of the trade secret or other specific characteristics of the trade secret;
- 2) the measures that have been taken to protect the trade secret;
- 3) the conduct of the defendant in acquiring, using or disclosing the trade secret;
- 4) the consequences of the unlawful use or disclosure of the trade secret;
- 5) the legitimate interests of the parties and the impact of the application of interim measures on them;
- 6) the legitimate interests of third parties and society;
- 7) the protection of fundamental rights.

(In the version of the law of 28.02.2019., which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

### 30. nodaļa

Cases arising from consumer collective actions

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

250.89 pants. Procedure for consideration of cases

Cases arising from consumer collective actions shall be considered by the court in action proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this Chapter.

(In the wording of the law of 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

250.90 pants. Persons who may submit an application

An application on behalf of a consumer group may be submitted by persons included in the list of qualified entities of Latvia or in the list of qualified entities compiled by the European Commission.

(In the wording of the law of 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

250.91 pants. Content of the application

The application shall indicate, in addition to what is provided for in Article 128 of this Law:

- 1) the first name, surname, personal identity number of those consumers who have given consent to the applicant to represent them in the particular action;
- 2) justification for combining the claims of the particular consumers into a consumer collective action;
- 3) specific compensation and its amount for each consumer indicated in the application.

(In the wording of the law of 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

250.92 pants. Actions of the judge in preparing the case

(1) The judge shall set a preparatory hearing and notify the parties thereof.

(2) The judge shall set a time limit for the applicant, which is not shorter than 60 days, for the applicant to announce repeated registration of consumers for the consumer collective action and to specify the application accordingly, supplementing it with new consumer claims.

(In the wording of the law of 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

250.93 pants. Basis for exemption from proving consumer rights violations

(1) A consumer rights violation established by an effective decision of the Consumer Rights Protection Centre or by a final court judgment need not be proved again when considering a consumer collective action.

(2) A consumer rights violation established by an effective decision of a consumer protection authority of another Member State shall be deemed to be proved unless a participant in the case submits evidence to the court of the absence of a consumer rights violation.

(In the wording of the law of 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)

250.94 pants. Settlement

(1) The settlement shall indicate, in addition to what is mentioned in Article 227 of this Law, also the specific consumers to whom the provisions of the settlement apply, as well as the obligations they voluntarily undertake to fulfil.

(2) A court-approved settlement is binding on the applicant, the respondent and the consumers represented in the consumer collective action.

(In the wording of the law of 14.09.2023., which enters into force on 15.10.2023.)
