Special procedure

31.nodaļa

General provisions

#### 251.pants. Cases which the court considers in special procedure

The court shall consider the following cases in special procedure:

- 1) on confirmation and revocation of adoption;
- 2) on restriction of legal capacity due to mental disorders or other health impairments, review and restoration of restriction of legal capacity;
- 21) on establishment and termination of temporary guardianship;
- 3) on restriction of legal capacity and establishment of guardianship for persons due to their extravagant or wasteful life, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicants;
- 31) on suspension of the rights of a future representative;
- 4) on establishment of guardianship over the property of absent or missing persons;
- 5) on declaring missing persons deceased;
- 6) on establishment of facts which have legal significance;
- 7) on extinction of rights by way of public notice;
- 8) on restoration of rights under debt instruments or bearer securities;
- 9) on inheritance rights;
- 10) on expropriation of immovable property;
- 11) on legal protection proceedings and insolvency proceedings;
- 12) on liquidation or insolvency of credit institutions;
- 13) on declaring a strike or strike notice unlawful;
- 14) on declaring a lockout or lockout notice unlawful;
- 15) on revocation of a natural person's discharge from debt obligations;
- 16) on introduction of an acquirer of immovable property into possession.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 01.11.2007., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

#### 252.pants. Initiation of cases

The judge shall initiate a case to be considered in special procedure on the basis of a written application.

#### 253.pants. Participants in the case

(1) In cases of special procedure, the participants in the case are the applicant and his or her representative, the interested person and his or her representative, as well as, in the cases provided for by law, the prosecutor, a State or local government institution.

(2) In cases of special procedure, the participants in the case have the procedural rights of parties set out in the second paragraph of Article 74 of this Law.

#### 254.pants. Application in special procedure

(1) The application shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the application is submitted;
- 11) the applicant's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the applicant consents to electronic communication with the court, the electronic mail address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included;
- 12) the interested person's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. The personal identity number or registration number of the interested person shall be indicated if it is known;
- 13) the electronic mail address of the applicant's representative or the person who has the right to submit the application and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also a reference to the registration, if the applicant's representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia or the person who has the right to submit the application consents to electronic communication with the court. If the address of the applicant's representative is outside Latvia, the electronic mail address shall additionally be indicated or notice of registration of his or her participation in the online system shall be given;
- 2) (deleted by the law of 29.11.2012.);
- 3) the subject matter and justification of the application;
- 4) the circumstances on which the application is based and the evidence confirming them;
- 5) the law on which the application is based;
- 6) the applicant's request;
- 7) the list of attached documents;
- 8) the time of drawing up the application.
  - (2) The application shall be signed by the applicant or his or her representative, or the applicant together with the representative if so determined by the court, except for the case specified in the fifth paragraph of Article 72 of this Law. If the application is signed by a representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to apply to the court shall be attached to the application.
  - (3) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)
  - (4) An unsigned application shall be deemed not submitted and shall be returned to the submitter.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 255.pants. Refusal to accept an application and leaving the application without progress

(1) If the application does not comply with the requirements of the second paragraph of Article 254 of this Law, the judge shall refuse to accept it and the consequences provided for in Article 132 of this Law shall apply.

(2) If the application does not comply with the requirements of the first paragraph of Article 254 of this Law and the requirements specified in the separate chapters of this Section or court costs have not been paid, the judge shall leave the application without progress and the consequences provided for in Article 133 of this Law shall apply.

(With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 256.pants. Procedure for consideration of cases

Cases in special procedure shall be prepared for consideration by the judge, and the court shall consider them in accordance with the provisions of this Law, observing the provisions of the separate chapters of the sixth Section.

#### 257.pants. Judgment

A judgment in cases examined in special proceedings must comply with the requirements of Article 193 of this Law, observing the provisions of this section.

#### 258.pants. Leaving an Application Without Examination

If in a case examined in special proceedings a dispute arises over rights and this dispute is to be resolved in court by way of action, the court, depending on the content of the dispute, leaves the application without examination or suspends the proceedings until the dispute is resolved. Chapter 32

Confirmation and Revocation of Adoption

#### 259.pants. Jurisdiction

(1) An application for confirmation of adoption shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of the adopter, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of the adopter, but an application for revocation of adoption — to the court according to the declared place of residence of one applicant, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of the applicant.

(2) An application by a foreign national or a person living abroad for confirmation of adoption shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of the adoptee, but if the adoptee is in out-of-family care — according to the address of the place where out-of-family care is provided.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003. un 29.11.2012. likumu, kas stājas spēkā

#### 260.pants. Content of Application

(1) The application shall indicate the circumstances referred to in Articles 162 to 169 of the Civil Law.

(2) The application shall be accompanied by decisions of the orphan's court on recognising a person as an adopter and on the compliance of the adoption with the interests of the child.

(3) If the applicant is a foreign national or a person living abroad, the application shall be accompanied by the adoption file and a valid adoption permit issued by the responsible minister.

(29.10.2015. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 03.12.2015.)

260.1 pants. Requesting Evidence from the Orphan's Court

Upon initiation of a case, the court, if necessary, shall request from the orphan's court evidence confirming the circumstances referred to in Articles 162 to 169 of the Civil Law.

(29.10.2015. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 03.12.2015.)

#### 261.pants. Examination of the Application

(1) The case shall be examined with the participation of at least one adopter personally and a prosecutor.

(2) The examination of the case shall invite the orphan's court that has decided on the compliance of the adoption with the interests of the child, and the adoptee, if it is necessary to hear them at the court hearing and they have reached 12 years of age.

(3) (Izslēgta ar 29.10.2015. likumu)

(4) If the adopter dies before the court has confirmed the adoption, this is not an obstacle to the confirmation of the adoption, but if the adoptee dies before confirmation, the case shall be terminated.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003. un 29.10.2015. likumu, kas stājas spēkā

#### 262.pants. Court Judgment on Confirmation of Adoption

(1) The court, having verified the merits of the application and compliance with the requirements of the law, shall render a judgment on confirmation of the adoption or on rejection of the application.

(2) The court judgment on confirmation of adoption shall indicate the information necessary to make an entry in the relevant birth register regarding the adopters and to annul the entry regarding the child's former parents.

(3) The court shall notify the child's former parents that the entry regarding the child's parents has been annulled in the relevant birth register.

(4) A court judgment on confirmation of adoption that has entered into legal force is grounds for making an entry in the relevant birth register and issuing a new birth certificate for the adoptee.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 20.06.2001., 31.10.2002. un 29.10.2015. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 03.12.2015.)

#### 263.pants. Revocation of Adoption

(1) The court may revoke an adoption upon a joint application of the adopter and the adult adoptee or upon an application of the adult adoptee (Article 175 of the Civil Law).

(2) A court judgment on revocation of adoption that has entered into legal force is grounds for making an entry in the relevant birth register and issuing a new birth certificate.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.10.2002., 07.09.2006. un 29.10.2015. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 03.12.2015.)

Chapter 33

Restriction of a Person's Legal Capacity and Establishment of Guardianship Due to Mental or Other Health Disorders

(Nodaļas nosaukums 29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013.)

#### 264.pants. Jurisdiction

An application for restriction of a person's legal capacity due to mental or other health disorders shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of this person, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of this person; if the person is placed in a medical institution — according to the address of the medical institution.

(29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013.)

264.1 pants. Applicants

An application for restriction of a person's legal capacity due to mental or other health disorders and establishment of guardianship may be submitted by the person itself, its children, siblings, parents, spouse or a prosecutor.

(29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013.)

#### 265.pants. Content of Application

The application shall indicate the restriction of legal capacity to be determined for the person. The application shall be accompanied by evidence confirming the necessity of restricting legal capacity in the interests of the person.

(29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013.)

#### 266.pants. Preparation of the Case for Trial and Examination of the Application

(1) The court shall examine a case on determining a restriction of a person's legal capacity and establishment of guardianship due to mental or other health disorders with the participation of a representative of the orphan's court and a prosecutor.

(2) The representative of the orphan's court shall participate by submitting evidence that is relevant to the case. The representative of the orphan's court has the right to familiarise themselves with the case materials, participate in the examination of evidence and make requests.

(3) The court is obliged to summon to the court hearing the person whose restriction of legal capacity is being examined. The application shall be sent to the person for whom restriction of legal capacity and establishment of guardianship is being initiated, except in a case where this person itself is the applicant, setting a time period, not longer than 30 days, for submission of an explanation.

(4) When examining the case, the court on its own initiative shall request a certificate from a medical institution and other evidence necessary for determining the scope of restriction of the person's legal capacity from the applicant and institutions.

(5) The court, when preparing the case for trial, may convene a preparatory hearing and, in case of insufficient evidence, order additional expert examinations or request other evidence.

(29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 267.pants. Appointment of Forensic Examination

(1) The court may decide on the appointment of a forensic psychiatric and, if necessary, forensic psychological examination. A decision on appointment of a forensic examination is appealable.

(2) If the person about whom the case has been initiated avoids the examination, the court, with the participation of a prosecutor, may adopt a decision to send this person for a forensic examination by compulsory means.

(3) (Izslēgta ar 29.11.2012. likumu)

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 07.09.2006., 29.11.2012. un 29.10.2015. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 03.12.2015.)

267.1 pants. Establishment of Temporary Guardianship

(1) At the request of case participants, the court may adopt a decision by which temporary guardianship is established for the respective person for the period until the rendering of a judgment on restriction of legal capacity in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 33.2 of this Law on establishment of temporary guardianship.

(2) The decision enters into force immediately. It loses force if another decision is adopted in the respective matter.

(3) An ancillary complaint may be submitted against a court decision to establish temporary guardianship. The submission of an ancillary complaint does not suspend the execution of the decision.

(29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013.)

#### 268.pants. Court Judgment

(1) If the court establishes on the basis of evidence that a person's legal capacity is to be restricted, it makes a judgment in which it indicates the extent of the restriction of legal capacity and by which it establishes guardianship for the person.

(2) When determining the extent of the restriction of legal capacity, the court is guided by the circumstances for which evidence has been submitted. When determining the extent of the restriction of legal capacity, the court may, at the request of a party to the case, assess the restriction of legal capacity in such areas as:

- 1) making and receiving payments;
- 2) conclusion of transactions;
- 3) dealing with property and its management, in particular the alienation, mortgaging and encumbrance of immovable property with rights in rem;
- 4) conducting commercial and economic activities.
  - (3) The court may also assess the extent of the restriction of legal capacity in other areas, except for the cases referred to in Article 356.1 of the Civil Law.
  - (4) The court, when assessing the person's abilities, determines whether and to what extent the guardian acts together with the person under guardianship, and only then the extent to which the guardian will act independently.
  - (5) After the judgment enters into legal force, the court sends it to the orphan's court - for the appointment of a guardian, as well as to the prosecutor and the person whose legal capacity has been restricted. The court also sends information about the judgment to the Population Register and, if necessary, the judgment for entering a note in the land register, movable property register or other relevant public register.
  - (6) (Deleted by the Law of 25.03.2021.) (In the wording of the Law of 29.11.2012. with amendments made by the Laws of 23.04.2015., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 269.pants. Court Costs

(1) Court costs in these cases are to be covered from state funds.

(2) If the court finds that the applicant has knowingly submitted an unfounded application, the court costs are to be imposed on the applicant.

(With amendments made by the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 270.pants. Recognition of a Person as Having Legal Capacity and Termination of Guardianship

(Deleted by the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 33. nodaļa

Review of the Restriction of a Person's Legal Capacity Due to Mental Disorder or Other Health Disorders

(Chapter in the wording of the Law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

270.1 pants. Jurisdiction

An application for review of the extent of restriction of a person's legal capacity is submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of the person whose legal capacity is proposed to be reviewed, but if there is none - according to this person's place of residence; if the person is placed in a medical institution - according to the address of the medical institution.

(In the wording of the Law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

270.2 pants. Applicants

(1) An application for review of the extent of restriction of a person's legal capacity may be submitted by the person themselves, their guardian, children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or prosecutor. The representative of the orphan's court participates in the examination of cases by submitting evidence that is relevant to the case. The representative of the orphan's court has the right to familiarize themselves with the case materials, participate in the examination of evidence and submit requests.

(2) The guardian has the obligation to submit to the court an application for review of the extent of restriction of legal capacity no less frequently than once every seven years from the day the court judgment on the restriction of legal capacity entered into force.

270.3 pants. Content of the Application

(1) The application indicates to what extent the restriction of legal capacity is to be reviewed.

(2) Evidence confirming this must be attached to the application for review of the extent of restriction of legal capacity. 270.4 pants. Preparation of the Case for Trial

(1) The application is sent to the person whose legal capacity is proposed to be reviewed, except in cases where this person is the applicant themselves. Then they are given a time, not longer than 30 days, for submitting an explanation.

(2) The court has the duty to summon to the court session the person whose restriction of legal capacity is being reviewed.

(3) When examining the case, the court on its own initiative requests a certificate from the medical institution and from the applicant and institutions other evidence that is necessary for reviewing the extent of restriction of legal capacity.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 11.11.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Court expertise is determined according to the rules applied in cases concerning the restriction of a person's legal capacity and establishment of guardianship due to mental disorder or other health disorders.

270.6 pants. Court Judgment

(1) If the court reviews a person's restriction of legal capacity, it indicates in its judgment whether the restriction:

- 1) is to be revoked in full;
- 2) is to be revoked in part;
- 3) is to be maintained;
- 4) is to be amended.
  - (2) The operative part of the court judgment indicates the revoked and maintained extent of the restriction.
  - (3) After the judgment enters into legal force, the court sends it to the orphan's court - for amending the scope of the guardian's rights and obligations or for revoking the guardian, as well as to the prosecutor, guardian and person whose restriction of legal capacity has been reviewed. The court also sends information about the judgment to the Population Register and, if necessary, the judgment for amending the note in the land register, movable property register or other relevant public register.
  - (4) (Deleted by the Law of 25.03.2021.) (With amendments made by the Laws of 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 33. nodaļa

Establishment of Temporary Guardianship

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

270.7 pants. Jurisdiction

An application for the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of this person, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of this person; if the person is placed in a medical institution — according to the address of the medical institution.

270.8 pants. Applicants

An application for the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person may be submitted by the person itself, its children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or prosecutor.

270.9 pants. Content of the application

In the application, in addition to that specified in Article 254 of this law, the circumstances referred to in Article 364.2 of the Civil Law shall be indicated, attaching evidence confirming these circumstances, and whether the applicant requests examination of the case in a court session.

270.10 pants. Action of the court after initiation of the case

(1) After a case has been initiated concerning the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person, the judge on his or her own initiative or at the request of a participant in the case requests evidence, including also a certificate from a medical institution as to whether, due to mental or other health disorders, the person has lost the ability to understand the meaning of his or her actions and to control them.

(2) The application shall be sent to the person for whom the establishment of temporary guardianship has been initiated, except in cases where this person is itself the applicant. Then it shall be given a time, not longer than 15 days, for submission of an explanation.

(3) After initiation of the case, without holding a court session, the court shall inform the prosecutor's office and the orphan's court about the initiation of the case. After explanations, all evidence and a certificate from the medical institution have been received, the court shall request the prosecutor to submit a written opinion in the case within 10 working days, and the orphan's court — evidence that is relevant to the case.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.11 pants. Examination of the application

(1) The judge shall decide on the application for the establishment of temporary guardianship immediately.

(2) If the applicant does not request examination of the case in a court session and the court does not consider it necessary to examine the case in a court session, the application shall be examined in written proceedings, timely notifying the participants in the case of the date when the decision will be available in the online system. This date shall be deemed to be the date of preparation of the decision. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the decision to the online system on the date of preparation of the decision, the decision shall be available at the court registry on the same date. In such case, the date when the decision is available at the court registry shall be deemed to be the date of preparation of the decision.

(3) If the application is examined by holding a court session, the prosecutor and a representative of the orphan's court shall participate in it. It is the duty of the court to summon to the court session the person for whom temporary guardianship is to be established.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.12 pants. Decision of the court

(1) If the court, based on evidence, establishes that temporary guardianship is to be established over a person, it shall make a decision on the establishment of such guardianship, indicating the guardian's duty to conduct specific matters and the period of validity of the decision, which shall not be longer than two years.

(2) The decision on the establishment of temporary guardianship over a person shall come into force immediately and shall be in force for the period specified in this decision.

(3) The decision on the establishment of temporary guardianship shall be sent to the orphan's court — for the appointment of a temporary guardian, as well as to the prosecutor and the person for whom temporary guardianship has been established.

(4) An appeal may be submitted against the court's decision to establish temporary guardianship. Submission of an appeal shall not suspend the execution of the decision.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.13 pants. Termination of temporary guardianship

(1) Temporary guardianship shall terminate within the period set by the court.

(2) If before the period referred to in the second paragraph of Article 270.11 of this law the circumstances that were the basis for the establishment of temporary guardianship have ceased to exist, the same court, upon application of the guardian or the person under guardianship, shall terminate the established temporary guardianship.

(3) The decision on the termination of temporary guardianship shall come into force immediately.

(4) The decision on the termination of the establishment of temporary guardianship shall be sent to the person for whom temporary guardianship had been established, the guardian, the prosecutor and the orphan's court — for the revocation of the temporary guardian.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

270.14 pants. Court costs

If the court finds that the applicant has knowingly submitted an unfounded application, the court costs shall be imposed on the applicant.

34.nodaļa

Restriction of Legal Capacity of a Person and Establishment of Guardianship due to a Reckless or Wasteful Life, as well as due to Excessive Use of Alcohol or Other Intoxicating Substances

(Title of Chapter in the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 271.pants. Jurisdiction

An application for the restriction of legal capacity and establishment of guardianship over a person due to a reckless or wasteful life, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances shall be submitted to the court according to the declared place of residence of this person, but if there is none — according to its place of residence.

(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

271.1 pants. Applicants

An application for the restriction of legal capacity of a person and establishment of guardianship over a person due to a reckless or wasteful life, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances may be submitted by the person itself, its children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or prosecutor.

(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 272.pants. Content of the application

(1) The application shall indicate on what basis and to what extent the person's legal capacity is to be restricted and guardianship established due to a reckless or wasteful life, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances, and what evidence confirms it.

(2) The application may request immediate security against dissipation of property by applying the security measures provided for in Article 138 of this law. The judge shall decide on such a request no later than the day following receipt of the application.

(With amendments made by the law of 07.09.2006. and the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 273.pants. Preparation of the case for examination

(1) The application shall be sent to the person for whom restriction of legal capacity and establishment of guardianship has been initiated, except in cases where this person is itself the applicant. Then it shall be given a time, not longer than 30 days, for submission of an explanation.

(2) The court may impose on the applicant the duty to submit additional evidence.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012. and the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 274.pants. Participation of a representative of the orphan's court and the prosecutor

A case concerning the establishment of guardianship over a person due to a reckless or wasteful life, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances shall be examined with the participation of a representative of the orphan's court and the prosecutor. The representative of the orphan's court shall participate in the examination of the case by submitting evidence that is relevant to the case. The representative of the orphan's court shall have the right to familiarize itself with the case materials, participate in the verification of evidence and submit requests.

(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)


This excerpt sits under: Izdevējs: Saeima Publicēts:

#### 275.pants. Court Judgment

(1) If the court finds that a person, by living wastefully or extravagantly or by excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances, threatens to bring themselves or their family to destitution or poverty, the court by judgment shall deprive that person of the right to manage their property, restrict their capacity to dispose of that property and establish guardianship for the person concerned. If the court, based on evidence, finds that the person's legal capacity should be restricted, it shall issue a judgment indicating the restriction of legal capacity and joint actions of the guardian with the person under guardianship or independent actions of the guardian.

(2) After the judgment enters into legal force, the court shall send it to the orphan's court — for the appointment of a guardian, as well as to the prosecutor and the person whose legal capacity has been restricted. The court shall also send information about the judgment to the Population Register and, if necessary, the judgment for entry of a notation in the land register, movable property register or other relevant public register.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 25.03.2021.)

(29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 25.03.2021. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā

#### 276.pants. Court Costs

(1) If the application is granted, court costs shall be recovered from the property of the person whose legal capacity has been restricted and for whom guardianship has been established.

(2) If the court finds the application to be unfounded, court costs shall be recovered from the person at whose application the case was initiated, but if the case was initiated at the application of the prosecutor — they shall be covered from state funds.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 07.09.2006. un 29.11.2012. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013.)

#### 277.pants. Review of Restriction of Person's Legal Capacity

When reviewing the restriction of a person's legal capacity for persons due to wasteful and extravagant living, as well as due to excessive use of alcohol or other intoxicating substances, the provisions of Chapter 33.1 of this law shall apply.

(29.11.2012. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013.)

### 34. nodaļa

Suspension of Future Agent's Rights

### (Nodaļa 29.

11.2012. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2013. Nodaļa stājas spēkā 01.07.2013. Sk. pārejas noteikumu 64.punktu un 29.11.2012. likumu)

277.1 pants. Jurisdiction

An application for the suspension of a future agent's rights according to the declared place of residence of the principal, but if there is none — according to the place of residence of the principal, may be submitted by the principal's children, brothers, sisters, parents, spouse or the prosecutor. 277.2 pants. Contents of the Application

The application shall indicate the circumstances that are grounds for suspension of the future agent's rights and attach evidence confirming these circumstances.

277.3 pants. Examination of the Application

(1) The court shall examine the case concerning the suspension of a future agent's rights with the participation of the prosecutor.

(2) The person who issued the future power of attorney shall be summoned to the court hearing.

277.4 pants. Preparation of the Case for Examination

The application shall be sent to the agent, setting a time limit, not longer than 30 days, for submission of an explanation.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

277.5 pants. Court Judgment

(1) If the court finds that the agent's activities are contrary to the principal's interests or the agent does not fulfill their duties at all, it shall suspend the rights granted to them by the future power of attorney.

(2) After the judgment enters into legal force, it shall be sent to the agent, the principal, the prosecutor and the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

277.6 pants. Court Costs

If the court finds that the agent's activities are contrary to the principal's interests or the agent does not fulfill their duties at all, court costs shall be recovered from the agent.

35.nodaļa

Establishment of Guardianship for Property of Absent or Missing Persons

#### 278.pants. Jurisdiction

Cases concerning guardianship of property of an absent or missing person shall be examined by the court according to the last place of residence of the absent or missing person.

#### 279.pants. Contents of the Application

(1) An application to establish guardianship for the property of an absent or missing person may be submitted by persons who are interested in preserving the property of the absent or missing person or in defending the rights of that person, or by the prosecutor.

(2) The application shall indicate the circumstances confirming the person's absence and the location where the property of that person is situated, for which guardianship needs to be established.

(3) If the location of the absent or missing person is known, the court shall summon them as an interested person.

#### 280.pants. Court Judgment

(1) If the court finds that the application is justified, it shall issue a judgment on the establishment of guardianship for the property of the absent or missing person.

(2) After the judgment enters into legal force, it shall be sent to the orphan's court for the appointment of a guardian and to the absent person, if their place of residence is known, but if it is not known, a notice shall be sent for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(3) (Izslēgta ar 11.11.2021. likumu)

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 07.09.2006., 29.11.2012. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 281.pants. Termination of Guardianship

Upon the occurrence of the circumstances specified in Section 375, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Law, guardianship shall be terminated by judgment of the court that established the guardianship.

36.nodaļa

Declaration of Missing Person as Dead

#### 282.pants. Jurisdiction

An application for declaration of a missing person as dead shall be submitted to the court according to the last known place of residence of that person.

#### 283.pants. Contents of the Application

The application shall indicate the name, surname, personal identity number, if known, year of birth of the missing person, as well as the time when they left their place of residence and when the last information about that person was received, and, if possible, the place of birth of the missing person, the name and surname of their parents and other information.

#### 284.pants. Notice of Missing Person

(1) After receiving the application, the judge shall issue a decision on publication of a notice in the official publication

"Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(2) The notice shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court that received the application;
- 2) the name, surname and year of birth of the person proposed to be declared dead, as well as other information about them indicated in the application;
- 3) a proposal that the missing person appear in court within three months or report their location, and also indicates that otherwise they will be declared dead;
- 4) an invitation to all who know the location of the missing person or who know about their death to report it to the court within three months.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 29.11.2012. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 285.pants. Participation of the Prosecutor

A case concerning declaration of a person as dead shall be examined with the participation of the prosecutor.

#### 286.pants. Court Judgment

(1) If the court finds that the application is justified, it shall issue a judgment declaring the missing person dead.

(2) If the court has established the presumed date of death of the missing person, it shall be indicated in the judgment.

(3) If the court cannot establish the presumed date of death, the date when the application was submitted to the court shall be considered the date of death of the missing person, which the court shall indicate in the judgment.

(4) After the judgment declaring a person dead has entered into legal force, it shall be sent to the civil registry office — for registration of the death of the missing person and to the orphan's court — for establishment of guardianship over the property of the person declared dead.

(5) After the judgment declaring a person dead has entered into legal force, the court shall send for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis" a notice indicating:

- 1) the name of the court that issued the judgment;
- 2) the name, surname, year of birth and other established personal data of the missing person;
- 3) that this person has been declared dead;
- 4) the presumed date of death of the missing person or the date on which this person is considered dead.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 07.09.2006., 29.11.2012. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 287.pants. Consequences of Appearance of a Person Declared Dead

(1) If a person who has been declared dead by court judgment appears or if their whereabouts become known, the court that issued the judgment shall, by a new judgment, revoke the judgment declaring this person dead.

(2) An application for revocation of the judgment may be submitted by the person declared dead, the person upon whose application the case was initiated, or a prosecutor.

(3) After the court judgment enters into legal force, it shall be sent to the civil registry office for annulment of the death record, and the relevant notice shall be sent for publication in the official gazette "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(As amended by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

37.nodaļa

Establishment of Legal Facts

#### 288.pants. Cases to be Heard by Court

(1) The court hears cases concerning the establishment of facts upon which the arising, modification, or termination of property and non-property rights of natural and legal persons depends.

(2) The court establishes facts concerning:

- 1) kinship relations of natural persons;
- 2) persons being dependents;
- 3) registration of adoption, registration of marriage or divorce, registration of death;
- 4) ownership of rights-establishing documents (except passports and certificates issued by civil status registration authorities) by a natural person whose first name, patronymic, surname, or birth data indicated in the document do not match this person's first name, patronymic, surname, or birth data indicated in the passport or birth certificate;
- 5) ownership of rights-establishing documents by a legal person whose name or registration data indicated in the document do not match this person's name or registration data indicated in the relevant register;
- 6) death of a person at a specific time and under specific circumstances, if the civil registry office refuses to register the death.
  - (3) The court also establishes other facts that have legal significance if the laws in force do not provide for a different procedure for their establishment.

(As amended by the law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 289.pants. Requirements for Establishment of Legal Facts

The court establishes legal facts only if it is not possible for the applicant to obtain the relevant documents confirming these facts in another manner, or if these documents have been lost, stolen, or destroyed and the possibility to restore them has been lost.

#### 290.pants. Jurisdiction

An application for establishment of a legal fact shall be submitted to the court according to the applicant's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence.

(As amended by the law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 291.pants. Content of Application

(1) The application shall indicate for what purpose the applicant needs to establish the relevant fact.

(2) Evidence shall be attached to the application confirming that it is not possible for the applicant to receive the relevant documents or that it is not possible to restore the lost, stolen, or destroyed documents.

#### 292.pants. Court Judgment

(1) Upon granting the application, the court shall indicate in the judgment what fact has been established and for what purpose.

(2) A court judgment on the establishment of a fact that is to be registered in the civil registry office or formalized in other institutions does not replace the documents issued by these institutions, but after entering into legal force is the basis for registration or formalization in these institutions.

38.nodaļa

Cases Concerning Extinguishment of Rights by Public Summons

#### 293.pants. Cases to be Heard by Public Summons

(1) The public summons procedure shall be applied only in cases specified by law.

(2) A public summons shall be issued on the basis of an application by the interested person, unless otherwise provided by law.

#### 294.pants. Submission of Application

(1) The application for issuing a public summons and extinguishment of rights shall indicate:

- 1) the circumstances on which the request for a public summons is based, specifying the evidence confirming them;
- 2) the interested persons known to the applicant;
- 3) the consequences of non-appearance of the persons summoned.
  - (2) An application for extinguishment of rights related to immovable property shall be submitted to the court according to the location of this property, but for other rights — according to the applicant's — natural person's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence or legal person's legal address, unless otherwise provided by law.

(As amended by the law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 295.pants. Preparation of Case for Hearing

(1) After accepting the application, the judge shall decide on the publication of a notice in the official gazette "Latvijas

Vēstnesis".

(2) The notice shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court where the application was received;
- 2) the first name and surname of the applicant, but for legal persons — the name;
- 3) the basis and subject of the public summons;
- 4) the deadline for claiming rights;
- 5) the consequences of failure to observe the deadline.
  - (3) The deadline, if not specified by law, shall be determined by the court, but it may not be less than three months from the date of publication of the notice.
  - (4) If the public summons relates to rights to immovable property or to claims secured by mortgage, the notice shall also be posted at the relevant district (city) court.

(As amended by the laws of 29.11.2012, 25.10.2018, and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 296.pants. Hearing of Application

(1) The court shall hear the case after the expiration of the deadline indicated in the notice, summoning the applicant, the interested persons indicated by the applicant, as well as the persons who have claimed their rights within the deadline.

(2) An application for rights submitted after the deadline indicated in the notice but before the judgment is issued in the case shall be deemed to have been submitted within the deadline.

(3) If in connection with the public summons a dispute arises concerning rights that may affect the judgment in the case, the court shall suspend the proceedings, setting a deadline for filing a claim.

(4) If the claim is not filed within the specified deadline or a judgment on the resolution of the dispute has been submitted, the proceedings shall be resumed.

#### 297.pants. Court Judgment

(1) Upon granting the application, the court shall issue a judgment recognizing all rights not claimed within the deadline as invalid.

(2) (Deleted by the law of 25.10.2018)

(As amended by the law of 25.10.2018, which entered into force on 28.11.2018.)

39.nodaļa

Restoration of Rights under Debt Instruments or Bearer Securities

#### 298.pants. Submission of Application

In cases where a debt instrument or bearer security has been lost, stolen, or destroyed, the creditor or the person to whom the document has been pledged, deposited, entrusted for management or commission, or otherwise entrusted, as well as its last holder, if the document was issued to bearer or the document had a blank endorsement, may request the court to annul this document and restore the rights under it

#### 299.pants. Jurisdiction

An application for annulment of a lost, stolen, or destroyed document and restoration of rights shall be submitted to the court according to the place of payment indicated in the document, but if the place of payment is not known — to the court according to the debtor's — natural person's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence or legal person's legal address; if it is also not known — according to the place of issue of the document.

(As amended by the law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 300.pants. Content of Application

(1) The application for annulment of a lost, stolen, or destroyed document shall indicate:

- 1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
- 2) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
- 3) the name, content, and distinguishing features of the document;
- 4) the circumstances under which the document was lost, stolen, or destroyed.
  - (2) If possible, a copy of the document shall be attached to the application.

(As amended by the laws of 29.11.2012, 23.11.2016, and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 301.pants. Preparation of the Case for Examination

(1) After accepting the application, the judge decides:

- 1) on a prohibition for the person who must fulfil an obligation under the document to make payments or deliveries under this document;
- 2) on the publication of an announcement in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".
  - (2) The announcement shall indicate:
- 1) the name of the court where the application was received;
- 2) the first name and surname of the applicant, but if the applicant is a legal person — its name and legal address;
- 3) the name, content and distinguishing features of the lost, stolen or destroyed document;
- 4) a proposal to the holder of the document to submit to the court within three months, but to the holder of a bill of exchange or cheque — within two months from the date of publication of the announcement, an application regarding their rights to this document, and also indicates that otherwise the document may be declared annulled.
  - (3) The court sends the decision provided for in paragraph 1 of the first part of this Article to the person who must fulfil an obligation in accordance with the document, and also notifies all persons mentioned in the document of the adopted decision, if possible.

(As amended by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 302.pants. Obligation of the Document Holder

(1) The document holder, after being notified of the loss, theft or destruction of the document, has the obligation to submit to the court that adopted the decision, within the time limit specified in the announcement, an application regarding their rights to this document together with the original document.

(2) If the document holder has not submitted such an application, but their rights are affected by the annulment of the document, they may defend their affected rights in claim proceedings.

#### 303.pants. Court Action After Receiving an Application from the Document Holder

(1) If an application from the document holder is received by the court within the time limit specified in the announcement, the court leaves without consideration the application of the person requesting to annul the document, and sets a time limit during which it is prohibited to make payments and deliveries in accordance with the document. This time limit may not exceed two months.

(2) At the same time, the court explains to the applicant their right to file a claim against the document holder for recovery of this document, and to the document holder — their right to demand from the submitter damages caused by the prohibition measures established by the court.

(3) An ancillary complaint may be filed against the court decision.

#### 304.pants. Examination of the Application

(1) The court examines the case on the annulment of the document and restoration of rights after the expiry of the time limit specified in the announcement, if no application has been received from the document holder.

(2) The court notifies the submitter and the person who issued the document, as well as all persons mentioned in the document, if possible, of the time and place of the examination of the case. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the case.

#### 305.pants. Court Judgment

(1) If the court finds that the document specified in the application has been lost, stolen or destroyed and that the applicant was the lawful holder of this document, it makes a judgment on the annulment of this document and restoration of the applicant's rights.

(2) A court judgment that has entered into legal force is the basis for issuing a new document in place of the annulled document, if this is provided for by law.

(3) If the law does not provide for the possibility of issuing a new document, the judgment is the basis for demanding satisfaction of the rights arising from the annulled document.

45.nodaļa

Redemption of Immovable Property

#### 336.pants. Jurisdiction Over Cases

An application for redemption of immovable property shall be submitted to the court according to the location of the immovable property to be redeemed.

#### 337.pants. Content of the Application

(1) The application shall indicate the location of the immovable property to be redeemed, its acquirer and the basis for the right of redemption

(Article 1382 of the Civil Law).

(2) The following shall be attached to the application:

- 1) a copy of the act on the basis of which the immovable property was alienated;
- 2) evidence of the submitter's right to redeem the immovable property;
- 3) information about the sale price of the immovable property, alienation costs and duties and their payment.

#### 338.pants. Sending the Application to the Acquirer of Immovable Property

The court sends the application to the acquirer of the immovable property, setting a one-month time limit for submitting an explanation and providing information about necessary and useful expenses made for the immovable property.

(As amended by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 339.pants. Examination of the Application

The application shall be examined in a court session to which the applicant and the acquirer of the immovable property are invited.

#### 340.pants. Court Judgment

Having found the application well-founded, the court makes a judgment on the submitter's right of redemption to the immovable property and the right of the acquirer of the property being redeemed to reimbursement of expenses.

#### 341.pants. Leaving the Application Without Consideration

If the acquirer of the immovable property disputes the submitter's right of redemption, the court leaves the application without consideration, explaining to the parties that the dispute shall be resolved in claim proceedings.

### Chapter 45

Legal Protection Proceedings Cases

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 30.09.2010., which comes into force on 01.11.2010.)

Article 341.1. Jurisdiction of Legal Protection Proceedings Cases

The court examines legal protection proceedings cases according to the debtor's legal address which was registered for the debtor three months before the submission of the application to the court.

(In the wording of the law of 08.12.2016., which comes into force on 04.01.2017.)

Article 341.2. Content of the Legal Protection Proceedings Application

(1) The legal protection proceedings application shall indicate:

- 1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);
- 2) that with respect to the debtor there do not exist the restrictions established in the Insolvency Law for the initiation of legal protection proceedings cases;
- 3) whether with respect to the debtor a legal protection proceedings case has been initiated within a year, but implementation of legal protection proceedings has not been declared;
- 4) the debtor's legal address which was registered for the debtor three months before the submission of the application to the court;
- 5) a candidate for the position of supervisor of the legal protection proceedings (hereinafter - the supervisor) and contact information;
- 6) if the debtor is an individual merchant - information about the respective natural person (name, surname and personal identity number);
- 7) if the debtor is an individual (family) enterprise, farm or fishing farm - information about the owner (natural person's name, surname and personal identity number).
  - (2) The following documents shall be attached to the application, confirming:
- 1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);
- 2) the circumstances on which the application is based;
- 3) payment of the legal person's insolvency proceedings deposit in the case when the legal protection proceedings application is submitted repeatedly within a year;
- 4) the candidate for the position of supervisor's consent to be appointed as supervisor and confirmation of compliance with the requirements of Article 12.3 of the Insolvency Law, as well as the ability to ensure the performance of duties if a cross-border element exists with respect to the debtor.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 08.12.2016., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Article 341.3. Receipt and Registration of the Legal Protection Proceedings Application

(1) The court accepts the legal protection proceedings application from the debtor on whose behalf the application is submitted, or from a person who is authorised to submit the application. The legal protection proceedings application shall be submitted in person in paper form or in the online system.

(2) Having received the legal protection proceedings application, the court verifies the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant who submitted the application in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the appropriate authorisation, the application shall not be accepted.

(3) The legal protection proceedings application shall be registered in a separate register, which is signed by the applicant and the recipient. If the legal protection proceedings application is received in the online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 341.4. Initiation of Legal Protection Proceedings Cases

(1) Within five days after receipt of the legal protection proceedings application, the judge shall adopt a decision:

- 1) to leave the legal protection proceedings application without movement;
- 2) to refuse to accept the legal protection proceedings application;
- 3) to accept the legal protection proceedings application and initiate the case.
  - (2) If the legal protection proceedings application is left without movement, the judge shall adopt a decision to accept the legal protection proceedings application and initiate the case no later than the next day after the elimination of deficiencies indicated in the decision. If the time limit for eliminating the deficiencies indicated in the decision has expired and they have not been eliminated, the application shall be deemed not submitted and returned to the applicant.
  - (3) When accepting the legal protection proceedings application and initiating the case, the judge shall adopt a decision on the candidate for the position of supervisor's compliance with the performance of duties in the respective legal protection proceedings and on his or her appointment as supervisor, simultaneously indicating the supervisor's contact information.
  - (4) Having established that with respect to the candidate for the position of supervisor proposed by the debtor there exist restrictions on the performance of duties in the specific legal protection proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the application without movement and send to the debtor an invitation to submit information about a new candidate for the position of supervisor.

(With amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Article 341.5. Court Actions to be Performed and Issues to be Decided After the Adoption of a Decision on the Initiation of Legal Protection Proceedings Cases

(1) The court decision on the initiation of legal protection proceedings cases shall be immediately sent to:

- 1) the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register;
- 2) the Bank of Latvia, if the decision is adopted regarding a financial market participant whose operations are supervised by the Bank of Latvia in accordance with the requirements of regulatory enactments;
- 3) the administrator of the procedure specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if in Latvia the case has been initiated following an application for the commencement of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(2) After the adoption of a decision on the initiation of legal protection proceedings cases, the judge:

- 1) adopts a decision on the removal of the supervisor, as well as on the candidate for the position of new supervisor's compliance with the performance of duties in the respective legal protection proceedings and on his or her appointment as supervisor;
- 2) decides on permission to sell the pledged property of the debtor following the application of a secured creditor (Article 37, paragraph two of the Insolvency Law);
- 3) decides on the extension or cancellation of the consequences provided for in Article 37, paragraph one, Points 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the Insolvency Law.
  - (3) (Deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.)
  - (4) (Deleted by the law of 01.06.2017.)
  - (5) (Deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.)
  - (6) Having established that with respect to the candidate for the position of supervisor proposed by the debtor there exist restrictions on the performance of the supervisor's duties in the specific legal protection proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the supervisor and send to the debtor an invitation to submit information about a new candidate for the position of supervisor.
  - (7) The decision on the appointment of the supervisor shall be sent to the supervisor and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Article 341.6. Procedure for Examination of the Legal Protection Proceedings Application and Decision in Legal Protection Proceedings Cases

(1) The court shall examine the legal protection proceedings application in written proceedings, except in the case when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the legal protection proceedings application is examined in a court session, the debtor and the supervisor shall be invited to the session. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the case.

(11) If the application has been submitted for the commencement of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall examine the application within the time limit specified in paragraph two of this Article in written proceedings, except in the case when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the applicant, the debtor and the administrators of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) and (2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be invited to the session. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the case.

(2) The court shall examine the legal protection proceedings application within 15 days from:

- 1) (deleted by the law of 31.05.2018.);
- 2) the day when the legal protection proceedings action plan was submitted to the court.
  - (21) A creditor whose claim the supervisor has recognised as prima facie unfounded, or a creditor who has expressed doubts about the validity of another creditor's claim, may request the court to summon or allow him or her in the case as an interested person. The creditor shall attach evidence of the validity of his or her claim to the request. The decision by which the request for the summoning or admission of an interested person in the case is granted or rejected shall not be subject to appeal.
  - (3) The court shall grant the application and make a judgment on the implementation of legal protection proceedings if, based on the supervisor's opinion and other evidence, as well as evaluating the sworn auditor's opinion, if such is attached to the legal protection proceedings action plan, and creditors' objections, if such have been received, it establishes that the legal protection proceedings action plan:
- 1) complies with the requirements of the Insolvency Law, including will ensure the achievement of the purpose of legal protection proceedings;
- 2) is supported in the manner and time limit established in the Insolvency Law.
  - (31) If, based on the supervisor's opinion and other evidence, the court establishes that the legal protection proceedings action plan contains obligations regarding which there is a dispute concerning rights, and the scope of obligations substantially affects the approval of the legal protection proceedings action plan, the court shall leave the legal protection proceedings application without examination.
  - (32) The court shall evaluate the compliance of the legal protection proceedings action plan with Article 40, paragraph four, Point 15 of the Insolvency Law only in the case when creditors' objections have been received regarding the non-compliance of the legal protection proceedings action plan with the mentioned provision of the Insolvency Law.
  - (4) If the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been commenced against the debtor in Latvia and the administrator of the main proceedings has not approved the legal protection proceedings action plan in the manner established in the Insolvency Law, the court shall grant the application and make a judgment on the implementation of legal protection proceedings if it establishes that the implementation of legal protection proceedings is in the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of the mentioned regulation.
  - (41) When examining an application for the commencement of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall take into account the provisions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
  - (42) When declaring insolvency proceedings in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall indicate in the judgment the type of insolvency proceedings, if the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are commenced, or indicate in the decision referred to in paragraph 4.3 of this Article the type of insolvency proceedings, if the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are commenced.

(43) If the court establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia, it shall declare a judgment on the commencement of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and adopt a decision by which it establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to commence the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. Regarding the court decision by which it has been established that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to commence the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the debtor or any creditor may submit a complaint in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the day of pronouncement of the decision. The submission of a complaint shall not suspend the commencement of insolvency proceedings.

(44) The court shall commence the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the debtor conducts or has conducted economic activity in Latvia within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council during a period of three months before the submission of the application. The court, having established that the court of another Member State, which commenced the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of this regulation against the debtor, was entitled to commence such proceedings, shall make a judgment on the commencement of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor. The court shall not commence the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the conditions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have occurred.

(5) When making a judgment on the implementation of legal protection proceedings, the court shall approve the legal protection proceedings action plan and simultaneously decide on the appointment of the supervisor, if it is provided for in the legal protection proceedings action plan. Having established that with respect to the candidate for the position of supervisor indicated in the legal protection proceedings action plan there exist restrictions on the performance of duties in the specific legal protection proceedings, the court shall leave the legal protection proceedings application without examination.

(6) In the judgment on the implementation of legal protection proceedings, the court shall indicate the list of pledged property to which the restrictions for secured creditors to exercise their rights are applicable until the termination of legal protection proceedings.

(7) When rejecting the legal protection proceedings application, the court shall simultaneously terminate the legal protection proceedings and collect court costs from the applicant of the legal protection proceedings application.

(8) The court judgment in a legal protection proceedings case may be appealed in the appeal procedure if there exists one of the grounds for the initiation of appeal proceedings specified in Article 440.2 of this Law. The appeal of the court judgment shall not suspend its execution.

(9) The judgment shall be issued to the applicant of the legal protection proceedings application and to the supervisor, as well as sent to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Article 341.7. Decision on the Implementation of Legal Protection Proceedings in Out-of-Court Legal Protection Proceedings

(1) In legal protection proceedings cases in out-of-court legal protection proceedings, the provisions of this Chapter shall apply if this Article does not provide otherwise.

(2) The court shall examine the legal protection proceedings application in out-of-court legal protection proceedings within 15 days in written proceedings, except in the case when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the application in a legal protection proceedings case is examined in a court session, the debtor and the supervisor shall be invited to the session. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the case.

(3) After the adoption of a decision on the initiation of legal protection proceedings cases in out-of-court legal protection proceedings, the court shall not decide the issue of permission to sell the pledged property of the debtor following the application of a secured creditor and on the appointment of the supervisor.

(4) If the conditions established in the Insolvency Law for the implementation of legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings exist, the court shall adopt a decision on the implementation of legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings and approve the legal protection proceedings action plan, as well as simultaneously appoint the supervisor indicated in the legal protection proceedings action plan, if the debtor has requested to approve the legal protection proceedings action plan in the manner specified in Article 42, paragraph 3.1 of the Insolvency Law or if the appointment of the supervisor has been requested by the debtor or the majority of creditors specified in Article 42, paragraph three of the Insolvency Law.

(5) A complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision in a legal protection proceedings case in out-of-court legal protection proceedings. The submission of a complaint shall not suspend the execution of the decision.

(6) The decision shall be issued to the applicant and to the supervisor, as well as sent to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015., 01.06.2017., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Article 341.8. Issues to be Decided After the Adoption of a Decision on the Implementation of Legal Protection Proceedings

(1) After the adoption of a decision on the implementation of legal protection proceedings, following a respective application, the court shall decide on:

- 1) amendments to the legal protection proceedings action plan;
- 2) the removal of the supervisor, setting a time limit for the preparation of the document and property acceptance and transfer act and for the transfer of documents and property;
- 3) the appointment of a new candidate for the position of supervisor as supervisor, if the previous supervisor has been removed from the respective legal protection proceedings;
- 31) the replacement of the supervisor;
- 32) the appointment of the supervisor for the supervision of the implementation of the legal protection proceedings action plan, if the supervisor has not previously been appointed for the supervision of the implementation of the legal protection proceedings action plan;
- 4) the performance of actions provided for in Article 51 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council;
- 5) the termination of legal protection proceedings.
  - (2) The supervisor may be removed by the court on its own initiative if it, when examining the application in a legal protection proceedings case, establishes that the supervisor does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or does not fulfil the court decision, or does not comply with the requirements of the Insolvency Law.
  - (3) The court shall send the decisions referred to in paragraph one of this Article to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. After the adoption of this decision, the court shall immediately send the decision on the removal of the supervisor to the debtor.
  - (4) After the receipt of the application of the majority of creditors specified in Article 42, paragraph three of the Insolvency Law, the court shall immediately decide on the appointment of the candidate for the position of supervisor as supervisor, if with respect to him or her there do not exist the restrictions established in the Insolvency Law on the performance of this duty in the respective legal protection proceedings. If within 15 days from the day when the supervisor's application for withdrawal from the specific legal protection proceedings has been received or a decision on the removal of the supervisor has been adopted, which is not based on the supervisor's application for withdrawal from the specific legal protection proceedings, and the majority of creditors specified in Article 42, paragraph three of the Insolvency Law have not submitted to the court a proposal regarding a candidate for the position of supervisor, the court shall decide on the termination of legal protection proceedings. The decision shall be sent to the Insolvency Control Service, the debtor and the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.
  - (5) For the examination of the issues referred to in this Article, the court may request that the supervisor of the legal protection proceedings submit a report of his or her activities or other information.
  - (6) The court shall examine the application within 15 days from the day of its receipt. The judge shall examine the application in written proceedings, without holding a court session, except in the case when he or she considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session or it is requested by a participant in the proceedings whose interests are affected by the application. The applicant, the supervisor, the representative of the debtor and other interested persons shall be invited to the court session. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the issue.
  - (7) Following the examination of the application, the court shall adopt a decision which is not subject to appeal. The court decision on the removal of the supervisor of legal protection proceedings on the basis of Point 1, 4 or 5 of Article 12.4, paragraph two of the Insolvency Law is subject to appeal in the part regarding the established non-compliance with the requirements of regulatory enactments or non-fulfilment of the court decision, or non-compliance with the requirements of the Insolvency Law, by submitting a complaint. The regional court shall examine this complaint within 15 days.
  - (8) The regional court, when examining the complaint referred to in paragraph seven of this Article, has the right to:
- 1) leave the decision unchanged but reject the complaint;
- 2) annul the decision and decide the issue on the merits by its decision.
  - (9) The decision referred to in paragraph eight of this Article shall come into force and is enforceable immediately.
  - (10) The decision referred to in paragraph eight, Point 1 of this Article shall be sent to the debtor.
  - (11) The regional court shall examine within 15 days the debtor's or creditor's complaint regarding the court decision by which it has been established that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to commence the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
  - (12) In the complaint referred to in paragraph eleven of this Article, in addition to the information provided for in Article 443.1 of this Law, the following shall be indicated:
- 1) from what time the debtor's legal address is located or main economic activity is conducted in the indicated Member State of the European Union;
- 2) facts showing that the debtor usually exercises his or her main interests in the Member State of the European Union indicated in the complaint;
- 3) information about creditors or a substantial part of assets, or economic activity in another Member State of the European Union;
- 4) whether the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been commenced against the debtor in another Member State of the European Union.
  - (13) The regional court, when examining the complaint referred to in paragraph eleven of this Article, has the right to:
- 1) leave the decision unchanged but reject the complaint;
- 2) annul the decision completely.
