  - (14) If the regional court has annulled the decision, the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall continue as the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) or (4) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
  - (15) The court shall also send the decision on the complaint to the administrator and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 21.06.2012., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Article 341.9. Examination in Court of Complaints Regarding the Decision Adopted by the Insolvency Administration Regarding the Administrator's Actions in Legal Protection Proceedings or the Imposition of a Legal Obligation

(Deleted by the law of 01.06.2017., which comes into force on 01.07.2017. See Transitional Provision Point 125)

Article 341.10. Decision on the Termination of Legal Protection Proceedings

(1) The court shall examine the issue of the termination of legal protection proceedings on its own initiative or following the debtor's application.

(2) The court on its own initiative shall adopt a decision on the termination of legal protection proceedings in the case specified in Article 341.8, paragraph four of this Law and in Article 51, paragraph one of the Insolvency Law.

(3) The court following the debtor's application shall adopt a decision on the termination of legal protection proceedings in the case specified in Article 51, paragraph four of the Insolvency Law.

(4) In the case specified in paragraph three of this Article, the debtor shall attach to the application for the termination of legal protection proceedings the supervisor's written opinion on the implementation of the legal protection proceedings action plan.

(41) The court following the application of the administrator of the procedure specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, submitted in accordance with Article 39 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may terminate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(5) The court shall immediately send the decision on the termination of legal protection proceedings to the applicant, the supervisor, as well as to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 341.11. Decision on the Termination of Legal Protection Proceedings by Declaring Insolvency Proceedings of a Legal Person or Natural Person

(1) The court on its own initiative shall adopt a decision on the termination of legal protection proceedings if insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person are declared based on Point 8 or 9 of Article 57, paragraph one of the Insolvency Law.

(2) The court on its own initiative shall adopt a decision on the termination of legal protection proceedings and declare insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person in the case specified in Article 51, paragraph two of the Insolvency Law.

(3) The court shall adopt a decision on the termination of legal protection proceedings and declare insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person following the application of the person referred to in Article 37(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if it establishes that the performance of actions provided for in Article 51 of this regulation is in the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of the mentioned regulation.

(4) The application for insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person in the case specified in paragraph one of this Article shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the legal protection proceedings case is located.

(5) The court shall immediately send the decision on the termination of legal protection proceedings to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Article 341.12. Examination in Court of Complaints Regarding the Decision Adopted by the Insolvency Control Service Regarding the Supervisor's Actions in Legal Protection Proceedings or Regarding the Imposition of a Legal Obligation

(1) The court shall examine the complaint of a creditor, debtor's representative, supervisor or third person whose legal rights are infringed, regarding the decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding the supervisor's actions in legal protection proceedings or regarding the imposition of a legal obligation. The court shall examine in the manner specified in this Article the complaint regarding the decision of the Insolvency Control Service which has been adopted after the termination of the respective legal protection proceedings.

(2) If the court recognises that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and decide on:

- 1) the annulment of the decision of the Insolvency Control Service in whole or in part;
- 2) the imposition of an obligation on the Insolvency Control Service to adopt or examine a complaint regarding the supervisor's actions;
- 3) the imposition of an obligation on the supervisor to eliminate the committed violation, except in cases when a decision has been adopted on the termination of the respective legal protection proceedings.
  - (3) Having established that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall reject the complaint.
  - (4) The complainant has the right to withdraw his or her complaint before the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on the termination of the complaint proceedings.
  - (5) After the examination of the complaint, the court shall immediately send a copy of the decision to the Insolvency Control Service.
  - (6) If the decision of the Insolvency Control Service regarding the supervisor's actions in legal protection proceedings has been adopted within a year after the termination of the respective legal protection proceedings, the complaint regarding the decision of the Insolvency Control Service shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the respective legal protection proceedings case was located.

(In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023., which comes into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision Point 179)

Chapter 46

Legal Protection Proceedings Cases

(Chapter deleted by the law of 30.09.2010., which comes into force on 01.11.2010.)

### Chapter 46

Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings Cases

(Chapter as worded by law of 30.09.2010., which comes into force on 01.11.2010.)

Article 363.1. Jurisdiction of Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings Cases

(1) The court shall examine legal entity insolvency proceedings cases according to an application by the debtor, creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section

42 of the Insolvency Law, based on the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before submission of the application to the court. (2) A case for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be examined by the court based on the location of the debtor's centre of main interests, but in the case of initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of this Regulation — based on the location of the debtor's establishment (within the meaning of point 10 of Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council). (With amendments made by laws of 29.11.2012., 08.12.2016., 01.06.2017. and 31.05.2018., which come into force

Article 363.2. Content of Creditor's or Creditors' Majority Legal Entity Insolvency Application

(1) A creditor shall indicate in a legal entity insolvency application (hereinafter in this Chapter — insolvency application):

- 1) (deleted by law of 11.11.2021.); - 2) (deleted by law of 11.11.2021.); - 3) the insolvency indicator; - 4) the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before submission of the application to the court. - (11) If the application is submitted by several creditors or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law, the information referred to in point 1.1 of the first paragraph of Section 254 of this Law shall be indicated for each creditor on whose authorisation the insolvency application is submitted. - (2) When submitting an insolvency application, the creditor shall attach a document certifying payment of the insolvency deposit. - (3) When submitting an insolvency application in accordance with the insolvency indicator referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law, evidence of the basis and amount of the claim, as well as a certificate issued by a bailiff regarding the impossibility of recovering the debt from the debtor, shall be attached to the application. - (4) When submitting an insolvency application in accordance with the insolvency indicator referred to in points 2 and
    - 3 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law, evidence of the basis and amount of the claim, a copy of the warning of intent to submit an insolvency application, documents regarding issuance or dispatch of the warning (receipt for dispatch of the document with confirmation of the content of the shipment) shall be attached to the application, and the application shall confirm that the debtor has not raised substantiated objections against it. - (5) When submitting an insolvency application in accordance with the insolvency indicator referred to in point 4 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law, the application shall indicate the period for which wages and compensation for harm have not been paid, and there shall be attached a certificate issued by the employer regarding the amount of wages and mandatory social insurance contributions, but if the employer has not issued the said certificate, this fact shall be indicated in the application. - (51) When submitting an insolvency application in accordance with the indicator referred to in point 7 or 8 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law, in addition to the information referred to in the first paragraph of this Section, the application shall indicate the case number of the legal protection proceedings. Documents substantiating the facts stated in the application shall be attached to the application. - (6) When submitting an insolvency application regarding initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 or 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, the creditor shall indicate the basis of the application and attach to it evidence confirming the circumstances on which the application is based, if such evidence is in his or her possession. - (7) When submitting an insolvency application regarding initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, the creditor shall send it to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of the said Regulation. (With amendments made by laws of 29.11.2012., 08.12.2016., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which come into force on 01.12.2021. The provision of the second paragraph regarding insolvency deposit payment, insofar as it relates to employees whose only legal remedy is declaration of the employer's insolvency, has been declared inconsistent with the first sentence of Article 92 of the Satversme of the Republic of Latvia by the Constitutional Court judgment of 20.04.2012., which comes into force on 24.04.2012.)

Article 363.3. Content of Debtor's Insolvency Application

(1) An insolvency application on behalf of the debtor may be submitted by the management institution or members of a personal company who have representation rights, or a specially authorised person. (2) The debtor shall indicate in the insolvency application:

- 1) (deleted by law of 11.11.2021.); - 2) the insolvency indicator; - 3) information on the location of the debtor's centre of main interests within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; - 4) whether the debtor conducts or has conducted establishment within another Member State of the European Union in the three-month period before submission of the application within the meaning of point
  - 10 of Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and its location; - 5) the case number of the legal protection proceedings if the insolvency application is submitted in accordance with the insolvency indicator referred to in point 9 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law; - 6) the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before submission of the application to the court. - (3) The debtor shall attach to the insolvency application:
- 1) a list of members of management institutions, auditors (members of audit institutions) and procurators, indicating first name, surname, address and other information by which they are identifiable and reachable; - 2) evidence that the company's shareholders (members), members of the association or other founders or members of the legal entity have been notified of the intention to submit an insolvency application; - 3) evidence of representation rights; - 4) a document certifying payment of the insolvency deposit. - (4) When submitting an application for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, in addition to the documents specified in the third paragraph of this Section, the debtor shall attach to the insolvency application a confirmation regarding the location of the debtor's centre of main interests. (With amendments made by laws of 29.11.2012., 18.04.2013., 08.12.2016., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which come into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.4. Content of Debtor's Insolvency Application in Liquidation Proceedings

(1) An insolvency application on behalf of the debtor shall be submitted by the liquidator in accordance with the insolvency indicator referred to in point 6 of the first paragraph of Section

57 of the Insolvency Law. (2) The provisions of the second, third and fourth paragraphs of Section 363.3 of this Law shall apply to the liquidator's insolvency application. (With amendments made by law of 01.06.2017., which comes into force on 01.07.2017.)

Article 363.5. Content of Insolvency Application by Person Referred to in Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council

(1) The person referred to in point (a) of paragraph 1 of Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall submit an insolvency application to the court to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of this Regulation against the debtor. (2) The person referred to in point (a) of paragraph 1 of Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall indicate in the insolvency application:

- 1) the debtor's firm (name), registration number and legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before submission of the application to the court, and the legal address on the day of submission of the application; - 2) the name of the court that has initiated insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, the date of adoption and entry into force of the court decision; 3) the basis for initiating insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor; 4) information on whether insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor in another Member State of the European Union (hereinafter — Member State). (3) The person referred to in point (a) of paragraph 1 of Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall attach to the insolvency application:

- 1) the court decision on initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor and its translation into the official language certified in the prescribed manner; - 2) the court decision or other confirmation of appointment of an administrator in the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and its translation into the official language certified in the prescribed manner; - 3) documents certifying that the debtor conducts or has conducted establishment in Latvia in the three-month period before submission of the application within the meaning of point
  - 10 of Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; - 4) a document certifying payment of the insolvency deposit. (With amendments made by laws of 29.11.2012., 08.12.2016., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which come into force

Article 363.6. Content of Administrator's Insolvency Application

(Deleted by law of 01.06.2017., which comes into force on 01.07.2017. See transitional provision 125)

Article 363.7. Receipt and Registration of Insolvency Application

(1) The court shall accept an insolvency application from the debtor on whose behalf the application is submitted or from a person authorised to submit the application. An insolvency application shall be submitted in person in paper form or in an online system. (2) Having received an insolvency application, the court shall verify the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant of an application submitted in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the appropriate authorisation, the application shall not be accepted. (3) An insolvency application shall be registered in a separate register, which shall be signed by the applicant and the recipient. If the insolvency application has been received in the online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient. (With amendments made by law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.8. Prohibition to Amend Subject of Insolvency Application and Debtor's Withdrawal of Insolvency Application

(1) Amendment of the subject of an insolvency application is not permitted in insolvency cases. (2) The debtor is not entitled to withdraw an insolvency application.

Article 363.9. Decision on Acceptance of Insolvency Application and Initiation of Case

(1) Within five days after receipt of an insolvency application, the judge shall adopt a decision:

- 1) to leave the insolvency application without movement; - 2) to refuse to accept the insolvency application; - 3) to accept the insolvency application and initiate the case. - (2) If an insolvency application has been left without movement, the judge shall adopt a decision to accept the insolvency application and initiate the case no later than the next day after rectification of the deficiencies indicated in the decision. If the time limit for rectification of the deficiencies indicated in the decision has expired and they have not been rectified, the application shall be deemed not submitted and shall be returned to the applicant. - (3) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the insolvency application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law if it is established that a legal entity insolvency case has been initiated against the debtor based on the debtor's insolvency application. - (4) The court shall initiate a legal entity insolvency case on its own initiative if, when adopting a decision to terminate legal protection proceedings, it establishes the legal entity insolvency indicator specified in point 7 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law. - (5) The judge shall adopt a decision to consolidate the initiated legal entity insolvency case in one set of proceedings if, before commencement of examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency case initiated based on an insolvency application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law, it is established that a legal entity insolvency case has been initiated against the debtor based on an insolvency application of another creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law. - (6) The judge shall adopt a decision to suspend proceedings in a case based on an insolvency application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law if, before commencement of examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency case initiated based on an insolvency application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law, it is established that a legal entity insolvency case has been initiated against the debtor based on the debtor's insolvency application. Upon declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings based on the debtor's insolvency application, the court shall resume proceedings in the suspended case based on the insolvency application of the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law and shall terminate it. The state fee paid shall be refunded to the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law in full. (With amendments made by laws of 18.04.2013., 01.06.2017. and 16.03.2023., which come into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Article 363.10. Court Actions in Preparing Legal Entity Insolvency Case for Hearing

(1) The judge shall send the decision on initiation of the case without delay to:

- 1) (deleted by law of 31.05.2018.); - 2) the Bank of Latvia if the decision has been adopted regarding a financial market participant whose activities are supervised by the Bank of Latvia in accordance with the requirements of regulatory enactments; - 3) the administrator of the proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if the case has been initiated in Latvia based on an application for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) the debtor. (2) If the case has been initiated based on an insolvency application of a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law, the judge shall send to the debtor the application of the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law and the decision on initiation of the case, shall inform the debtor and the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law of the date of examination of the insolvency application, as well as of the debtor's right to raise substantiated objections to the claim specified in the insolvency application, including to provide evidence that the debtor is able to cover the obligations specified in the insolvency application, no later than three days before the date of examination of the insolvency application. (3) After initiation of a legal entity insolvency case, a candidate for the position of administrator shall be selected from the list of candidates for the position of administrator (hereinafter — the List of Candidates) maintained in the Electronic Insolvency Accounting System of the Insolvency Control Service, using automated selection ensured by the Court Information System, and the judge shall assess his or her suitability for performing the duties of administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings. (4) Having established that there are restrictions for the candidate for the position of administrator to perform the duties of administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. A new candidate for the position of administrator shall be selected from the List of Candidates using automated selection ensured by the Court Information System, and the judge shall assess his or her suitability for performing the duties of administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings. (With amendments made by laws of 18.04.2013., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which come into force on 29.03.2023.)

Article 363.11. Procedure for Examination of Insolvency Application

(1) An insolvency application submitted by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law shall be examined by the court within 15 days from the date of initiation of the case. The applicant of the insolvency application and the debtor shall be summoned to the court session. If several creditors' insolvency applications have been consolidated in one set of proceedings, those applicants shall be summoned to the court session regarding whom it is possible to notify about the court session at least seven days before the relevant session. The failure of these persons to appear is not an obstacle to examination of the case. (2) An insolvency application submitted by the debtor shall be examined by the court in written proceedings within seven days from the date of initiation of the case. The application shall be examined by the court in written proceedings, except when it deems it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the insolvency application is examined in a court session, the debtor shall be summoned to the session. The failure of this person to appear is not an obstacle to examination of the case. (3) (Deleted by law of 01.06.2017.)

(31) If an application has been submitted for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the application shall be examined in written proceedings within 15 days from the date of initiation of the case or, if the court deems it necessary, in a court session. If the insolvency application is examined in a court session, the applicant, the debtor and the administrator of the insolvency proceedings specified in point

3 of Article 1 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be summoned to the session. The failure of these persons to appear is not an obstacle to examination of the case. (4) If by the time of drafting the judgment the court establishes that the applicant has not paid the state fee or the insolvency deposit, except when the court has initiated a legal entity insolvency case on its own initiative or has exempted an employee from payment of the deposit, it shall leave the insolvency application without examination. The exception specified in this paragraph does not apply to cases where a legal protection proceedings application has been submitted repeatedly within one year. (5) The judge may adopt a decision to fully or partially exempt an employee from payment of the insolvency deposit if he or she submits the insolvency application after it has not been possible to execute a court decision on recovery of debt from the debtor by applying enforcement measures and the employee, taking into account his or her financial situation, cannot pay the insolvency deposit. (6) When examining an application for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall take into account the provisions of Article

38 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (With amendments made by laws of 18.04.2013., 12.02.2015., 01.06.2017. and 31.05.2018., which come into force on 01.07.2018. See transitional provision 146)

Article 363.12. Order of Examination of Insolvency Application and Legal Protection Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall suspend proceedings if, before commencement of examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency case, it establishes that a legal protection proceedings case has been initiated with respect to the debtor. (2) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency case shall be suspended until a decision is adopted in the legal protection proceedings case. (3) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency case shall be terminated if, in accordance with a decision, legal protection proceedings are implemented with respect to the debtor. (4) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency case shall be resumed and examined in the procedure specified in this Chapter if legal protection proceedings with respect to the debtor are terminated on the basis of the second paragraph of Section 341.10 of this Law.

Article 363.13. Court Decision in Legal Entity Insolvency Case

(1) Legal entity insolvency proceedings shall be declared by the court, and its judgment is not subject to appeal, except for a judgment by which a legal entity insolvency application has been refused. A judgment by which a legal entity insolvency application has been refused may be appealed in appellate proceedings if there is one of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings specified in Section 440.2 of this Law. (2) The court shall declare legal entity insolvency proceedings if on the day of examination of the application it establishes the insolvency indicator specified in the application. (3) Upon granting the application, the court shall appoint the candidate for the position of administrator selected in the procedure specified in Section 363.10 of this Law as administrator. (4) When declaring insolvency proceedings in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall indicate in the judgment the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated, or shall indicate in the decision referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Section the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated. (5) If the court establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia, it shall declare a judgment on initiation of the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and shall adopt a decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The debtor or any creditor may submit a subsidiary appeal in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the court decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the date of declaration of the decision. The submission of a subsidiary appeal does not suspend the initiation of insolvency proceedings. (6) The court shall initiate the insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the debtor conducts or has conducted establishment in Latvia within the meaning of point

2 of Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council in the three-month period before submission of the application. Having established that the court of another Member State that has initiated the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor had the right to initiate such proceedings, the court shall issue a judgment on initiation of the insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, without observing the provisions of the second paragraph of this Section. The court shall not initiate the insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the conditions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been met. (7) The court, when declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings and terminating legal protection proceedings, shall appoint the candidate for the position of administrator selected in the procedure specified in Section 363.10 of this Law as administrator. (8) When declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings, the court shall send the judgment to the appointed administrator, to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it has initiated the insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of this Regulation against the debtor in Latvia, and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. (9) If the insolvency indicator specified in the application is not established, the court shall refuse the insolvency application and shall terminate the legal entity insolvency case, as well as shall decide whether the insolvency application is to be recognised as unfounded or deliberately false. The court shall refuse an insolvency application submitted in accordance with the insolvency indicator referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law if it establishes that the debtor has raised substantiated objections to the claim specified in the insolvency application no later than three days before the date of examination of the case or that the obligations regarding which the insolvency application was submitted have been covered in full. (10) Having recognised the insolvency application as unfounded or deliberately false, the court shall recover the litigation costs from the applicant of the insolvency application. If the applicant of the insolvency application withdraws his or her application because the debtor has voluntarily covered the obligations specified in the insolvency application before the date of examination of the case, the court, when deciding on termination of the case, shall, at the request of the applicant of the insolvency application, award from the debtor the court costs paid by the applicant. In other cases, these costs shall be specified in the court judgment and included in the insolvency costs. (11) When refusing an insolvency application submitted in accordance with the insolvency indicator referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Section 57 of the Insolvency Law because the court does not establish on the date of examination of the application the insolvency indicator specified in it, as the debtor has covered part of the obligations specified in the application before the date of examination of the case in order to prevent declaration of legal entity insolvency proceedings, it, when deciding on termination of the case, shall award from the debtor the court costs paid by the applicant. (12) When refusing an insolvency application, the court shall send the judgment to the Insolvency Control Service. (With amendments made by laws of 18.04.2013., 12.02.2015., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which come into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.14. Issues to Be Decided by Court After Declaration of Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings

(1) After declaration of the debtor's insolvency proceedings, the court, based on the relevant application, shall decide on:

- 1) removal of the administrator in cases specified in the Insolvency Law, setting a time limit for preparation of a document and asset acceptance and transfer certificate and transfer of documents and assets to another administrator; - 2) appointment of a new candidate for the position of administrator as administrator if the previous administrator has been removed from the relevant insolvency proceedings; - 3) performance of actions specified in Article 46 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; - 4) confirmation of the auction certificate for immovable property or an enterprise (Sections 611 and 613) and registration of the sold immovable property in the name of the buyer, as well as deletion of the insolvency notice in the Land Register; - 5) (deleted by law of 11.09.2014.); - 6) termination of insolvency proceedings. - (2) The administrator may be removed by the court on its own initiative if, when examining an application or complaint in an insolvency case, it establishes that the administrator does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or does not execute a court decision. - (3) If after declaration of insolvency proceedings the court has adopted a decision to remove the administrator, after its adoption the court shall appoint a candidate for the position of administrator, who is selected from the List of Candidates using automated selection ensured by the Court Information System, as administrator. - (4) (Deleted by law of 31.05.2018.)
  - (5) Having established that there are restrictions for the candidate for the position of administrator to perform the duties of administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. The judge shall adopt a decision to appoint a candidate for the position of administrator as administrator in the procedure specified in the third paragraph of this Section. - (6) If, based on an application of the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court establishes that performance of the actions specified in paragraph 1 of Article 46 of this Regulation No. 2015/848 is in the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of this Regulation, it shall adopt a decision on performance of the actions specified in paragraph 1 of Article 46 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and shall determine appropriate measures to ensure the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of this Regulation. - (7) If, based on an application of the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in point 1 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in point 2 of Article 3 of this Regulation or a creditor, the court establishes that performance of the actions specified in paragraph 1 of Article 46 of this Regulation No. 2015/848 is no longer justified, it shall adopt a decision on performance of the action specified in paragraph
    - 2 of Article 46 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. - (8) The court shall send the decision on performance of the actions specified in Article 46 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council to the debtor's representative and the administrator. - (9) The court shall send the decisions referred to in points 1, 2, 3 and 6 of the first paragraph of this Section to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. - (10) The court shall examine a complaint against a creditors' meeting decision, a complaint against an administrator's decision, as well as a complaint against a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding an administrator's actions in insolvency proceedings or imposition of a legal obligation. The court shall send a decision adopted after examination of the said complaints, except for a decision on a complaint against a creditors' meeting decision, to the Insolvency Control Service. - (11) The court shall examine an application and complaint within 15 days from the date of receipt of the application or complaint. The judge shall examine an application in written proceedings without holding a court session, except when he or she deems it necessary to examine the case in a court session. The judge shall examine a complaint in written proceedings without holding a court session, except when the administrator requests the case to be examined in a court session or the court deems it necessary to examine the complaint in a court session. The applicant of the application or complaint, the administrator, the debtor's representative and other interested persons shall be summoned to the court session. The failure of these persons to appear is not an obstacle to examination of the issue. (12) The court decision on examination of an application or complaint is not subject to appeal. A court decision on removal of an administrator on the basis of point 1, 2, 3, 4 or 7 of the second paragraph of Section 22 of the Insolvency Law is subject to appeal in the part regarding the established non-compliance with the requirements of regulatory enactments or non-execution of a court decision, by submitting a subsidiary appeal. This subsidiary appeal shall be examined by the regional court within 15 days. (121) A subsidiary appeal may be submitted against the court decision in a case on confirmation of an auction certificate. (13) For examination of the issues referred to in this Section, the court may request that the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings submits information necessary for adoption of the decisions referred to in this Section. (14) The regional court, when examining the subsidiary appeal referred to in the twelfth paragraph of this Section, has the right to:

- 1) leave the decision unchanged and refuse the complaint; - 2) annul the decision and decide the issue on the merits with its own decision. - (15) The decision referred to in the fourteenth paragraph of this Section shall enter into force and be enforceable immediately.- (16) The regional court shall send the decisions mentioned in the fourteenth part of this section to the Insolvency Control Service.
- (17) The regional court shall examine within 15 days the debtor's or creditor's ancillary complaint regarding the court decision which establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to open the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
- (18) In the ancillary complaint, in addition to what is provided for in Section 443.1 of this Law, the following shall be indicated:
- 1) from what time the debtor's registered address is located or the main economic activity is carried out in the specified Member State of the European Union;
- 2) facts showing that the debtor usually exercises its main interests in the Member State of the European Union specified in the ancillary complaint;
- 3) information about creditors or a substantial part of assets, or economic activity in another Member State of the European Union;
- 4) whether insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been opened against the debtor in another Member State of the European Union.
- (19) The regional court, when examining the ancillary complaint mentioned in the seventeenth part of this section, has the right to:
- 1) leave the decision unchanged, but reject the complaint;
- 2) revoke the decision completely.
- (20) If the regional court has revoked the decision, the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be continued as insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) or (4) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
- (21) The court shall also send the decision on the ancillary complaint to the administrator and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.
(As amended by the laws of 21.06.2012., 29.11.2012., 18.04.2013., 11.09.2014., 31.05.2018., 25.10.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 363.15. Decision on Approval of the Asset Sale Deed in Insolvency Proceedings

(1) If the administrator has sold immovable property or an enterprise by auction, the auction deed shall be submitted to the court for approval after the successful bidder has paid the entire amount due from him or her. In the application, the administrator shall indicate information about the actions taken in the case related to the sale of the property, attaching supporting documents, as well as documents confirming that the court costs for submitting the said application to the court have been paid.
(2) The court shall approve the auction deed in accordance with the provisions of this Law on the auction of immovable property (except as provided for in the third and ninth parts of Section 613 of this Law). The court shall examine the application for approval of the auction deed of immovable property (Sections 611 and 613) and for registration of the sold immovable property in the name of the acquirer in written proceedings within 15 days from the submission of the administrator's application to the court. When granting the application, the court shall simultaneously adopt the decisions provided for in the fifth part of Section 613 of this Law.
(3) The actions specified in this section shall be performed by the court in whose proceedings the legal person's insolvency case is located.
(4) Not later than within three days from the day the court decision on approval of the auction deed has entered into force, the administrator shall pay the state and chancellery fee specified in point 4 of the second part of Section 611 of this Law into the state budget and notify the acquirer and the district (city) court thereof.
(In the wording of the law of 11.09.2014. as amended by the laws of 25.10.2018. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force

Section 363.16. Procedure for Examination of an Application for Legal Protection Proceedings in Out-of-Court Legal Protection Proceedings after Declaration of Insolvency Proceedings of a Legal Person

(1) After declaration of insolvency proceedings of a legal person, an application for legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the legal person's insolvency case is located.
(2) After declaration of insolvency proceedings of a legal person, the court shall examine the application for legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings in the procedure specified in Chapter 45.1 of this Law.

Section 363.17. Examination by the Court of Complaints Regarding the Administrator's Decision in Insolvency Proceedings of a Legal Person

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, representative of the debtor, or third party whose legal rights are affected, regarding the administrator's decision or auction calculation in insolvency proceedings of a legal person in cases specified in the Insolvency Law.
(11) If there is reason to believe that the rights of the complainant may be affected, the complainant has the right, simultaneously with the submission of a complaint regarding the administrator's decision, to request the court to impose interim protection measures in the procedure specified in Chapter 30.7 of this Law.
(2) If the court finds that the appealed administrator's decision or auction calculation does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and instruct the administrator to remedy the violation.
(3) If the court finds that the appealed administrator's decision or auction calculation complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint.
(4) If, when examining a complaint regarding the administrator's decision, the court finds that there is a dispute concerning rights, it shall set a time limit, not exceeding one month, within which the complainant may bring an action in the procedure specified in Chapter 30.7 of this Law. If the court on its own initiative finds that there is a dispute that cannot be examined in civil proceedings, it shall set a time limit, not exceeding 15 days, within which the complainant may submit an application to an institution or court in the general procedure.
(5) The complainant has the right to withdraw his or her complaint before the examination of the complaint on its merits has been completed. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on termination of the complaint proceedings.
(As amended by the laws of 18.04.2013., 12.02.2015. and 31.05.2018., which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Section 363.18. Examination by the Court of Complaints Regarding a Decision of the Meeting of Creditors in Insolvency Proceedings of a Legal Person

(1) A complaint by a creditor, representative of the debtor, or administrator regarding a decision of the meeting of creditors in insolvency proceedings of a legal person shall be examined by the court.
(2) Having found the appealed decision of the meeting of creditors to be non-compliant with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall revoke it.
(3) When revoking a decision of the meeting of creditors on non-approval of insolvency proceedings expenses, non-approval of the administrator's remuneration, or refusal to extend the time limit for insolvency proceedings, the court may simultaneously decide on approval of insolvency proceedings costs, approval of the administrator's remuneration, or extension of the time limit for insolvency proceedings.
(4) Having found that the appealed decision of the meeting of creditors complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall reject the complaint.
(5) The complainant has the right to withdraw the complaint before the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on termination of the complaint proceedings.

Section 363.19. Examination by the Court of Complaints Regarding a Decision Adopted by the Insolvency Control Service on the Administrator's Actions in Insolvency Proceedings of a Legal Person or Imposition of a Legal Duty and on Deposit Payment

(1) Courts shall examine a complaint by a creditor, representative of the debtor, administrator, or third party whose legal rights are affected, regarding a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service on the administrator's actions in insolvency proceedings or imposition of a legal duty and on deposit payment. The court shall examine a complaint regarding a decision of the Insolvency Control Service adopted after the termination of the relevant legal person's insolvency proceedings, except for a decision on deposit payment, in the procedure specified in this section.
(2) If the court finds that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and decide on:

- 1) revocation of the decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service in whole or in part;
- 2) imposition of a duty on the Insolvency Control Service to adopt or examine a complaint regarding the administrator's actions;
- 3) imposition of a duty on the administrator to remedy the violation, except in cases where the debtor has been deleted from the relevant public register.
- (3) If the court finds that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint.
- (4) The complainant has the right to withdraw his or her complaint before the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on termination of the complaint proceedings.
- (5) The court shall immediately send the adopted decision to the Insolvency Control Service after examination of the complaint.
- (6) If a decision of the Insolvency Control Service on the administrator's actions in insolvency proceedings of a legal person is adopted within one year after the termination of the relevant legal person's insolvency proceedings, a complaint regarding the decision of the Insolvency Control Service shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the relevant legal person's insolvency case was located.
(As amended by the laws of 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 363.20. Termination of a Legal Person's Insolvency Case

(1) The court shall terminate a legal person's insolvency case by rejecting the application for insolvency proceedings or by terminating the insolvency proceedings.
(2) The court shall adopt a decision on termination of insolvency proceedings of a legal person if:

- 1) the debtor has settled all its obligations;
- 2) legal protection proceedings have been declared for the debtor (transition from insolvency proceedings to legal protection proceedings);
- 3) a proposal to terminate insolvency proceedings has been expressed in the report on the absence of the debtor's assets and no agreement has been reached on the source of financing for insolvency proceedings;
- 4) the plan for satisfaction of creditors' claims has been fulfilled.
- (3) In the case mentioned in point 2 of the second part of this section, the plan of legal protection measures coordinated in the procedure specified in the Insolvency Law shall be attached to the application for termination of insolvency proceedings.
- (4) In the case mentioned in point 3 of the second part of this section, the administrator shall attach to the application for termination of insolvency proceedings a report on the absence of the debtor's assets, objections by creditors, if any have been expressed, and the response provided by the administrator.
- (5) In the case mentioned in point 4 of the second part of this section, the administrator shall indicate in the application information about disregarded objections by creditors regarding the report on the fulfilment of the plan for satisfaction of creditors' claims and attach a report on the fulfilment of this plan.
- (6) The administrator shall attach to the application for termination of the insolvency case a report on his or her activities and a certificate of payment of the cash surplus to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if the court has opened against the debtor the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of the said Regulation.
- (61) Following an application by the administrator of the proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, submitted in accordance with Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court may terminate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
- (7) The court shall send the decision on termination of insolvency proceedings to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.
(As amended by the laws of 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Chapter 46

Cases of Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 30.09.2010, which came into force on 01.11.2010.)

Section 363.21. Norms Applicable to Case Examination

In natural person insolvency proceedings, the court shall apply the provisions of Chapter 46.1 of this Law, insofar as this Chapter does not provide otherwise.

Section 363.22. Jurisdiction over Natural Person Insolvency Proceeding Cases

(1) The court shall examine a natural person insolvency proceeding case in accordance with the debtor's application at the debtor's declared place of residence that was registered for the debtor three months prior to submission of the application to the court, but if there is no such place - at the place of residence.

(2) A case regarding the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be examined by the court at the location of the debtor's centre of main interests, but in the case of initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation - at the location of the debtor's establishment (within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council).

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016 and 31.05.2018, which came into force on 01.07.2018.)

Section 363.23. Content of Natural Person Insolvency Proceeding Application

(1) In a natural person insolvency proceeding application (hereinafter in this Chapter - insolvency proceeding application), the debtor shall indicate:

- 1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
- 2) the circumstances due to which the natural person is unable to perform obligations;
- 3) all obligations not performed within the time limit and their amounts;
- 31) all obligations whose performance deadline will occur in accordance with Part Three of Section 134 of the Insolvency Law;
- 4) the total amount of all obligations whose performance deadline will occur within one year;
- 5) the composition of the debtor's property, including the debtor's share in the spouses' joint property and other co-ownership;
- 6) whether the provisions of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are applicable to the insolvency proceedings;
- 7) the debtor's declared place of residence that was registered for the debtor three months prior to submission of the application to the court, but if there is no such place - the place of residence;
- 8) if the debtor is simultaneously a sole trader - information about the relevant sole trader (firm (name) and registration number);
- 9) if the debtor is simultaneously the owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery - information about the relevant individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery (firm (name) and registration number).

- (11) If an insolvency proceeding application is submitted by the debtor together with their spouse or with a person who is related to the debtor by consanguinity or affinity up to the second degree, then the information referred to in Part One of this Section shall be indicated for each applicant separately.
- (12) If an insolvency proceeding application is submitted by a person who is not the debtor, it shall be prepared in observance of:
- 1) the provisions of Section 363.2 of this Law, if the insolvency proceeding application is submitted by a creditor or majority of creditors;
- 2) the provisions of Section 363.4 of this Law, if the insolvency proceeding application is submitted by a liquidator;
- 3) the provisions of Section 363.5 of this Law, if the insolvency proceeding application is submitted by a person referred to in Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
- (13) In the cases referred to in Part 1.2 of this Section, the insolvency proceeding application shall additionally indicate the information referred to in Clause 8 or 9 of Part One of this Section.
- (2) The following documents confirming shall be attached to the insolvency proceeding application:
- 1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
- 2) payment of the natural person insolvency proceeding deposit;
- 3) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
- 4) if the debtor is simultaneously the owner of a family enterprise - that the other owners of the family enterprise have been notified of the intention to submit an insolvency proceeding application.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015, 09.06.2016, 08.12.2016, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which came into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Section 363.24. Receipt and Registration of Insolvency Proceeding Application

(1) The court shall receive an insolvency proceeding application from the debtor, their guardian or custodian, a creditor or majority of creditors, a liquidator or a person referred to in Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. An insolvency proceeding application shall be submitted in person in paper form or in an online system.

(2) Upon receipt of an insolvency proceeding application, the court shall verify the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant who has submitted the application in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the relevant authorisation, the application shall not be accepted.

(3) An insolvency proceeding application shall be registered in a separate register, which shall be signed by the applicant and the receiver. If an insolvency proceeding application is received in the online system, the receiver shall make the entry in the register.

(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021 with amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023, which came into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Section 363.25. Decision on the Issue of Acceptance of Insolvency Proceeding Application and Initiation of Case

(1) Within five days after receipt of the insolvency proceeding application, the judge shall adopt a decision:

- 1) to leave the insolvency proceeding application without progress;
- 2) to refuse to accept the insolvency proceeding application;
- 3) to accept the insolvency proceeding application and to initiate the case.

- (2) If an insolvency proceeding application has been left without progress, the judge shall adopt a decision to accept the insolvency proceeding application and to initiate the case no later than the next day after the deficiencies indicated in the decision have been remedied. If the deadline for remedying the deficiencies indicated in the decision has expired and they have not been remedied, the application shall be deemed not to have been submitted and shall be returned to the applicant.
- (3) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the insolvency proceeding application if it is established that:
- 1) the debtor is not a subject of natural person insolvency proceedings;
- 2) (deleted by the law of 04.08.2011);
- 3) the applicant has not paid the natural person insolvency proceeding deposit;
- 4) a natural person insolvency proceeding case has been initiated against the debtor, who is simultaneously a sole trader, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, or business operator, following an insolvency proceeding application by the debtor.
- (4) If the debtor is simultaneously a sole trader or owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, the court shall initiate a natural person insolvency proceeding case on its own initiative if, upon adopting a decision to terminate legal protection proceedings, it establishes the sign of natural person insolvency proceedings specified in Sub-paragraph "b" of Clause 5 of Part One of Section 129 of the Insolvency Law.
- (5) If the debtor is simultaneously a sole trader, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, or business operator, the judge shall adopt a decision to consolidate the initiated natural person insolvency proceeding cases in one set of proceedings if, by the day when the natural person insolvency proceeding case initiated following an insolvency proceeding application by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law is examined in substance, it is established that a natural person insolvency proceeding case has been initiated against the debtor following an insolvency proceeding application by another creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law.
- (6) If the debtor is simultaneously a sole trader, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, or business operator, the judge shall adopt a decision to suspend proceedings in the case following an insolvency proceeding application by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law if, by the day when the natural person insolvency proceeding case initiated following an insolvency proceeding application by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law is examined in substance, it is established that a natural person insolvency proceeding case has been initiated against the debtor following an insolvency proceeding application by the debtor. Upon declaring natural person insolvency proceedings following an insolvency proceeding application by the debtor, the court shall resume proceedings in the suspended case following an insolvency proceeding application by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law and shall terminate it. The state fee paid shall be refunded to the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law in full.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 12.02.2015 and 16.03.2023, which came into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Section 363.26. Court Actions in Preparing a Natural Person Insolvency Proceeding Case for Examination

(1) After initiation of a natural person insolvency proceeding case, using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, a candidate for the position of administrator shall be selected from the Candidate List and the judge shall evaluate their suitability for performing the duties of administrator in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings.

(2) Having established that there are restrictions for the candidate for the position of administrator to perform the duties of administrator in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. Using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, a new candidate for the position of administrator shall be selected from the Candidate List, and the judge shall evaluate their suitability for performing the duties of administrator in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings.

(3) The court shall immediately send the decision on initiation of the case following an application for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council to the administrator of the proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(4) If the debtor is simultaneously a sole trader, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, or business operator and the case has been initiated following an insolvency proceeding application by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law, the judge shall send the application by the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law and the decision on initiation of the case to the debtor, shall inform the debtor and the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section

42 of the Insolvency Law about the day of examination of the insolvency proceeding application, as well as about the debtor's rights to raise substantiated objections to the claim referred to in the insolvency proceeding application no later than three days before the day of examination of the insolvency proceeding application, including to provide evidence that the debtor is able to cover the debt obligations referred to in the insolvency proceeding application.

(In the wording of the law of 31.05.2018 with amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023, which came into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Section 363.27. Examination of Insolvency Proceeding Application and Judgment in Natural Person Insolvency Proceeding Case

(1) The court shall examine a natural person insolvency proceeding case following the debtor's application within seven days from the day of its initiation. The court shall examine the application in written proceedings, except in cases when it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the insolvency proceeding application is examined in a court session, the debtor shall be invited to the session. Failure of this person to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the case.

(11) If the application is submitted for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the application shall be examined within 15 days from the day of initiation of the case or, if the court considers it necessary, in a court session. If the insolvency proceeding application is examined in a court session, the applicant, the debtor and the administrator of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be invited to the session. Failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the case.

(12) If the debtor is simultaneously a sole trader, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, or business operator, then the court shall examine the insolvency proceeding application submitted by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in Part Three of Section 42 of the Insolvency Law within 15 days from the day of initiation of the case. The applicant of the insolvency proceeding application and the debtor shall be invited to the court session. If insolvency proceeding applications by several creditors are consolidated in one set of proceedings, the applicants shall be notified of the court session at least seven days before the relevant session. Failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the case.

(13) If, before drawing up the judgment, the court establishes that the applicant has not paid the state fee or insolvency proceeding deposit, except in cases when the court has initiated a natural person insolvency proceeding case on its own initiative or has released an employee from payment of the deposit, it shall leave the insolvency proceeding application without examination. The exception referred to in this Part shall not apply to cases when a legal protection proceeding application has been submitted repeatedly within one year.

(14) If the debtor is simultaneously a sole trader, owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, or business operator, the judge may adopt a decision to release an employee fully or partially from payment of the insolvency proceeding deposit if they submit an insolvency proceeding application after it has not been possible to execute a court decision on recovery of debt from the debtor by applying enforcement measures and the employee, taking into account their financial situation, cannot pay the insolvency proceeding deposit.

(15) The court shall suspend proceedings if, by the day when examination in substance of the natural person insolvency proceeding case begins, it establishes that a legal protection proceeding case has been initiated in relation to the debtor's sole trader, individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery.

(16) In the case referred to in Part 1.5 of this Section, proceedings in the natural person insolvency proceeding case shall be suspended until a decision is adopted in the legal protection proceeding case.

(17) Proceedings in the natural person insolvency proceeding case shall be terminated if, in accordance with the decision, legal protection proceedings are implemented in relation to the debtor's sole trader, individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery.

(18) Proceedings in the natural person insolvency proceeding case shall be resumed and examined in the procedure specified in this Chapter if legal protection proceedings in relation to the debtor's sole trader, individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery are terminated on the basis of Part Two of Section 341.10 of this Law.

(2) The court shall declare natural person insolvency proceedings for the debtor if it establishes that:

- 1) there is a sign of insolvency proceedings;
- 2) natural person insolvency proceedings that were terminated without discharging obligations have not been declared in the last year;
- 3) natural person insolvency proceedings within which obligations were discharged have not been declared in the last 10 years;
- 4) the applicant has paid the state fee for submission of the natural person insolvency proceeding application;
- 5) the applicant has paid the natural person insolvency proceeding deposit;
- 6) an application for release of the natural person from debt obligations has not been accepted in relation to the debtor in the procedure specified in the Law on Release of Natural Persons from Debt Obligations.

- (3) Upon granting the application, the court shall appoint the candidate for the position of administrator selected in the procedure specified in Section 363.26 of this Law as administrator.
- (31) The court shall reject the insolvency proceeding application and terminate the natural person insolvency proceeding case if:
- 1) the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in the application is not established;
- 2) natural person insolvency proceedings within which obligations were discharged have been declared for the debtor in the last 10 years;
- 3) the applicant has not paid the natural person insolvency proceeding deposit or state fee for submission of the natural person insolvency proceeding application;
- 4) the application submitted by the debtor on declaration of natural person insolvency proceedings for a sole trader, individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery does not indicate information about the relevant natural person;
- 5) an application for release of the natural person from debt obligations has been accepted in relation to the debtor in the procedure specified in the Law on Release of Natural Persons from Debt Obligations.
- (32) If the court rejects an insolvency proceeding application whose applicant is not the debtor, it shall simultaneously decide the issue of whether the insolvency proceeding application is to be recognised as unfounded or deliberately false.
- (33) The court shall reject an insolvency proceeding application that has been submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in Sub-paragraph "b" of Clause 4 of Part One of Section 129 of the Insolvency Law if it establishes that no later than three days before the day of examination of the case the debtor has raised substantiated objections to the claim referred to in the insolvency proceeding application or that the debt obligations in respect of which the insolvency proceeding application has been submitted have been covered in full.
- (4) A judgment of the court in natural person insolvency proceedings shall not be subject to appeal, except for a judgment on rejection of a natural person insolvency proceeding application. A judgment on rejection of a natural person insolvency proceeding application may be appealed in appellate procedure if any of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings specified in Section 440.2 of this Law exists.
- (41) When examining an application for initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall take into account what is specified in Article
    - 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
- (42) Upon declaring insolvency proceedings in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall indicate in the judgment the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated, or shall indicate in the decision referred to in Part 4.3 of this Section the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated.

(43) If the court establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia, it shall declare a judgment on initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and shall adopt a decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The debtor or creditor may submit an appeal against this court decision in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the day of declaration of the decision. Submission of the appeal shall not suspend initiation of insolvency proceedings.
