(44) The court, having established that a court of another Member State that initiated insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor had the right to initiate such proceedings, shall issue a judgment on initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, disregarding what is specified in Part Two of this Section. The court shall not initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the conditions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have occurred.

(5) The court shall issue the judgment to the applicant and the administrator, as well as to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it has initiated the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation against the debtor in Latvia. The court shall send the judgment to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(6) The court, upon declaring natural person insolvency proceedings for a debtor who is simultaneously a sole trader or owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, shall also indicate in the judgment the firm (name) and registration number of the sole trader, individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery.

(7) Upon rejecting the insolvency proceeding application, the court shall send the judgment to the Insolvency Control Service.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 18.04.2013, 12.02.2015, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which came into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Section 363.28. Issues to be Decided by the Court after Declaration of Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(1) After declaration of natural person insolvency proceedings, the court shall decide, on the basis of a relevant application, on:

- 1) dismissal of the administrator, setting a deadline for drawing up a document and property acceptance and handover act and handover of documents and property to another administrator;
- 2) appointment of a new candidate for the position of administrator as administrator if the previous administrator has been dismissed from the relevant insolvency proceedings;
- 3) approval of completion of bankruptcy proceedings;
- 4) approval of a natural person debt discharge plan and amendments thereto;
- 41) extension of the term of performance of a natural person debt discharge plan in the cases referred to in Part 2.1 of Section 164 of the Insolvency Law;
- 5) termination of natural person insolvency proceedings;
- 6) approval of an immovable property auction act (Sections 611 and 613) and registration of the sold immovable property in the name of the purchaser, as well as deletion of the insolvency mark in the Land Register;
- 7) (deleted by the law of 11.09.2014).

- (11) An application for approval of an immovable property auction act (Sections 611 and 613) and registration of the sold immovable property in the name of the purchaser shall be examined by the court in whose proceedings the insolvency proceeding case is located, in the procedure specified in Chapter 46.1 of this Law.
- (2) The administrator may be dismissed by the court on its own initiative if, when examining an application or complaint in a natural person insolvency proceeding case, it establishes that the administrator does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or does not perform court decisions.
- (3) If, after declaration of insolvency proceedings, the court has adopted a decision to dismiss the administrator, after adoption of this decision, it shall appoint the candidate for the position of administrator selected from the Candidate List using automated selection provided by the Court Information System as administrator.
- (4) (Deleted by the law of 31.05.2018)
  - (5) Having established that there are restrictions for the candidate for the position of administrator to perform the duties of administrator in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. The judge shall adopt a decision to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator in the procedure specified in Part Three of this Section.
- (6) The court shall immediately send the decisions referred to in Clauses 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 of Part One of this Section to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.
- (7) The court shall examine a complaint regarding a decision by the administrator, as well as a complaint regarding a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service on the administrator's actions in natural person insolvency proceedings or imposition of a legal obligation. The court shall immediately send the decision adopted after examination of the complaint to the Insolvency Control Service.
- (8) The court shall examine an application and a complaint within 15 days from the day of receipt of the application or complaint. The judge shall examine the application in written proceedings, without convening a court session, except in cases when they consider it necessary to examine the case in a court session. The judge shall examine the complaint in written proceedings, without convening a court session, except in cases when the administrator requests that the case be examined in a court session or the court considers it necessary to examine the complaint in a court session. The applicant or complainant, the administrator, the debtor's representative and other interested persons shall be invited to the court session. Failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the issue.

(9) A decision of the court on examination of an application and a complaint shall not be subject to appeal. A decision of the court to dismiss the administrator on the basis of Clause 1, 2, 3, 4 or 7 of Part Two of Section 22 of the Insolvency Law may be appealed in the part regarding the established failure to comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or failure to perform a court decision by submitting an appeal. This appeal shall be examined by a regional court within 15 days.

(91) An appeal may be submitted against a court decision in a case regarding approval of an auction act.

(10) For examination of the issues referred to in this Section, the court may request that the administrator submit a report on their activities or other information.

(11) A regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in Part Nine of this Section, shall have the right to:

- 1) leave the decision unchanged, but reject the complaint;
- 2) revoke the decision and decide the issue in substance with its decision.

- (12) The decision referred to in Part Eleven of this Section shall come into force and be enforceable immediately.
- (13) A regional court shall send the decisions referred to in Part Eleven of this Section to the Insolvency Control Service.
- (14) A regional court shall examine an appeal by the debtor or creditor against a court decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 15 days.
- (15) In addition to what is referred to in Section 443.1 of this Law, the following shall be indicated in the appeal:
- 1) from what time the debtor's permanent place of residence has been in the European Union Member State indicated in the appeal;
- 2) whether insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor in another European Union Member State.
- (16) A regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in Part Fourteen of this Section, shall have the right to:
- 1) leave the decision unchanged, but reject the complaint;
- 2) revoke the decision in full.
- (17) If a regional court has revoked the decision, insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be continued as insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) or (4) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
- (18) The decision on the appeal shall also be sent by the court to the administrator and the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 21.06.2012, 29.11.2012, 18.04.2013, 11.09.2014, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and

16.03.2023, which came into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Section 363.29. Termination of Bankruptcy Proceedings

(1) Upon application by the administrator, the court shall decide on termination of bankruptcy proceedings.

(2) In the application for termination of bankruptcy proceedings, the administrator shall indicate the grounds for termination of bankruptcy proceedings.

(21) Upon application by the debtor, the court shall decide on termination of bankruptcy proceedings if creditor claims have not been submitted against the debtor.

(22) In the application for termination of bankruptcy proceedings in the case specified in Part 2.1 of this Section, the debtor shall indicate all their obligations and the basis thereof.

(23) If the court, upon terminating bankruptcy proceedings, establishes that the debtor's obligations have become time-barred in the procedure specified in the Insolvency Law, it shall simultaneously adopt a decision to terminate natural person insolvency proceedings.

(24) Upon application by a debtor who is simultaneously a sole trader or owner of an individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, the court shall decide on declaration of legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings for the sole trader, individual (family) enterprise, peasant farm or fishery, in observance of what is specified in Chapter 45.1 of this Law and simultaneously terminating natural person insolvency proceedings.

(3) The court shall terminate bankruptcy proceedings if it establishes restrictions on application of natural person insolvency proceedings.

(4) Upon terminating bankruptcy proceedings, the court shall simultaneously adopt a decision to terminate insolvency proceedings.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015 and 16.03.2023, which came into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Section 363.30. Completion of Bankruptcy Proceedings

(1) Upon application by the administrator, the court shall decide on completion of bankruptcy proceedings.

(2) In the application for completion of bankruptcy proceedings, the administrator shall indicate:

- 1) the grounds for completion of bankruptcy proceedings;
- 2) the measures performed within the bankruptcy proceedings;
- 3) a list of the debtor's property sold, including the sold debtor's property share in the spouses' joint property and other co-ownership and the income obtained from sale of the debtor's property and its distribution;
- 4) whether the debt discharge procedure is applicable to the debtor;
- 5) the objections and proposals received from the debtor and creditors that have not been taken into account.

- (3) If the debt discharge procedure is planned to be applied to the debtor, the debtor shall submit a debt discharge plan to the court for approval and the creditor objections and proposals received in relation to this plan that have not been taken into account.
- (4) When examining the issue of completion of bankruptcy proceedings, the court shall verify whether the bankruptcy proceedings have taken place in the procedure specified by law.
- (5) If the court approves completion of bankruptcy proceedings and the debt discharge procedure is not applied to the debtor, the court shall simultaneously adopt a decision to terminate insolvency proceedings.

Section 363.31. Approval of Debt Discharge Plan

(1) Upon approving completion of bankruptcy proceedings, the court shall simultaneously examine the issue of approval of the debt discharge plan.

(2) The court shall not approve the debt discharge plan if it establishes restrictions on application of the debt discharge procedure.

(3) The court shall verify whether the debt discharge plan complies with the requirements of law.

(4) If the court establishes deficiencies in the debt discharge plan, it shall set a deadline for the debtor to remedy the deficiencies, and it may not be shorter than 10 or longer than 30 days.

(5) The court shall approve the debt discharge plan if it complies with the requirements of law and creditor and debtor objections have not been received or these objections are to be recognised as unfounded.

Section 363.32. Examination in Court of Complaints Regarding Administrator's Decision in Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor or third party whose legitimate rights have been violated regarding an administrator's decision in natural person insolvency proceedings.

(2) If the court recognises that the appealed administrator's decision does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and shall instruct the administrator to remedy the violation committed.

(3) If the court establishes that the appealed administrator's decision complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint.

(4) If, when examining a complaint regarding an administrator's decision, the court establishes that there is a dispute regarding rights, it shall set a deadline within which the complainant may bring an action in court in the general procedure or may request resumption of proceedings suspended in respect of the subject matter of the dispute.

(5) The complainant shall have the right to withdraw their complaint before examination in substance of the complaint has been completed. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision to terminate complaint proceedings.

(With amendments made by the law of 18.04.2013, which came into force on 22.05.2013.)

Section 363.33.363.33 pants.
Sūdzības par kreditoru sapulces lēmumu fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesā izskatīšana tiesā

(1) Kreditora, parādnieka pārstāvja vai administratora sūdzību par kreditoru sapulces lēmumu fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesā izskata tiesa. (2) Atzīstot pārsūdzēto kreditoru sapulces lēmumu par neatbilstošu normatīvo aktu prasībām, tiesa to atceļ. (3) Atceļot kreditoru sapulces lēmumu par maksātnespējas procesa izdevumu neapstiprināšanu, administratora atlīdzības neapstiprināšanu vai atteikšanos pagarināt maksātnespējas procesa termiņu, tiesa vienlaikus var lemt par maksātnespējas procesa izmaksu apstiprināšanu, administratora atlīdzības apstiprināšanu vai maksātnespējas procesa termiņa pagarināšanu. (4) Konstatējusi, ka pārsūdzētais kreditoru sapulces lēmums atbilst normatīvo aktu prasībām, tiesa sūdzību noraida. (5) Sūdzības iesniedzējam ir tiesības atsaukt sūdzību līdz tās izskatīšanas pēc būtības pabeigšanai. Ja sūdzības iesniedzējs atsauc iesniegto sūdzību, tiesa pieņem lēmumu par sūdzības tiesvedības izbeigšanu. 363.34 pants. Sūdzības par Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta pieņemto lēmumu par administratora rīcību fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesā vai tiesiskā pienākuma uzlikšanu izskatīšana tiesā

(1) Tiesa izskata kreditora, parādnieka, administratora vai trešās personas, kuras likumiskās tiesības ir aizskartas, sūdzību par Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta pieņemto lēmumu par administratora rīcību maksātnespējas procesā vai tiesiskā pienākuma uzlikšanu. Sūdzību par Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta lēmumu, kas pieņemts pēc attiecīgā fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesa izbeigšanas, tiesa izskata šajā pantā noteiktajā kārtībā. (2) Ja tiesa atzīst, ka pārsūdzētais Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta lēmums neatbilst normatīvo aktu prasībām, tā apmierina sūdzību un lemj par:

- 1) Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta lēmuma atcelšanu pilnībā vai daļēji; - 2) pienākuma uzlikšanu Maksātnespējas kontroles dienestam pieņemt vai izskatīt sūdzību par administratora rīcību; - 3) pienākuma uzlikšanu administratoram novērst pieļauto pārkāpumu, izņemot gadījumu, kad fiziskās personas maksātnespējas process ir izbeigts. - (3) Ja tiesa konstatē, ka pārsūdzētais Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta lēmums atbilst normatīvo aktu prasībām, tā sūdzību noraida. - (4) Sūdzības iesniedzējam ir tiesības atsaukt savu sūdzību, kamēr nav pabeigta tās izskatīšana pēc būtības. Ja sūdzības iesniedzējs atsauc iesniegto sūdzību, tiesa pieņem lēmumu par sūdzības tiesvedības izbeigšanu. - (5) Tiesa pēc sūdzības izskatīšanas nekavējoties nosūta pieņemto lēmumu Maksātnespējas kontroles dienestam. - (6) Ja Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta lēmums par administratora rīcību fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesā vai tiesiskā pienākuma uzlikšanu pieņemts gada laikā pēc attiecīgā fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesa izbeigšanas, sūdzību par Maksātnespējas kontroles dienesta lēmumu iesniedz tiesai, kuras tiesvedībā atradās attiecīgā lieta par fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesu. 363.35 pants. Saistību dzēšanas procedūras izbeigšana

(1) Tiesa izskata jautājumu par saistību dzēšanas procedūras izbeigšanu pēc parādnieka vai administratora pieteikuma. (2) Tiesa apstiprina saistību dzēšanas procedūras izbeigšanu, ja konstatē, ka parādnieks ir izpildījis saistību dzēšanas plānu un nav saņemti kreditoru un parādnieka iebildumi vai arī saņemtie iebildumi atzīstami par nepamatotiem. (3) Apstiprinot saistību dzēšanas procedūras izbeigšanu, tiesa lemj par to saistību dzēšanu, kuras nav izpildītas saistību dzēšanas procesa laikā. (4) Pieteikumam par saistību dzēšanas procedūras izbeigšanu parādnieks, kreditors vai administrators pievieno pierādījumus, kas apstiprina pieteikumā norādītos apstākļus. 363.37 pants. Pieteikums par parādnieka atbrīvošanas no saistībām atcelšanu un tā pieņemšana

(1) Parādnieks, kreditors vai cita persona, kuras likumiskās tiesības ir aizskartas, ir tiesīga Maksātnespējas likuma 165.1 pantā noteiktajā termiņā un gadījumos iesniegt pieteikumu par parādnieka atbrīvošanas no saistībām atcelšanu. Pieteikums nosūtāms administratoram, kurš bija iecelts attiecīgajā fiziskās personas maksātnespējas procesā, nosakot tam termiņu viedokļa iesniegšanai, ne ilgāku par 30 dienām. (1) Pieteikumu izskata rakstveida procesā, nerīkojot tiesas sēdi, izņemot gadījumu, kad tiesa uzskata par nepieciešamu pieteikumu izskatīt tiesas sēdē vai to lūdz lietas dalībnieks, pamatojot savu lūgumu. (2) Tiesa apmierina pieteikumu, ja konstatē, ka pastāv Maksātnespējas likuma 165.1 panta otrajā vai trešajā daļā noteiktais pamats atcelt parādnieka atbrīvošanu no saistībām. #### 364.pants. Jurisdiction of Cases

Insolvency or liquidation cases of a credit institution shall be heard by the court at the registered office of the credit institution.

(As amended by the Law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 365.pants. Applicants for Insolvency Petition

An insolvency petition may be submitted to the court by:

- 1) a credit institution or liquidator of a credit institution;
- 2) a creditor or group of creditors;
- 3) an administrator in other insolvency proceedings;
- 4) the Bank of Latvia.

(As amended by the Laws of 20.06.2001, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 366.pants. Applicant for Liquidation Petition

A liquidation petition shall be submitted to the court by the Bank of Latvia.

(As amended by the Laws of 20.06.2001, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 367.pants. Procedure for Submission of Insolvency Petition

(1) A credit institution, liquidator of a credit institution, creditor or group of creditors, or administrator in other insolvency proceedings may submit an insolvency petition of a credit institution to the court after it has been reviewed by the Bank of Latvia.

(2) The insolvency petition shall be submitted to the court by the Bank of Latvia, attaching its decision to submit the petition to the court and other documents that may be relevant to the case. The applicant in this case shall be considered the person on whose behalf the insolvency petition was prepared and who submitted it to the Bank of Latvia. The insolvency petition must comply with the requirements of Sections 368 and 369 of this Law.

(3) If the Bank of Latvia has rejected the insolvency petition, the persons referred to in paragraph one of this Section may submit it directly to the court. In such case, the decision of the Bank of Latvia to refuse to submit the insolvency petition to the court must be attached to the insolvency petition.

(As amended by the Laws of 20.06.2001, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

Insolvency Proceedings

- 5) documents attached to the insolvency petition.
  - (2) Documents confirming the actual insolvency of the credit institution, as well as the decision of the Bank of Latvia to refuse to submit the insolvency petition to the court, shall be attached to the insolvency petition.

- 4) documents attached to the insolvency petition.
  - (2) The following shall be attached to the insolvency petition:

- 2) the latest balance sheet of the credit institution prepared in accordance with the instructions of the Bank of Latvia on the preparation of the annual report;

- 4) a list of property belonging to third parties held in the possession or custody of the credit institution, excluding deposits and interest thereon;
- 5) the decision of the Bank of Latvia to refuse to submit the insolvency petition to the court.

#### 372. pants. Submission and Registration of Credit Institution Insolvency Petition and Liquidation Petition

(1) A credit institution insolvency petition or liquidation petition may be submitted to the court by a representative of the Bank of Latvia, but in the case provided for in paragraph three of Section 367 of this Law — by the applicant or their representative. A credit institution insolvency petition or liquidation petition shall be submitted in person in paper form or through an online system.

(2) Upon receiving a credit institution insolvency petition or liquidation petition, the court shall verify the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant who submitted the petition in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the appropriate authorisation, the petition shall not be accepted.

(3) Credit institution insolvency petitions and liquidation petitions shall be registered in a separate register, which shall be signed by the applicant and the recipient. If a credit institution insolvency petition or liquidation petition is received through an online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient.

(In the wording of the Law of 11.11.2021 as amended by the Law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 373.pants. Initiation of Credit Institution Insolvency Case and Liquidation Case

(1) The judge shall adopt a decision on the initiation of a credit institution insolvency case and liquidation case or on the refusal to accept the petition no later than the next day after receipt of the petition by the court, but if the petition has been left without progress — no later than the next day after the deficiencies indicated in the judge's decision have been remedied or the time limit for remedying the deficiencies has expired.

(2) Upon initiating a case, the court shall seize the property of the credit institution, except in cases where the insolvency petition is submitted in the procedure provided for in paragraph three of Section 367 of this Law.

#### 374.pants. Judge's actions in preparing a credit institution's insolvency case for examination

(1) After initiation of a credit institution's insolvency proceedings case, a candidate for the administrator's position is selected from the List of Candidates using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, and the judge assesses their suitability for performing administrator's duties in the relevant credit institution insolvency proceedings.

(11) Having established that there are restrictions on the candidate for the administrator's position performing administrator's duties in the specific credit institution's insolvency proceedings, the judge adopts a decision refusing to appoint the candidate for the administrator's position as administrator. Using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, another candidate for the administrator's position is selected from the List of Candidates, and the judge assesses their suitability for performing administrator's duties in the relevant credit institution insolvency proceedings.

(2) A person subject to restrictions specified in the Credit Institution Law may not be appointed as administrator.

(3) Upon appointing an administrator, they are instructed to:

- 1) prepare a list of persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory;
- 2) prepare a report on the credit institution's assets (property) at their real (market) value;
- 3) identify property owned by third parties that is in the credit institution's possession or holding and prepare a list of such property;
- 4) prepare a list of creditors according to data in the credit institution's accounting, indicating information about creditors, amounts of debts and obligations, and performance deadlines;
- 5) submit the aforementioned information to the court before the case examination.
  - (4) A declaration signed by the administrator is attached to the case, which confirms their consent to assume the position and undertake the responsibility specified by law.
  - (5) (Deleted as of 01.09.2023. by the law of 16.03.2023. See point 181 of transitional provisions) (With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.

The new version of the first part, part 1.1 and the amendment on deletion of the fifth part enters into force on 01.09.2023. See point 181 of transitional provisions)

#### 375.pants. Examination of credit institution insolvency cases and liquidation cases

(1) The court examines a credit institution's insolvency case and liquidation case within 10 days from the day of case initiation.

(2) The applicant, the credit institution's representative, the Bank of Latvia representative are invited to the court session, and in an insolvency case – also the administrator.

(3) In a credit institution's insolvency case and liquidation case, withdrawal from the application or its amendment is not permitted.

(4) When examining a credit institution's insolvency case, the court verifies whether there is any of the circumstances specified in the Credit Institution Law indicating the credit institution's insolvency, and whether the pre-court examination procedure for the application specified in Section 367 of this law has been observed.

(5) When examining a credit institution's liquidation case, the court does not assess the credit institution's solvency.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. The amendment in the first part replacing the word "seven" with the number "10" enters into force on 01.09.2023. See point 181 of transitional provisions)

#### 376.pants. Court judgment in a credit institution's insolvency case

(1) If the court establishes any of the circumstances indicating the credit institution's insolvency, it declares the credit institution insolvent by its judgment and determines that the credit institution's insolvency commences on the day of the court judgment announcement. The judgment is final and not appealable.

(2) When making a judgment on the credit institution's insolvency, the court confirms the appointed administrator.

(3) Based on the Bank of Latvia's application and the list prepared by the administrator, the court determines those representatives of the credit institution and persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory.

(4) The judgment is grounds for suspension of proceedings in civil cases initiated against the credit institution, and for termination of judgment enforcement proceedings in cases concerning awarded but not recovered amounts from the credit institution.

(5) If the court does not establish circumstances indicating the credit institution's insolvency, it rejects the application, simultaneously terminating the insolvency proceedings and deciding the question whether the application, in accordance with the Credit Institution Law, should not be recognized as deliberately false.

(6) Recognizing the application as deliberately false, the court recovers from the applicant court expenses, as well as the administrator's and administrator's assistant's remuneration.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 08.09.2011., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force

#### 377.pants. Court judgment in a credit institution's liquidation case

(1) If the court establishes that the European Central Bank has annulled the license issued for the credit institution's operation in accordance with the Credit Institution Law, it recognizes the credit institution as subject to liquidation. The judgment is final and not appealable.

(2) When making a judgment on the credit institution's liquidation, the court appoints a liquidator of the credit institution. The court appoints a person recommended by the Bank of Latvia as the credit institution's liquidator.

(3) A person subject to restrictions specified in the Credit Institution Law may not be appointed as liquidator.

(4) Based on the Bank of Latvia's application, the court determines those representatives of the credit institution and persons whose participation in the credit institution's liquidation is mandatory.

(5) The judgment is grounds for suspension of proceedings in civil cases initiated against the credit institution, and for termination of judgment enforcement proceedings in cases concerning awarded but not recovered amounts from the credit institution. (With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force

#### 378.pants. Court actions after declaration of credit institution's insolvency or liquidation

(1) After announcement of the judgment, the court issues to the administrator or liquidator the judgment with a note on the judgment entering into force.

(2) The judge warns the representatives of the credit institution and persons specified in the judgment, whose participation in the insolvency proceedings or the credit institution's liquidation is mandatory, that:

- 1) it is their duty to appear at all court sessions, their non-appearance is not an obstacle to examination of the matter at the court session, but the court may recognize their appearance as mandatory and order them to be brought by force;
- 2) they have a duty to provide the court and the administrator or liquidator with necessary information;
- 3) if contact information for communication with the court changes, they must notify the court and the administrator or liquidator of current contact information for communication with the court within three days;
- 4) in case of non-performance of duties, they may be held to account as specified by law.
  - (21) After announcement of the judgment, the court informs the Bank of Latvia thereof, ensuring that the Bank of Latvia receives the relevant information on the day of the judgment announcement. The procedure for informing the Bank of Latvia is determined by the Minister of Justice.
  - (3) Upon request of the administrator or liquidator, the court adopts a decision on releasing property from pledge and transferring it to the administrator or liquidator.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 29.11.2012., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force

#### 379.pants. Issues to be decided by the court after declaration of insolvency of a credit institution

(1) After declaration of insolvency of a credit institution, the court shall decide on the basis of a relevant application on:

- 1) (deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.);
- 2) (deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.);
- 3) costs of the insolvency proceedings;
- 4) the procedure and time limits for debt settlement;
- 5) completion of insolvency proceedings and approval of the administrator's report;
- 6) (deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.);
- 7) acceptance of the administrator's resignation or his removal and appointment of another administrator.
  - (2) The court shall also examine complaints about the administrator's actions and decide on other issues related to the insolvency proceedings.
  - (3) The court may, in connection with the examination of the issues referred to in this Article, request that the administrator submit a report on his activities or other information.
  - (4) The court shall examine applications and complaints within 15 days from the date of their receipt. The submitter of the application or complaint, the administrator, the representatives of the credit institution appointed by the court and persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory shall be invited to the court hearing. The non-appearance of the invited persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the issue at the court hearing. However, the court may determine that the representatives of the credit institution or persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory must appear at the court hearing and order their forced attendance.
  - (5) The court shall adopt decisions on the examination of applications and complaints, which are not subject to appeal.

(With amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 380.pants. Issues to be decided by the court after declaration of liquidation of a credit institution

(1) After declaration of liquidation of a credit institution, the court shall decide on the basis of a relevant application on:

- 1) appointment of several liquidators;
- 2) acceptance of the liquidator's resignation or his removal and appointment of another liquidator;
- 3) completion of liquidation and approval of the liquidator's report.
  - (2) The court shall also examine complaints about the liquidator's actions and decide on other issues related to the liquidation.
  - (3) The court may, in connection with the examination of the issues referred to in this Article, request that the liquidator submit a report on his activities or other information.
  - (4) The court shall examine applications and complaints within 15 days from the date of their receipt. The submitter of the application or complaint, the liquidator, the representatives of the credit institution appointed by the court and persons whose participation in the liquidation of the credit institution is mandatory shall be invited to the court hearing. The non-appearance of the invited persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the issue at the court hearing. However, the court may determine that the representatives of the credit institution or persons whose participation in the liquidation is mandatory must appear at the court hearing and order their forced attendance.
  - (5) The court shall adopt decisions on the examination of applications and complaints, which are not subject to appeal.

#### 381.pants. Cancellation of reorganisation

(Deleted by the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 382.pants. Decision on initiation of bankruptcy proceedings

(Deleted by the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 383.pants. Contesting of the procedure for settling costs and debts of insolvency proceedings and liquidation

(1) Following an application by a creditor or a group of creditors, the court shall decide whether the decision of the administrator or liquidator establishing the procedure for settling costs and debts of insolvency proceedings or liquidation complies with the law.

(2) If the court finds that the procedure for settling costs and debts of insolvency proceedings established by the administrator or the procedure for settling costs and debts of liquidation established by the liquidator does not comply with the law, it shall adopt a decision establishing the procedure for settling costs and debts of insolvency proceedings or liquidation, at the same time, if necessary, deciding the issue of covering unjustified costs of insolvency proceedings or liquidation from the administrator's or liquidator's security.

#### 384. pants. Decision on completion of insolvency proceedings

The court shall decide on the completion of insolvency proceedings following an application by the administrator, to which documents certifying payment of money are attached.

(Wording of the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 385.pants. Decision on completion of liquidation

(1) The court shall decide on the completion of liquidation following an application by the liquidator.

(2) The court shall adopt a decision on completion of liquidation, at the same time approving the liquidator's report for the entire liquidation period.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 16.03.2023.)

(With amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 386.pants. Complaints about the actions of the administrator or liquidator

(1) When examining a complaint about the actions of the administrator or liquidator, the court may request a report on the activities of the administrator or liquidator and an opinion of Latvijas Banka on the activities of the administrator or liquidator and decide on his removal.

(2) If the court finds that the contested action does not comply with the law, it shall uphold the complaint and instruct the administrator or liquidator to remedy the violation committed.

(3) If the court finds that the contested action is lawful, it shall reject the complaint.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 387.pants. Decision on acceptance of the administrator's or liquidator's resignation or his removal

(1) The court shall accept the resignation of the administrator or liquidator if he submits a reasoned application to which a report on his activities is attached.

(2) The administrator or liquidator may be removed by the court following an application by Latvijas Banka. A decision of Latvijas Banka on expressing no confidence in the administrator or liquidator in connection with one of the following circumstances shall be attached to the application:

- 1) the administrator or liquidator does not comply with the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 131 or the first paragraph of Article 131.1 of the Credit Institution Law or one of the circumstances referred to in Article 132 or 132.1 is revealed;
- 2) the administrator or liquidator is not competent;
- 3) the administrator or liquidator abuses his powers.
  - (3) The court may examine the issue of removal of the administrator or liquidator following an application by a creditor or a group of creditors or on its own initiative, if it has evidence that the administrator or liquidator, in performing his duties, does not comply with the provisions of the Credit Institution Law and other regulatory enactments and court decisions, does not comply with the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 131 or the first paragraph of Article 131.1 of the Credit Institution Law or one of the circumstances referred to in Article 132 or 132.1 is revealed, the administrator or liquidator is not competent or abuses his powers.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on

#### 388. pants. Appointment of a new administrator or liquidator in case of resignation or removal of the administrator or liquidator

(1) In case of resignation or removal of the administrator, the court shall immediately appoint as administrator a candidate for the position of administrator, who is selected from the List of Candidates using an automated selection provided by the Court Information System, and shall also set a time limit for submission of a document certifying security.

(2) Having established that there are restrictions on the performance of the administrator's duties by the candidate for the position of administrator in the specific insolvency proceedings of the credit institution, the judge shall adopt a decision on refusal to appoint the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator. The judge shall adopt a decision on the appointment of the candidate for the position of administrator as administrator in the procedure established in the first paragraph of this Article.

(3) In case of resignation or removal of the liquidator, the court shall, following a recommendation by Latvijas Banka, immediately appoint another liquidator, and shall also set a time limit for submission of a document certifying security.

(Wording of the law of 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. The new wording of the Article enters into force on 01.09.2023. See transitional provision point 181.)

#### 389.pants. Appointment of Multiple Administrators or Liquidators

Chapter 48

Recognition of a Strike or Strike Notice as Unlawful

#### 390.pants. Submission of Application

(1) An application for the recognition of a strike or strike notice as unlawful in accordance with the grounds and procedure specified in the Strike Law may be submitted by the employer.

(2) The application for the recognition of a strike or strike notice as unlawful shall be submitted to the court according to the place where the strike takes place.

#### 391.pants. Content of Application

(1) The application shall indicate the strike initiators, the demands of the strike initiators or strikers, the head of the strike committee, its composition, location, the grounds specified in the Strike Law according to which the strike or strike notice is to be recognized as unlawful.

(2) The protocol of strike negotiations between the employer and the employees or the employees' trade union shall be attached to the application.

#### 392.pants. Examination of Application

(1) The court shall examine the application within 10 days from the date of its receipt. The application shall be examined in a court session, which is announced in advance to the employer, the State Labour Inspectorate and the strike committee.

(2) The participation of the applicant in the court session is mandatory. In the event of his or her non-appearance, the court has grounds to terminate the case.

#### 393.pants. Obligation of Prosecutor's Participation

Cases in connection with applications for the recognition of a strike or strike notice as unlawful shall be examined by the court with mandatory participation of a prosecutor.

#### 394.pants. Court Judgment on Application

(1) Having examined the application, the court makes a judgment by which:

- 1) recognises the employer's application as unfounded and rejects it;
- 2) recognises the employer's application as founded, and the strike or strike notice as unlawful.
  - (2) The court judgment is final and may not be appealed by way of appeal.

### Chapter 48.

Recognition of a Lockout or Lockout Notice as Unlawful

(Chapter in the version of the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

Section 394.1 Submission of Application

(1) An application for the recognition of a lockout or lockout notice as unlawful in accordance with the grounds and procedure specified in the Labour Disputes Law may be submitted by employee representatives.

(2) The application for the recognition of a lockout or lockout notice as unlawful shall be submitted to the court according to the place where the lockout takes place.

Section 394.2 Content of Application

The application shall indicate the lockout initiator and the grounds specified in the Labour Disputes Law according to which the lockout or lockout notice is to be recognized as unlawful.

Section 394.3 Examination of Application

(1) The court shall examine the application within 10 days from the date of its receipt. The application shall be examined in a court session, which is announced in advance to the employee representatives, the State Labour Inspectorate and the lockout initiators.

(2) The participation of the applicant in the court session is mandatory. If the applicant does not appear at the court session, the court has grounds to terminate the case.

Section 394.4 Obligation of Prosecutor's Participation

Cases in connection with applications for the recognition of a lockout or lockout notice as unlawful shall be examined by the court with mandatory participation of a prosecutor.

Section 394.5 Court Judgment on Application

(1) Having examined the application, the court makes a judgment by which the employee representatives' application is recognized as:

- 1) unfounded and is rejected;
- 2) founded, and the lockout or lockout notice as unlawful.
  - (2) The court judgment is final and may not be appealed by way of appeal.

### Chapter 48.

Cases on Revocation of Discharge of Natural Person from Debt Obligations

(Chapter in the version of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

Section 394.6 Jurisdiction of Cases on Revocation of Discharge of Natural Person from Debt Obligations

(1) Cases on revocation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations shall be examined by the court according to the debtor's declared place of residence or, if there is none, according to the place of residence.

(2) The case shall be examined on the basis of an application for revocation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations, which is submitted by a creditor, a sworn notary who made the notarial deed on discharge of the natural person from debt obligations, or another person whose legal rights have been infringed.

(In the version of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

Section 394.7 Resolution of Application for Revocation of Discharge of Natural Person from Debt Obligations

(1) A copy of the application shall be sent to the person concerning whose discharge from debt obligations the application has been submitted, setting a time limit for submission of explanations, not exceeding 30 days.

(2) If the applicant is not the sworn notary who made the notarial deed on discharge of the natural person from debt obligations, the court shall inform the sworn notary who made the notarial deed on discharge of the natural person from debt obligations about the initiation of the case, at the same time setting a time limit, not exceeding 30 days, for submission to the court of copies of the notarial deed on discharge of the natural person from debt obligations and other case materials.

(3) Acceptance of the application shall not suspend the operation of the notarial deed by which the natural person was discharged from debt obligations.

(4) The applicant may submit an appeal against the court decision to refuse to accept the application.

(5) If, when examining the appeal referred to in paragraph four of this Section, the court revokes the decision, the court shall refer the matter for examination to the court that made the decision.

(In the version of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

Section 394.8 Examination of Application for Revocation of Discharge of Natural Person from Debt Obligations and Court Judgment

(1) The application shall be examined in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where the court considers it necessary to examine the application in a court session or a party to the case so requests, substantiating its request.

(2) If the court grants the application, after the judgment enters into force it shall send a copy of the judgment to the responsible institution that maintains records in the insolvency register and to the sworn bailiff in whose proceedings there is an enforcement case against the debtor.

(3) Parties to the case may appeal the judgment by way of appeal within 20 days from the date of drawing up the judgment, if any of the grounds for initiating appeal proceedings referred to in Section 440.2 of this Law exists.

(In the version of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 48. nodaļa

Introduction of the real estate acquirer into possession

(Chapter in the edition of the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

394.9 pants. Jurisdiction

An application for the introduction of the real estate acquirer into possession of the real estate shall be submitted to the court that confirmed the real estate auction act (Article 613), after the decision on the confirmation of the auction act has entered into force.

(In the edition of the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

394.10 pants. Content of the application

(1) The application shall indicate information about the real estate into possession of which the introduction is to be made, and the acquirer.

(2) If introduction into possession is requested for real estate in which premises are used on the basis of a previously concluded lease agreement, the following shall be attached to the application:

- 1) documents proving the fulfilment of the requirements set by law regarding informing the tenant about the change of the real estate owner and the obligation to vacate the residential premises within two months, or
- 2) a certificate issued by a sworn notary about persons who, in response to the notary's invitation, have submitted a notification about residential premises lease agreements within the specified term, together with documents proving the fulfilment of the requirements set by law regarding informing the tenant about the obligation to vacate the residential premises within one month, or
- 3) a certificate issued by a sworn notary that no person entitled to rent the residential premises has applied within the term specified in the notary's invitation.

(In the edition of the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

394.11 pants. Examination of the application

(1) The application shall be examined in written proceedings within 20 days from the date of receipt of the application, after notifying the applicant in advance.

(2) When examining the application, Article 258 of this law shall not be applicable.

(In the edition of the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

394.12 pants. Court decision

Having found the application to be well-founded, the court shall make a decision on the introduction of the applicant into possession of the real estate. The applicant may appeal the court's refusal to introduce into possession of the real estate by way of appeal.

(In the edition of the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

Septītā sadaļa

Enforcement of obligations through court

49.nodaļa

Voluntary sale of real estate at auction through court

#### 395.pants. Jurisdiction

An application for the voluntary sale of real estate at auction through court shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the location of the real estate.

#### 396.pants. Application for the voluntary sale of real estate at auction through court

(1) An application for the voluntary sale of real estate at auction through court may be submitted by the owner or the pledgee who has the right to sell the pledge at a free price.

(2) The application for the voluntary sale of real estate at auction through court shall be accompanied by the terms of sale and a printout from the relevant land register section indicating the entries and notes in force, but if the application has been submitted by the pledgee — also the pledge agreement, evidence of warning the debtor, unless the law provides that such warning is not necessary. Confirmation of the issuance of the warning may also be an act drawn up by a sworn bailiff or his assistant regarding the refusal to receive the warning.

(3) The terms of sale shall indicate:

- 1) the composition of the real estate to be sold;
- 2) encumbrances and pledges of the real estate;
- 3) the starting price of the auction;
- 4) the method and procedure of payment of the highest bid price;
- 5) rights to the real estate that the owner reserves for himself;
- 6) other terms of sale that the seller considers necessary.
  - (4) If the real estate to be sold is in the joint ownership of several persons, then, when ordering the sale at auction through court upon the owner's application, the consent of all co-owners is required.
  - (5) If the same pledgee has registered first mortgages on the real estate of the same debtor and they are functionally related to each other or have a common border, the applicant has the right to request the court to auction the real estate indicated in the application as a whole.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009., the Constitutional Court judgment of 24.11.2010., the laws of 20.12.2010., 08.09.2011. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 397.pants. Judge's decision

(1) The application for the voluntary sale of real estate at auction shall be examined by a judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the attached documents within seven days from the date of submission of the application, without notifying the applicant and the debtor thereof.

(2) The judge shall make a decision to allow the sale at auction, having ascertained that:

- 1) the real estate belongs to the applicant or to the pledgee's debtor and the pledgee has the right to sell the real estate at a free price;
- 2) there are no legal obstacles to the sale of this real estate with the terms indicated in the application.

(In the edition of the law of 31.10.2002., which comes into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 398.pants. Auction procedure

The sale at auction shall be carried out by a bailiff in the procedure established in this law for the enforcement of court judgments, observing

the provisions of Articles 2075, 2083, 2084, 2087, 2089 and 2090 of the Civil Law and the following conditions:

- 1) the real estate shall be described and appraised only if requested by the person on whose application the sale takes place;
- 2) the announcement shall indicate the terms of sale, as well as that the sale is voluntary;
- 3) the auction shall be commenced by reading out the terms of sale;
- 4) upon the request of the applicant, the auction may be deemed to have taken place even if only one buyer has appeared;
- 5) if, in accordance with the terms of sale, the acceptance of the highest bid price depends on the person on whose application the sale takes place, and if he has not expressed his opinion thereon within the time provided for in the terms of sale or set by the court, it shall be deemed that he has tacitly agreed to the highest bid price.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which comes into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 399.pants. Documents to be issued to the buyer

(1) After the buyer of the real estate has fulfilled all the terms of sale, the district (city) court shall decide on the confirmation of the auction act (Articles 611 and 613) and the registration of the sold real estate in the name of the buyer. If insolvency proceedings have been declared for the owner of the real estate, the district (city) court in whose proceedings the legal person's insolvency case is located shall decide on the confirmation of the auction act and the registration of the sold real estate in the name of the buyer.

(2) The court decision, together with the auction terms and the auction act, shall be issued to the buyer.

(In the edition of the law of 19.06.2003. with amendments made by the laws of 30.09.2010., 11.09.2014. and 25.10.2018., which comes into force on 28.11.2018. The amendment in the first part regarding the replacement of the words "land register department of the district (city) court" with the words "district (city) court" comes into force on 01.06.2019. See transitional provision 151.) 50.nodaļa

Uncontested forced enforcement of obligations

#### 400.pants. Obligations Subject to Uncontested Enforcement

(1) Uncontested enforcement of obligations is permitted:

- 1) under contracts for obligations secured by a public mortgage or commercial pledge;
- 2) under notarially certified and legally equivalent term contracts for payment of money or return of movable property;
- 3) under notarially certified or registered in the land register term property lease or rent contracts that provide for the lessee's or tenant's obligation to vacate the leased or rented property due to expiry of the term or non-payment of lease or rent, as well as the obligation to pay lease or rent;
- 4) under protested bills of exchange that have not been issued in the form of a notarial deed.
  - (11) The first part of this article does not apply to notarial deeds made in the procedure specified in Section D1 of the Notarial Law.
  - (2) The obligations specified in the first part of this article are not subject to uncontested enforcement if:
- 1) this enforcement is directed against state or municipal property;
- 2) the obligation has been extinguished by limitation, the expiry of which is clearly evident from the deed itself.

(As amended by the laws of 23.05.2013., 25.03.2021. and 16.06.2022., which entered into force on 07.07.2022. The new version of point 4 of the first part enters into force on 01.10.2022. See transitional provision point 178)

#### 401.pants. Persons Who May Submit an Application for Uncontested Enforcement

An application for uncontested enforcement may be submitted by:

- 1) the person in whose name the deed (contract, bill of exchange) has been issued;
- 2) the person to whom the deed has been transferred by a separate land register deed or notarial deed;
- 3) the heir of the aforementioned persons, if his or her inheritance rights are proven by a court judgment, certificate of inheritance or European Certificate of Succession on the entry into legal force of a will or confirmation of inheritance rights, or a court decision by which he or she has been introduced into possession of the bequeathed property (Article 638 of the Civil Law), or a court decision or notarial certificate recognizing that he or she has accepted the inheritance (Article 697 of the Civil Law);
- 4) a guarantor who has paid on behalf of the debtor on the basis of a court judgment or by way of enforcement, or whose payment has been confirmed by an inscription on the deed;
- 5) under real estate lease or rent contracts — the acquirer of this property, if the acquirer's rights are certified by a land register deed or by the documents specified in point 3 of this article on the transfer of property by inheritance;
- 6) under protested bills of exchange — the holder of the bill of exchange in whose name the bill has been protested, as well as the guarantor, endorser (endorser) and intermediary who have paid the bill and are raising a recourse claim.

(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002., 23.05.2013. and 28.05.2015., which entered into force on 02.07.2015.

The amendment to point 3 enters into force on 17.08.2015. See transitional provision point 108)

#### 402.pants. Persons Against Whom Uncontested Enforcement is Permitted

Uncontested enforcement is permitted:

- 1) against the person in whose name the deed has been issued (contracting party), but under a protested bill of exchange — against all persons liable for it;
- 2) against a guarantor, if he or she has assumed an obligation as the debtor himself or herself (second part of Article 1702 of the Civil Law);
- 3) against the heir of the person who assumed the obligation, if there is evidence of acceptance of the inheritance as mentioned in point 3 of Article 401 of this law.

#### 403.pants. Jurisdiction

(1) Applications for uncontested enforcement in monetary payment obligations, movable property return obligations or obligations under contracts secured by a commercial pledge shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence or legal address.

(2) Applications for uncontested enforcement under real estate mortgage deeds and under obligations to vacate or return leased or rented real estate shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the location of the real estate. If the obligation is secured by several real estates and the applications fall under the jurisdiction of different district (city) courts, the application shall be examined by the district (city) court at the applicant's choice — according to the location of one real estate.

(3) Applications for uncontested enforcement under a ship mortgage obligation shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the place of registration of the mortgage.

(As amended by the laws of 08.09.2011., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012. and 25.10.2018., which entered into force on 28.11.2018. The amendments to the article enter into force on 01.06.2019. See transitional provision point 151)

#### 404.pants. Content of Application

(1) The application shall indicate which obligation and under which deed the creditor requests to subject to uncontested enforcement.

(11) The application shall include a confirmation that truthful information about the facts has been provided to the court and that the applicant or representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed that the Criminal Law provides for liability for submitting a false application.

(2) The application for uncontested enforcement for payment of money shall indicate the principal debt to be recovered, contractual penalties and interest — both agreed and stipulated by law, but under a bill of exchange — also expenses related to the protest and compensation stipulated by law, as well as the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment is to be made.

(3) The application shall be accompanied by:

- 1) the deed to be executed by uncontested enforcement;
- 11) under a protested paper form bill of exchange — the bill of exchange, its derivative and protest deed in paper form;
- 12) under a protested electronic bill of exchange — the electronic bill of exchange and electronic protest deed;
- 2) a document on payment of state duty, except when the application has been submitted and payment made in an online system;
- 3) proof of issuance of a warning to the debtor (including to the owner of the real estate or the pledgor of the commercial pledge), if it does not follow from the law that such a warning is not necessary. Confirmation of the issuance of a warning may also be a deed drawn up by a sworn bailiff or his assistant on refusal to receive a warning.

(As amended by the laws of 08.09.2011., 19.12.2013., 22.06.2017., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 405.pants. Judge's Decision

(1) An application for uncontested enforcement of obligations shall be decided by a judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and attached documents within seven days from the date of submission of the application, without notifying the applicant and the debtor thereof.

(2) The judge, having verified the validity of the submitted application and recognized that it is satisfactory, adopts a decision determining which obligation and to what extent is to be executed by uncontested enforcement. The decision shall be notified to the applicant and the debtor.

(21) If the decision establishes a person's obligation to vacate the leased or rented property before the end of the term specified in the contract, the judge shall determine in this part a two-month period for voluntary execution of the decision.

(3) The judge's decision shall enter into force immediately and has the force of an enforcement document. The decision shall be executed in accordance with the rules for execution of judgments. It shall be submitted for execution together with a copy of the deed subject to uncontested enforcement.

(4) If the judge recognizes that the application is not justified or the amount of contractual penalty specified in the application is disproportionate to the principal debt, or the enforceable deed contains unfair contract terms violating consumer rights, he or she shall adopt a decision to reject it. The judge shall send the decision together with the submitted documents to the applicant.

(As amended by the laws of 05.02.2009., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 406.pants. Procedure for Contesting Undisputed Enforcement

(1) If the debtor considers that the creditor's claim is not substantiated in substance, within six months from the date of sending the decision, he may bring an action against the creditor to contest the claim. The action shall be brought before a court in accordance with the general procedure for bringing an action established in this law.

(2) If the debtor considers that the creditor's claim is not substantiated in substance, within six months from the date when the notarial enforcement document issued by a sworn notary was sent to the debtor, he may bring an action against the creditor to contest the claim.

(3) When bringing an action, the debtor may request to suspend the undisputed enforcement or the execution of a notarial enforcement document issued by a sworn notary, but if the claimant has already received satisfaction in this manner — to request securing of the claim.

(31) When bringing an action against the creditor to contest a claim that is based on a court decision on undisputed enforcement of obligations, the insolvency administrator may request the court to apply an interim protection measure — withdrawal of voting rights.

(4) When adopting a decision on a debtor's application for suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial enforcement document, the court or judge takes into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim.

(41) When adopting a decision on an insolvency administrator's application for an interim protection measure — withdrawal of voting rights, the court takes into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim. The court's decision is not subject to appeal.

(5) A decision on a debtor's application for suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial enforcement document, by which the debtor's application has been granted, is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. The debtor may file a separate complaint against a decision rejecting the application.

(6) Upon a reasoned application by the creditor, the court which has suspended the execution or in whose proceedings the case to be examined on the merits is located, may revoke the suspension of execution. A decision to revoke the suspension of execution is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. The creditor may file a separate complaint against a decision rejecting the application.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.05.2013., 30.10.2014., 12.02.2015. and 11.11.2021., which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 50. nodaļa

Enforcement of obligations by way of warning

(Chapter as amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which entered into force on 01.01.2003.)

406.1 pants. Obligations for which enforcement by way of warning is permissible

(1) Enforcement of obligations by way of warning is permissible in respect of payment obligations which are substantiated by a document and for which the enforcement term has arrived, as well as in respect of payment obligations for remuneration agreed in a contract for the supply of goods, purchase of goods or provision of services, if these obligations are substantiated by a document and no enforcement term has been specified for them.

(2) Enforcement of obligations by way of warning is not permissible:

- 1) for payments which are connected with unfulfilled counter-performance;
- 2) if the debtor's declared place of residence or place of residence is not known;
- 3) if the debtor's declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is not in the Republic of Latvia;
- 4) if the contractual penalty claimed exceeds 10 percent of the principal debt amount;
- 5) if the interest claimed exceeds the principal debt amount;
- 6) for payment obligations if the debt amount exceeds 15,000 euros;
- 7) for joint and several payment obligations.

(As amended by the laws of 07.09.2006, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 29.11.2012 and 19.12.2013, which entered into force on 04.01.2014.)

406.2 pants. Jurisdiction

(1) Enforcement of obligations by way of warning shall be initiated upon the application of the creditor.

(2) An application for the enforcement of an obligation by way of warning has jurisdiction in a district (city) court if the debtor's declared place of residence or, if there is none, place of residence or legal address is in the Republic of Latvia. (As amended by the laws of 04.08.2011, 29.11.2012, 25.10.2018 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 406.3 pants. Submission of application

(1) An application shall be submitted using the online form available in the online system.

(2) The application shall indicate:

- 1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);

- 3) the debtor's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and the additional address indicated in the declaration, or, if there is none, — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;
- 4) the applicant's representative's (if the application is submitted by a representative) name, surname, personal identity number, for a legal person
  - its name, registration number and an indication that the applicant's representative agrees to communicate with the court using the online system;
- 5) the payment obligation in connection with which the application is submitted, indicating identifying information of the document substantiating the obligation and the term of performance of the obligation, as well as the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment is to be made, if any;
- 6) the amount claimed and its calculation, indicating the principal debt, contractual penalty, agreed or statutory interest and court costs;
- 7) the applicant's confirmation that the claim is not dependent on counter-performance or that counter-performance has been made, or that the payment obligation is not joint and several;
- 8) a request to the court to issue a warning to the debtor;
- 9) a request to decide on the enforcement of the payment obligation and the recovery of court costs;
- 10) a confirmation that true information about the facts has been provided to the court and that the applicant or representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed that the Criminal Law provides for liability for submitting a false application.
  - (21) In the application, the applicant may include an indication to the court to issue a warning to the debtor through a bailiff.
  - (3) Documents confirming payment of the state fee and expenses related to the issuance of court documents shall be attached to the application, except when payment has been made in the online system.
  - (4) Non-compliance of the application with the requirements of Articles 406.1, 406.2 and 406.3 of this Law is an obstacle to the submission of the application. If non-compliance of the application with the requirements of Articles 406.1, 406.2 and 406.3 of this Law has not been an obstacle to the submission of the application in the manner specified in paragraph one of this Article, the judge shall adopt a reasoned decision to refuse to accept the application and shall send it to the applicant. The decision to refuse to accept the application is not subject to appeal.
  - (5) The judge's refusal to accept an application is not an obstacle to the submission of the same application to the court when the deficiencies have been remedied, or to the bringing of an action in adversarial proceedings. In such cases, the state fee paid and the expenses related to the issuance of the warning shall be credited if, after remedying the deficiencies, the same application is submitted to the court or an action is brought in adversarial proceedings.

(As amended by the laws of 05.02.2009, 29.11.2012, 19.12.2013, 23.04.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017, 01.03.2018, 11.11.2021, 09.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which entered into force on 07.07.2022.)

406.4 pants. Basis for non-acceptance of application
