406.5 pants. Content of warning

(1) A warning shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) The warning shall indicate:

- 1) the warning number and the name of the court issuing the warning;
- 2) the applicant, the payment obligation, identifying information of the documents substantiating the obligation, the term of performance of the obligation, the amount claimed and its calculation, the name of the credit institution and the account number to which payment is to be made, if any;
- 3) the debtor;
- 4) that the court has not verified the validity of the claim;
- 5) a proposal to the debtor to pay the amount specified in the application within 14 days from the date of issuance of the warning, notifying the court thereof, or to submit objections to the court;
- 6) that the obligation specified in the warning will be referred for enforcement if objections or evidence of payment are not submitted within the specified 14 days.
  - (3) The warning shall be certified with a qualified electronic seal within the meaning of point 27 of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 July 2014 on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC (hereinafter — Regulation No.

910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council).

(As amended by the laws of 05.02.2009 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

406.6 pants. Issuance of warning to debtor

(1) The warning and response form, which is drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers, shall be issued to the debtor against signature. The document with the signature of receipt and a note on the date of issuance of the warning shall be submitted to the court.

(11) If the application contains an indication for the issuance of the warning to the debtor through a bailiff, the warning and response form referred to in paragraph one of this Article shall be issued to the applicant for delivery to the debtor. In such a case, the confirmation of the issuance of the warning is an act of the bailiff or his assistant submitted to the court on the delivery of the warning or an act on the refusal to receive the warning. The delivery of the warning shall be performed by the bailiff at the expense of the applicant, and the expenses related to the delivery are not recoverable from the debtor.

(2) In a case where the issuance of the warning to the debtor is not possible, or in the case referred to in paragraph 1.1 of this Article — within one month from the date when the warning was sent to the applicant for delivery to the debtor and the bailiff or his assistant does not submit to the court an act on the delivery of the warning or an act on the refusal to receive the warning,

— the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the application without consideration. The decision shall be communicated to the applicant in the online system.

(3) Leaving the application without consideration is not an obstacle to the repeated submission of an application for the enforcement of an obligation by way of warning or to the bringing of an action in adversarial proceedings. In such cases, the state fee paid shall be credited.

(As amended by the laws of 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 01.03.2018 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 406.7 pants. Debtor's response

(1) The debtor's response shall be drawn up in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers. The debtor may provide a response using the online form available in the online system. In such a case, the debtor has agreed to communicate with the court using the online system.

(2) Objections of the debtor submitted within the time limit against the validity of the payment obligation or payment of the debt is a basis for terminating the proceedings for the enforcement of the obligation by way of warning.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(4) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(5) If the debtor acknowledges the application in part, the judge shall adopt a decision in the acknowledged part in accordance with the requirements of Article 406.9 of this Law, but in the remaining part the proceedings shall be terminated.

(6) A debtor's response submitted after the specified time limit, but before the adoption of a decision in the case, shall be deemed to have been submitted within the time limit.

(7) If the debtor's response does not contain a confirmation that true information has been provided to the court, and that the debtor or representative, if the response is submitted by a representative, has been informed that the Criminal Law provides for liability for submitting a false response, the debtor's response shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.

(As amended by the laws of 19.06.2003, 05.02.2009, 23.04.2015 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 406.8 pants. Termination of proceedings

(1) The judge shall adopt a decision on the termination of proceedings for the enforcement of an obligation by way of warning. A decision on the termination of proceedings is not subject to appeal.

(2) The decision and the debtor's response shall be communicated to the applicant.

(3) A decision on the termination of proceedings for the enforcement of an obligation by way of warning due to objections of the debtor is not an obstacle to the bringing of an action in adversarial proceedings. In such cases, the state fee paid shall be credited.

(As amended by the laws of 19.06.2003, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 406.9 pants. Judge's decision on enforcement of obligation

(1) If the debtor has not submitted objections within the time limit specified in the warning, the judge shall adopt a decision on the enforcement of the payment obligation specified in the application and the recovery of court costs within seven days from the date of expiry of the time limit for objections. The decision shall be sent to the debtor within three days. The decision shall be communicated to the applicant.

(2) The judge's decision shall enter into force immediately, has the force of an enforcement document, and is enforceable in accordance with the rules for the enforcement of court judgments.

(As amended by the law of 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

406.10 pants. Procedure for contesting enforcement of obligation

(1) If the debtor considers that the applicant's claim is not substantively justified, he may bring an action against the creditor to contest the claim within three months from the date of sending of the decision. The action shall be brought in court in the general procedure for bringing an action specified in this Law.

(2) When bringing an action, the debtor may request the suspension of the enforcement of the obligation, but if the creditor has already received satisfaction in such a manner, request the securing of the action.

(3) When adopting a decision on the debtor's application for the suspension of enforcement by way of warning, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the action.

(4) A decision by which the application is granted is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. The debtor may submit an incidental appeal against a decision by which the application is rejected.

(5) Upon a reasoned application of the creditor, the court which suspended the enforcement or in whose proceedings the case to be examined on the merits is pending may cancel the suspension of enforcement. A decision on the cancellation of the suspension of enforcement is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. The creditor may submit an incidental appeal against a decision by which the application is rejected.

(6) When bringing an action against the creditor to contest a claim substantiated by a court decision on the enforcement of an obligation by way of warning, the insolvency proceedings administrator may request the court to apply an interim protection measure — deprivation of voting rights.

(7) When adopting a decision on the insolvency proceedings administrator's application for an interim protection measure — deprivation of voting rights, the court shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the action. The court's decision is not subject to appeal.

(As amended by the laws of 29.11.2012, 23.05.2013, 30.10.2014, 12.02.2015 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

## Part C

Appeal of Court Judgments and Decisions

Eighth Division

Appeal Proceedings

Chapter 52

Submission of Appeal

#### 413.pants. Right to Submit Appeal or Appeal Protest

(1) Parties to a case may submit an appeal, but a prosecutor — an appeal protest, regarding a first instance court judgment (supplementary judgment) in the manner prescribed in this chapter, except for judgments for which the law does not provide for appeal. A representative shall submit an appeal in accordance with the requirements of Section 86 of this law.

(2) An appeal protest shall be submitted and examined in the same manner as an appeal, unless otherwise provided in this division.

#### 414.pants. Procedure for Submission of Appeal

(1) A judgment of a district (city) court that has not entered into legal force may be appealed to the respective regional court.

(2) (Deleted by the law of 30.10.2014)

(3) An appeal addressed to the appellate court shall be submitted to the court that made the judgment.

(4) If an appeal is submitted directly to the appellate court within the time limit, the time limit shall not be considered missed.

(With amendments made by the law of 30.10.2014, which comes into force on 01.01.2015.)

#### 415.pants. Time Limits for Submission of Appeal

(1) An appeal regarding a first instance court judgment may be submitted within 20 days from the date of announcement of the judgment.

(2) If a judgment is prepared after a date set by the court (Section 199), the time limit for appeal of the judgment shall be calculated from the date of actual preparation of the judgment.

(21) (Deleted by the law of 22.05.2008)

(22) In the cases provided for in paragraphs one and two of this section, a party to whom a judgment has been sent in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law may submit an appeal within 20 days from the date of issuance of the judgment.

(3) An appeal submitted after expiry of the time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002, 01.11.2007, 22.05.2008, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 416. pants. Content of Appeal and Documents to Be Attached Thereto

(1) An appeal shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the appeal is addressed;
- 2) the name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence of the submitter of the appeal, but if there is none — place of residence, for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the submitter of the appeal agrees to electronic communication with the court, an email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, an indication of registration shall also be included;
- 21) the email address of the representative and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, an indication of registration shall also be included, if the appeal is submitted by a representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia and who agrees to electronic communication with the court. If the representative's address is outside Latvia, an email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of participation in the online system shall be provided;
- 3) the judgment about which the appeal is submitted and the court that made the judgment;
- 4) to what extent the judgment is being appealed;
- 5) how the incorrectness of the judgment manifests itself, with reasoning as to why the submitter of the appeal considers that the facts have been incorrectly established in the case or the evidence has been incorrectly assessed, an incorrect legal assessment of the circumstances of the case has been given or a substantive law provision has been incorrectly applied, a procedural law provision has been violated;
- 6) whether new evidence is being presented, what kind, about what circumstances and why this evidence was not submitted to the first instance court;
- 7) the request of the submitter of the appeal;
- 8) a list of documents attached to the appeal.
  - (2) An appeal shall be signed by the submitter or their authorized representative. An appeal protest shall be signed by the official of the prosecutor's office as prescribed by law.
  - (3) (Deleted by the law of 23.04.2015)
  - (4) An unsigned appeal shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.
  - (5) A judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept an appeal if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorization to appeal a court judgment is not attached thereto.
  - (6) In cases provided for by law, a certified translation shall be attached to the appeal and the documents attached thereto if the documents are intended for issuance to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law.

A translation need not be attached by a person who is exempt from payment of court costs.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002, 29.11.2012, 23.04.2015, 28.05.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017 and

11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 417.pants. Copies of Appeal

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 418.pants. Limits of Appeal

(1) An appeal may not change the subject or basis of a claim, include new claims that have not been brought in the first instance court.

(2) The following shall not be considered new claims:

- 1) specification of claims;
- 2) correction of obvious errors in the claim;
- 3) addition of interest and increments to the claim;
- 4) a claim to compensate for the value of property due to alienation, loss or changes in the composition of the claimed property;
- 5) modification of components of the total amount of the claim within the limits of this amount;
- 6) modification of a claim requesting recognition of rights to a claim to restore infringed rights due to circumstances that have changed during the course of the case;
- 7) increase in the amount of the claim due to market prices that have increased during the course of the case.

#### 419.pants. Joining an Appeal

(1) Co-participants and third parties participating in the proceedings on the side of the party that has submitted the appeal may join the submitted appeal.

(2) Joining an appeal shall be notified in writing to the appellate court no later than 10 days before the hearing of the case in the appellate instance.

(3) An application for joining an appeal shall not be subject to payment of a state fee.

#### 420.pants. Leaving Appeal Without Movement

(1) A judge of the first instance court shall adopt a decision to leave an appeal without movement and shall set a time limit for the submitter to remedy deficiencies if:

- 1) an appeal has been submitted that does not comply with the requirements of paragraph one of Section 416 of this law;
- 2) in cases provided for by law, a certified translation of the appeal and documents attached thereto has not been attached;
- 3) an appeal has been submitted for which a state fee has not been paid;
- 4) from the power of attorney attached to the appeal or other document, authorization for the representative to appeal a court judgment does not follow.
  - (2) If the deficiencies are remedied within the set time limit, the appeal shall be considered as submitted on the day it was submitted for the first time. Otherwise, the appeal shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the submitter.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009, 23.04.2015 and 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 421.pants. Appeal of Judge's Decision

A separate appeal may be submitted regarding a judge's decision to refuse to accept an appeal, except in the case referred to in paragraph five of Section

416 of this law.

(With amendments made by the law of 23.04.2015, which comes into force on 26.05.2015.)

#### 422.pants. First instance court action after receiving an appeal complaint

(1) The first instance court judge, having ascertained that the appeal complaint meets the requirements of Article 416 of this law, immediately notifies the other parties to the case about this complaint and sends them the complaint, specifying the deadline for submission of written explanation. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the appeal complaint may also be sent to the other parties to the case.

(2) After the expiry of the deadline for submitting the appeal complaint, the judge immediately sends the case with the complaint and the documents attached to it to the appellate court.

(With amendments made by the laws of 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### 423.pants. Written explanation of a party to the case

(1) A party to the case may submit a written explanation regarding the submitted appeal complaint to the appellate court within 30 days from the day the appeal complaint was sent to them, but in cases concerning children — within 15 days from the day the appeal complaint was sent to them.

(2) The court sends the explanation to the other parties to the case.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 22.05.2008.)

(4) If the appeal complaint was sent to a party to the case in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law, the deadline for submission of written explanation is counted from the day the appeal complaint was issued to the party to the case.

(With amendments made by the laws of 01.11.2007, 22.05.2008, 05.02.2009, 29.10.2015 and 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 424.pants. Counter-appeal complaint

(1) After the issuance of an appeal complaint, a party has the right to submit a counter-appeal complaint.

(2 ) The counter-appeal complaint must comply with the requirements of Articles 413, 416 and 418 of this law.

(3) The counter-appeal complaint must be submitted to the appellate court within the deadline provided for in Article 423 of this law.

(4) After receiving a counter-appeal complaint, the appellate court immediately sends it to the other parties to the case.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009 and 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

53.nodaļa

Examination of cases in the appellate instance

#### 425.pants. Initiation of appellate proceedings

(1) Having ascertained that the procedure for submitting the appeal complaint has been observed, the judge, after receiving the explanation or after the expiry of the deadline set for its submission, adopts a decision to initiate appellate proceedings and schedules the case for examination at a session of the appellate court.

(11) In cases concerning the reinstatement of an employee to work and in cases concerning the recognition of an employer's dismissal as invalid, the date of the court session must be set no later than 15 days after receiving the explanation or the expiry of the deadline for its submission.

(12) In cases concerning claims by administrators on behalf of insolvent debtors in the cases specified in Chapter XVII of the Insolvency Law and concerning the recovery of damages from members of management institutions of legal entities and members (shareholders) of capital companies, based on their obligation to be liable for damages caused, as well as from personally liable members of partnerships, based on their obligation to be liable for the obligations of the partnership, the court session must be set no later than three months after receiving the explanation or the expiry of the deadline for its submission.

(2) Having found that the appeal complaint was sent to the appellate court in violation of the procedure for submitting appeal complaints established in this law, the judge adopts one of the following decisions:

- 1) to refuse to initiate appellate proceedings if the deadline set for submitting the appeal complaint has been missed or if the appeal complaint is not accompanied by a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorization to appeal the court judgment; in this case, the complaint together with the case is sent to the first instance court, which returns the complaint to the submitter;
- 2) to send the case to the first instance court for the performance of actions established by law if, when submitting the appeal complaint, the deficiencies specified in the first paragraph of Article 416 of this law were committed, the state fee has not been paid, or the authorization for the representative to appeal the court judgment does not follow from the power of attorney or other document attached to the appeal complaint.
  - (3) If the circumstances specified in point 1 of the second paragraph of this article are established at a session of the appellate court, the court adopts a decision to leave the appeal complaint without examination.
  - (4) Before the appellate court initiates the transfer of an appeal case under its examination to another regional court for examination in accordance with Article 32.1 of this law, the court sends information to the parties about the court's proposal to transfer the case for examination to another court and about the obligation to notify the court within the specified deadline if the transfer of the case for examination to another court will create significant obstacles for any of the parties to appear at the court session.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002, 07.04.2004, 01.11.2007, 22.05.2008, 30.09.2010, 21.01.2021 and

16.03.2023, which comes into force on 29.03.2023.)

#### 426.pants. Limits of case examination in the appellate instance

(1) The appellate court examines the case on its merits in connection with the appeal complaint and counter-appeal complaint to the extent requested in these complaints.

(2) The appellate instance examines only those claims that were examined in the first instance court. Amendment of the subject or basis of the claim is not permitted.

(3) The appellate court examines the case on its merits without sending it for new examination to the first instance court, except in the cases specified in Article 427 of this law.

#### 427.pants. Cases when a first instance court judgment is to be revoked and the case sent for new

examination in the first instance court

(1) The appellate court, regardless of the grounds of the appeal complaint, revokes the judgment of the first instance court by decision and sends the case for new examination to the first instance court if the appellate court establishes that:

- 1) the court examined the case in an unlawful composition;
- 2) the court examined the case in violation of procedural law norms that establish the obligation to notify the parties to the case of the time and place of the court session;
- 3) procedural law norms concerning the language of proceedings were violated;
- 4) the court judgment grants rights or imposes obligations on a person who was not joined in the case as a party;
- 5) there is no court session protocol or court judgment in the case.
  - (2) The appellate court, recognizing as justified an appeal complaint regarding the part of the court judgment by which the proceedings in the case were terminated or the claim was left without examination, revokes the first instance judgment in this part and sends the case for examination to the first instance court.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.05.2018, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 428.pants. Procedure for trial in the appellate court

(1) Parties to the case are invited and other persons are summoned to court in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 6 of this law.

(2) The session of the appellate court takes place in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 21 of this law, observing the specifics established in this chapter.

#### 429.pants. Provision of explanations in the appellate court

(1) At the session of the appellate court, the submitter of the appeal complaint provides explanations first, but if both parties have submitted complaints — the plaintiff.

(2) If the prosecutor has submitted an appeal protest, they provide explanations before the explanations of the other parties to the case.

#### 430.pants. Examination of Evidence in the Court of Appeal

(1) The court of appeal itself decides which evidence to examine in the court session.

(2) When examining and evaluating evidence, the court of appeal observes the provisions of the third section of this law.

(3) Facts established in the first instance court need not be examined in the court of appeal if they have not been contested in the appeal.

(4) If in the court of appeal a party submits or requests to examine evidence which it was possible for them to submit in the examination of the case in the first instance court, and if the court of appeal does not establish justifiable reasons why the evidence was not submitted in the first instance court, the court of appeal shall not accept the evidence.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 431.pants. Termination of Appeal Proceedings

(1) The appellant (counter-appellant) has the right to withdraw it until the examination of the case on the merits has been completed.

(2) If the appeal is withdrawn, the court of appeal adopts a decision to terminate the appeal proceedings, except in cases where other parties have submitted appeals (counter-appeals) or where an appeal protest has been filed.

(3) If the appellant fails to appear at the court session twice without justifiable reason and has not requested the case to be examined in their absence, the court may terminate the appeal proceedings.

(4) If the appeal proceedings are terminated, the state fee shall not be refunded.

54.nodaļa

Judgment or Decision of the Court of Appeal

#### 432.pants. Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1) The decision of the court of appeal by which the case is adjudicated on the merits shall be made in the form of a judgment.

(2) The court of appeal makes the judgment in the procedure established in Articles 189—198 of this law, unless otherwise provided in this Article.

(3) In the introductory part of the judgment, in addition to the circumstances mentioned in the third paragraph of Article 193 of this law, the court shall indicate the appellant and the court judgment against which the appeal has been filed.

(4) In the descriptive part of the judgment, the court shall include a brief exposition of the reasoning and operative part of the first instance court judgment, as well as a brief content of the appeal (counter-appeal) and objections.

(5) In the reasoning part of the judgment, the circumstances mentioned in the fifth paragraph of Article 193 of this law shall be indicated, and the attitude towards the first instance court judgment shall be reasoned. If the court, when examining the case, recognizes that the reasoning contained in the lower instance court judgment is correct and fully sufficient, it may indicate in the reasoning part of the judgment that it agrees with the argumentation of the lower instance court judgment. In such case, the considerations established in the fifth paragraph of Article 193 of this law may not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.

(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 28.05.2015. and 09.06.2016., which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

#### 433.pants. Pronouncement of the Court of Appeal Judgment

(1) The court of appeal pronounces the judgment in the procedure established in Article 199 of this law.

(2) The judgment shall be sent to the parties in the cases and procedure provided for in Article 208 of this law.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 434.pants. Entry into Legal Force of the Court of Appeal Judgment

(1) The court of appeal judgment enters into legal force when the time limit for appealing it in cassation has expired and a cassation appeal has not been filed.

(2) If a cassation appeal has been filed, the court of appeal judgment enters into legal force simultaneously with:

- 1) the decision of the procedural session of the Supreme Court, if it has refused to initiate cassation proceedings (third paragraph of Article 464 and Article 464.1);
- 2) the judgment of the cassation court, if the court of appeal judgment has not been set aside or the judgment or part thereof has been set aside and the application has been left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated (Article 474).
  - (3) The provisions of the second, third, fourth and fifth paragraphs of Article 203 of this law apply to the legal force of the court of appeal judgment.
  - (31) If with respect to any party the time limit for filing a cassation appeal against the court of appeal judgment is determined in accordance with paragraph 2.2 of Article 454 of this law, the court of appeal judgment enters into legal force after the time limit for appealing it has elapsed, counting the time limit from the later date of issuance of the judgment, if a cassation appeal has not been filed.
  - (32) If in the cases mentioned in paragraph 3.1 of this Article the relevant confirmation of the issuance of the judgment has not been received (Article 56.2), the judgment enters into legal force six months after its pronouncement.
  - (4) The court of appeal judgment shall be enforced in accordance with Articles 204, 204.1 and the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 205 of this law. Immediate enforcement of the judgment in the case provided for in point 7 of the first paragraph of Article 205 of this law is permissible only by demanding from the creditor adequate security in case the cassation court adopts the judgment mentioned in points 2, 3 or 4 of Article 474 of this law.

(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008. with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 435.pants. Correction of Clerical and Mathematical Calculation Errors in the Court of Appeal

Judgment

(1) The court of appeal, on its own initiative or at the request of a party, has the right to correct clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment.

(2) The question of correcting errors shall be decided in written proceedings, having previously notified the parties thereof. If the application has been submitted by a party, simultaneously with sending the notice to the parties, the court shall send them the application for correction of clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment.

(3) A party may file an ancillary appeal against the court's decision to make a correction of an error in the judgment.

(With amendments made by the law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

#### 436.pants. Additional Judgment of the Court of Appeal

(1) The court of appeal may, on its own initiative or at the request of a party, make an additional judgment if:

- 1) a judgment has not been made on any of the claims which have been the subject of examination by the court of appeal;
- 2) the court has not determined the amount of the sum awarded, the property to be transferred, or the actions to be performed;
- 3) the judgment has not decided on the reimbursement of litigation costs.
  - (2) The making of an additional judgment may be initiated within the time limit for appealing the judgment established by law.
  - (3) The court makes an additional judgment after examining the question at a court session, having previously notified the parties thereof. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to making an additional judgment or rejecting the application.
  - (4) (Excluded by the law of 05.02.2009.)
  - (5) An ancillary appeal may be filed against the court's decision to refuse to make an additional judgment.

(With amendments made by the law of 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### 437.pants. Clarification of the Court of Appeal Judgment

(1) The court of appeal may, at the request of a party, clarify the judgment by its decision without changing its content.

(2) Clarification of the judgment is permissible if it has not yet been enforced and the time limit for enforcement of the judgment has not elapsed.

(3) The question of clarification of the judgment shall be examined in written proceedings, having previously notified the parties thereof. Simultaneously with the notice, the court shall send to the parties the application for clarification of the judgment.

(4) An ancillary appeal may be filed against the court's decision on the question of clarification of the judgment.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

#### 438.pants. Postponement of enforcement of the judgment of the court of appeal, division into installments, amendment of its method and procedure of enforcement

(1) The court of appeal has the right, upon application of a party to the case, taking into account the financial situation of the parties or other important circumstances, to postpone the enforcement of the judgment or divide it into installments, as well as to amend the method and procedure of its enforcement. A decision on the postponement of enforcement of the judgment, division into installments or amendment of the method and procedure of enforcement shall be enforced immediately.

(2) The application shall be examined in written proceedings, after prior notification to the parties to the case. Simultaneously with the notification, the court, setting a time limit for submission of explanations, sends to the parties to the case the application for postponement of enforcement of the judgment, division into installments, amendment of the method or procedure of its enforcement.

(3) Against the court decision to postpone the enforcement of the judgment or to divide it into installments, as well as to amend the method and procedure of its enforcement, an ancillary complaint may be submitted. The submission of an ancillary complaint does not suspend the enforcement of the decision.

(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 29.10.2015, which came into force on 03.12.2015.)

#### 439.pants. Actions of the court of appeal if the judgment is not appealed in cassation proceedings

After expiry of the time limit provided for submission of a cassation complaint, if a cassation complaint has not been submitted, the court of appeal sends the case to the court of first instance.

439.1 pants. Actions of the court of appeal after performance of actions by the court of cassation

After the court of appeal, following the performance of actions by the court of cassation specified in Section 477.1 of this Law, has received the case, it issues a writ of execution. After issuing the writ of execution, the court of appeal sends the case to the court of first instance.

(As amended by the Law of 22.05.2008, which came into force on 25.06.2008. See transitional provisions.)

#### 440.pants. Suspension of proceedings, leaving the claim without examination, termination of proceedings in the court of appeal

The court of appeal suspends proceedings, leaves the claim without examination or terminates proceedings in the cases and procedure specified in Chapters 24, 25 or 26 of this Law.

### 54. nodaļa

Specifics of examination of cases of certain categories in the court of appeal

### (Chapter 20.

In the wording of the law of 03.2014; chapter title in the wording of the law of 12.02.2015, which entered into force

Article 440.1 Procedure for Examining Cases in the Appellate Instance

Appeals in simplified procedure cases and in cases concerning rights in which the dispute was examined by the Industrial Property Board of Appeal, concerning judgments by which an application for legal protection proceedings has been granted or rejected, an application for insolvency proceedings of a legal person or natural person has been rejected, in cases concerning disputes over rights in insolvency proceedings cases, in cases of revocation of discharge of a natural person from debt obligations, shall be examined in the appellate instance in the procedure established in Chapters 52, 53 and 54 of this Law, taking into account the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021 with amendments made by the law of 16.03.2023, which entered into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Article 440.2 Right to Submit an Appeal or Appeal Protest

The judgments referred to in Article 440.1 of this Law may be appealed if:

- 1) the court of first instance has incorrectly applied or interpreted a substantive law provision and this has led to incorrect resolution of the case;
- 2) the court of first instance has violated a procedural law provision and this has led to incorrect resolution of the case;
- 3) the court of first instance has incorrectly established facts or incorrectly evaluated evidence or provided an incorrect legal evaluation of the circumstances of the case and this has led to incorrect resolution of the case.

(With amendments made by the law of 12.02.2015, which entered into force on 01.03.2015.)

Article 440.3 Term for Submission of Appeal

If the judgment was made in written proceedings, in addition to the provisions of Article 415 of this Law, the appeal term is counted from the day of drafting of the judgment.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 440.4 Content of Appeal

In the appeal regarding the incorrectness of the judgment, in addition to the provisions of Article 416 of this Law, the following shall be indicated:

- 1) which substantive law provision the court of first instance incorrectly applied or interpreted, which procedural law provision it violated and how this affected the resolution of the case;
- 2) which facts the court of first instance incorrectly established, which evidence it incorrectly evaluated, how the incorrectness of the legal evaluation of the circumstances of the case is manifested and how this affected the resolution of the case.

Article 440.5 Leaving the Appeal Without Progress

(1) The judge of the court of first instance shall adopt a decision to leave the appeal without progress and set a term for the submitter to remedy deficiencies if:

- 1) an appeal has been submitted which does not comply with the requirements of the first paragraph of Article 416 and Article 440.4 of this Law;
- 2) in cases provided for by law, a translation of the appeal and the documents attached thereto, certified in the prescribed manner, has not been attached.
  - (2) If the deficiencies are remedied within the prescribed term, the appeal shall be deemed to have been submitted on the day on which it was submitted for the first time. Otherwise, the complaint shall be deemed not to have been submitted and shall be returned to the submitter.

(With amendments made by the laws of 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which entered into force on 07.07.2022.)

Article 440.6 Non-acceptance of Appeal

(1) An appeal which is not signed or which has been submitted by a person who is not authorised to appeal a court judgment, or for which the state fee has not been paid, shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter.

(2) A decision to refuse to accept an appeal is not subject to appeal.

Article 440.7 Actions of the Court of First Instance After Receipt of the Appeal

(1) The judge of the court of first instance, having ascertained that the appeal complies with the requirements of Articles 416, 440.2 and 440.4 of this Law, shall immediately notify the other participants in the case of this complaint and send them the complaint. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the complaint may also be sent to the other participants in the case.

(2) The judge of the court of first instance, when sending the appeal and the documents attached thereto to the other participants in the case, shall inform them that written explanations shall be submitted after the appellate instance has sent the participants in the case a notice of the initiation of appellate proceedings.

(3) After the expiration of the term for submission of the appeal, the judge of the court of first instance shall immediately send the case with the appeal and the documents attached thereto to the court of the appellate instance.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015, 19.10.2017, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which entered into force on Article 440.8 Initiation of Appellate Proceedings in the Court of Appellate Instance

(1) Having ascertained that the procedure for submission of the appeal has been observed, the judge or, in the case provided for in paragraph five of this Article, three judges collegially shall decide on the initiation of appellate proceedings within 30 days of receipt of the appeal.

(2) Having established that the appeal was sent to the court of the appellate instance in violation of the procedure for submission of appeals established in this Law, the judge shall adopt one of the following decisions:

- 1) a decision to refuse to initiate appellate proceedings if the term prescribed for submission of the appeal has been missed, the appeal has been submitted by a person who is not authorised to appeal a court judgment, or if the state fee has not been paid;
- 2) a decision to send the case to the court of first instance for performance of the actions prescribed by law if, upon submission of the appeal, the deficiencies specified in the first paragraph of Article 416 or Article 440.4 of this Law have been committed.
  - (3) In the case provided for in point 1 of paragraph two of this Article, the complaint shall be sent together with the case to the court of first instance, which shall return the complaint to the submitter.
  - (4) If at least one of the grounds for initiation of appellate proceedings referred to in Article 440.2 of this Law exists, the judge shall adopt a decision to initiate appellate proceedings and shall immediately notify the participants in the case thereof, indicating the term for submission of written explanations.
  - (5) If the judge to whom the appeal has been assigned for resolution considers that the initiation of appellate proceedings should be refused, the question of initiation of appellate proceedings shall be decided by three judges collegially.
  - (6) If at least one of the three judges considers that at least one of the grounds for initiation of appellate proceedings referred to in Article 440.2 of this Law exists, the judges shall adopt a decision to initiate appellate proceedings and shall immediately notify the participants in the case thereof. shall immediately notify the participants in the case thereof.
  - (7) If the judges unanimously acknowledge that none of the grounds for initiation of appellate proceedings referred to in Article 440.2 of this Law exists, they shall adopt a decision to refuse to initiate appellate proceedings and shall immediately notify the participants in the case thereof.
  - (8) The decision referred to in paragraph seven of this Article shall be drafted in the form of a resolution and is not subject to appeal.
  - (9) The decision to refuse to initiate appellate proceedings shall be returned to the submitter of the appeal together with the submitted appeal.

Article 440.9 Written Explanation of a Participant in the Case

A participant in the case may submit a written explanation regarding the submitted appeal to the court of the appellate instance within 20 days from the day on which the appellate instance sent the participants in the case a notice of the initiation of appellate proceedings.

(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 440.10 Counter-appeal

(1) After a notice of the initiation of appellate proceedings has been sent, a party has the right to submit a counter-appeal within 20 days.

(2) The counter-appeal must comply with the requirements of Articles 250.27, 416, 418 and 440.4 of this Law.

(3) After receipt of the counter-appeal, the court of the appellate instance shall immediately send it to the other participants in the case.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 440.11 Examination of Cases in Written Proceedings, Drafting of Judgment and Sending of Copy

(1) The court shall examine the cases referred to in this chapter in written proceedings, timely notifying the parties of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system, informing them of the composition of the court that will examine the case, and explaining the right to challenge a judge. This date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be deemed to be the date of drafting of the judgment. If, for technical reasons, it is not possible to attach to the online system on the date of drafting of the judgment, the judgment on the same date shall be available in the court registry. In such case, the date when the judgment is available in the court registry shall be deemed to be the date of drafting of the judgment.

(11) The examination in written proceedings of cases concerning disputes over rights in insolvency proceedings cases shall be initiated no later than within 30 days after receipt of the explanation or expiration of the term for its submission.

(12) When examining an appeal against a court judgment by which an application for legal protection proceedings has been granted, if the appeal is based on the non-compliance of the plan of measures for legal protection proceedings with point 15 of paragraph four of Article 40 or point 2 of paragraph 3.1 of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law, the court shall set a term for the appointed supervisory person or the last appointed supervisory person within which an assessment of the debtor's economic activity shall be submitted.

(2) At the written request of a party, the judgment shall be sent to the party immediately.

(3) If the court deems it necessary, the case may be heard in a court session. In cases concerning disputes over rights in insolvency proceedings cases, the court shall set the date of the court session no later than within 30 days after receipt of the explanation or expiration of the term for its submission.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which entered into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

Article 440.12 Entry into Legal Force of the Judgment of the Court of Appellate Instance

The judgment of the court of the appellate instance is not subject to appeal in the cassation instance and enters into force on the day of its promulgation or, if the case was examined in written proceedings, on the day of its drafting.

Ninth Part

Appeal of Decisions of the Court of First Instance and the Court of Appellate Instance

Chapter 55

Submission and Examination of Ancillary Complaints

#### 441.pants. Grounds for appealing or protesting decisions of first instance courts and appellate instance courts

(1) Decisions of first instance courts and appellate instance courts may be appealed separately from the court judgment by parties to the case by submitting an ancillary complaint, as well as by the prosecutor by submitting an ancillary protest:

- 1) in cases provided for in this law;
- 2) if the court decision obstructs the progress of the case.
  - (2) No ancillary complaint shall be submitted regarding other decisions of first instance courts and appellate instance courts, but objections to these decisions may be expressed in an appeal or cassation complaint.
  - (3) An ancillary protest shall be submitted and examined in the same manner as an ancillary complaint.

#### 442. pants. Time limit for submitting an ancillary complaint

(1) An ancillary complaint may be submitted within 10 days from the day of pronouncement of the decision, unless otherwise provided in this law. The time limit by which an ancillary complaint regarding a decision adopted in written proceedings or regarding procedural actions outside a court session must be submitted shall be counted from the day the decision was issued.

(11) A party to the case to whom the court decision has been sent in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law may submit an ancillary complaint within 15 days from the day of issuance of the decision.

(2) An ancillary complaint submitted after the expiration of the specified time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter, refunding the security deposit.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 443.pants. Procedure for submitting an ancillary complaint

(1) An ancillary complaint shall be submitted to the court that adopted this decision, and it shall be addressed:

- 1) regarding a first instance court decision — to the respective appellate instance court;
- 2) regarding an appellate instance court decision — to the cassation instance court;
- 3) (deleted by the law of 30.10.2014.).
  - (2) (Deleted by the law of 05.02.2009.)

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014. and 25.10.2018., which enters into force on 28.11.2018. The amendment regarding the deletion of the words "and the judge of the land registry department of the district (city) court" in point 1 of the first part enters into force on 01.06.2019. See point 151 of the transitional provisions)

443.1 pants. Content of an ancillary complaint and documents to be attached to it

(1) An ancillary complaint shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the complaint is addressed;
- 2) the name, surname, personal identity code, declared place of residence of the complainant, but if there is none — the place of residence, for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the complainant agrees to electronic communication with the court, also indicate the e-mail address and, if the complainant has registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of registration;
- 3) if the complaint is submitted by a representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, and he or she agrees to electronic communication with the court — the representative's e-mail address and, if he or she has registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of registration. If the representative's address is outside Latvia, additionally indicate the e-mail address or notify about the registration of his or her participation in the online system;
- 4) the decision regarding which the complaint is submitted, and the court that adopted this decision;
- 5) how the incorrectness of the decision manifests itself and its justification;
- 6) evidence confirming the complainant's objections;
- 7) the complainant's request and the extent to which the decision is being appealed;
- 8) a list of documents attached to the complaint.
  - (2) In cases provided for by law, translations of documents certified in the prescribed manner shall be attached to the ancillary complaint and the documents attached to it, if the documents are intended to be issued to a person in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law.

A person exempted from payment of court costs shall not attach translations.

(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 444.pants. Copies of an ancillary complaint

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

444.1 pants. Security deposit for an ancillary complaint

(1) When submitting an ancillary complaint, a security deposit shall be paid in the amount specified in point 1 of the first part of Article 43.1 of this law.

(2) If the court revokes or amends the appealed court decision in full or in any part thereof, the security deposit shall be refunded. If the ancillary complaint is rejected or it has been submitted regarding a decision that is not appealable, the security deposit shall not be refunded, except in cases where the appealed decision erroneously indicates that it is appealable.

(21) If the ancillary complaint is withdrawn, the security deposit shall not be refunded.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 25.03.2021.)

(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018., 01.10.2020. and 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 445.pants. Grounds for non-acceptance of an ancillary complaint and leaving without movement

(1) An unsigned ancillary complaint shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter, refunding the security deposit.

(2) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept an ancillary complaint if the security deposit has not been paid in the manner and amount prescribed by law or if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorization to appeal the court decision has not been attached to the ancillary complaint.

(3) The judge's decision to refuse to accept an ancillary complaint is not appealable. In the cases referred to in the second part of this Article, the paid security deposit shall be refunded.

(4) If an ancillary complaint has been submitted that does not comply with the requirements of Article 443.1 of this law, or in cases provided for by law a translation of the ancillary complaint and the documents attached to it certified in the prescribed manner has not been attached, or the power of attorney or other document attached to the ancillary complaint does not show authorization for the representative to appeal the court decision, the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the ancillary complaint without movement and shall set a time limit for remedying the deficiencies.

(5) If the submitter remedies the deficiencies indicated in the decision to leave the ancillary complaint without movement within the specified time limit, the ancillary complaint shall be considered as submitted on the day it was first submitted to the court. Otherwise, the ancillary complaint shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the submitter without refunding the security deposit.

(In the wording of the law of 23.04.2015. with amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 446.pants. Court action upon receipt of an ancillary complaint

(1) Upon receipt of an ancillary complaint, the judge shall immediately send the complaint to the parties to the case. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the ancillary complaint may also be sent to the parties to the case.

(2) Upon expiration of the appeal time limit, the judge shall immediately send the case with the ancillary complaint to the court instance to which the complaint is addressed.

(With amendments made by the laws of 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### 447.pants. Procedure for Examining Subsidiary Complaints

(1) A subsidiary complaint is examined in written proceedings. The court notifies the parties of the day of examination of the subsidiary complaint. The decision is sent to the parties within three days from the day of examination of the subsidiary complaint.

(2) If a subsidiary complaint is examined in a court session, then its examination takes place in the same manner as prescribed in this law for examination of cases in the appellate court.

(3) A subsidiary complaint regarding the judge's decisions mentioned in Articles 640 and 651.5 of this law is examined in a court session.

(4) A subsidiary complaint in cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings (Chapter 30.7) is examined by the court within 15 days from the day of receipt of the complaint.

(In the wording of the law of 04.08.2011. with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

447.1 pants. Decision Adopted Regarding a Subsidiary Complaint

(1) In a decision on a subsidiary complaint, in addition to what is mentioned in Article 230 of this law, the court indicates the submitter of the subsidiary complaint, includes a statement of the subsidiary complaint and the appealed decision, and also motivates its attitude towards the appealed decision.

(2) If the court, when examining a subsidiary complaint, recognizes that the motives contained in the appealed decision are correct and sufficient, it may indicate in the decision that it joins the motives of the appealed decision. In such case, the motivational part prescribed in Article 230 of this law may not be included.

(In the wording of the law of 04.08.2011. with amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015., which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

#### 448.pants. Competence of the Regional Court and the Supreme Court

(1) The Regional Court and the Supreme Court, when examining a subsidiary complaint, have the right to:

- 1) leave the decision unchanged but reject the complaint;
- 2) revoke the decision in full or in any part thereof and refer the matter for new examination to the court which adopted the decision;
- 3) revoke the decision in full or in any part thereof and with its own decision decide the matter on the merits;
- 4) amend the decision.
  - (2) The Regional Court, when examining a subsidiary complaint regarding a decision by which an application for renewal of proceedings and re-examination of a case in which a default judgment was made has been rejected, has the right to:
- 1) leave the decision unchanged but reject the complaint;
- 2) revoke the decision, renew the proceedings and send the case for re-examination to the court of first instance.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 30.10.2014., which comes into force on 01.01.2015.)

#### 449.pants. Legal Force of a Decision Adopted Regarding a Subsidiary Complaint

(1) A decision adopted regarding a subsidiary complaint is not subject to appeal and it enters into legal force at the moment of its adoption, except for the cases provided for in this Article and Article 641 of this law.

(2) A decision of the Regional Court on a subsidiary complaint, except in cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings (Chapter 30.7), may be appealed to the Supreme Court within 10 days from the day of issuance of the decision, if by this decision:

- 1) a subsidiary complaint regarding a decision to refuse to accept a claim based on points 1 and 2 of the first part of Article 132 of this law has been rejected;
- 2) a subsidiary complaint regarding termination of proceedings based on points 1 and 2 of Article 223 of this law has been rejected;
- 3) when deciding the matter on the merits in accordance with point 3 of Article 448 of this law, a decision has been adopted to refuse to accept a claim based on points 1 and 2 of the first part of Article 132 of this law, or a decision to terminate proceedings based on points 1 and 2 of Article 223 of this law.
  - (3) A decision of the Regional Court on a subsidiary complaint regarding a decision of the district (city) court in land register cases, except for a decision on a subsidiary complaint regarding an application for registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer, may be appealed to the Supreme Court, observing the time limits prescribed in Article 442 of this law.
  - (31) The time limits mentioned in the second and third parts of this Article with respect to a party to whom the decision has been sent in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law are counted from the day of issuance of the decision.
  - (4) When appealing to the Supreme Court the decisions provided for in the second and third parts of this Article, as well as in the first part of Article 641 of this law, security money must be paid in the amount prescribed in point 1 of the first part of Article 43.1 of this law.

The procedure for refunding security money is determined in accordance with the requirements of Article 43.2 and this chapter of this law. (With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 07.04.2004., the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 14.03.2006., and the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)
