Kasācijas tiesvedība

56.nodaļa

Kasācijas sūdzības iesniegšana

#### 450.pants. Right to Submit a Cassation Complaint or Cassation Protest

(1) A judgment of the court of first instance made by applying the provisions of Chapter 30.4 of this law, and a judgment (supplementary judgment) of the appellate court may be appealed by the parties in cassation, and the prosecutor may submit a cassation protest.

(2) A cassation protest shall be submitted and examined in the same manner as a cassation complaint, unless otherwise provided in this Part.

(3) In cassation, a judgment of the court of first instance made by applying the provisions of Chapter 30.4 of this law, and a judgment of the appellate court may be appealed if the court has incorrectly applied a substantive law norm, violated a procedural law norm, or, when examining the case, exceeded the limits of its competence.

(With amendments made by the laws of 22.05.2008., 08.09.2011., 18.04.2013., 20.03.2014. and 09.06.2016., which comes into force on 13.07.2016.)

#### 451.pants. Incorrect Application of Substantive Law Norms

(1) The court has applied a substantive law norm incorrectly if it has been incorrectly applied to the circumstances established by the court or if the substantive law norm has been incorrectly interpreted.

(2) Incorrect application of a substantive law norm may be grounds for appealing a judgment in cassation if it has led or could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case.

(22.05.2008. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 09.06.2016. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 13.07.2016.)

#### 452.pants. Violation of Procedural Law Norms

(1) The court has committed a violation of procedural law norms if during the proceedings it has not ensured procedural order in accordance with the law or observance of the procedural rights of persons, by not applying or incorrectly interpreting the relevant law norms.

(2) A violation of procedural law norms may be grounds for appealing a judgment in cassation if it has led or could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case.

(3) In any case, a violation of procedural law norms that could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case is considered to be that:

- 1) the court examined the case in an unlawful composition;
- 2) the court examined the case in violation of procedural law norms that prescribe the obligation to notify participants in the proceedings of the time and place of the court session;
- 3) procedural law norms on the language of proceedings have been violated;
- 4) the court judgment grants rights or imposes duties on a person who has not been summoned to the case as a participant in the proceedings;
- 5) there is no court session record or court judgment in the case.

(With amendments made by the laws of 22.05.2008., 09.06.2016., 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on

#### 453. pants. Content of cassation complaint and documents to be attached

(1) The cassation complaint shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the complaint is addressed (Civil Cases Department of the Supreme Court);
- 2) the name, surname, personal identification number, declared place of residence of the complainant, but if there is none — the place of residence, for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the complainant agrees to electronic communication with the court, also indicate the email address and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of registration;
- 21) (deleted by law of 11.11.2021);
- 3) the judgment in respect of which the complaint is submitted, and the court that delivered the judgment;
- 4) to what extent the judgment is being appealed;
- 5) which substantive law provision the court applied incorrectly, which procedural law provision was violated and how this affected the adjudication of the case, or how the violation of the limits of the court's jurisdiction was manifested;
- 6) (deleted by law of 09.06.2016);
- 7) the request submitted to the Supreme Court.
  - (11) If the cassation complainant considers that the examination of the cassation complaint in cassation proceedings is of significant importance in ensuring uniform court practice or in the further development of law, he or she shall provide reasoned indication thereof in the cassation complaint.
  - (2) The cassation complaint shall be signed by the complainant — a natural person, an official referred to in the fourth part of Article 82.1 of this law, an advocate or — in accordance with the fifth part of Article 82.1 of this law — a professional patent attorney. If the cassation complaint has been signed by a professional patent attorney or an official of a legal person, a document certifying the person's right to represent the complainant shall be attached to the complaint. If the cassation complaint has been signed by an advocate, a power of attorney and warrant shall be attached to the complaint. A cassation protest shall be signed by an official of the prosecutor's office as provided by law.
  - (3) (Deleted by law of 23.04.2015)
  - (4) A document certifying payment of the security deposit shall be attached to the cassation complaint, except when the cassation complaint has been submitted and payment made in the online system.
  - (41) In the cases provided for by law, a translation certified in the prescribed manner shall be attached to the cassation complaint if the document is intended to be issued to a person in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law. A person exempt from payment of court costs does not attach the translation.
  - (5) An unsigned cassation complaint shall be considered as not submitted and sent back to the complainant, refunding the security deposit.
  - (6) A judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the cassation complaint if:
- 1) the security deposit has not been paid in the manner and amount prescribed by law;
- 2) a document certifying the right of the person referred to in the second part of this Article to appeal the court judgment by way of cassation has not been attached to the cassation complaint or has not been submitted in the case.
  - (7) In the case referred to in point 2 of the sixth part of this Article, the security deposit shall be refunded.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 27.06.2003, laws of 12.02.2004, 22.05.2008, 29.11.2012, 30.10.2014, 23.04.2015, 09.06.2016, 23.11.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 454. pants. Time limit for submission of cassation complaint

(1) A cassation complaint may be submitted within 30 days from the day of pronouncement of the judgment.

(2) If the judgment has been prepared after the date specified by the court (Article 199), the time limit for appealing the judgment shall be counted from the day of actual preparation of the judgment. If the judgment was delivered in written proceedings, the time limit for appeal shall be counted from the day of preparation of the judgment.

(21) A participant in the case to whom the judgment has been sent in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law may submit a cassation complaint within 30 days from the day of issuance of the judgment.

(3) A complaint submitted after the expiry of this time limit shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the complainant, refunding the security deposit.

(With amendments made by laws of 31.10.2002, 22.05.2008, 05.02.2009, 29.10.2015, 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 455.pants. Appeal against a judge's decision

An ancillary complaint may be submitted against a judge's decision to refuse to accept a cassation complaint, except in the cases referred to in the sixth part of Article

453 of this law.

(With amendments made by the law of 23.04.2015, which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

#### 456.pants. Procedure for submission of cassation complaint

(1) A cassation complaint shall be submitted to the court that delivered the judgment.

(2) If the cassation complaint is submitted within the time limit directly to the cassation instance court, the time limit shall not be considered as missed.

#### 457.pants. Copies of cassation complaint

(Deleted by law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 458.pants. Security deposit

(1) Upon submission of a cassation complaint, a security deposit shall be paid into the deposit account of the Supreme Court in the amount specified in point 2 of the first part of Article 43.1 of this law.

(2) If the Supreme Court fully or partially annuls or modifies the appealed court judgment, the security deposit shall be refunded. If the cassation complaint is rejected, the security deposit shall not be refunded.

(3) If the cassation complaint is withdrawn before the procedural session of the Supreme Court, the security deposit shall be refunded to the complainant.

(4) (Deleted by law of 25.03.2021)

(With amendments made by laws of 22.05.2008, 20.12.2010, 12.09.2013, 30.10.2014, 09.06.2016, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 459.pants. Leaving the cassation complaint without movement

(1) If in cases provided for by law a translation of the cassation complaint and documents attached thereto certified in the prescribed manner has not been attached, the judge shall adopt a decision to leave the cassation complaint without movement and set a time limit for remedying the deficiencies.

(2) If the complainant remedies the deficiencies specified in the decision within the specified time limit, the cassation complaint shall be considered as submitted on the day it was first submitted to the court.

(3) If the complainant has not remedied the deficiencies specified in the decision within the specified time limit, the cassation complaint shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the complainant, without refunding the security deposit.

(4) An ancillary complaint may be submitted against the judge's decision by which the cassation complaint has been returned to the complainant.

(5) If the deficiencies specified in the first part of this Article, the fifth and sixth parts of Article 453 of this law have been identified at the Supreme Court, the cassation complaint shall be returned to the appellate instance court, but in the case referred to in the first part of Article 450 of this law — to the first instance court, for performance of the actions provided for in the second, third, fourth parts of this Article, the fifth and sixth parts of Article 453 of this law.

(With amendments made by laws of 19.06.2003, 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014, 23.04.2015, 09.06.2016, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 460.pants. Actions of the court upon receipt of cassation complaint

(1) The judge of the appellate instance court or, in the case referred to in the first part of Article 450 of this law, the judge of the first instance court shall send the cassation complaint to the other participants in the case and notify them that they have the right to submit an explanation to the Supreme Court in connection with the cassation complaint within 30 days from the day of its sending.

(11) If the cassation complaint has been sent to a participant in the case in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law, the time limit for submission of the explanation shall be counted from the day the cassation complaint was issued to the participant in the case.

(2) Upon expiry of the time limit for appealing the judgment, the court shall immediately send the civil case together with the cassation complaint to the Supreme Court.

(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014, 09.06.2016, 09.06.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 461.pants. Joining the cassation complaint

(1) Co-participants and third parties participating in the proceedings on the side of the person who has submitted the cassation complaint may join the submitted complaint within 30 days from the day of sending the cassation complaint by submitting a respective application to the Supreme Court.

(2) Upon submission of an application to join the cassation complaint, a security deposit does not have to be paid.

(With amendments made by laws of 31.10.2002, 09.06.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 462.pants. Withdrawal of a Cassation Appeal

(1) A person who has submitted a cassation appeal has the right to withdraw it until the cassation instance court session.

(2) If the cassation appeal is withdrawn before the Supreme Court procedural session, cassation proceedings are not initiated; if after the Supreme Court procedural session, — cassation proceedings in the case are terminated.

(With amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

#### 463.pants. Submission of a Counter-Appeal

(1) A party to the case may submit its counter-appeal to the Supreme Court within 30 days from the date of dispatch of the cassation appeal. A party to the case to whom the cassation appeal has been sent in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law may submit its counter-appeal to the Supreme Court within 30 days from the date of issuance of the cassation appeal.

(2) When submitting a counter-appeal, the provisions of Articles 450, 451, 452, 453 and 458 of this law must be observed.

(3) The Supreme Court sends the counter-appeal to the other participants in the proceedings and notifies them that they have the right to submit an explanation to the Supreme Court in connection with the counter-appeal within 30 days from the date of its dispatch.

(4) If the cassation appeal is withdrawn, the counter-appeal is examined independently.

(With amendments made by the laws of 22.05.2008, 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force

Chapter 57

Initiation of Cassation Proceedings and Examination of Cases in the Cassation Instance

(Title of chapter in the wording of the law of 22.05.2008, which enters into force on 25.06.2008.)

#### 464.pants. Procedural Session of the Supreme Court

(1) In order to decide the question of initiating cassation proceedings, cassation appeals, counter-appeals and protests are examined, after the expiry of the time limit for submission of explanations provided for in the first part of Article 460 and the third part of Article 463 of this law, at a procedural session of the Supreme Court by a panel of judges consisting of three judges formed in the manner determined by the President of the Department.

(2) If at least one of the judges considers that the case should be examined by the cassation instance, the panel of judges adopts a decision to initiate cassation proceedings. The decision determines examination of the case in written proceedings or examination in a court session.

(3) If the panel of judges unanimously recognizes that initiation of cassation proceedings must be refused, it refuses to initiate cassation proceedings by its procedural session decision.

(4) By a unanimous decision of the panel of judges, the case may be referred for examination in cassation procedure to an extended composition of the Supreme Court.

(41) The decisions referred to in the second, third, fourth and seventh parts of this Article may be drawn up in the form of a resolution, observing the provisions of the second part of Article 229 of this law.

(5) If cassation proceedings are initiated, at the request of a party the panel of judges may adopt a decision to suspend the execution of the judgment until examination of the case in cassation procedure.

(6) At a procedural session of the Supreme Court, the panel of judges may also decide the question of refusal to accept a submitted ancillary appeal and other procedural questions for the resolution of which a court session is not necessary, as well as adopt a decision to submit a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union for the adoption of a preliminary ruling or to submit an application to the Constitutional Court regarding the compliance of legal norms with the Constitution or an international legal norm (act).

(7) If the panel of judges has no obvious grounds to consider that, when examining the ancillary appeal, the appealed decision will be revoked or amended in whole or in part, it may, by a unanimous decision at a procedural session of the Supreme Court, refuse to accept the ancillary appeal. In such case, the security deposit paid for the ancillary appeal is not refunded.

(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008 with amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011, 15.03.2012, 30.10.2014, 12.02.2015, 09.06.2016 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment in the seventh part regarding the replacement of the words "state fee" with the words "security deposit" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provisions paragraphs 139 and 140)

464.1 pants. Grounds for Refusal to Initiate Cassation Proceedings

(1) The panel of judges refuses to initiate cassation proceedings if the cassation appeal does not comply with the requirements of Articles 450-454 of this law.

(2) If the cassation appeal formally complies with the requirements referred to in the first part of this Article and if the court which rendered the appealed judgment has not committed a violation of the provisions of the third part of Article 452 of this law, the panel of judges may also refuse to initiate cassation proceedings in the following cases:

- 1) case law of the Supreme Court has been established in the questions of application of legal norms indicated in the cassation appeal, and the appealed judgment complies with it;
- 2) when evaluating the arguments mentioned in the cassation appeal, there are no obvious grounds to consider that the outcome of the case contained in the appealed judgment is incorrect and that the case to be examined has essential importance in ensuring uniform court practice or in the further development of law.

(3) If the cassation appeal formally complies with the requirements referred to in the first part of this Article and if the court has not violated the provisions of the third part of Article 452 of this law and the case to be examined has no essential importance in ensuring uniform court practice and in the further development of law, the panel of judges may also refuse to initiate cassation proceedings in disputes of a proprietary nature if the part regarding which the judgment is being appealed is less than 2000 euros.

(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008 with amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014, 12.02.2015 and 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

464.2 pants. Determination of Case Examination

Case examination is determined in written proceedings if it is possible to adopt a decision based on the materials available in the case. If additional explanations from the parties to the case are necessary or, in the opinion of the Supreme Court, the relevant case may have special importance in the interpretation of legal norms, examination of the case is determined in a court session.

(In the wording of the law of 15.03.2012 with amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 09.06.2016, which enters into force

464.3 pants. Examination of a Case in Written Proceedings and Drafting and Pronouncement of a Judgment

(1) The case is examined in written proceedings based on the materials available in the case, observing the competence of the cassation instance court.

(2) Persons who have submitted an appeal or protest, as well as persons whose interests are affected by the appeal or protest, are notified that the case will be examined in written proceedings, their procedural rights are explained to them, they are informed about the composition of the court that will examine the case, the right to file a challenge against a judge is explained and they are informed about the date when the judgment will be available in the online system. This date is considered the date of pronouncement of the judgment. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach to the online system on the date of pronouncement of the judgment, the judgment is available on the same date at the court office. In such case, the date when the judgment is available at the court office is considered the date of pronouncement of the judgment.

(21) If the court, during the drafting of the judgment, determines that, due to the complexity of the case, a longer time limit is necessary for drafting the judgment, it may extend the said time limit, but not longer than two months. The court immediately informs the parties to the case referred to in the second part of this Article about the new date when the judgment will be available in the online system.

(3) The civil procedural rights mentioned in this law that are related to the preparation of the case for trial, the parties are entitled to exercise no later than seven days before the date when the judgment will be available in the online system.

(4) If necessary, the court requests submission of the prosecutor's opinion within 10 days.

(5) (Deleted as of 01.03.2018 by the law of 14.12.2017. See transitional provisions paragraph 137)

(6) Upon a party's written request, the judgment is immediately sent to the party.

(7) In written proceedings, a decision may also be adopted to refer the case for examination in a court session.

(In the wording of the law of 15.03.2012 with amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2016, 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 465.pants. Scheduling of a case for hearing at the Supreme Court session

(1) The time of examination of the case, the composition of the court and the rapporteur shall be determined by the chairperson of the department of the Supreme Court. The participants in the case shall be notified of the time and place of examination of the case.

(2) In the cassation instance, the case shall be examined by three judges, but in the cases specified in this law — by a panel of judges consisting of not less than seven judges.

(With amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014. and 12.02.2015., which enter into force on 01.03.2015.)

#### 466.pants. Commencement of examination of a case

(1) The chairperson of the session opens the court session and announces which case the Supreme Court is examining.

(2) The chairperson of the session ascertains which participants in the case have appeared, their identity and the authorisation of representatives.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 12.02.2004. and 30.10.2014., which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

#### 467.pants. Explanation of rights and obligations to the participants in the case

(1) The chairperson of the session announces the composition of the court, as well as names the prosecutor and interpreter, if such participates in the court session, and explains to the participants in the case their right to file challenges, as well as other procedural rights and obligations.

(2) The grounds for challenge and the procedure for deciding on a challenge shall be determined by Articles 19 to 21 of this law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 12.02.2004., which enters into force on 10.03.2004.)

#### 468.pants. Consequences arising if participants in the case do not appear at the court session

The non-appearance of those participants in the case who have been duly notified of the time and place of the court session of the cassation instance is not an obstacle to the examination of the case.

#### 469.pants. Decision on an application

Applications of the participants in the case related to the examination of the case shall be decided after hearing the opinion of other participants in the case.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the law of 12.02.2004., which enters into force on 10.03.2004.)

#### 470.pants. Report on the case

The examination of the case begins with the report on the case by the judge rapporteur.

(With amendments made by the law of 12.02.2015., which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

#### 471.pants. Explanations of the participants in the case and opinion of the prosecutor

(1) After the judge's report, the court hears the explanations of the parties or their representatives. The court may determine in advance the time for giving explanations, but it shall be allocated equally to both parties.

(2) The first to speak is the participant in the case who has submitted the cassation complaint, or the prosecutor if he has submitted a protest. If both parties have appealed the judgment, the claimant speaks first.

(3) Judges may ask questions to the participants in the case.

(4) Each party has the right to one rebuttal.

(5) If the prosecutor participates in a case in which no cassation protest has been submitted, he gives an opinion after the parties' explanations and rebuttals.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 12.02.2004. and 12.02.2015., which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

#### 472. pants. Procedure for rendering a judgment

(1) After the explanations of the participants in the case and the opinion of the prosecutor, the court retires to deliberation to render a judgment.

(2) If, when examining a case in a composition of three judges, the court does not reach a unanimous opinion or all judges consider that the case should be examined in an expanded composition, the court adopts a decision to transfer the case for examination in an expanded composition of the Supreme Court.

(3) When examining a case in an expanded composition, the judgment shall be rendered by a majority of votes and it shall be signed by all judges.

(4) After the judges' deliberation, the court returns to the courtroom and the chairperson of the session announces the judgment by reading its operative part and announces when the participants in the case may familiarise themselves with the judgment.

(5) A judge who, when examining a case in the expanded composition of the Supreme Court, had a different opinion on the interpretation of the law or the application of the law, has the right within 15 days after the preparation of the judgment to express in writing his separate opinion, which shall be attached to the case.

(6) If the judges recognise that it is not possible to render a judgment in this court session, the Supreme Court schedules the next court session, which shall take place within the next 14 days and in which it shall announce the judgment.

(With amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003., 05.02.2009., 30.10.2014., 12.02.2015., 09.06.2016., 14.12.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

472.1 pants. Suspension of proceedings in the cassation instance

If the court of the cassation instance adopts a decision to refer a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union for the adoption of a preliminary ruling, it suspends the proceedings until the decision of the Court of Justice of the European Union enters into legal force.

(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2004. with amendments made by the law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

58.nodaļa

Judgment of the court of cassation instance

#### 473.pants. Limits of examination of a case

(1) The court, when examining a case in cassation procedure, reviews the legality of the judgment in the case in the appealed part with regard to persons who have appealed the judgment or joined the cassation complaint, and with regard to the arguments specified in the cassation complaint.

(2) The court may annul the entire judgment, even though only a part thereof has been appealed, if it finds such violations of law that have led to incorrect adjudication of the entire case.

#### 474.pants. Rights of the court of cassation instance

The court, having examined the case, may render one of the following judgments:

- 1) leave the judgment unchanged and reject the complaint;
- 2) annul the entire judgment or a part thereof and refer the case for new examination to the court of appeal or first instance;
- 3) annul the entire judgment or a part thereof and leave the application without examination or terminate the proceedings if the second instance court has not complied with the provisions of Article 219 or 223 of this law;
- 4) amend the judgment in the part concerning the amount of the claim if it has been incorrectly determined by erroneous application of a substantive law norm.

(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 475.pants. Content of the judgment of the court of cassation instance

(1) The judgment of the court of cassation instance consists of an introductory, descriptive, reasoning and operative part.

(2) In the introductory part, the court indicates:

- 1) the name and composition of the court;
- 2) the time of rendering the judgment;
- 3) the participants in the case and the subject of the dispute;
- 4) the persons who have submitted a cassation complaint (counter-complaint) or joined it.
  - (3) In the descriptive part, the court indicates:
- 1) a brief statement of the circumstances of the case;
- 2) the essence of the judgment of the court of appeal instance;
- 3) the arguments of the cassation complaint;
- 4) the arguments of the counter-complaint or the essence of the explanation.
  - (4) In the reasoning part, the court indicates:
- 1) when rejecting the cassation complaint — the arguments for which the complaint has been rejected;
- 2) when granting the cassation complaint — the arguments about the violations of legal norms committed by the court, their incorrect application or violation of the scope of competence.
  - (5) In the operative part, the court indicates the decision in accordance with the relevant point of Article 474 of this law.
  - (6) If the court, when examining a case, recognises that the reasoning contained in the appealed judgment on the issue of application of legal norms is correct, it may indicate in the reasoning part of the judgment that it recognises the respective argumentation as correct. In such a case, the arguments specified in point 1 of paragraph (4) of this Article may not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.
  - (7) If the court, when examining a case, recognises that the appealed judgment does not comply with the case law of the Supreme Court established in other similar cases and the appealed judgment does not contain reasoned indication of why there has been a deviation from the case law, the court may render a judgment in the reasoning part of which it indicates the case law that has not been observed or the non-observance of which has not been justified. In such a case, the descriptive part may not be included in the judgment and the arguments specified in point 2 of paragraph (4) of this Article may not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.

(With amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016., which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

#### 476.pants. Binding nature of the instructions of the court of cassation instance

(1) The interpretation of law expressed in the judgment of the court of cassation instance is binding on the court that examines this case anew.

(2) The court of cassation instance does not indicate in its judgment what judgment should be rendered when examining the case anew.

#### 477.pants. Legal Force of Cassation Court Judgment

A cassation court judgment is not appealable and enters into force at the moment of its pronouncement.

477.1 pants. Action of Cassation Court After Examination of Cassation Complaint and Cassation Protest After making (adopting) the decision referred to in Article 462, second paragraph, Article 464, third paragraph, Article 464.3, second paragraph, and Article 474, points 1 and 4 of this law, the cassation court immediately sends the case to the court of appeals for issuance of a writ of execution.

(In the version of the law of 22.05.2008 with amendments made by the laws of 15.03.2012 and 14.12.2017, which enter into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment to the article concerning the deletion of the word "pilna" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provision point 137)

Eleventh Section

Reopening of a Case in Which a Judgment or Decision Has Entered into Legal Force

Chapter 59

Reopening of a Case Due to Newly Discovered Circumstances

#### 478.pants. Submission of Application

(1) Reopening of a case due to newly discovered circumstances is initiated upon application of a party to the case. The application is submitted to the same court whose judgment or decision completed the examination of the case on the merits.

(2) The application may be submitted within three months from the day when the circumstances that constitute grounds for reopening the case were discovered.

(3) The application may not be submitted if more than 10 years have passed since the entry into force of the judgment or decision. This condition does not apply to cases where the newly discovered circumstances are a decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court (Article 479, point 6).

(31) An unsigned application shall be considered as not submitted and sent back to the submitter, refunding the security deposit.

(4) A judge shall adopt a decision refusing to accept an application if:

- 1) a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to apply to the court is not attached to the application;
- 2) the security deposit has not been paid in the manner and amount prescribed by law;
- 3) the time limit established in the second or third paragraph of this article has been missed;
- 4) the application does not indicate circumstances that, in accordance with Article 479 of this law, can be recognized as newly discovered circumstances;
- 5) the application has been submitted repeatedly and it does not follow that the factual or legal circumstances material to the resolution of the issue have substantially changed.
  - (5) A judge's decision refusing to accept an application in accordance with points 1 and 2 of the fourth paragraph of this article is not appealable. An ancillary complaint may be submitted against a judge's decision refusing to accept an application in accordance with points 3, 4 and 5 of the fourth paragraph of this article.
  - (6) If the power of attorney or other document attached to the application does not indicate authority of the representative to submit this application to the court, the judge shall leave the application without action and the consequences provided for in Article 133 of this law shall ensue.
  - (7) When submitting an application, a security deposit shall be paid in the amount specified in point 4 of the first paragraph of Article 43.1 of this law. If the court fully or partially reverses the contested court decision or if the application is withdrawn before its examination, the security deposit shall be refunded.
  - (8) If the court refuses to accept an application on the basis of points 1 and 2 of the fourth paragraph of this article, the paid security deposit shall be refunded. If the court refuses to accept an application on the basis of points 3, 4 and 5 of the fourth paragraph of this article, the security deposit shall not be refunded.
  - (9) Persons who are exempt from the state fee in accordance with law are not required to pay the security deposit. The court or judge, taking into account the financial situation of a natural person, may fully or partially exempt a person from payment of the security deposit.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014, 09.06.2016, 19.10.2017, 01.10.2020, 25.03.2021 and

11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 479.pants. Newly Discovered Circumstances

Newly discovered circumstances are recognized as:

- 1) material circumstances of the case that existed at the time of examination of the case but were not and could not have been known to the submitter of the application;
- 2) deliberately false witness testimony, deliberately false expert opinion, deliberately false translation, forged written or physical evidence, on the basis of which a judgment was made, established by a court judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force;
- 3) criminal activities established by a court judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force, as a result of which an unlawful or unfounded judgment was made or a decision was adopted;
- 4) reversal of that court judgment or decision of another institution on the basis of which a judgment was made or a decision was adopted in this case;
- 5) recognition of the legal norm applied in adjudication of the case as inconsistent with a legal norm of higher legal force;
- 6) a decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court in this case, from which it follows that proceedings must be reopened. In such a case, the court, when adopting a decision in the reopened case, must base itself on the facts established in the decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court and their legal assessment.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001 and 22.05.2008, which enter into force on 25.06.2008.)

#### 480. pants. Time Limit for Submitting Application

The time limit for submitting an application is calculated:

- 1) for circumstances referred to in point 1 of Article 479 of this law — from the day of discovery of these circumstances;
- 2) in the cases referred to in points 2 and 3 of Article 479 of this law — from the day when the judgment in the criminal case entered into legal force;
- 3) in the cases referred to in point 4 of Article 479 of this law — from the day when a court decision entered into legal force reversing a judgment in a civil case or a criminal case, or when a decision of another institution was reversed, on the basis of which the judgment or decision sought to be reversed due to newly discovered circumstances is based;
- 4) in the case referred to in point 5 of Article 479 of this law — from the day when the judgment or other decision entered into force as a result of which the applied legal norm ceases to be in force as inconsistent with a legal norm of higher legal force.

(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 481.pants. Examination of Application

(1) An application due to newly discovered circumstances shall be examined in written proceedings.

(2) When examining an application, the provisions of law on inadmissibility of a judge's participation in repeated examination of a case are not applicable.

(In the version of the law of 05.02.2009 with amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

#### 482.pants. Court Decision

(1) The court, having examined the application, verifies whether the circumstances indicated by the applicant are to be recognized as newly discovered circumstances in accordance with Article 479 of this law.

(2) If the court establishes newly discovered circumstances, it shall reverse the contested judgment or decision in whole or in part and refer the case for new examination to the same court or a lower instance court.

(3) If the court finds that the circumstances indicated in the application are not to be considered newly discovered, it shall reject the application.

(4) An ancillary complaint may be submitted against a court decision rejecting an application for reopening of a case due to newly discovered circumstances.

(With amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

Chapter 60

Reopening of Cases Due to Substantial Violations of Material and Procedural Legal Norms

#### 483.pants. Submission of Protest

The Prosecutor General may submit a protest to the Supreme Court against a court decision that has entered into force if no more than 10 years have passed since the decision entered into force.

(In the version of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

#### 484.pants. Grounds for Submitting Protest

The grounds for submitting a protest against a court decision that has entered into force are substantial violations of material or procedural legal norms established in cases that have been examined only by a first instance court, if the court decision has not been appealed in the manner prescribed by law for reasons independent of the parties to the case or if the court decision has violated the rights of state or municipal institutions or persons who have not been parties to the case.

#### 485.pants. Procedure for Examining Protests

Protests are examined by the Supreme Court in the procedure specified in Articles 464-477 of this law.

(As amended by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

### 60. nodaļa

Rehearing of a Case in Connection with the Review of a Decision in Cases Provided for by European Union Legal Norms

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

485.1 pants. Submission of Application

(1) A rehearing of a case in connection with the review of a decision may be initiated by the defendant, based on Article 19 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 April 2004 creating a European Enforcement Order for uncontested claims (hereinafter - Regulation No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council), Article 18 of Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council, Article 20 of Regulation No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council or Article 19 of Council Regulation (EC) No 4/2009 of 18 December 2008 on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions and cooperation in matters relating to maintenance obligations (hereinafter - Council Regulation No 4/2009), by submitting an application:

- 1) for the review of a judgment or decision of a district (city) court — to the relevant regional court;
- 2) for the review of a judgment or decision of a regional court — to the Supreme Court;
- 3) for the review of a judgment or decision of the Court Chamber — to the Civil Cases Department of the Supreme Court.
  - (2) The application may be submitted within 45 days, but in accordance with Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the day when the review circumstances provided for in the European Union legal norms mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article became known.
  - (3) The application may not be submitted if the limitation period has expired for submitting for execution the enforcement document regarding the relevant decision.
  - (4) An application in which the circumstances that may be recognized as circumstances for review of the decision in accordance with the European Union legal norms mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article are not indicated shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the applicant.

The judge shall refuse to accept for examination an application for rehearing of a case in connection with the review of a decision also when the application has been submitted repeatedly and it does not follow from it that the circumstances for review of the decision for deciding the matter have changed. An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding such decision of the judge.

(As amended by the laws of 30.10.2014, 29.10.2015 and 01.06.2017, which enters into force on 01.07.2017. The amendment in the second paragraph in connection with Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council enters into force on 14.07.2017. See transitional provision 126)

485.2 pants. Examination of the Application

The application for review of a decision shall be examined in written proceedings.

485.3 pants. Court Decision

(1) The court, having examined the application, shall verify whether the circumstances indicated by the applicant are recognizable as circumstances for review of the decision in accordance with the European Union legal norms mentioned in the first paragraph of Article 485.1 of this law.

(2) If the court establishes circumstances for review of the decision, it shall revoke the contested decision in full and refer the case for rehearing to the court of first instance.

(3) If the court finds that the circumstances indicated in the application are not to be considered as circumstances for review of the decision, it shall reject the application.

(4) An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision.

#### 534.pants. Submission of Application for Issuance of Writ of Execution for Forced Enforcement of Permanent Arbitration Court Award

(1) If a permanent arbitration court award is enforceable in Latvia and is not voluntarily complied with, the interested party may submit an application for the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award to the district (city) court according to the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the debtor's place of residence or legal address or according to the place of enforcement of the arbitration court award.

(2) The application for the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award shall be accompanied by:

- 1) the permanent arbitration court award;
- 2) the arbitration agreement certifying the parties' written agreement to refer the civil dispute for examination to the arbitration court;
- 3) (deleted by Law of 11.11.2021.);
- 4) documents confirming the payment of state fee and expenses related to the application for the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award.
  - (3) The documents referred to in paragraph 4 of the second part of this Article may not be attached if the application has been submitted and payment has been made in the online system or if the application includes information about the state fee payment and the payment of expenses related to the application for the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award, indicating the payer's identification data — name, surname, personal code or name and registration number, if they differ from the applicant's data, as well as the date and number of the payment order. When making a payment, information about the debtor — his or her name, surname, personal code or name and registration number — shall be indicated in the purpose of the payment order. In this case, the district (city) court recognises the said payments as received in the state budget by using the budget electronic settlement system.
  - (4) (Deleted by Law of 11.11.2021.) (As worded by Law of 11.09.2014. with amendments made by Law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

534.1 pants. Sending of Application for Issuance of Writ of Execution for Forced Enforcement of Permanent Arbitration Court Award to Participants of the Case

(1) When an application for the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award is received in the district (city) court, it shall be immediately sent to the other participants of the case to their official electronic addresses or by registered mail, setting a time limit for submission of a written explanation which is not shorter than 20 days from the date of sending the application.

(2) In the explanation, the participant of the case shall indicate:

- 1) whether he or she acknowledges the application in full or in any part thereof;
- 2) his or her objections to the application and their justification;
- 3) evidence confirming his or her objections and their justification, as well as the law on which they are based;
- 4) requests for acceptance or obtaining of evidence;
- 5) other circumstances which he or she considers significant in the examination of the application.
  - (3) (Deleted by Law of 11.11.2021.)
  - (4) After receiving the explanation, the judge shall immediately send it to the other participants of the case.
  - (5) Failure to submit an explanation is not an obstacle to the examination of the application for the issuance of a writ of execution.

(As worded by Law of 17.02.2005. with amendments made by Laws of 11.09.2014. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on

#### 535.pants. Deciding on Application for Issuance of Writ of Execution for Forced Enforcement of Permanent Arbitration Court Award

(1) The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award or the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award shall be adopted by the judge on the basis of the submitted documents, without summoning the participants of the case, within 20 days from the date when the explanations were sent to the other participants of the case or within 20 days from the date when the time limit for providing explanations has expired. When adopting a decision on the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award, the judge shall also decide the question whether the state fee for the issuance of such writ of execution is reimbursable and whether the expenses related to the examination of the case are reimbursable. The decision shall be sent to the parties within three days. The decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award shall be sent to the permanent arbitration court to the electronic mail address indicated on its website.

(2) The court may request from the permanent arbitration court the case file or other information if it is necessary for the adoption of the decision referred to in the first part of this Article.

(3) The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award is not appealable.

(4) Against the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award, an appeal may be lodged within 10 days from the date of receipt of the decision.

(5) The decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution for the forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration court award shall enter into force after the time limit for lodging an appeal has expired and no appeal has been lodged.

(As worded by Law of 11.09.2014. with amendments made by Law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 536.pants. Grounds for Refusal to Issue an Enforcement Order for Compulsory Execution of a Permanent Arbitration Court Judgment

(1) A judge shall refuse to issue an enforcement order for compulsory execution of a permanent arbitration court judgment if:

- 1) the specific civil dispute can be resolved only by a court;
- 2) the arbitration agreement was concluded by a natural person with limited legal capacity or by a minor;
- 3) the arbitration agreement has been cancelled or declared invalid in the procedure established by law;
- 4) a party was not properly notified of the arbitration proceedings or for other reasons was unable to submit its explanations and this substantially affected the arbitration proceedings;
- 5) a party was not properly notified of the appointment of arbitrators and this substantially affected the arbitration proceedings;
- 6) an arbitrator does not meet the requirements of the Arbitration Law, the arbitration court was not established, or the arbitration proceedings did not take place in accordance with the provisions of the arbitration agreement or the Arbitration Law;
- 7) the arbitration court judgment was rendered on a civil dispute that is not provided for in the arbitration agreement or that does not comply with the provisions of the arbitration agreement, or it resolved issues not covered by the arbitration agreement.
  - (2) If an enforcement order for compulsory execution of a permanent arbitration court judgment cannot be issued with respect to a part of the permanent arbitration court judgment for the reasons referred to in paragraph one of this Article, it may be issued with respect to the remaining part of the arbitration court judgment.

(With amendments made by the Law of 11.09.2014., which enters into force on 01.11.2014. The new version of the Article enters into force on 01.01.2015. See transitional provision 83)

#### 537.pants. Consequences of Refusal to Issue an Enforcement Order for Compulsory Execution of a Permanent Arbitration Court Judgment

#### 537.pants. Consequences of Refusal to Issue an Enforcement Order for Compulsory Execution of a Permanent Arbitration Court Judgment

After the decision to refuse to issue an enforcement order for compulsory execution of a permanent arbitration court judgment has entered into force:

- 1) the civil dispute may be resolved in court in general procedure if the issuance of an enforcement order for compulsory execution of a permanent arbitration court judgment has been refused based on points 1, 2, 3 and 7 of paragraph one of Article 536 of this Law;
- 2) the civil dispute may be resubmitted for resolution to an arbitration court if the issuance of an enforcement order for compulsory execution of a permanent arbitration court judgment has been refused based on points 4, 5 and 6 of paragraph one of Article 536 of this Law.

(With amendments made by the Law of 11.09.2014., which enters into force on 01.11.2014. The new version of the Article enters into force on 01.01.2015. See transitional provision 83)

Part E

Execution of Court Judgments

Section Thirteen

General Provisions for Execution of Court Judgments

Chapter 67

Enforcement Documents

#### 538.pants. Execution of Court Judgments and Decisions

Court judgments and decisions shall be executed after they have entered into legal force, except in cases where, in accordance with law or a court judgment, they are to be executed immediately. The indication that a judgment or decision is to be executed immediately must be in the enforcement document itself.

(With amendments made by the Law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 539.pants. Court and Other Institution Decisions to be Executed

(1) The following court decisions, judges' decisions or decisions of other institutions shall be executed in the procedure for execution of court judgments established by this Law:

- 1) court judgments and court or judge's decisions in civil cases, as well as in cases arising from administrative legal relations;
- 2) court decisions and decisions of a process manager or prosecutor's instructions in criminal cases regarding pecuniary recoveries;
- 3) judge's or court's decisions in cases of administrative violations regarding pecuniary recoveries;
- 4) court decisions approving a settlement;
- 5) permanent arbitration court decisions;
- 6) decisions of foreign courts or competent authorities and foreign arbitration courts in cases provided for by law;
- 7) court or judge's decisions on application of procedural sanctions — fines or coercive fines;
- 8) decisions of labour dispute committees;
- 9) decisions of the public services regulatory authority (hereinafter — the regulator) on examination of disputes or disagreements.
  - (2) In the procedure established for execution of court judgments, unless otherwise provided by law, the following shall also be executed:
- 1) decisions of institutions and officials in administrative violation proceedings and in cases of law violations in cases provided for by law;
- 2) administrative acts issued by authorities and officials vested with state power aimed at monetary payments;
- 3) decisions of persons belonging to the judicial system (notaries, advocates, bailiffs) on official remuneration, remuneration for legal assistance provided and on expenses related to services provided, and state duty;
- 4) acts of the European Council, Commission or European Central Bank adopted pursuant to Article 299 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
- 5) notarial acts drawn up in the procedure established in Section D1 of the Notarial Law.
- 6) acts of protest regarding promissory notes issued in the form of a notarial act.
  - (3) (Deleted as of 01.03.2016. by the Law of 04.02.2016. See transitional provision 113) (With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 12.02.2004., 07.04.2004., 17.02.2005., 07.09.2006., 26.10.2006., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 23.05.2013., 04.02.2016., 22.06.2017., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022. Point 6 of paragraph two enters into force on 01.10.2022. See transitional provision 178)

- 21) decisions of courts or judges in administrative offence proceedings;

- 9) (deleted as of 01.03.2016. by the law of 04.02.2016. See point 113 of the transitional provisions);

#### 541.pants. Preparation of Writ of Execution

(1) The writ of execution is prepared by the first instance or appellate instance court after the judgment or decision enters into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the judgment is announced or the decision is adopted.

(2) If a time period for voluntary execution has been set for the execution of a court judgment and the judgment has not been executed, the writ of execution is available in the online system for enforcement after the expiry of the time period for voluntary execution.

(3) (Deleted by Law of 11.11.2021.)

(31) In the case referred to in Clause 4 of Paragraph two of Section 539 of this Law, the writ of execution is prepared by Riga City Court.

(32) In the cases referred to in Sections 544.1 and 544.2 of this Law, the writ of execution is prepared by the district (city) court according to the place of execution of the decision or according to the declared place of residence of the debtor — natural person, but if there is none — according to the debtor's place of residence or the legal address of a legal person.

(33) If several writs of execution are to be prepared for one judgment or a writ of execution is necessary in a case in which a settlement has been concluded, then the writ of execution is prepared by the court that adopted the decision, based on the creditor's written request.

(4) If, according to a court judgment, monetary sums are to be collected as state revenue, the court, after the expiry of the time period for voluntary execution set by the court, sends the writ of execution to the bailiff according to the declared place of residence of the debtor — natural person, but if there is none — according to the debtor's place of residence or the legal address of a legal person.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 17.02.2005., 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 30.10.2014., 11.11.2021., 16.06.2022. and 16.06.2022., which enter into force on 01.08.2022.)

541.1 pants. Issuance of European Union Enforcement Documents and Documents Related to Enforcement

(1) The court issues a European Enforcement Order, based on Regulation No. 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council, upon the creditor's request, when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the judgment is announced or the decision is adopted.

(2) The certificate referred to in point 1 of Article 41 or point 1 of Article 42 of Council Regulation No. 2201/2003, based on the provisions of this Regulation, is issued by the court on its own initiative or at the request of a party to the case, when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the judgment is announced or the decision is adopted.

(3) The certificate referred to in Articles 54 and 58 of the Lugano Convention of 30 October 2007 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters and the certificate referred to in Article 39 of Council Regulation No. 2201/2003 is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case.

(4) The forms referred to in points 2 and 3 of Article 6 of Regulation No. 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council are issued by the court at the request of a party to the case.

(41) The certificate referred to in point 2 of Article 20 of Regulation No. 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case. The court, at the request of a party to the case, issues the certificate referred to in this Paragraph in any other language in accordance with point 2 of Article 20 of Regulation No. 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(42) The court issues a European payment order in accordance with Article 18 of Regulation No. 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(43) The extract from the decision referred to in point "b" of point 1 of Article 20 of Council Regulation No. 4/2009 is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case, when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the judgment is announced or the decision is adopted.

(44) The certificate referred to in Articles 53 and 60 of Regulation No. 1215/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case, when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the judgment is announced or the decision is adopted.

(45) The certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 June 2013 on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters (hereinafter — Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council) is issued by the court at the request of the applicant, when the decision is adopted. The court informs the respondent of the issuance of the certificate referred to in this Paragraph in accordance with Article 8 of Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The court, at the request of the applicant, performs transliteration and translation of the certificate referred to in this Paragraph, based on point 3 of Article 5 of Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(46) The certificate referred to in Article 14 of Regulation No. 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council is issued by the court at the request of a party to the case.

(47) The certificates referred to in Article 36 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 are issued by the court at the request of a party, when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the judgment is announced or the decision is adopted.

(48) The certificates referred to in Article 47 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 are issued by the court at the request of a party, when the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the judgment is announced or the decision is adopted.

(5) The documents referred to in Paragraphs one, two, three, four, 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and 4.8 of this Section are issued by the court where the case is located at that time.

(6) The court adopts a reasoned decision regarding refusal to issue the documents referred to in Paragraphs one, two, 4.5 and 4.8 of this Section.

(7) An appeal may be filed against a court decision to refuse to issue the documents referred to in Paragraphs one, two, 4.5 and 4.8 of this Section.

#### 542. pants. Preparation of Several Writs of Execution for One Judgment

(1) One writ of execution is prepared for each judgment, except in the cases specified in Paragraph two of this Section.

(2) Several writs of execution are prepared for one judgment, if:

- 1) the execution of the judgment is to be performed in different places;
- 2) the judgment is immediately enforceable in a certain part thereof;
- 3) the judgment has been rendered in favour of several claimants or is directed against several defendants;
- 4) a different enforcement procedure is provided by law for the execution of the claim satisfied or partially satisfied by the judgment.
  - (3) When preparing several writs of execution, each of them shall precisely specify the place of execution or the part of the judgment that is enforceable under this writ of execution, as well as the creditor in whose favour and the debtor against whom collection is to be directed under this writ of execution.

(11.11.2021. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

#### 543.pants. Content of a Writ of Execution

(1) The writ of execution shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court that issued the writ of execution;
- 2) the case in which the writ of execution was issued;
- 3) the time of making the decision;
- 4) the operative part of the decision or a part thereof;
- 5) the time when the decision enters into legal force, or an indication that the decision is to be executed immediately;
- 6) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);
- 7) information about the creditor and debtor: for natural persons — name, surname, personal identification number, declared place of residence, additional address (addresses) indicated in the declaration and place of residence if it differs, but for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number;
- 8) information about the child — name, surname, personal identification number and location — in cases where a decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence or a decision in a case arising from custody or contact rights is to be executed;
- 9) information about the contact person in whose presence contact rights are to be exercised (for natural persons — name, surname, personal identification number and address, for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number), if the decision in a case arising from contact rights specifies a contact person in whose presence contact is to be exercised, and that person is not a representative of the orphan's court or a person authorized by the orphan's court;
- 10) information about the place where contact rights are to be exercised, if the decision in a case arising from contact rights specifies for the exercise of contact a place that is not the premises of the orphan's court;
- 11) information about the forced opening of premises — the address and time period when the premises are to be opened —, if the court has determined in the decision on the review of the time and place of exercise of contact rights that the premises are to be opened by force (paragraph eleven of Section 244.13 of this Law).
  - (2) The writ of execution shall be signed by the judge.
  - (3) The content of other enforcement documents shall be determined by the respective laws.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

543.1 pants. Correction of Errors in European Union Enforcement Documents

(1) The court which issued the judgment or adopted the decision, upon application of a party or, if provided for in

European Union legal norms, — also on its own initiative may correct errors:

- 1) in a European Enforcement Order, based on Article 10 of Regulation No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council;
- 2) in the certificate referred to in Article 41(1) or Article 42(1) of Council Regulation No 2201/2003, based on Council Regulation No 2201/2003;
- 3) in the certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council, based on point (a) of Article 9(1) of Council Regulation No 606/2013;
- 4) in the certificate referred to in Article 36 or 47 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, based on Article 37 or 48 of Council Regulation
  - (EU) 2019/1111.
    - (2) When submitting an application for the correction of a European Enforcement Order, the form referred to in Article 10(3) of Regulation No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be used.
    - (3) The question of correcting errors shall be considered at a court session, after prior notice thereof to the parties. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the consideration of the question.
    - (4) Errors in the enforcement documents referred to in paragraph one of this Section shall be corrected by a court decision.
    - (5) An appeal may be filed against a court decision to make a correction of errors in enforcement documents.

#### 544.pants. Issuance of a Duplicate Writ of Execution

(1) If a writ of execution is lost, stolen or destroyed, the court which adopted the decision, upon application of the creditor, but if it occurred in the process of execution of a judgment, — upon application of the bailiff may issue a duplicate writ of execution. The application shall indicate the circumstances in which the writ of execution was lost, stolen or destroyed.

(2) The application for the issuance of a duplicate shall be considered at a court session, after prior notice thereof to the creditor and the debtor. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the consideration of the application for the issuance of a duplicate writ of execution.

(3) When adopting a decision on the issuance of a duplicate writ of execution, the court shall simultaneously declare the lost, stolen or destroyed writ of execution invalid and shall release the creditor from payment of the state fee, if his or her fault in the loss, destruction or theft of the writ of execution has not been established.

(4) An appeal may be filed against the court decision.

(5) A duplicate writ of execution shall be issued to the creditor after the decision enters into force and payment of the state fee, if the creditor has not been released from it.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

544.1 Forced Execution of a Decision of a Labour Disputes Committee

(1) The decision of the labour disputes committee shall be attached to the application submitted to the court for the issuance of a writ of execution.

(2) The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution or a reasoned refusal to issue it shall be adopted by the judge unilaterally on the basis of the submitted application and the decision of the labour disputes committee attached thereto within three days from the date of submission of the application, without summoning the parties.

(3) The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution shall enter into force immediately.

(4) An appeal may be filed against the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution within 10 days from the date when the decision was issued to the claimant.

(5) The court shall refuse to issue a writ of execution if it finds that, in accordance with law, the particular dispute may be resolved only in court.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 544.2 pants. Forced Execution of a Regulator's Decision on Consideration of a Dispute or Disagreement

(1) The regulator's decision on consideration of a dispute or disagreement shall be attached to the application submitted to the court for the issuance of a writ of execution.

(2) The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution or a reasoned refusal to issue it shall be adopted by the judge unilaterally on the basis of the submitted application and the regulator's decision on consideration of a dispute or disagreement attached thereto within three days from the date of submission of the application, without summoning the parties.

(3) The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution shall enter into force immediately.

(4) An appeal may be filed against the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution within 10 days from the date when the decision was issued to the claimant.

(5) The court shall refuse to issue a writ of execution if it finds that, in accordance with law, the particular dispute or disagreement may be resolved only in court.

545.1 pants. Revocation of European Union enforcement documents
