#### 574.pants. General provisions for seizure of debtor's movable property

(1) The bailiff shall seize the debtor's movable property in such quantity as is necessary to extinguish the amount to be recovered and to cover the costs of enforcement of the judgment. The bailiff shall not seize accessories of the principal thing separately from the principal thing.

(2) The bailiff may seize the debtor's movable property the value of which exceeds the amount awarded to the creditor and the costs of enforcement of the judgment if the debtor has no other property subject to seizure or the value of such property does not cover the amount to be recovered and the costs of enforcement of the judgment.

(3) After seizing movable property, the bailiff shall request information from movable property registers regarding the ownership of such property by the debtor, and shall also ascertain in the commercial pledge register whether movable property belonging to the debtor is not pledged. If the bailiff establishes that the seized property belongs to third parties, he shall immediately release it from seizure. If a commercial pledge in favour of third parties is registered in the commercial pledge register on the debtor's movable property, the bailiff shall request that the debtor and the pledgee notify of the remaining amount of the debt.

(4) The bailiff may bring enforcement proceedings against movable property pledged as a commercial pledge or manual pledge to secure claims of third parties with the consent of the relevant pledgee, and may also bring enforcement proceedings against the cash surplus in the event of sale of the pledge. If the pledgee does not consent to the sale and himself without justifiable reason delays in selling the pledged property, the bailiff shall explain to the creditor that he may request the court to set a time for the sale of the pledged property so that enforcement proceedings may be brought against the cash surplus, and shall also explain the right to establish a commercial pledge.

(5) If the bailiff establishes that movable property has already been seized for another enforcement, he shall compare the property with the inventory of property drawn up during the previous seizure and shall seize only those items which have not been entered in the earlier inventory, but if he has already carried out the seizure, he shall immediately release the items seized for the second time from seizure.

(6) If the debtor is absent or evades enforcement of the decision, the bailiff shall seize movable property in the presence of a representative of the local government or police.

(7) During seizure of the debtor's movable property, the debtor and the creditor have the right to invite not more than two witnesses. The failure of witnesses to appear shall not halt the seizure of property.

(8) During the seizure of movable property, the debtor is entitled to notify the bailiff as to which items enforcement should first be brought against. The bailiff shall satisfy such an application if it is not contrary to the provisions of this law and does not hinder enforcement of the decision.

(9) (Deleted by the Law of 05.02.2009.)

(10) (Deleted by the Law of 01.03.2018.)

(11) (Deleted by the Law of 01.03.2018.)

(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the Laws of 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009. and 01.03.2018., which came into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 575. pants. Seizure of debtor's movable property if the property is with another person

(1) If there is evidence that the debtor's property is with another person, the bailiff shall seize this property in the general procedure. If the person refuses to admit the bailiff to the location where the movable property is situated, the bailiff shall, for ensuring public order, invite a police representative in whose presence he shall open the premises or storage facility and carry out the seizure. Locked premises or storage facilities in respect of which there is evidence that the debtor's property is located therein and which no person opens may be opened by force in the presence of a police representative, or the bailiff, having assessed the specific circumstances, shall adopt a decision to postpone the seizure.

(2) If no adult person is found in the premises or other storage facilities after their opening, the bailiff shall, after forced opening of the premises, ensure their secure closure and sealing. The bailiff shall leave at the relevant premises or storage facility a notice with an invitation to come to the place of practice of the bailiff in order to receive the keys to the premises.

(3) Items located in premises or storage facilities opened in the procedure specified in this Article which the bailiff does not seize shall not be indicated in the inventory of property.

(4) If the location of the debtor's property with another person is determined by a mutually concluded contract, the bailiff shall seize this property, but the question of preservation of rights of another person arising from the contract shall be decided by a court in action proceedings.

(In the wording of the Law of 01.03.2018., which came into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 576. pants. Description of corporeal things

(1) When describing corporeal things, their individual characteristics and quantity shall be precisely indicated and photographic recording of the things shall be carried out.

(2) When describing corporeal things, new items shall be distinguished from used ones.

(3) When describing precious metals, the hallmark (fineness) shall be indicated if it is known. When describing items decorated with precious stones, the number and colour of these stones, as well as size and name, if they are known, shall be indicated.

(4) When describing goods, as well as products and materials contained in packaging of goods, the numbers or marks present on the packaging and the name and description of the goods stored in such packaging shall be indicated.

(5) The bailiff may pack items of the same type into packages, indicating in the inventory of property the general name of the packaged items. Individual items may be packed into packages, indicating on the packaging the names of the items described.

(In the wording of the Law of 01.03.2018., which came into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 577.pants. Property Inventory Record

(1) The property inventory record shall indicate:

- 1) the time and place of drawing up the record;
- 2) the place of office and place of practice of the bailiff, the name and surname of the bailiff;
- 3) the decision of the court or other institution or official being executed;
- 4) the name and surname of the creditor and debtor or their authorized representatives present at the property inventory;
- 5) the name, surname, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration of witnesses, but if there is none — the place of residence, but for an official — the name, surname and position held;
- 6) the name of each inventoried item, its special characteristics (Article 576), the valuation of each item separately and the value of all property;
- 7) (deleted by law of 31.10.2002);
- 8) the name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration of the natural person to whom the inventoried property has been handed over for safekeeping, but if there is none — the place of residence, or the name, registration number, legal address of the legal person and the name, surname, personal identity number and declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none — the place of residence of the representative of this legal person to whom the inventoried property has been handed over for safekeeping;
- 81) the place of storage of the items;
- 9) that the procedure and time limit for appealing the bailiff's actions have been explained to the creditor and debtor;
- 10) that the custodian of the property has been explained the procedure for storing the inventoried property, his or her civil liability, as well as criminal liability if he or she wastes, alienates, conceals or exchanges the property handed over for safekeeping;
- 11) remarks and objections expressed by the creditor, debtor or other persons present at the property inventory.
  - (11) Photographs (Article 576, first paragraph) shall be stored electronically in the enforcement case files and attached to the property inventory record as an annex thereto only at the request of the creditor or debtor.
  - (2) The property inventory record shall be signed by the bailiff, the creditor, the debtor, the custodian of the property and other persons who participated in the property inventory. If the creditor, debtor or their representatives do not sign the property inventory record, the bailiff shall make a note thereof in the record.
  - (3) A creditor or debtor who has signed the inventory record without any remarks shall not have the right to subsequently submit a complaint about the incorrectness of the inventory record.
  - (4) The property inventory record shall be issued to the creditor, the debtor and the custodian of the property. If the creditor or debtor did not participate in the property inventory, the property inventory record shall be sent to him or her within three days after completion of the inventory.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002, 29.11.2012 and 01.03.2018, which enter into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 578. pants. Valuation of Inventoried Tangible Items

(1) The inventoried tangible items, taking into account their degree of wear and tear, shall be valued by the bailiff, determining the forced sale value of the items according to the prices existing in this area. If, due to the item or its characteristics, special knowledge in science or art is required for valuation or if precious stones, precious metals and their products are to be valued, the bailiff shall engage an expert to determine the forced sale value of the item. The bailiff may also engage an expert to determine the forced sale value of the item in other cases. If it is not possible to engage an expert on the day of the property inventory, the bailiff shall indicate in the property inventory record the value of the property determined by himself or herself, which is then replaced by the expert's valuation.

(2) The creditor or debtor may request the bailiff to engage an expert for re-valuation of items within 10 days after the property inventory has been completed or the written property inventory record has been sent, but if an expert was initially engaged to determine the value — after the bailiff's notification of the valuation has been sent. Before engaging the expert, the bailiff shall notify in writing the person who requested the engagement of the expert about the amount of valuation costs. The valuation costs shall be covered by the person who requested the engagement of the expert by depositing the necessary amount of money into the bailiff's account within the time limit set by the bailiff, which shall not be shorter than five days. If the amount of money necessary for valuation has not been deposited, the bailiff shall reject the request to engage an expert.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 579.pants. Protection of Property

(1) To ensure the protection of the seized property, the bailiff shall appoint a custodian of the property. The seized property shall be handed over for safekeeping to the debtor or a member of the debtor's family, unless there are circumstances that give rise to reasonable doubts about the custodian's ability to ensure the performance of his or her duties or that during the protection period the property handed over for safekeeping could be wasted, alienated, concealed, exchanged or its value otherwise significantly reduced. The bailiff shall hand over the inventoried property of the debtor for safekeeping to a natural person against signature. In the cases provided for in this Law, items may also be handed over for safekeeping to a legal person against the signature of its representative. If the custodian of the property cannot ensure the protection of the property at the address where it was inventoried, the bailiff shall remove the property and hand it over to the custodian of the property, indicating in the property inventory record the address at which the custodian of the property has undertaken to store the property. The bailiff shall be entitled to make a decision to replace the custodian of the property at any stage of execution of the decision if the custodian cannot continue to perform his or her duties, does not ensure proper storage of the items or does not comply with the bailiff's order.

(2) The debtor or members of his or her family may use the property left in their safekeeping if, due to the characteristics of this property, its use does not destroy the property or significantly reduce its value.

(3) If the custodian is not the debtor or a member of the debtor's family, he or she shall receive remuneration for safekeeping.

(4) When seizing movable property, a signature must be obtained from the debtor or custodian that he or she will not alienate, pledge or use it for another task or purpose and that he or she may be held criminally liable for wasting, alienating, concealing or exchanging it.

(5) The custodian of the property may change the place of storage of the seized items after prior coordination with the bailiff. The custodian of the property shall show the property handed over for safekeeping to the bailiff upon the bailiff's request, if necessary, delivering it to the place designated by the bailiff.

(6) When cancelling the seizure or replacing the custodian of the property, the bailiff shall issue an order to the custodian to hand over the property handed over for safekeeping to the person indicated in the order at the time and place designated by the bailiff. The bailiff shall draw up a record of the handover of the property. If the custodian of the property does not hand over the property or has not ensured its proper safekeeping, the bailiff shall draw up a record thereof and send it to the prosecutor for deciding on the liability of the custodian of the property.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 01.03.2018, which enter into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 580. pants. Storage of Money and Valuables Seized from the Debtor

(1) The bailiff seizes the described gold and silver articles and other valuables and, if unable to ensure their safekeeping, deposits them for safekeeping in a credit institution.

(2) Money found at the debtor's in the amount necessary to cover the debt being recovered and enforcement expenses, the bailiff seizes and deposits into the bailiff's deposit account.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 01.03.2018, which enter into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.1 pants. Seizure and Sale of Tangible Items Subject to Registration

(1) The bailiff issues an order to the institution whose duties include maintaining the registration of items subject to registration, to register or, if technically possible, registers itself a prohibition on alienation or other actions in respect of the debtor's vehicle or other tangible item subject to registration.

(2) Simultaneously with the placement of the auction announcement on the electronic auction website or the adoption of a decision on the sale of seized property without auction, the bailiff notifies persons in whose favor a pledge right or prohibition note is registered in the register about the auction or sale of property without auction. If the seized vehicle is sold, the bailiff, after the acquirer has paid the entire amount due from the acquirer, within five days notifies the State Revenue Service of the date of alienation of the vehicle and the acquirer and makes a corresponding entry in the State Register of Vehicles and Their Drivers.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.2 pants. Seizure and Sale of Ships and Floating Structures

(1) Ships and floating structures registered in the Latvian Ship Register of the state joint-stock company "Latvijas Jūras administrācija" (hereinafter - Ship Register) are seized in the procedure specified in this chapter, insofar as this section does not provide otherwise. Vessels registered in the state joint-stock company "Ceļu satiksmes drošības direkcija" are seized and sold in the procedure specified in Section 580.1 of this law.

(2) The seizure of a ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register applies not only to the hull of the ship or floating structure, but also to all accessories of the ship or floating structure, including those that ensure navigation. A ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register that is in co-ownership is seized in its entirety, without prior separation of the debtor's rights to his share. The Ship Register is notified of the seizure of the ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register. An expert is invited to assess the ship and floating structure registered in the Ship Register. A legal person may also be appointed as the custodian of a ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register.

(3) A ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register is sold at auction in the procedure specified in this law for the sale of immovable property. The notice of auction of a ship or floating structure registered in the Ship Register is also sent to the persons specified in Section 55 of the Maritime Code.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.3 pants. Procedure for Seizure and Sale of Intangible Items

(1) The bailiff seizes intangible items (rights) by adopting a decision in which the seized rights, their legal basis of origin and valuation are indicated. The bailiff sends the decision within three days to the person who, according to the seized rights, has the obligation to perform to the debtor (the bound person), indicating that from the date of receipt of the decision, performance under the obligation is to be given to the bailiff, not to the debtor. After sending the decision to the bound person, the bailiff sends the decision on seizure of the rights to the creditor and the debtor.

(2) From the date of receipt of the bailiff's decision, the debtor is prohibited from demanding or receiving performance under the seized right. The debtor and the bound person have the obligation, upon the bailiff's request, to provide all requested information relating to the seized right.

(3) Rights that are purely personal or whose alienation is prohibited by law or court decision cannot be seized.

(4) Intangible items are valued by the bailiff, determining their forced sale value according to the prices prevailing in this area. If necessary, the bailiff may, on his own initiative, invite an expert to determine the forced sale value.

(5) When sending the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section to the creditor and the debtor, the bailiff explains their right, within 10 days from the date of sending the decision, to request the bailiff to invite an expert for re-valuation of the items. The person who has requested re-valuation covers the valuation expenses within the term set by the bailiff, which is not shorter than five days, by depositing the necessary amount of money into the bailiff's account. If the amount of money necessary for valuation has not been deposited, the bailiff rejects the request to invite an expert.

(6) The bailiff sells seized intangible items at auction or without auction in the procedure specified in Section 583.1 of this law.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.4 pants. Procedure for Seizure and Sale of Shares or Stock of a Capital Company and Shares of a Cooperative Society

(1) The bailiff adopts a decision on the seizure of a share or stock of a capital company or share of a cooperative society owned by the debtor, in which the seized items and their valuation are indicated.

(2) The forced sale value of a share or stock or share is determined by the bailiff, but not lower than the nominal value of the share or stock or share. If necessary, the bailiff may, on his own initiative, invite an expert to determine the forced sale value.

(3) The bailiff sends the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section within three days to the creditor and the debtor, while explaining their right, within 10 days from the date of sending the decision, to request the bailiff to invite an expert for re-valuation of the items. The person who has requested re-valuation covers the valuation expenses within the term set by the bailiff, which is not shorter than five days, by depositing the necessary amount of money into the bailiff's account. If the amount of money necessary for valuation has not been deposited, the bailiff rejects the request to invite an expert.

(4) From the date of receipt of the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section, the debtor is prohibited from alienating the seized shares or stock or shares, encumbering them with other property or obligation rights, changing their nominal value, as well as performing other actions that reduce the value of the shares or stock or shares.

(5) Simultaneously with the adoption of the decision on seizure of shares, the bailiff issues an order to the board of the limited liability company and the commercial register institution to observe the prohibition on alienating or pledging the shares owned by the debtor, encumbering them with other property or obligation rights and, if necessary to ensure the sale of the seized shares, - also the prohibition on changing the nominal value of the shares and performing other actions that reduce the value of the shares owned by the debtor.

(6) Simultaneously with the adoption of the decision on seizure of stock or shares, the bailiff issues an order to the board of the stock company or cooperative society, respectively, to observe the prohibition on alienating or pledging the stock or shares owned by the debtor, encumbering them with other property or obligation rights and, if necessary to ensure the sale of the seized stock or shares, - also the prohibition on changing their nominal value and performing other actions that reduce the value of the stock or shares owned by the debtor.

(7) Simultaneously with the adoption of the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this section, the bailiff may issue an order to the board of the capital company or cooperative society to deposit all money due to the debtor into the bailiff's deposit account.

(8) The bailiff sells shares or stock or shares at auction, but if it has not been successful and no one has applied to retain the shares or stock or shares for themselves after an unsuccessful auction in the procedure specified in this chapter, they may also be sold without auction, observing the procedure for determining the forced sale value specified in the second paragraph of this section. After the alienation of the shares or stock or shares, the bailiff notifies the board of the capital company or cooperative society and the commercial register of the cancellation of the seizure.

(9) Simultaneously with the placement of the auction announcement for shares on the electronic auction website, the bailiff notifies the board of the limited liability company about the auction.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.5 pants. Procedure for Exercising Pre-emptive Rights for Shares of a Limited Liability Company

(1) The bailiff immediately notifies the board of the limited liability company that other members of the company may exercise pre-emptive rights for the seized shares if:

- 1) the auction of shares has been declared unsuccessful for the reasons provided for in points 1 or 2 of the first paragraph of Section 589 of this law and the creditor has deposited into the bailiff's deposit account the necessary amount for retaining the shares for himself in the procedure specified in Section 590 of this law;
- 2) the successful bidder or last outbid bidder has deposited into the bailiff's deposit account the entire amount due from him;
- 3) the bailiff sells the seized shares without auction in the procedure specified in Section 583.1 of this law, and the buyer has deposited the purchase price into the bailiff's deposit account.
  - (2) In the notice to the board of the limited liability company, the bailiff indicates the amount that is to be deposited into the bailiff's deposit account within the term set by the bailiff, which cannot be shorter than 10 days from the date of sending the notice, as well as that if the board organizes a closed auction among the members in accordance with the ninth paragraph of Section 189 of the Commercial Law, the board has the obligation to deposit into the bailiff's deposit account the additionally obtained part of the purchase price that exceeds the amount transferred indicated to the bailiff in the notice, within 10 days from the date of payment of the purchase price bid at the closed auction.
  - (3) If the indicated amount has not been deposited into the bailiff's deposit account within the term specified in the notice, the bailiff notifies the buyer, the successful bidder, the creditor or the last outbid bidder, respectively, that the members of the company have not exercised their pre-emptive rights.
  - (4) If the entire indicated amount is deposited into the bailiff's deposit account within the term specified in the notice, the bailiff draws up an act on the transfer of the seized shares to the limited liability company and sends it to the board of the company. After sending the act, the bailiff notifies the creditor, the debtor and the person who bid or expressed the wish to retain the shares for themselves or was the last outbid bidder about the exercise of pre-emptive rights, immediately refunding to that person the amount deposited by it.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.6 pants. Procedure for Seizure and Sale of Financial Instruments

(1) If the debtor owns financial instruments, the bailiff issues an order to the credit institution or investment brokerage company in which the debtor's financial instruments account is opened and which acts with his financial instruments at the debtor's instruction, prohibiting the alienation, pledging or otherwise encumbering with property or obligation rights the financial instruments owned by the debtor. If the seized financial instruments are located in the initial register of the central securities depository (within the meaning of the Financial Instruments Market Law), such an order is given to the central securities depository.

(2) Only paper-form securities are described in the procedure specified in Section 576 of this law. When describing securities, their number, class, numbers and nominal value, if known, are indicated. If the nominal value is not known, the bailiff values paper-form securities in the procedure specified in the first paragraph of Section 578 of this law. The creditor or debtor may request the bailiff to invite an expert for re-valuation of securities in the procedure specified in the second paragraph of Section 578 of this law. The bailiff seizes the described securities and, if unable to ensure their safekeeping, deposits them for safekeeping in a credit institution.

(3) For the sale of financial instruments, the bailiff issues an order to the credit institution or investment brokerage company in which the debtor's financial instruments account is opened and which acts with his financial instruments at the debtor's instruction, to sell the seized financial instruments on the regulated market at the market price of these financial instruments within a term not exceeding one month and to transfer the obtained money to the bailiff's deposit account. If it has not been possible to sell all of the debtor's financial instruments or part of them within the term set by the bailiff, the bailiff may extend the sale term by issuing a new order.

(4) If the debtor owns such financial instruments that are held in the debtor's financial instruments account but which cannot be sold in the procedure specified in the third paragraph of this section because they are not included in the regulated market, the bailiff issues an order to the credit institution or investment brokerage company to realize these financial instruments in accordance with the procedure established in the relevant market for determining the value and sale of financial instruments.

(5) The bailiff sells paper-form securities at a movable property auction. In such a case, the starting price is set as the nominal value of the paper-form securities or the forced sale value determined by the bailiff or expert, if the bailiff has invited an expert to determine it. If two expert valuations have been made, the starting price is the highest expert valuation.

(6) The bailiff sells rights to financial instruments located in the initial register of the central securities depository at a movable property auction. In such a case, the starting price is determined as the average market price of the financial instruments in the previous month before the announcement of the auction. If the debtor owns financial instruments of several types and categories, their sale in parts is permitted on the condition that all financial instruments of one type and one category are sold in one transaction. After the successful bidder has paid the purchase price in full into the bailiff's deposit account and informed the bailiff of his financial instruments account in a credit institution or investment brokerage company, the bailiff draws up an act about it and issues an order to the central securities depository to deregister the financial instruments to the acquirer's financial instruments account.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

580.7 pants. Procedure for Seizure and Sale of Items with Restricted Circulation

(1) Items with restricted circulation may be deposited for safekeeping only with such a natural or legal person who has been issued a special permit (licence) necessary for carrying out operations with items of the relevant type.

(2) The bailiff sells items with restricted circulation at auction or without auction in the procedure specified in Section 583.1 of this law. A person who wishes to acquire an item with restricted circulation presents to the bailiff documents that certify its right to acquire such items as property.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 581. pants. Sale of Pledged Property

(1) The bailiff has the right to sell the debtor's property if, within the period specified in this law, no request has been submitted for the engagement of an expert for repeated valuation of the property, but if a request for the engagement of an expert has been submitted — after repeated valuation of the property or rejection of the request.

(2) If, due to special circumstances, delay in the execution of the decision may cause significant losses to the creditor or debtor, or enforcement itself may become impossible, the property shall be seized and sold immediately in the procedure specified in Section 583.1 of this law. In such cases, the creditor or debtor may not request repeated valuation of the property, and appeal of the bailiff's decision on the sale of property without auction does not suspend the sale of the property, except in the case specified in the third paragraph of Section 632 of this law. If the debtor is registered as a value added tax payer, the bailiff shall apply value added tax to the sale price.

(3) The bailiff may sell pledged items as one object if identical items are pledged or a principal item and its accessories or if it is impractical to sell the pledged items separately.

(4) If the debtor is registered as a value added tax payer, the bailiff, before the sale of the pledged property, except in the case specified in the second paragraph of this Section, shall send an invitation to the debtor to provide information on whether, when selling his pledged property, the sale or auction price is subject to value added tax in accordance with the regulatory enactments governing value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018. as amended by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 582. pants. Sale Procedure of Pledged Property

(1) The bailiff sells the pledged property at auction, but in the cases and procedure specified in this law, the pledged property may also be sold without auction.

(2) The bailiff may seize the pledged movable property:

- 1) before sale at auction, if necessary;
- 2) in order to transfer it in the cases specified in this law to the purchaser, bidder, creditor or debtor of movable property.
  - (3) If the debtor fully pays the debt and the costs of execution of the judgment before the sale of the pledged property, but if the property is sold at auction — no later than seven days before the auction closing date specified in the auction announcement, the sale shall be cancelled, the auction already started shall be terminated and the pledged property shall be returned to the debtor, drawing up a record thereof.
  - (4) After the sale or transfer of the pledged property to the creditor, the bailiff shall adopt a decision on the release of the sold property from the pledge, and shall also send a notice to the relevant holder of the register of movable property or other public register on the cancellation of the prohibition and the release of the property from the pledge.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 583.pants. Sale of Pledged Property on Commission

(Deleted by the law of 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

583.1 pants. Sale of Pledged Property without Auction

(1) The bailiff sells the pledged property to a specific person (purchaser) without auction in the cases specifically indicated in this law, as well as when it may be impossible to sell the pledged property at auction or it has not been possible to sell it at auction. The bailiff shall adopt a decision on the sale of pledged property without auction, indicating the circumstances that allow the sale of the property without auction. The decision shall be sent to the debtor and the creditor. The decision may be appealed in the procedure specified in Section 632 of this law.

(2) With regard to the purchaser of pledged property, the restrictions set out in Section 586 of this law on persons who do not have the right to participate in bidding shall apply.

(3) After the expiry of the term for appeal of the decision issued by the bailiff, but if the bailiff's decision has been appealed — after a court decision rejecting the complaint has entered into legal force, the bailiff shall notify the purchaser of the time limit, which may not exceed one month, within which the purchase price shall be paid into the bailiff's deposit account.

(4) The price at which the pledged property may be sold (purchase price) may not be lower than that indicated by the bailiff in the property description record, but if an expert is engaged — than the forced sale value determined by the expert. If two expert valuations have been carried out, the purchase price may not be lower than the highest forced sale value determined by the expert. After the purchase price has been received in full in the bailiff's deposit account, the bailiff shall transfer the pledged property to the purchaser, drawing up a record thereof, and shall inform the State Revenue Service of the fact of the sale of the property and the price at which the property was sold.

(5) If the purchaser of the pledged property is the creditor, he shall be allowed to offset in the purchase price his claim based on an enforcement document. If the purchase price is insufficient to satisfy all enforcement and commercial pledge holders' claims, the creditor may offset in the purchase price his claims only to the extent of the amount due to him according to the calculation after the claims that have priority over his claim have been satisfied.

(6) If several persons have expressed a wish to purchase the pledged property, an auction shall be held.

(7) If the purchaser does not pay the purchase price into the bailiff's deposit account within the time limit specified in the third paragraph of this Section, the bailiff may sell the pledged property at auction or without auction in the procedure specified in this Section.

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018. as amended by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

583.2 pants. Sale of Movable Property at Auction

For the sale of movable property and the organisation of auctions, the procedure in which actions are carried out on the electronic auction website and in which information about a person is included, updated and deleted in the auction participants' register shall apply (Sections 605.1 and 605.2).

(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 584. Article. Announcement of Movable Property Auction

(1) The bailiff shall place the announcement of the movable property auction on the electronic auction website and, if he/she considers it appropriate, also post it at his/her place of practice. An interested person may, at their own expense, place the auction announcement in newspapers and other mass media, as well as post the announcement in public places in accordance with the procedure established by the respective municipality.

(2) The announcement of the movable property auction shall indicate:

- 1) the bailiff's first name, surname, official location and place of practice;
- 2) the debtor's first name and surname, for a legal person — the name and registered address;
- 3) the item to be sold and its valuation;
- 4) which auction in sequence it is;
- 5) the starting price of the auction and the auction step;
- 6) the start date and end date and time of the auction;
- 7) whether the auction price is subject to value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price;
- 8) the security amount to be paid into the bailiff's deposit account;
- 9) the date by which a person wishing to participate in the auction may request the bailiff to authorize them to participate in the auction and pay the security amount;
- 10) a reference to the website where information is available on the auction procedure and the conditions under which persons may register to participate in the auction and participate in bidding.
  - (3) Simultaneously with the posting of the auction announcement on the electronic auction website, the bailiff shall notify the creditor and the debtor of the auction.
  - (4) The movable property auction shall commence from the bailiff's valuation, but if one or two expert valuations have been performed — from the highest expert valuation.
  - (5) The bailiff shall determine the auction step, not less than one percent and not more than 10 percent of the starting price of the movable property auction.
  - (6) During the period from the date of announcement of the auction until the date set for submission of the request for authorization to participate in the auction, persons wishing to participate in the auction shall have the right to inspect the item to be sold. The bailiff shall notify the custodian of the property of the time and place of inspection of the property. If several persons have expressed a wish to inspect the item to be sold, the bailiff shall ensure that the inspection of the property is, if possible, organized simultaneously.

(As worded by the Law of 01.03.2018 with amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

584.1 Article. Security for Purchase of Movable Property and Authorization of Auction Participants

(1) A person wishing to participate in a movable property auction, using the electronic auction website, shall, within 10 days from the auction start date indicated in the movable property auction announcement, send a request to the bailiff to authorize them to participate in the auction and pay into the bailiff's deposit account specified in the auction announcement a security deposit in the amount of 10 percent of the valuation of the item to be sold.

(2) If the valuation of the item to be sold is 10,000 euros or more, the time limit within which a person shall send a request to the bailiff to authorize them to participate in the auction in the manner specified in paragraph one of this Article and pay the security into the bailiff's deposit account shall be 20 days from the auction start date indicated in the movable property auction announcement.

(3) The bailiff shall authorize a person to participate in the auction within three, but in the case referred to in paragraph two of this Article — five working days from the date of receipt of the security and the person's request, if the restrictions mentioned in Article 586 of this Law do not exist. If the security or authorization request has not been received within the time limit specified in paragraph one or two of this Article, or if the person does not have the right to participate in the auction in accordance with Article 586 of this Law, the bailiff shall refuse to authorize the person to participate in the auction.

(4) The security paid by the person who has bid for the item to be sold shall be credited towards the purchase price. The security paid by the other auction participants, except for the last outbid bidder, shall be returned immediately after the conclusion of the auction. The security paid by the last outbid bidder shall be returned within two working days after the successful bidder has paid the full amount bid. If the property is retained by the last outbid bidder after an auction that has not taken place, their paid security shall be credited towards the purchase price.

(As worded by the Law of 01.03.2018, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 585.Article. Announcement of Ship Auction

(Deleted by the Law of 01.03.2018, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 586. Article. Persons Who Do Not Have the Right to Participate in Bidding

The debtor, their guardian or custodian, the person who performed the valuation mentioned in Article 578 of this Law, as well as the bailiff who organizes the auction do not have the right to participate in bidding. The creditor has the right to participate in the auction under the general procedure. The auction participants themselves are responsible for compliance with the restrictions established in other normative acts regarding the acquisition of the item to be auctioned.

(As worded by the Law of 01.03.2018, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 587. Article. Procedure for Auction of Movable Property

(1) An auction participant may electronically make bids from the moment they are authorized to participate in the auction in the manner specified in Article 584.1 of this Law until the moment the auction has ended.

(2) Bidding shall take place in the manner specified in paragraphs two and three of Article 608 of this Law.

(3) The auction shall conclude on the twentieth day from the auction start indicated in the movable property auction announcement at 13.00. If the valuation of the item to be sold is 10,000 euros or more, the auction shall conclude on the thirtieth day from the auction start date indicated in the movable property auction announcement at 13.00, but if the thirtieth day falls on a day off or a public holiday — on the next working day at 13.00.

(4) If a bid is registered during the last five minutes before the time set for the conclusion of the auction, the auction time shall be automatically extended by five minutes. If significant technical disruptions that may affect the auction result are detected during the last hour before the conclusion of the auction and they are not related to system security breaches, the auction time shall be automatically extended until the next working day at 13.00. After the conclusion of the auction, bids are no longer registered and the electronic auction website shall indicate the auction conclusion date, time and the last bid made.

(5) The bailiff may suspend a movable property auction in the cases provided for in this Law. The notice of suspension of the auction shall be published on the electronic auction website.

(6) The creditor, by submitting an application to the bailiff, may request to postpone the auction or issue an enforcement document according to which enforcement has not been carried out or has been carried out incompletely, if such request of the creditor has been received no later than seven days before the auction conclusion date indicated in the auction announcement.

(7) After the conclusion of the auction, a notice shall be sent electronically to the successful bidder to the account of the electronic auction website user registered in the Auction Participants Register that they have bid a higher price than others and the obligation to pay the entire amount due from them has arisen.

(As worded by the Law of 01.03.2018, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 588. pants. Auction Record

(1) In the auction record, the bailiff indicates:

- 1) the start date and end date and time of the auction;
- 2) the bailiff's first name, surname, official position and place of practice;
- 3) the decision being enforced;
- 4) the name of the item being sold;
- 5) the starting auction price of the item being sold;
- 6) the person authorized to participate in the auction, indicating their first name, surname, personal code or date of birth (for a person who has not been assigned a personal code), the contact address indicated in the Auction Participants Register; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;
- 7) the prices bid at the auction and the bidder's first and last name or company (name);
- 8) the highest price bid, the successful bidder's first and last name or name, personal code or registration number and address.
  - (2) An auction record electronically prepared on the electronic auction website is valid without the bailiff's signature.

(As worded by the law of 01.03.2018, which entered into force on 01.07.2018.)

588.1 pants. Consequences of the Auction

(1) The person who has successfully bid for the item being sold shall pay the full amount bid and value added tax, if the auction price is subject to value added tax, no later than within two working days after the conclusion of the auction. If the amount bid exceeds 1420 euros, the bailiff may, at the request of the successful bidder, postpone the payment of the full purchase price and value added tax for a period of up to seven days. If the amount bid exceeds 142 280 euros, the bailiff may, at the request of the successful bidder, postpone the payment of the full purchase price and value added tax for a period of up to 14 days. When the amount bid and the value added tax have been paid in full, the bailiff shall draw up a record indicating to whom and for what price the auctioned items have been sold, and shall also inform the State Revenue Service of the fact and price of the sale of the property. The record and the purchased items shall be handed over to the successful bidder.

(2) After the time limit for appealing the calculation prepared by the bailiff has expired and this calculation has not been appealed or, if this calculation has been appealed, after the court decision on the calculation has entered into force, the bailiff shall pay the value added tax paid by the successful bidder into the state budget and notify the debtor and the State Revenue Service thereof.

(As worded by the law of 01.03.2018, which entered into force on 01.07.2018.)

588.2 pants. Set-off of Purchase Price

(1) The successful bidder is allowed to set off against the purchase price their claim based on an enforcement document.

(2) If the amount received from the sale is insufficient to satisfy all claims and claims of commercial pledgees, the successful bidder may set off their claims against the purchase price only to the extent of the amount which, according to the calculation, is due to them after those claims which have priority over their claim have been covered.

(As worded by the law of 01.03.2018, which entered into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 589. pants. Auction That Did Not Take Place

(1) The bailiff shall declare the auction as not having taken place if:

- 1) no auction participant has been authorized for the auction;
- 2) none of the participants authorized for the auction has bid over the starting price;
- 3) the successful bidder has not paid the full amount due from them within the specified time limit (Article 588.1, paragraph one);
- 4) during the auction, except in the case referred to in Article 587, paragraph four of this Law, or within 24 hours after the conclusion of the auction, a notice has been received from the electronic auction website security administrator about significant technical disruptions that may affect the auction result or about a system security breach.
  - (2) In the cases referred to in points 1 or 2 of paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff shall draw up a record that the auction has been declared as not having taken place and shall notify the claimant and the debtor. Notifications shall be sent to participants authorized to participate in the auction using the electronic auction website.
  - (3) In the case referred to in point 3 of paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff shall draw up a record that the auction has been declared as not having taken place and shall notify the successful bidder, the debtor and the claimant.
  - (4) If the notice referred to in point 4 of paragraph one of this Article is received during the auction, the bailiff shall suspend the auction and post a notice thereof on the electronic auction website.
  - (5) In the case referred to in point 4 of paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff shall draw up a record that the auction has been declared as not having taken place and shall notify the claimant and the debtor. Notifications shall be sent to participants authorized to participate in the auction using the electronic auction website.
  - (6) In the case referred to in point 3 of paragraph one of this Article, the security deposit paid shall not be refunded but shall be added to the total amount received for the property. The security deposit paid shall also be added to the total amount if it is found that the successful bidder had no right to participate in the auction (Article 586, third sentence), and if the last highest bidder has not notified of retaining the property for themselves at their highest bid price or has refused to retain it (Article 590, paragraphs four and eight).

(As worded by the law of 01.03.2018, which entered into force on 01.07.2018.)

#### 590. pants. Consequences of an unsuccessful auction and second auction

(1) If an auction is declared unsuccessful due to the reason provided in Paragraph 1 or 2 of Part 1 of Article 589 of this Law, the bailiff shall immediately notify the creditor thereof, inviting them to retain the pledged property for themselves at the opening auction price. The creditor has the right within two weeks from the date of sending the bailiff's invitation to notify the bailiff in writing of retaining the pledged property for themselves.

(2) If several creditors wish to retain the pledged property for themselves at the opening auction price, a repeated first auction shall be held in which creditors who wish to retain the pledged property for themselves at the opening price participate, and bidding starts from the opening price of the first auction. The bailiff shall notify the creditors in writing of the time and place of the auction seven days in advance. The failure of a creditor to appear at the auction shall be considered as their renunciation of the right to retain the property for themselves. If one creditor appears at the auction, they may retain the pledged property for themselves without bidding. If no creditor appears at the auction, the bailiff shall immediately announce a second auction.

(3) If no one has applied to retain the pledged property for themselves, the bailiff shall immediately hold a second auction. The second auction shall be announced in accordance with the rules of the first auction, but bidding at the second auction for movable property shall commence from an amount equal to 75 percent of the opening price of the first auction.

(4) If the auction is declared unsuccessful due to the reason provided in Paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Article 589 of this Law, the bailiff shall immediately notify the last outbid bidder thereof, inviting them to retain the pledged property for themselves at their highest bid price. The last outbid bidder has the right within two weeks from the date of sending the bailiff's invitation to notify the bailiff in writing of retaining the pledged property for themselves. If the last outbid bidder has not notified of retaining the pledged property within the time limit set by law or has refused to retain it for themselves, the bailiff shall immediately announce a repeated first auction.

(5) If the auction is declared unsuccessful due to the reason provided in Paragraph 4 of Part 1 of Article 589 of this Law, the bailiff shall immediately announce a repeated first auction.

(6) In the cases provided for in paragraphs one, two and four of this Article, the person who retains the pledged property for themselves, as well as the person who has bid on the item for sale at the second auction, shall make payment and receive the pledged property in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 588.1 of this Law.

(7) If the second auction is declared unsuccessful due to the reason provided in Paragraph 1 or 2 of Part 1 of Article 589 of this Law and no one has notified in the procedure laid down in the first paragraph of this Article of the wish to retain the pledged property for themselves at the opening price of the second auction, the property may be returned to the debtor, releasing it from pledge, or the bailiff may decide on the sale of the property in another manner provided for in this Chapter. The bailiff shall draw up an act on the return of the property to the debtor.

(8) If the second auction is declared unsuccessful due to the reason provided in Paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Article 589 of this Law and the last outbid bidder has not notified in the procedure laid down in the fourth paragraph of this Article of the wish to retain the pledged property for themselves at their highest bid price, or if the second auction is declared unsuccessful due to the reason provided in Paragraph

4 of Part 1 of Article 589 of this Law, the bailiff shall immediately announce a repeated second auction.

(9) A person subject to sanctions may not retain the pledged property if the acquisition of the property is not compatible with the restrictions imposed by the sanctions.

(In the wording of the Law of 01.03.2018 with amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 591.pants. Recognition of an auction as invalid

(1) The court shall declare an auction invalid if:

- 1) someone has been unjustifiably not allowed to participate in the auction or a bid has been wrongly rejected;
- 2) the property has been purchased by a person who was not entitled to participate in the auction;
- 3) (deleted by the Law of 01.03.2018);
- 4) the bailiff, creditor or purchaser has committed malpractice.
  - (11) A complaint regarding the actions of the bailiff, creditor or purchaser that give grounds to demand recognition of the auction as invalid may be submitted by an interested person within 10 days from the date of conclusion of the auction to the district (city) court at the bailiff's place of office.
  - (2) An appeal may be filed against the court's decision.
  - (3) If an auction is declared invalid, a repeated auction shall be held according to the rules of the auction that was declared invalid.

(With amendments made by the Law of 01.03.2018, which came into force on 01.07.2018.)

591.1 pants. Procedure for enforcement of confiscation of movable property

(1) The bailiff shall pledge and sell confiscated movable property in accordance with the procedure laid down in this Chapter, insofar as this Article does not provide otherwise.

(2) Having received the writ of execution and the attached extract from the protocol or decision on seizure of property, the bailiff shall immediately verify the existence of the property indicated therein. If the custodian of the property presents all the property placed in custody and its value has not significantly changed, the bailiff shall not pledge the property again. If enforcement of the confiscation of property cannot be carried out because the confiscated property has not been found, the bailiff shall close the enforcement case without enforcement and notify the court of first instance that adopted the enforceable judgment and the prosecutor's office so that it may decide on the liability of the custodian of the property.

(3) If the confiscated items could be impossible to sell and the costs of enforcement of the judgment could exceed the amount of money obtained from the sale, the bailiff shall transfer them to the State Revenue Service.

(4) A person whose property confiscation is being enforced does not have the debtor's rights provided for in this Law.

(5) If the auction is declared unsuccessful or property placed for sale on commission is not sold, the right to retain the property in the procedure laid down in this Chapter belongs to the creditor in other enforcement cases for recovery from the person whose property confiscation is being enforced. If the second auction has not taken place and no one has wished to retain the confiscated property for themselves, the bailiff shall transfer the property to the State Revenue Service.

(In the wording of the Law of 22.06.2017, which came into force on 01.08.2017.)

72.nodaļa

Recovery from wages, payments equivalent thereto and other monetary amounts

(Title of Chapter in the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the Law of 07.09.2006, which came into force on 11.10.2006.)

#### 592.pants. Recovery from wages

(1) Recovery from the debtor's wages, including remuneration that the debtor receives for civil service or military service, shall be enforced if:

- 1) a decision on recovery of periodic payments is being enforced;
- 2) the amount of recovery does not exceed that part of monthly wages or payments equivalent thereto from which recovery may be enforced by law;
- 3) the creditor has requested to enforce recovery from wages or payments equivalent thereto.
  - (2) Recovery from the debtor's wages shall also be enforced if the debtor has no property or it is insufficient to recover the debt.

(With amendments made by the Law of 31.10.2002, which came into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 593.pants. Information on the debtor's wages and payments equivalent thereto

The employer shall, at the request of the bailiff, within the time limit set by the bailiff, provide information on whether the debtor works for them, what their wages and payments equivalent thereto are in the period indicated by the bailiff.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, which came into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 594.pants. Amount of deductions from the debtor's wages and equivalent payments

(1) From the debtor's payable wages and equivalent payments, deductions according to enforcement documents are made until the debt to be recovered is discharged:

- 1) in maintenance recovery cases for the maintenance of minor children or for the benefit of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration — retaining for the debtor wages and equivalent payments in the amount of 50 percent of the minimum monthly wage and additionally for each dependent minor child — funds in the amount of 15 percent of the minimum monthly wage;
- 2) when recovering maintenance, damages or compensation in connection with personal injury resulting in mutilation or other health damage or death of a person, or compensation for harm caused by a criminal offense or administrative violation, as well as when executing decisions made in administrative violation proceedings — 50 percent, retaining for the debtor wages and equivalent payments in the amount of 50 percent of the minimum monthly wage and additionally for each dependent minor child — funds in the amount of 15 percent of the minimum monthly wage;
- 3) in other types of recovery, if not otherwise provided by law — 30 percent, retaining for the debtor wages and equivalent payments in the amount of the minimum monthly wage and additionally for each dependent minor child — funds in the amount of 15 percent of the minimum monthly wage.
  - (2) If enforcement against wages is levied according to several enforcement documents, the employee in each case must retain wages and equivalent payments in the amount of 50 percent, but not less than the amount of the minimum monthly wage and additionally for each dependent minor child — funds in the amount of 15 percent of the minimum monthly wage, except in the cases specified in points 1 and 2 of paragraph one of this Article.
  - (21) If within the framework of one enforcement case, enforcement is simultaneously levied both against wages and equivalent payments and against deposits in a credit institution, the bailiff, at the debtor's request, gives an order to the credit institution to retain in the account in which the debtor receives wages or equivalent payments, monetary funds in the amount specified in paragraph one or two of this Article.
  - (3) (Deleted by the Law of 31.10.2002.)
  - (4) The amount of deductions from wages and equivalent payments is calculated from the amount that the debtor is to receive after payment of taxes.
  - (5) Funds in the amount of 15 percent of the minimum monthly wage for each minor child dependent on the debtor are retained if a minor child is dependent on the debtor at the time when deductions are made from the debtor's wages or equivalent payments. The amount of funds to be retained is calculated by the employer or the relevant legal person, taking into account the number of persons dependent on the debtor at the time of making the deduction.

(As amended by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 17.06.2004., 23.05.2013., 19.12.2013., 28.05.2015., 22.06.2017., 11.11.2021. and 22.12.2021., which enters into force on 24.12.2021.)

#### 595.pants. Enforcement against other income of the debtor outside of wages

(1) The conditions and procedure specified in this chapter to be observed when levying enforcement against wages shall also apply in cases where the debtor receives:

- 1) a scholarship of a student of an educational institution;
- 2) amounts for compensation of damages for personal injury resulting in mutilation or other health damage or death of a person;
- 3) (deleted by the Law of 17.12.2009.).
  - (2) When levying enforcement against state pensions, state social insurance benefits and compensations, the provisions on levying enforcement against wages are applicable, unless other restrictions on deductions are provided in other laws.

(As amended by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 17.12.2009. and 19.12.2013., which enters into force on 04.01.2014.)

#### 596.pants. Amounts against which enforcement cannot be levied

Enforcement cannot be levied against:

- 1) severance pay, funeral benefit, one-time benefit to the deceased's spouse, state social benefits, state support for a child with celiac disease, survivor's pension and compensation for loss of a breadwinner;
- 2) compensation payments for wear and tear of tools owned by the employee and other compensations in accordance with regulatory enactments governing labour legal relations;
- 3) amounts payable to an employee in connection with business trips, transfer and posting to work in another locality;
- 4) social assistance benefits;
- 5) child maintenance in the amount of the minimum child maintenance established by the Cabinet of Ministers, which, based on a court decision or decision of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration, is paid by one of the parents, as well as against child maintenance payable by the Maintenance Guarantee Fund.

(As amended by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 17.12.2009., 12.02.2015. and 08.12.2016., which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The amendment to point 5 regarding non-enforcement against child maintenance in the minimum amount established by the Cabinet of Ministers, which, based on a decision of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration, is paid by one of the parents, enters into force on 01.04.2017. See transitional provision point 122)

#### 597.pants. Procedure for enforcement against the debtor's wages, equivalent payments and

other income

(1) The bailiff sends to the employer or the relevant legal person an order with an instruction to make deductions from the debtor's wages or other remuneration, pension, scholarship or benefit and to pay the deducted amounts into the bailiff's deposit account at the debtor's expense.

(2) Upon terminating employment relations with the debtor, the employer informs the bailiff thereof and also indicates the debtor's new place of work, if it is known. These provisions also apply to legal persons that have made deductions from the pension, scholarship or benefit payable to the debtor, if the payment thereof is discontinued.

(As amended by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003. and 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### 598.pants. Control over the correctness of deductions

The bailiff, at the written request of the creditor, verifies whether the employer (relevant legal person) has made deductions from the debtor's wages and other types of income correctly and in a timely manner and whether the deducted amounts have been paid into the bailiff's deposit account.

(As amended by the Laws of 31.10.2002. and 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)
