#### 599.pants. Enforcement against monetary funds due from other persons

(1) If enforcement is levied against monetary funds due from other persons, including from another bailiff, the bailiff sends a request to these persons to declare whether they have an obligation to pay any sums to the debtor, on what basis and within what time limit.

(2) Simultaneously with the request, the bailiff notifies that these monetary funds are being pledged in the amount of the sum to be collected and the costs of execution of the judgment, and that until the complete discharge of the sum to be collected and the costs of execution of the judgment, these persons must deposit the monetary funds in the bailiff's deposit account.

(3) (Deleted from 01.07.2017. by the law of 23.11.2016., which enters into force on 01.01.2017.)

(07.09.2006. law version with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 23.11.2016., which enters into force on 01.01.2017. Amendment on the deletion of paragraph three enters into force on 01.07.2017. See transitional provision 120. point) 599.1 pants. Enforcement against monetary funds in credit institutions or with other payment service providers

(1) When levying enforcement against the debtor's monetary funds in a credit institution or with another payment service provider, the bailiff prepares and sends to the credit institution or other payment service provider an order for the pledge of monetary funds in the amount specified in the order. The order is sent to the respective credit institution or payment service provider in accordance with the account register data on the debtor's opened accounts.

(2) In the order referred to in paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff, in relation to a debtor who is a natural person, indicates to one of the credit institutions or payment service providers the restriction specified in point 3 of Annex 1 of this Law.

(3) Within three working days after receiving the order, the credit institution or other payment service provider, using the State Information System Integrator under the supervision of the State Regional Development Agency, sends a notification to the issuer of the order in the Register of Enforcement Cases on the amount of the pledged sum.

(4) The credit institution or other payment service provider has no right to pay out to another person the monetary funds pledged for enforcement or to allow the debtor to dispose of them.

(5) Within four working days after receiving the notification provided by the credit institution or other payment service provider, the bailiff evaluates the information provided in the notification and sends to the credit institution or other payment service provider an order for:

- 1) transfer of monetary funds to the bailiff's deposit account in the amount specified in the order until the discharge of the sum to be collected and the costs of execution of the judgment;
- 2) transfer of monetary funds to the bailiff's deposit account in the amount specified in the order, preserving the monetary funds of the debtor who is a natural person in the amount specified in point 3 of Annex 1 of this Law, until the discharge of the sum to be collected and the costs of execution of the judgment;
- 3) specification of the action or the amount of monetary funds or cancellation of the order.
  - (6) A debtor who is a natural person has the right to inform the bailiff about the account in which monetary funds shall be preserved as unpledged in the amount specified in point 3 of Annex 1 of this Law.
  - (7) The order referred to in point 3 of paragraph five of this Article for the specification of the bailiff's previously issued order may be prepared and sent to the credit institution or other payment service provider through the Register of Enforcement Cases system, observing the amount of the sum to be collected and the costs of execution of the judgment remaining in the enforcement case.
  - (8) If the debtor has only one account or an order for the pledge of monetary funds is already being executed in another enforcement case in the proceedings of the same bailiff, the bailiff may immediately issue to the credit institution or other payment service provider the order referred to in paragraph five of this Article.
  - (9) The bailiff supervises that the total sum of monetary funds received in the deposit account from credit institutions or other payment service providers does not exceed the amount necessary to cover the debt sum and the costs of execution of the judgment. If the total sum of monetary funds received exceeds the amount necessary to cover the debt sum to be collected and the costs of execution of the judgment, the bailiff immediately, but not later than within seven days from the day they are credited to the bailiff's deposit account, refunds to the debtor the overpaid monetary funds. If, due to objective circumstances, it is not possible to comply with this time limit, the bailiff, after the elimination or termination of the objective circumstances, immediately refunds to the debtor the monetary funds in the amount of the excess sum.
  - (10) The bailiff sends the orders specified in this Article to the credit institution or other payment service provider and receives notifications from the credit institution or other payment service provider electronically, using the State Information System Integrator under the supervision of the State Regional Development Agency.
  - (11) Upon receiving several orders for the pledge of the debtor's monetary funds or the orders referred to in paragraph eight of this Article, the credit institution or other payment service provider executes them in the order in which they are entered in the State Information System Integrator under the supervision of the State Regional Development Agency.

(23.11.2016. law version, which enters into force on 01.01.2017. Article enters into force on 01.07.2017. See transitional provisions 118., 119. and 120. point)

599.2 pants. Procedure for execution of confiscation of financial assets

If financial assets are confiscated, the bailiff issues an order to the state or local government institution in whose account these financial assets are located, to transfer them to the bailiff's deposit account. If the confiscated financial assets are in the account of another person, the order for their transfer to the bailiff's deposit account is issued to the credit institution. The bailiff's order is to be executed immediately.

(22.06.2017. law version, which enters into force on 01.08.2017.)

73.nodaļa

Enforcement against immovable property

#### 600.pants. Notice of enforcement against immovable property

(1) If the judgment creditor requests enforcement against immovable property, the bailiff sends a notice to the debtor and invites him to settle the debt, as well as to provide information on whether the debtor is registered as a value added tax payer and whether, when selling his immovable property at auction, the auction price is subject to value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price.

(2) The bailiff submits to the district (city) court a request for affirmation to enter an enforcement note. The consequences of this note are specified in the first part of Article 1077, Articles 1081 and 1305 of the Civil Law, as well as in Article 46 of the Land Register Law.

(3) The bailiff, in accordance with the transcript of the relevant land register section, sends a notice to the owner of the immovable property, holders of building rights, co-owners of the immovable property, except co-owners of a residential house that has not been divided into apartment properties, as well as to all mortgage creditors, including persons in whose favor a pledge right or prohibition note has been entered, indicating:

- 1) the satisfaction of which person's claim enforcement is being directed against the immovable property;
- 2) how large is the amount of the debt and whether the debt is secured by a mortgage on the relevant immovable property.
  - (4) In the notice referred to in paragraph three of this Article, the bailiff requests that the mortgage creditors submit within the time limit set by the bailiff, which shall not be less than 10 days, information on the amount of the remaining mortgage debt.
  - (5) The bailiff requests from the municipality information on the immovable property tax debt and invites the municipality to submit a decision on the recovery of the tax debt, if such exists.
  - (6) If the debtor has fully paid the debt and the costs of enforcement of the judgment to the bailiff no later than seven days before the auction closing date specified in the auction announcement, the sale of the immovable property shall be cancelled, and the auction already started shall be discontinued.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 05.02.2009., 20.12.2010., 08.09.2011. 23.05.2013., 11.09.2014., 28.05.2015., 01.03.2018., 25.10.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 601.pants. Debtor's obligations

(1) From the day of receipt of the bailiff's notice, the debtor is prohibited from:

- 1) alienating this immovable property or pledging it;
- 2) cutting forest therein, except what is necessary for maintaining the household;
- 3) alienating or damaging accessories of the immovable property;
- 4) transferring this immovable property into possession of another person, including entering into lease, rent and other contracts encumbering the immovable property.
  - (2) Contracts which the debtor has concluded regarding the immovable property after an enforcement note has been made in the land register shall not be valid in relation to the judgment creditor and the purchaser of the immovable property at auction.
  - (3) The force of contracts which the debtor has concluded in relation to the immovable property before an enforcement note was entered in the land register shall be determined both in relation to the parties who participated in these contracts and in relation to the purchaser of the immovable property at auction, in accordance with the Civil Law.
  - (4) The debtor has an obligation to notify within the time limit set by the bailiff of the actual possessor and manager of the immovable property, if such exists, as well as of all lease, rent and other contracts encumbering the immovable property concluded in relation to this immovable property, submitting copies of the said contracts, while presenting their originals.
  - (5) The debtor has an obligation to notify the bailiff whether he is registered as a value added tax payer and whether, when selling his immovable property at auction, the auction price is subject to value added tax.

If the auction price is subject to value added tax in accordance with the legal acts regulating value added tax, in the said information the debtor shall indicate the taxable value of this price.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009., 20.12.2010., 08.09.2011. and 23.05.2013., which enter into force on 01.11.2013.)

#### 602.pants. Rights of judgment creditors and other creditors

(1) The judgment creditor, regardless of the enforcement against the immovable property, has the right to request that a mortgage be affirmed for him in the land register in the amount of the sum to be recovered.

(2) The mortgage creditor has the right to participate in the description of the immovable property, to receive the description act and to publish announcements about the auction at his own expense, notifying the bailiff thereof.

(3) The mortgage creditor and the judgment creditor have the right to participate in bidding by paying the security specified in the first part of Article 607 of this Law.

(4) The judgment creditor, by submitting an application to the bailiff, may request to postpone the auction or to issue the enforcement document by which enforcement has not been made or has been made incompletely, if such request of the judgment creditor is received no later than seven days before the auction closing date specified in the auction announcement.

(5) A mortgage creditor to whom sanctions apply may not exercise the rights granted to him in this and other Articles of this Law insofar as these rights are not compatible with the restrictions imposed by the sanctions. The foregoing does not prevent the performance of official duties in the enforcement case.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009., 04.02.2016. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force

#### 603.pants. Description of immovable property

(1) The bailiff describes the immovable property upon the judgment creditor's request. He notifies the debtor of the time of description of the immovable property by sending the notice provided for in Article 600 of this Law, and the judgment creditor. At the description of the immovable property, the debtor and the judgment creditor have the right to invite no more than two witnesses. Non-appearance of the debtor, judgment creditor or witnesses does not prevent the description.

(2) The description act indicates:

- 1) the name, surname, official place and place of practice of the bailiff;
- 2) the decision of the court or other institution which is being executed;
- 3) the name and surname of the judgment creditor and the debtor or their authorized persons or representatives, if such participate in the description;
- 4) the name, surname, declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration of the witnesses, but, if there are none, — the place of residence, if such participate in the description;
- 5) the place where the immovable property is located;
- 6) of what parts the immovable property consists;
- 7) on the basis of the land register entry:
  - a) the value of the immovable property being described, if such is indicated, its owner, encumbrances with debts and their amounts, as well as restrictions and encumbrances imposed on the immovable property,
  - b) information on the condition of the immovable property and contracts concluded in relation to this property, if the bailiff knows of such, as well as information on movable property which is an accessory of the immovable property;
- 8) the actual possessor or manager of the immovable property, if such are known.
  - (3) When describing a technologically interrelated complex of equipment and buildings, it is also indicated in which buildings it is located, the size of the buildings occupied, composition, number of work premises, number of workshops and other equipment.
  - (4) When describing immovable property, the provisions of Articles 576 and 577 of this Law shall also apply.
  - (5) The debtor shall submit documents and plans by which the area of the immovable property being described and the debtor's rights to this property are determined, as well as notify the bailiff who is the actual possessor and manager of the immovable property.
  - (6) The bailiff, at the request of interested persons and at their expense, may request from the district (city) court those documents which relate to the immovable property being described.
  - (7) Non-receipt of the documents specified in the fifth and sixth parts of this Article does not prevent the description.
  - (8) If the debtor or the judgment creditor has not participated in the description of the immovable property, the bailiff shall send them the description act within three days after the description.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 25.10.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 604.pants. Valuation of Immovable Property

(1) The immovable property shall be valued at the debtor's expense upon request of the bailiff by a certified real estate appraiser, determining the forced sale value of the immovable property.

(2) The bailiff shall notify the debtor, the creditor and the mortgage creditor of the valuation, simultaneously explaining their right to request a re-valuation of the immovable property within 10 days from the date of sending the notification.

(3) The person who has requested a re-valuation shall cover the valuation costs within the time limit set by the bailiff by depositing the necessary amount of money into the bailiff's account. If the amount of money required for the valuation is not deposited within this time limit, the bailiff shall reject the request for re-valuation of the immovable property.

(In the version of the law of 05.02.2009 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 605.pants. Management of Immovable Property

(1) The described immovable property shall remain under the management of the previous holder or administrator until transfer to the new owner.

(2) The property holder or administrator shall preserve the described immovable property in the same condition as it was at the time of description, together with the same movable property.

(3) If the holder or administrator of the immovable property is not known, the bailiff may at his or her discretion appoint an administrator of the immovable property. The administrator of immovable property appointed by the bailiff shall have the same liability as the custodian of movable property specified in this law.

(4) The holder and administrator of the immovable property shall provide an account to the bailiff for the period of management of the described property. The income received from the immovable property shall be transferred to the bailiff and added to the amount received from the sale of this property.

(In the version of the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

605.1 pants. Electronic Auction Website

(1) The electronic auction website is a module of the Register of Enforcement Matters that ensures the placement of auction announcements, registration of auction participants, accumulation of information about registered auction participants, authorization of registered auction participants to participate in the announced auction, as well as a set of technological tools for making and registering bids.

(2) The bailiff, in performing official duties, places auction announcements on the electronic auction website, registers auction participants, authorizes them to participate in the announced auction, and performs other actions related to organizing the auction. auction.

(3) The procedure for performing actions on the electronic auction website shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(In the version of the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015. See transitional provision 106.punktu)

605.2 pants. Register of Auction Participants

(1) The register of auction participants of the electronic auction website contains information about persons who have agreed to the terms of use of the electronic auction website and are registered as auction participants. Persons included in the register of auction participants have an obligation to notify about changes in their data. Information included in the register of auction participants is restricted access information.

(2) The Cabinet of Ministers shall determine the procedure by which information about a person is included in the register of auction participants, the scope of information to be included, as well as the procedure for updating and deleting this information.

(In the version of the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015. See transitional provision 106.punktu)

#### 606.pants. Announcement of Auction of Immovable Property

(1) The bailiff shall announce the auction of immovable property if, within the time limit specified in Section 604 of this law, no request for a new valuation of the immovable property has been submitted or it has been rejected.

(2) The bailiff shall send the announcement of the auction of immovable property for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis" and place it on the electronic auction website.

(3) The announcement of the auction of immovable property shall indicate:

- 1) the name and surname of the owner of the immovable property and the creditor, for legal persons — the name and legal address;
- 2) the name, surname, place of office and place of practice of the bailiff;
- 3) a brief description of the immovable property, its location and cadastral number;
- 31) the date, subject and term of the building right agreement if the building right is being auctioned;
- 4) the valuation of the immovable property;
- 5) which auction in order it is;
- 6) the starting price of the auction and the auction step;
- 7) the start date and end date and time of the auction;
- 8) whether the auction price is subject to value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price;
- 9) the amount of security to be paid into the bailiff's deposit account;
- 10) the date by which a person who wishes to participate in the auction may pay the security amount and request the bailiff to authorize them to participate in the auction;
- 11) a reference to the website where information is available on the auction procedure and conditions under which persons may register to participate in the auction and participate in bidding.
  - (4) The start date of the auction indicated in the announcement may not be later than 10 working days from the date on which the announcement was sent for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".
  - (5) Simultaneously with sending the announcement of the auction of immovable property for publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis", the bailiff shall notify the debtor and the creditor, the owner of the immovable property, building rights holders, co-owners, except co-owners of a residential house that has not been divided into apartment properties, mortgage creditors and persons in whose favour pledge rights or a prohibition mark have been registered, of the auction. The notification shall also indicate whether the auction price is subject to value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price.
  - (6) The bailiff shall determine the auction step, not less than one percent and not more than 10 percent of the starting price of the auction of the immovable property.
  - (7) From the day of the announcement of the auction, all documents relating to the sale of immovable property at auction shall be available to all persons who wish to become acquainted with them.
  - (8) Participants who are authorized for the auction may make bids throughout the duration of the auction.

(In the version of the law of 28.05.2015 with amendments made by the laws of 01.03.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force

#### 607.pants. Security for the purchase of immovable property and authorisation of auction participants

(1) A person who wishes to participate in an auction of immovable property shall, within 20 days from the auction start date indicated in the immovable property auction notice, pay security in the amount of 10 percent of the valuation of the immovable property into the bailiff's deposit account indicated in the auction notice and, using the electronic auction website, send a request to the bailiff to authorise them to participate in the auction.

(2) The bailiff shall authorise a person to participate in the auction within five working days from the date of receipt of the security and the person's request, if the restrictions referred to in paragraph three of this Article do not exist. If the security or the request for authorisation has not been received within the time limit specified in paragraph one of this Article or if the person does not have the right to participate in the auction in accordance with paragraph three of this Article, the bailiff shall refuse to authorise the person to participate in the auction.

(3) The debtor, except in an auction held for the execution of a court judgment on the division of joint property, his or her guardian or custodian, a person who has performed the valuation referred to in Article 604 of this Law, as well as the bailiff who conducts the auction, shall not have the right to participate in the auction. The auction participants themselves shall be responsible for compliance with the restrictions set out in other regulatory enactments regarding the acquisition of immovable property.

(4) The security paid by a person who has purchased immovable property at auction shall be set off against the purchase price. The other auction participants shall be immediately returned the security they have paid after the conclusion of the auction. The last outbid bidder shall be returned the security he or she has paid within two working days after the successful bidder has paid the full amount bid. If, after an unsuccessful auction, the immovable property is retained by the last outbid bidder, the security he or she has paid shall be set off against the purchase price.

(As amended by the Law of 28.05.2015 with amendments made by the Laws of 04.02.2016, 25.10.2018 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

607.1 pants. Auction starting price

The auction starts from the forced sale value indicated in the valuation of the immovable property. If there have been two valuations, the auction starts from the highest valuation amount of the immovable property.

(As amended by the Law of 05.02.2009, which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### 608.pants. Procedure for auctioning immovable property

(1) An auction participant may electronically make bids from the moment he or she has been authorised to participate in the auction in accordance with the procedure set out in Article 607 of this Law until the auction has concluded.

(2) Bidding starts from the auction starting price. A bidder may not register a bid that is less than or equal to the auction starting price, differs from the auction step specified in the auction notice, or is less than or equal to previously registered bids. Registered bids may not be revoked or changed.

(3) On the electronic auction website, bids are registered in chronological order, recording the amount bid and the time of registration of the bid. During the auction, this information is available to the bailiff and auction participants. During the auction and after the conclusion of the auction, information about the highest price bid is publicly available on the electronic auction website.

(4) The auction concludes on the thirtieth day from the auction start date indicated in the immovable property auction notice at 13.00, but if the thirtieth day falls on a day off or a public holiday, on the next working day by 13.00. If a bid is registered during the last five minutes before the time set for closing the auction, the auction time is automatically extended by five minutes. If significant technical disruptions are detected during the last hour before the close of the auction that may affect the outcome of the auction and are not related to system security breaches, the auction time is automatically extended until 13.00 on the next working day. After the auction closes, bids are no longer registered and the electronic auction website indicates the date and time of the auction close and the last bid made.

(5) A bailiff may suspend an auction of immovable property in the cases provided for in this Law. A notice of suspension of the auction shall be published on the electronic auction website.

(6) After the conclusion of the auction, a notice is sent electronically to the successful bidder to the electronic auction website user account registered in the Auction Participants Register, stating that he or she has bid a higher price than others and that the obligation to pay the entire amount due from him or her has arisen (Article 611, paragraph two).

(As amended by the Law of 28.05.2015 with amendments made by the Laws of 04.02.2016 and 01.03.2018, which enters into force

#### 609.pants. Double auction

(1) A double auction may be requested by a mortgage creditor if, after the establishment of the mortgage, an encumbrance on the immovable property has been registered in the land register without his or her consent, which may affect the amount of satisfaction of the mortgage creditor, and the auction is held directly for the recovery of his or her claim or for the claim of a mortgage creditor registered earlier in the land register than him or her.

(2) The immovable property shall be sold at auction on the condition that the said encumbrance is to be retained and on the condition that the said encumbrance is to be deleted.

(3) If no one wishes to acquire the immovable property with the retained encumbrance, it remains with the successful bidder on the condition that the encumbrance is to be deleted.

(4) If there are bidders who wish to buy the immovable property both by retaining the encumbrance and by deleting it, the immovable property remains with the successful bidder on the condition of deleting the encumbrance only if the price bid exceeds not only the highest price bid on the condition of retaining the encumbrance, but also the amount of claims that have priority in comparison with the claims of the mortgage creditor who requested the double auction.

(With amendments made by the Law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

#### 610.pants. Auction record

(1) In the auction record, the bailiff shall indicate:

- 1) the date and time of the start and conclusion of the auction;
- 2) the bailiff's name, surname, place of office and place of practice;
- 3) the decision being executed;
- 4) what immovable property is being auctioned and the auction starting price;
- 5) persons authorised to participate in the auction, indicating their name, surname, personal identity number or date of birth (for a person who has not been assigned a personal identity number), contact address indicated in the Auction Participants Register; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;
- 6) the prices bid at the auction and the bidder's name and surname or company (name);
- 7) the highest price bid, the successful bidder's name and surname or name, personal identity number or registration number and address;
- 8) encumbrances, if the immovable property is sold on the condition that they are to be retained.
  - (2) An auction record prepared electronically on the electronic auction website is valid without the bailiff's signature.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002, 05.02.2009, 28.05.2015 and 01.03.2018, which enters into force

#### 611.pants. Consequences of Auction

(1) The real estate remains with the one who promised a higher price than others.

(2) The bidder must pay within one month from the day of the auction closing:

- 1) the entire amount that he/she bid;
- 2) value added tax, if the auction price is subject to value added tax;
- 3) the state fee specified in Point 15 of Part One of Article 34 of this Law for an application for registration of real estate in the name of the acquirer;
- 4) the state and chancellery fee specified in regulatory enactments for registration of property rights in the Land Register.
  - (21) Payment of the full amount shall also be deemed to include a credit institution's demand guarantee letter submitted to the bailiff, indicating the subject of the guarantee, the amount and the term, which may not be shorter than three months from the date of confirmation of the auction deed, if the creditor and the mortgage creditor have consented to the use of such demand guarantee letter. The bailiff shall accept a credit institution's demand guarantee letter for payment if it is accompanied by a request from the credit institution for the establishment of a pledge right on the sold real estate and a pledge agreement between the credit institution and the bidder regarding pledging of the bid real estate, as well as a payment made to the bailiff's deposit account for payment of the state fee for registration of the pledge right in the Land Register. In such case, the bailiff shall indicate in the application for registration of the real estate in the name of the acquirer that, on the basis of the request from the credit institution attached to the application, simultaneously with the registration of the real estate in the name of the acquirer, a mortgage in favour of the credit institution that issued the respective guarantee shall also be registered.
  - (3) After the bidder of the real estate has paid the entire amount due from him/her, the bailiff shall submit the application for registration of the real estate in the name of the acquirer electronically to the district (city) court, using the Court Information System, and request that the property rights be registered in the Land Register in the name of the acquirer.
  - (31) After the bailiff submits to the credit institution the court decision on confirmation of the auction deed, the credit institution shall, within three days, transfer to the bailiff's deposit account the amount indicated in the credit institution's demand guarantee letter.
  - (32) After the time limit for appeal of the calculation compiled by the bailiff has expired and this calculation has not been appealed, or, if this calculation has been appealed, after a court ruling on the compiled calculation has entered into force, the bailiff shall pay the value added tax paid by the bidder to the state budget and notify the debtor and the State Revenue Service thereof.
  - (4) If the bidder does not pay the entire amount due from him/her within the specified time limit, the paid security deposit shall be added to the total amount received for the property and distributed in the same manner as that amount. The paid security deposit shall also be added to the total amount if it is established that the bidder did not have the right to participate in the auction (Part Three of Article 607), as well as if the last outbid bidder has not notified of retaining the real estate for himself/herself for his/her highest bid price or has refused to retain it for himself/herself (Part Two of Article 615).

(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009., 17.12.2009., 20.12.2010., 12.09.2013., 11.09.2014.,

#### 612.pants. Credit of Purchase Price

(1) The bidder is allowed to credit against the purchase amount his/her mortgage claim, which is substantiated by an enforcement document, as well as other mortgage debts, if the mortgage creditors agree to leave them on the real estate by transferring these debts to the bidder.

(2) If the amount received from the sale is insufficient to satisfy all claims and mortgage debts, the bidder may credit against the purchase price his/her claims only in the amount to which he/she is entitled according to the calculation after those claims that have priority over his/her claim have been covered.

(With amendments made by the Law of 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### 613.pants. Confirmation of Real Estate Auction Deed

(1) The court examines the case concerning registration of real estate in the name of the acquirer (person who has taken over the real estate, or the bidder) in written proceedings within 30 days from the submission of the bailiff's application to the court. The court shall notify the bailiff, as well as the creditor, the debtor, the acquirer of the real estate, the owner of the real estate, the mortgage creditor and the person who has submitted the complaint referred to in Part Two of Article 617 of this Law, if such complaint has been submitted, about the examination of the case.

(2) The bailiff shall include in the application information about the enforcement actions performed in the case related to enforcement against the real estate, and certify the payment of court costs specified in Points 3 and 4 of Part Two of Article 611 of this Law for submission of the said application to the court.

(3) When examining the case, the court shall review the data of the Enforcement Case Register. The court is entitled to request additional written explanations and evidence from the persons involved in the case in order to clarify the facts and evidence of the case.

(4) Simultaneously with the application for registration of the real estate in the name of the acquirer, the court may also examine a complaint about the actions of the bailiff if the complainant requests that the auction be declared invalid (Part Two of Article 617).

(5) Upon granting the application, the court shall adopt a decision:

- 1) on confirmation of the auction deed and registration of the sold real estate in the name of the acquirer;
- 2) regardless of the creditor's consent, on deletion of all debt obligations entered in the Land Register on this property, which the acquirer has not directly declared that he/she assumes upon himself/herself;
- 3) regardless of the creditor's consent, on deletion of those encumbrances that have been accepted as a condition for acquiring the property (Article 609);
- 4) on deletion of prohibition notes entered in the Land Register on this property;
- 5) on rejection of the complaint for declaring the auction invalid, if such complaint has been submitted.
  - (6) Upon rejecting the application, the court shall declare the auction invalid.
  - (7) (Deleted by the Law of 11.11.2021.)
  - (8) Upon granting the application for confirmation of the auction deed and registration of the real estate in the name of the acquirer in cases where a credit institution's demand guarantee letter has been used for payment of the purchase amount, the court shall, on the basis of the credit institution's request, simultaneously with the registration of the real estate in the name of the acquirer, also register a mortgage in favour of the credit institution that issued the respective guarantee.
  - (9) The decision by which the auction deed is confirmed or the application for registration of the real estate in the name of the bidder, co-owner or creditor is granted (Part Five of Article 615) shall be prepared by the court in the form of a resolution, except in cases where a complaint for declaring the auction invalid has been submitted in the case.
  - (10) An ancillary complaint may be submitted to the regional court regarding the court decision.
  - (11) After a court decision by which the application for registration of the real estate in the name of the acquirer is granted has entered into force, the bailiff shall pay the state and chancellery fee referred to in Point 4 of Part Two of Article 611 of this Law or Point 2 of Part Four of Article 615, as specified in regulatory enactments for registration of property rights in the Land Register, to the state budget and notify the acquirer and the respective district (city) court thereof.
  - (12) In the procedure specified in this Article, insofar as it relates to the adoption of a decision on confirmation of the auction deed, the district (city) court shall also confirm the ship auction deed.

(In the wording of the Law of 11.09.2014. with amendments made by the Laws of 01.06.2017., 25.10.2018., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)


This excerpt sits under: Izdevējs: Saeima Publicēts: > C daļa > 60. nodaļa

#### 614.pants. Auction That Did Not Take Place

(1) The bailiff recognizes the auction as not having taken place if:

- 1) no auction participant has been authorized for the auction;
- 2) none of the participants authorized for the auction exceeds the starting price;
- 3) the highest bidder does not pay the full amount due from them within the specified period (Article 611, paragraph two);
- 4) during the auction, except for the case referred to in Article 608, paragraph four of this Law, or within 24 hours after the conclusion of the auction, a notification has been received from the electronic auction site security administrator about significant technical disruptions that may affect the auction result.
  - (2) Regarding the fact that the auction is considered not to have taken place in the cases referred to in points 1 or 2 of paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff draws up an act and notifies the debtor and the owner of the immovable property. The notification is sent to participants authorized to participate in the auction using the electronic auction site.
  - (3) Regarding the fact that the auction is considered not to have taken place in the case referred to in point 3 of paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff draws up an act and notifies the highest bidder, the debtor and the owner of the immovable property.
  - (4) Having received the notification referred to in point 4 of paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff suspends the auction and posts a notification about it on the electronic auction site during the auction.
  - (5) Regarding the fact that the auction is considered not to have taken place in the case referred to in point 4 of paragraph one of this Article, the bailiff draws up an act and notifies the claimant, the debtor and the owner of the immovable property. The notification is sent to participants authorized to participate in the auction using the electronic auction site.

(In the wording of the Law of 28.05.2015 with amendments made by the Law of 04.02.2016, which came into force on 29.02.2016.)

#### 615.pants. Consequences of an Auction That Did Not Take Place

(1) If the auction is recognized as not having taken place due to the reason provided in points 1 or 2 of paragraph one of Article 614 of this Law, the bailiff immediately notifies all creditors and co-owners, as well as building rights holders, inviting them to retain the immovable property for themselves for the starting price of the auction that did not take place. Each creditor and co-owner, as well as building rights holder, has the right within two weeks from the date of sending the bailiff's invitation to notify the bailiff of retaining the immovable property for themselves.

(2) If the auction is recognized as not having taken place due to the reason provided in point 3 of paragraph one of Article 614, the bailiff immediately notifies the last outbid bidder, inviting them to retain the immovable property for the highest price they bid. The last outbid bidder has the right within two weeks from the date of sending the bailiff's invitation to notify the bailiff of retaining the immovable property for themselves. If the last outbid bidder has not notified of retaining the immovable property within the period specified by law or has refused to retain the immovable property for themselves, the bailiff immediately announces a repeat auction.

(21) If the auction is recognized as not having taken place due to the reason provided in point 4 of paragraph one of Article 614, the bailiff immediately announces a repeat auction.

(3) If several persons wish to retain the immovable property for themselves, an auction shall be held in which these persons participate, and bidding starts from the starting price of the auction that did not take place. The bailiff notifies in writing the persons who wish to retain the immovable property for themselves of the auction time and place seven days in advance. Non-appearance of a person at the auction is considered a waiver of the right to participate in bidding. If one person appears at the auction, they may retain the immovable property for themselves for the starting price of the held auction. If no one appears at the auction, the bailiff immediately announces a second auction.

(31) A person subject to sanctions cannot retain the immovable property if the acquisition of the property is not compatible with the restrictions imposed on them by sanctions.

(4) A person who retains the immovable property for themselves pays into the bailiff's deposit account within one month:

- 1) the state fee specified in point 15 of paragraph one of Article 34 of this Law for an application for registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer;
- 2) state and chancellery fees as specified in regulatory enactments for registration of property rights in the land register;
- 3) the amount specified in paragraph one, two or three of this Article;
- 4) value added tax, if the auction price is subject to value added tax, in accordance with the calculation prepared by the bailiff (Article 631, paragraph three) and taking into account the provisions of Article 612 of this Law.
  - (5) After payment of the amount referred to in paragraph four of this Article, the bailiff electronically submits to the district (city) court, using the Court Information System, an application for registration of the immovable property in the name of the highest bidder, co-owner, building rights holder or creditor and for deletion of debts recorded in the land register (Article 613) and requests to register the property rights in the land register.
  - (6) If no one has applied to retain the immovable property for themselves, a second auction shall be held.

(In the wording of the Law of 05.02.2009 with amendments made by the laws of 17.12.2009., 20.12.2010., 08.09.2011., 12.09.2013.,

#### 616.pants. Second Auction

(1) The second auction is announced and held in accordance with the rules of the first auction. However, bidding for the immovable property starts from an amount equal to 75 percent of the starting price at the first auction.

(2) (Deleted by the Law of 17.12.2009)

(3) If the second auction did not take place due to the reasons provided in points 1 and 2 of paragraph one of Article 614 of this Law and no one wished to retain the immovable property for themselves, the immovable property remains in the ownership of the previous owner and the enforcement note in the land register shall be deleted. If the second auction did not take place due to the reason provided in point 3 of paragraph one of Article 614 and the last outbid bidder has not notified of retaining the immovable property in the procedure specified in paragraph two of Article 615 of this Law or has refused to retain the immovable property for themselves, or if the second auction is recognized as not having taken place due to the reason provided in point 4 of paragraph one of Article 614, the bailiff immediately announces a repeat second auction.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 17.12.2009. and 25.10.2018., which came into force on 28.11.2018.)

#### 617.pants. Invalid Auction

(1) The court recognizes the auction as invalid if:

- 1) someone was unlawfully not allowed to participate in the auction or some bid was incorrectly rejected;
- 2) the immovable property was purchased by a person who was not entitled to participate in the auction;
- 3) (deleted by the Law of 28.05.2015);
- 4) (deleted by the Law of 05.02.2009);
- 5) the claimant or bidder acted in bad faith;
- 6) in enforcing execution on the immovable property, the bailiff committed significant procedural violations or other significant circumstances have been identified that do not allow the registration of the immovable property in the name of the buyer.
  - (2) A complaint regarding the bailiff's actions that give grounds to request recognition of the auction as invalid may be submitted by interested persons to the district (city) court within 10 days from the date of conclusion of the auction.
  - (3) An appeal may be submitted against the court's decision.
  - (4) If the auction of immovable property is recognized as invalid, a repeat auction shall be held according to the rules of the auction that was recognized as invalid.
  - (5) (Deleted by the Law of 05.02.2009.)

(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 11.09.2014., 28.05.2015., 01.06.2017. and 25.10.2018., which came into force on 28.11.2018. The amendment in paragraph two to replace the words "land register department of the district (city) court" with the words "district (city) court" comes into force on 01.06.2019. See transitional provision point 151)

#### 618.pants. Sale of Real Property in Joint Ownership

(1) When enforcing recovery from one or more owners of undivided real property, this property shall be described in its entirety, but only the debtor's right to his share shall be sold at auction, without separating it beforehand.

(2) Real properties in joint ownership may also be sold in their entirety if all co-owners so wish and if the creditors do not raise objections thereto. The money obtained from the sale shall be divided among the owners of the real property, but the sum due to the debtor shall be used to discharge the debt.

618.1 pants. Procedure for Enforcement of Confiscation of Real Property

(1) The bailiff shall sell the confiscated real property specified in the writ of execution and in the extract of the protocol or decision attached thereto on the attachment of property in the procedure laid down in this chapter.

(2) A person whose confiscation of real property is being enforced does not have the rights of a debtor provided for in this law.

(3) If the auction is declared unsuccessful, the right to retain the real property in the procedure laid down in this chapter shall belong to the last outbid bidder, the debtor's co-owner, and the creditor in the enforcement case for recovery from the person whose real property is being confiscated. If the second auction has not taken place and no one has wished to retain the real property, the bailiff shall send a notice to the State Revenue Service transferring the real property to its disposal.

(22.06.2017. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.08.2017.)

### 73. nodaļa

Enforcement of Recovery on Right of Superficies

(Nodaļa 01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.07.2018.)

618.2 pants. Notice of Enforcement of Recovery on Right of Superficies

(1) If the creditor has requested enforcement of recovery on the right of superficies, the bailiff shall send a notice to the debtor and invite him to settle the debt, as well as provide information on whether the debtor is registered as a value added tax payer, whether, when selling his right of superficies at auction, the auction price is subject to value added tax and what is the taxable value of this price. When executing decisions that provide for the voluntary sale of the right of superficies at auction through the court or the sale of the right of superficies at forced auction, the notice shall not include an invitation to the debtor to settle the debt.

(2) The bailiff shall submit to the district (city) court a request for registration to enter a recovery note. The consequences of this note are specified in the first paragraph of Section 1077, Sections 1081 and 1305 of the Civil Law, as well as in Section

46 of the Land Register Law. The recovery note shall also be entered when executing decisions that provide for the voluntary sale of the right of superficies at auction through the court or the sale of the right of superficies at forced auction.

(3) The bailiff, in accordance with the relevant land register section, shall send a notice to the owner of the land plot, to the holders of the right of superficies who own an ideal share of the right of superficies, as well as to all mortgage creditors, including persons in whose favour a pledge right or prohibition note has been entered in respect of the right of superficies, indicating:

- 1) for the satisfaction of which person's claim the recovery is being enforced on the right of superficies;
- 2) what is the amount of the debt and whether the debt is secured by a mortgage on the relevant right of superficies.
  - (4) In the notice referred to in the third paragraph of this Section, the bailiff shall require that the mortgage creditors submit information on the amount of the outstanding mortgage debt within the time limit set by the bailiff, which shall not be less than 10 days.
  - (5) The bailiff shall request from the municipality information on the real property tax debt and invite the municipality to submit a decision on the recovery of the tax debt, if any.
  - (6) The bailiff shall request from the relevant land register section a copy of the superficies contract and other documents certifying registration, if any.
  - (7) If the necessary information for the evaluation of the right of superficies regarding the construction process initiated on the basis of the right of superficies is not available in the databases of state information systems, the bailiff, specifically indicating the necessary documents, shall request them from the construction board or institution that performs the functions of the construction board, unless the necessary information or the original document is available in another state or municipal institution. A certified real property appraiser shall be entitled, at the request of the bailiff, to familiarise himself with the information available to state or municipal institutions for the evaluation of the right of superficies.
  - (8) If the debtor has paid the debt and the costs of execution of the judgment in full to the bailiff no later than seven days before the auction closing date indicated in the auction announcement, the sale of the right of superficies shall be cancelled and the auction already commenced shall be suspended. This shall not apply when executing decisions that provide for the sale of the right of superficies at forced auction.

(01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 25.10.2018. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā

618.3 pants. Debtor's Obligations

(1) From the day of receipt of the bailiff's notice, the debtor is prohibited from:

- 1) alienating the right of superficies or pledging it;
- 2) alienating or damaging the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on the basis of the right of superficies or its accessories;
- 3) concluding lease and other contracts that reduce or may reduce the value of the right of superficies or the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on its basis.
  - (2) Contracts concluded by the debtor in contravention of the prohibitions laid down in the first paragraph of this Section after a recovery note has been made in the land register shall not be valid in respect of the creditor and the buyer of the right of superficies at auction.
  - (3) The debtor has an obligation to notify within the time limit set by the bailiff who is the actual possessor or manager of the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on the basis of the right of superficies, if any, as well as regarding all concluded lease and other contracts relating to the right of superficies or the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on its basis, to submit copies of these contracts and to produce their originals.
  - (4) The debtor has an obligation to notify the bailiff whether he is registered as a value added tax payer and whether, when selling his right of superficies at auction, the auction price is subject to value added tax. If the auction price is subject to value added tax in accordance with the regulatory enactments regulating value added tax, the debtor shall indicate the taxable value of this price in the said information.

(01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.07.2018.)

618.4 pants. Description and Management of Non-Residential Building (Engineering Structure) Erected on the Basis of Right of Superficies

The bailiff shall describe the non-residential building (engineering structure) erected on the basis of the right of superficies at the request of the creditor in the procedure laid down in Section 603 of this law. The management of the described non-residential building (engineering structure) shall be ensured in accordance with Section 605 of this law.

(01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.07.2018.)

618.5 pants. Evaluation of Right of Superficies

The right of superficies shall be evaluated by a certified real property appraiser at the expense of the debtor upon the request of the bailiff, determining the forced sale value of the right of superficies. The evaluation shall be announced, as well as the right to request a re-evaluation and the procedure by which a re-evaluation is carried out shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Section 604 of this law.

(01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.07.2018.)

618.6 pants. Sale of Right of Superficies

(1) The auction of the right of superficies, confirmation of the auction deed and registration of the right of superficies in the name of the acquirer shall take place in accordance with the provisions provided for the auction of real property. The bailiff shall also send the notice of the auction to the owner of the land plot.

(2) In the case of an unsuccessful auction, in addition to the persons referred to in Section 615 of this law, if they are not debtors, the right to retain the right of superficies shall also belong to the owner of the land plot.

(01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

### 74. nodaļa

Compulsory transfer of property awarded by court and performance of actions imposed by court decision

(Chapter title in the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force 20.04.2021.)

#### 619.pants. Transfer of objects specified in court judgment to the claimant

(1) If specific objects specified in a court judgment have been awarded to the claimant, the bailiff notifies the debtor of the obligation to execute the judgment in the manner specified in Article 555 of this Law. In the notice, the bailiff also indicates the date when the compulsory enforcement of the court judgment will be carried out if it is not executed. If the court judgment is to be executed immediately, the bailiff does not give the debtor a time limit for execution of the court judgment in the notice, but indicates the date and time when the compulsory enforcement of the court judgment will be carried out.

(2) During the time of compulsory execution of the judgment set by the bailiff, at the bailiff's request, the debtor has the obligation to present the objects specified in the writ of execution to be transferred to the claimant. Upon transfer of objects, the debtor and the claimant have the right to invite no more than two witnesses. The non-appearance of witnesses does not suspend the execution of the judgment.

(3) If during the time of compulsory execution of the court judgment the debtor does not present the objects specified in the judgment to be transferred to the claimant, refuses to disclose their location, and after inspection of the premises the objects are not found, the bailiff draws up a report thereon, which is signed by the bailiff, the claimant and the witnesses, if any have participated. After a report on the absence of property to be transferred to the claimant has been drawn up, the bailiff carries out compulsory enforcement actions for the recovery of the amount specified in the court judgment (Article 196) in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the law of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force

#### 620. pants.

Consequences arising from failure to execute a decision imposing an obligation on the debtor to perform specific actions

(1) If a decision imposing an obligation on the debtor to perform specific actions not related to the transfer of property or a sum of money is not executed, the bailiff draws up a report on the non-execution of the decision.

(2) If the decision specifies the consequences of non-execution of the decision provided for in the second part of Article 197 of this Law, the drawn-up report is sent to the district (city) court according to the place of execution, so that it may adopt a decision on the application of the consequences specified in the decision in connection with the debtor's failure to perform specific actions.

(3) If the consequences of non-execution are not specified in the decision, the drawn-up report is sent to the court which made the decision in the case, and this court decides the question of the procedure for execution of the decision in accordance with the provisions of Articles 206 and 438 of this Law.

(4) If a decision imposing an obligation on the debtor to perform actions which can be performed only by the debtor himself (first part of Article 197) is not executed within the time limit set by the court, the bailiff sends the drawn-up report to the court according to the bailiff's place of office. The question of non-execution of the decision is decided in a court session. The claimant and the debtor are notified of the time and place of the session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to considering the question of non-execution of the decision. If the debtor does not execute, within the time limit set by the court, a decision imposing an obligation on him to perform actions which can be performed only by himself, the court may impose a fine of up to 3000 euros on the debtor, setting a new time limit for execution of the decision. The fine is to be recovered from the debtor into state revenues. Payment of the fine does not release the debtor from the obligation to perform the actions provided for in the court decision.

(5) If the debtor continues to fail to execute the decision after the imposition of a fine, the sworn bailiff sends an application to the prosecutor for the initiation of criminal proceedings.

(6) If an employer does not execute a court decision on the reinstatement to work of an unlawfully dismissed or transferred employee, the court, at the request of the employee, adopts a decision on wages for the entire period from the date of making the decision until the date of its execution.

(7) An ancillary complaint may be filed against the court's decision.

(With amendments made by the law of 12.09.2013, 09.06.2016, 31.05.2018 and 25.03.2021, which enters into force

### 74. nodaļa

Eviction of Persons and Property from Premises

(Chapter in the version of the law of 31.10.2002., which comes into force on 01.01.2003.)

620.1 pants. Notice of Obligation to Execute Decision

(1) The bailiff shall deliver the notice of the obligation to execute the court decision and to vacate the premises together with family members and other resident persons to the debtor in the procedure prescribed in Section 555 of this law.

(2) In the notice, the bailiff shall also indicate the date on which the forced execution of the decision will take place if the debtor does not execute it.

(In the version of the law of 25.03.2021., which comes into force on 20.04.2021.)

620.1A pants. Protection of Third Party Rights in Forced Eviction

Forced eviction does not affect the rights of other persons to use the premises if the rights to use the premises arise from an entry in the land register.

(In the version of the law of 25.03.2021., which comes into force on 20.04.2021.)

620.2 pants. Eviction in the Debtor's Presence

(1) During forced eviction, the creditor and the debtor have the right to invite no more than two witnesses each. The bailiff shall verify the identity of the witnesses and indicate these persons in the record. The non-appearance of witnesses does not stop the forced execution.

(2) The bailiff shall call upon the debtor to clear the premises specified in the court decision of property and to vacate these premises together with family members and other resident persons.

(3) If the debtor does not comply with the bailiff's invitation, all persons present in the premises shall be evicted, but the bailiff shall describe and evaluate the property in accordance with the provisions of Sections 577 and 578 of this law, as well as appoint a custodian of the property.

(4) The bailiff shall issue one copy of the record to the debtor.

(5) After execution of the decision, the premises shall be handed over to the creditor.

(6) If perishable items have been inventoried, the bailiff shall sell them in accordance with the provisions of the second part of Section 581 of this law. The money received shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus money shall be paid to the debtor.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018. and 25.03.2021., which comes into force on 20.04.2021.)

620.3 pants. Eviction in the Debtor's Absence

(1) If the debtor does not appear at the time set for the eviction and there is no information about the reason for his non-appearance or he has not appeared for a justified reason, the bailiff shall postpone the eviction.

(2) If the debtor has not appeared at the time repeatedly set for the eviction and has not reported the reason for non-appearance or has not appeared for such a reason that the bailiff does not recognize as justified, the premises shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. The bailiff shall make a note in the record about the forced opening of the premises.

(3) The eviction shall be carried out in the procedure prescribed in Section 620.2 of this law.

(4) The debtor is entitled to receive one copy of the property inventory record.

620.4 pants. Dealing with the Debtor's Property

(1) The debtor has the right to receive the property placed in custody within a month by paying the costs of execution of the judgment.

(2) If the debtor refuses to pay the costs of execution of the judgment, the bailiff shall seize the debtor's property in such value as is necessary to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but shall hand over the remaining property to the debtor.

(3) The bailiff shall sell the seized property in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this law.

(4) The money received from the sale of the property shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus money shall be paid to the debtor. The bailiff shall notify the debtor about the sale of the property if he has information about the debtor's official electronic address, e-mail address or place of residence.

(5) If the debtor does not appear within a month to receive the property placed in custody, the bailiff shall sell it in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this law.

(6) Property that has no market value or that cannot be sold and which the debtor has not appeared to receive within the time and procedure specified in the first part of this section, the bailiff shall destroy in the presence of witnesses, drawing up a record thereof.

(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 25.03.2021., which comes into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 74. nodaļa

Introduction into Possession of Immovable Property

(Chapter in the version of the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

620.5 pants. Notice of Obligation to Execute Decision

(1) The notice of obligation to execute the court decision, together with family members and other persons to vacate the immovable property and transfer it to the acquirer, shall be sent by the bailiff to the debtor in the manner prescribed in Section 555 of this Law.

(2) In the notice, the bailiff shall also indicate the date on which the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property will take place if the debtor fails to fulfil the obligation.

(3) Introduction into possession shall also take place if the acquirer has not yet registered the property rights in the Land Register.

(4) If introduction into possession of immovable property is to be carried out which the bailiff has alienated as heirless property, the bailiff shall prepare a notice about the date and time of introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property and issue it to the person encountered in the immovable property. If no adult person is encountered in the immovable property, the bailiff shall leave the notice at the relevant immovable property.

(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

620.6 pants. Introduction into Possession of Immovable Property in the Presence of the Debtor

(1) The bailiff shall perform the introduction into possession of immovable property in the presence of the acquirer of the immovable property and the debtor or another adult person living with them in the immovable property. These persons have the right to each invite no more than two witnesses. The bailiff shall verify the identity of the witnesses and indicate these persons in the record. Failure of witnesses to appear shall not suspend the enforcement.

(2) The bailiff shall invite the debtor to vacate the immovable property from the property belonging to them and leave the immovable property together with family members and other persons.

(3) If the bailiff's invitation is not complied with, all persons in the premises shall be evicted, and the bailiff shall describe and evaluate the property in accordance with the provisions of Sections 577 and 578 of this Law, and also appoint a custodian of the property, remove the property and transfer it to the custody of the property custodian according to the inventory record. Movable things belonging to the immovable property shall not be included in this inventory record and shall not be removed. Introduction into possession shall not affect the rights of other persons to use the premises if the rights to use the premises arise from registration in the Land Register.

(4) The bailiff shall issue one copy of the record to the debtor or to the person in whose presence the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property was performed.

(5) At the request of the debtor or acquirer, the bailiff shall prepare a separate record regarding the immovable property to be transferred to the acquirer, which indicates the condition of the immovable property and the movable things belonging to it that are transferred to the acquirer.

(6) If items that quickly deteriorate have been described and removed, the bailiff shall sell them in accordance with the provisions of the second part of Section 581 of this Law. The money received shall be credited to cover the costs of enforcement of the judgment, and any surplus of money shall be payable to the debtor.

(In the version of the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

620.7 pants. Introduction into Possession of Immovable Property in the Absence of the Debtor

(1) If at the time set for introduction into possession of the immovable property neither the debtor nor any of the other adult persons living with the debtor in the immovable property appears and there is no information about the reason for their non-appearance, or they have not appeared due to a justified reason, the bailiff shall postpone the introduction into possession.

(2) If neither the debtor nor any of the other adult persons living with the debtor in the immovable property appears at the time repeatedly set for introduction into possession of the immovable property and there is no information about the reason for their non-appearance, or they have not appeared for a reason which the bailiff does not recognize as justified, the premises shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. The bailiff shall make a note in the record about the forced opening of the premises.

(3) Introduction into possession of the immovable property shall be performed in accordance with the provisions of Section 620.6 of this Law.

(4) The debtor is entitled to receive one copy of the property inventory record.

(5) Introduction into possession of immovable property that the bailiff has alienated as heirless property shall be performed in the presence of a police representative and the acquirer of the immovable property. If persons are encountered in the immovable property, the bailiff shall act in the manner prescribed in Section 620.6 of this Law.

(In the version of the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

620.8 pants. Disputes and Complaints in Connection with Introduction into Possession of Immovable Property

(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

620.9 pants. Handling of Property Deposited in Custody

(1) The debtor has the right to receive the property deposited in custody within one month by paying the costs of enforcement of the judgment.

(2) If the debtor refuses to pay the costs of enforcement of the judgment, the bailiff shall seize the debtor's property in such value as is necessary to cover the costs of enforcement of the judgment, and transfer the remaining property to the debtor.

(3) The bailiff shall sell the seized property in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this Law.

(4) The money received from the sale of the property shall be credited to cover the costs of enforcement of the judgment, and any surplus of money shall be payable to the debtor. The bailiff shall notify the debtor of the sale of the property if they have information about the debtor's official electronic address, email address or place of residence.

(5) If the debtor does not appear to receive the property deposited in custody within one month, the bailiff shall sell it in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this Law.

(6) Property that has no market value or that cannot be sold and which the debtor has not appeared to receive within the term and in the manner specified in paragraph (1) of this Section, the bailiff shall destroy in the presence of witnesses, preparing a record thereof.

(7) Property that has been described in the immovable property that has been alienated as heirless property and that has no market value, the bailiff shall destroy in the presence of witnesses, preparing a record thereof, and the bailiff shall send the property inventory record in the part concerning property that has market value to the notary who prepared the notarial deed on termination of the inheritance matter, for making an amendment therein.

(In the version of the law of 08.09.2011. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 74. nodaļa

Return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence

(Chapter in the wording of the Law of 04.08.2011., which enters into force on 01.10.2011.)

620.10 pants. Costs of enforcement of the decision and procedure for their payment

(1) The creditor, when submitting an enforcement document for enforcement, pays the state fee and covers the costs of enforcement of the decision in accordance with the first part of Section 567 of this Law.

(2) The creditor who does not participate in the enforcement of the decision, at the request of the bailiff, in addition to the costs of enforcement of the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this Section, pays a sum of money to cover the costs related to the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence (including costs related to the child's stay in a crisis centre or other safe conditions, travel costs, costs for interpreter and psychologist services and other costs). The amount of these costs and the procedure for payment shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(3) After the child has been handed over to the representative of the orphan's court, the bailiff shall immediately transfer the costs referred to in the second paragraph of this Section to the account specified by the orphan's court.

(4) When issuing the enforcement document to the creditor (Points 7 and 8 of the first part of Section 565 and the third part of Section 620.13), the bailiff or the orphan's court shall reimburse the creditor for the costs referred to in the second paragraph of this Section that have not been used for the enforcement of the decision.

(5) The costs of enforcement of the decision shall be recovered by the bailiff from the debtor.

(With amendments made by the Law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

620.10A pants. Time limit within which an enforcement document must be submitted for enforcement

An enforcement document concerning the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence, including the relevant European Union enforcement document, may be submitted for enforcement within one year from the date of entry into force of the court or foreign court decision.

(In the wording of the Law of 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.11 pants. Notice of the obligation to enforce the decision

(1) The bailiff, when commencing enforcement in the procedure established in Section 555 of this Law, shall notify the debtor of the obligation to enforce the decision within 10 days. If the creditor submits the enforcement document for enforcement repeatedly after the bailiff has issued it to him or her in accordance with the third part of Section 620.13 of this Law, no notice shall be sent.

(2) Upon receiving a European Union enforcement document for enforcement, which does not specify a time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision, the bailiff shall send a notice to the debtor in the procedure established in Section 555 of this Law regarding the obligation to enforce the decision within 30 days. In the notice, the bailiff shall warn the debtor of the consequences provided for in this Chapter that will occur if the decision is not enforced.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 29.10.2015. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.12 pants. Consequences arising if the debtor does not enforce the decision voluntarily

(1) The bailiff shall send information that the debtor has not enforced the decision voluntarily to:

- 1) the district (city) court that has adopted the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence — upon receiving the said decision for enforcement;
- 2) the district (city) court in whose territorial jurisdiction a foreign court decision is to be enforced — after the expiry of the time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision specified in the enforcement document or in accordance with Section 620.11 of this Law.
  - (2) The court, after receiving the information referred to in the first paragraph of this Section, shall impose a fine of 750 euros on the debtor.
  - (3) The matter of imposing the fine shall be considered in written proceedings.
  - (4) The court decision on the imposition of the fine shall be sent to the debtor.
  - (5) An appeal may be submitted against the court decision on the imposition of the fine.
  - (6) The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues.
  - (7) Payment of the fine does not release the debtor from the obligation to enforce the decision.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.09.2013., 09.06.2016., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on

620.13 pants. Ascertaining the child's daily routine

(1) Simultaneously with the sending of the information referred to in the first paragraph of Section 620.12 of this Law, the bailiff, if necessary for the enforcement of the decision, shall issue an order to the orphan's court at the place where the child is located to ascertain the child's daily routine within 15 days from the date of receipt of the order and to inform the bailiff thereof.

(2) The orphan's court shall immediately inform the bailiff of the information relating to the child and the child's location that it has obtained in the execution of the order specified in the first paragraph of this Section. If it is not possible to obtain the said information, the orphan's court shall inform the bailiff thereof.
