### 77. nodaļa

Cases concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 07.09.2006, which enters into force on 11.10.2006.)

644.13 pants. Procedure for examination of cases

Cases concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia, if the child's place of residence is in another country, shall be examined in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, observing the general provisions of this law. 644.14 pants. Jurisdiction over cases

(1) Cases concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia, if the child's place of residence is in another country, shall be examined in Riga City Court.

(2) (Deleted by the law of 30.10.2014)

(3) If in a case concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia the parties conclude a settlement, Riga City Court has jurisdiction to approve the said settlement also in the part concerning custody and access rights.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 30.10.2014, 14.12.2017, 16.06.2022 and 16.06.2022, which enter into force on 01.08.2022.)

644.15 pants. Application for the return of a child to the country of his or her residence

(1) In order to ensure the return of a child unlawfully removed to Latvia or retained in Latvia to the country of his or her residence, a person whose rights to exercise custody or guardianship have been infringed may submit to the court an application for the return of the child to the country of his or her residence, if the country in question is a contracting state to the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction or the Hague Convention of 19 October 1996 on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition, Enforcement and Co-operation in Respect of Parental Responsibility and Measures for the Protection of Children.

(2) The application referred to in paragraph one of this Article may also be submitted to the court by the competent authorities in order to apply the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, the Hague Convention of 19 October 1996 on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition, Enforcement and Co-operation in Respect of Parental Responsibility and Measures for the Protection of Children or Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.

(3) The application shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court to which the application has been submitted;
- 2) the applicant's name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none — other identification data), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there are none — place of residence or information about his or her whereabouts, as well as an address in Latvia for communication with the court in order to receive court documents. If the applicant agrees to electronic communication with the court, an e-mail address shall also be indicated and, if he or she has registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of the registration;
- 3) the name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none, other identification data) of the unlawfully removed or retained child and other information about the child, as well as information about the child's possible whereabouts and the identity of the person with whom the child may be;
- 4) the respondent's name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none, other identification data), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, as well as place of residence, if it differs from the declared place of residence and the additional address indicated in the declaration or information about his or her whereabouts;
- 5) circumstances confirming the custody or guardianship rights of the person concerned in respect of the child;
- 6) circumstances confirming the fact of unlawful removal or retention of the child and the civil aspects;
- 7) the applicant's request;
- 71) whether the applicant or his or her representative will participate in the voluntary enforcement of the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her residence in the territory of Latvia;
- 72) the applicant's opinion on the possibility of using mediation to resolve the issue of the return or non-return of the child to the country of his or her residence;
- 73) whether an action has been brought before a foreign court to examine a case concerning custody rights on the merits, and the name and address of such foreign court;
- 8) a list of attached documents;
- 9) the time of preparation of the application.
  - (4) The application shall be accompanied by:
- 1) the documents on which it is based;
- 2) information certified by the competent authorities of the foreign country concerned on the legal regulation in the country of the child's residence;
- 3) a translation into the official language of the application and of the documents referred to in points 1 and 2 of this paragraph, certified in the prescribed manner.
  - (5) The application shall be signed by the applicant or his or her representative. If the application is submitted by the applicant's representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the authority to apply to the court with this application shall be attached to the application. If the address of the applicant's representative is outside Latvia, an e-mail address shall additionally be indicated or notification shall be given of the registration of his or her participation in the online system.
  - (6) An unsigned application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.
  - (7) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application if it is not accompanied by a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to apply to the court with this application. The decision is not subject to appeal.

(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 29.11.2012, 23.04.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enter into force on 07.07.2022. The amendment to paragraph two and points 7.2 and 7.3 of paragraph three enter into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision point 177)

644.16 pants. Leaving the application without progress

(1) If the application does not comply with the requirements of paragraphs one, two, three and four of Article 644.15 of this law or if the power of attorney or other document attached to the application does not show the representative's authority to apply to the court with this application, the court shall leave the application without progress only if the absence of documents or necessary information significantly affects the possibility of examining the application.

(2) If the court leaves the application without progress in accordance with paragraph one of this Article, the consequences provided for in Article 133 of this law shall occur.

(With amendments made by the law of 23.04.2015, which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

644.17 pants. Search for the respondent and child

(1) If the place of residence or whereabouts of the respondent or of a child unlawfully removed to Latvia or retained in Latvia is not known, but there is reason to believe that the child is in Latvia, the judge, upon receipt of the application referred to in Article 644.15 of this law, shall adopt a decision to search for the respondent or child with the assistance of the police.

(2) The court shall suspend proceedings if a decision has been adopted to search for the respondent or child with the assistance of the police.

(3) Proceedings shall be suspended until the respondent or child is found.

(In the wording of the law of 04.08.2011, which enters into force on 01.10.2011.)

644.18 pants. Action of the court after institution of the case

(1) The court shall notify the Ministry of Justice of the institution of the case. The Ministry of Justice shall inform the competent authority of the country of the child's residence thereof in order to apply the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, the Hague Convention of 19 October 1996 on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition, Enforcement and Co-operation in Respect of Parental Responsibility and Measures for the Protection of Children, Council Regulation No 2201/2003 or Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.

(2) If the application is based on a decision adopted by the competent authority of the foreign country concerned on the return of the child, the court may additionally also directly inform the competent authority of the foreign country concerned that adopted the decision on the return of the child to the country in question.

(3) Court documents and court summons shall be sent to the respondent in the manner provided for in Article 56 of this law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.06.2009, 29.11.2012, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enter into force on 07.07.2022. The amendment to paragraph one enters into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision point 177)

644.18A pants. Interim decision

(1) The court, at the request of a party or on its own initiative, shall adopt an interim decision prohibiting the removal of the child from the country until the adoption of a decision in a case concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia. The court shall immediately after its adoption send the decision to the State Police and the State Border Guard to the e-mail addresses indicated by them.

(11) The court, at the request of a party, may adopt an interim decision to ensure contact between the child and the applicant until the adoption of a decision in a case concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia, if it is in the interests of the child.

(2) The request for an interim decision shall be examined in written proceedings and the decision shall be adopted in the form of a resolution within one working day from the date of receipt of the request. The court decision is not subject to appeal.

(21) If the court considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances for the resolution of the request for contact, the court shall resolve the request for contact no later than at the court hearing examining the case concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia

(3) The interim decision shall cease to have effect when it is revoked or when a decision on the return or non-return of the child to the country of his or her residence or a decision terminating proceedings in the case enters into force in the case concerning the unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia. In this decision, the court may provide that the prohibition on the removal of the child from the country, except for removal to the country of the child's permanent residence, shall remain in force even after the entry into force of the decision on the return or non-return of the child to the country of his or her residence or the decision terminating proceedings in the case, but for no longer than until the enforcement of the decision.

(4) In exceptional cases, if circumstances have significantly changed and it is in the interests of the child, a party may, after the adoption of an interim decision, request the court to revoke the interim decision. If the court does not find grounds for revoking the interim decision, it shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application. The court shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application in the form of a resolution, and it is not subject to appeal.

(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021 with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

644.19 pants. Examination of the application

(1) The application shall be examined at a court hearing within 15 days after the institution of the case, with the participation of the parties. A representative of the orphan's court shall be invited to participate in the court hearing, and the child's opinion shall also be ascertained if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity. The orphan's court shall have the rights of a participant in the case as provided for in paragraph two of Article 88 of this law.

(2) If the respondent fails to appear following the court's invitation without justifiable reason, he or she may be brought to court by force.

(3) If one of the parties lives far away or for another reason cannot appear following the court's invitation, the court may consider that written explanations from this party or the participation of its representative are sufficient for the examination of the case.

(4) When examining the application, the court shall, on its own initiative, request evidence, using the most appropriate procedural possibilities, as well as the fastest means of obtaining evidence.

(5) If the court finds that the child is in a foreign country, it may adopt a decision to leave the application without examination.

(6) If the court finds that the child has been unlawfully removed to Latvia or retained in Latvia, it shall adopt a decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her residence.

(7) The court shall adopt a decision on the return or non-return of the child to the country of his or her residence, applying the provisions of the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, Council Regulation No 2201/2003 or Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.

(8) During the examination of the case, the court shall attempt to reconcile the parties, and shall also propose to resolve the dispute using mediation, if the court considers that in the particular case it is possible to resolve the dispute using mediation. The court shall also ascertain whether an action has been brought before a foreign court to examine a case concerning custody rights on the merits, and the opinion of the participants in the case on the measures for voluntary enforcement of a possible decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her residence.

(9) When adopting a decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her residence, the court shall indicate the time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision and, if possible, the procedure for voluntary enforcement of the decision. The time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision shall be set not longer than 30 days from the date of entry into force of the decision. In the decision, the court shall warn the respondent that if the decision is not enforced voluntarily, a fine will be imposed and forced enforcement will be carried out in the manner prescribed by this law, and the issue of initiating criminal proceedings may also be resolved.

(10) In the decision, the court shall impose on the respondent the obligation to immediately notify the Ministry of Justice if he or she changes his or her place of residence or whereabouts before the enforcement of the decision or if the child's whereabouts are changed.

(11) The court, at the request of a party or on its own initiative, in a decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her residence, on the basis of Article 27(5) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, may include provisional measures. (In the wording of the law of 04.08.2011 with amendments made by the laws of 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enter into force on 07.07.2022. The amendments to paragraphs five and seven, the new wording of paragraph eight and paragraph 11 enter into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision point 177)

644.20 pants. Entry into force and appeal of the decision

(1) An appeal may be lodged against the court decision. If the decision was adopted without the presence of a participant in the case, the time limit for lodging an appeal shall be counted from the date of delivery of the decision.

(2) The decision of the court of first instance shall enter into legal force after the expiry of the time limit for its appeal.

(In the wording of the law of 04.08.2011 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

644.21 pants. Competence of the regional court

(1) The regional court shall examine the appeal within 15 days after the institution of appellate proceedings. When examining the appeal, the regional court has the right to:

- 1) leave the decision unchanged and reject the appeal;
- 2) revoke the decision and resolve the issue on the merits.
  - (2) The decision shall enter into force and shall be enforceable immediately.

(With amendments made by the law of 04.08.2011, which enters into force on 01.10.2011.)

644.22 pants. Action after adoption of the decision

The court shall submit the adopted decision on the non-return of the child to the country of his or her residence and other case materials to the Ministry of Justice.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.06.2009 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)


This excerpt sits under: Izdevējs: Saeima Publicēts: > C daļa

### 77. nodaļa. Cases on European Account Preservation Orders

### (Chapter enacted on 08.

12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The chapter enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.23. Jurisdiction of cases on European Account Preservation Orders

(1) An application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order shall be submitted to the court in which the claim to be secured is to be brought, or to the court where the case for consideration on the merits is pending.

(2) If, in the case referred to in Article 6(2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the case on the merits falls within the jurisdiction of a foreign court, the application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the defendant's declared place of residence or place of residence.

(3) In the case referred to in Article 6(4) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the claimant may submit the application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order, at his or her choice, to any district (city) court located in the territory of operation of the regional court where the sworn notary who drew up the relevant notarial act is located.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.24. Application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order

(1) In addition to the application referred to in Article 8 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, a document confirming payment of the state fee in the procedure and amount specified by law shall be attached, except where the application has been submitted and payment has been made in the online system.

(2) The application shall be signed by the claimant or his or her representative. If the application has been signed by a representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to apply to the court with the application shall be attached to the application.

(3) An unsigned application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the submitter.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 644.25. Information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at a credit institution

(1) If the claimant requests, pursuant to Article 14(1) and (2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, that the court obtain information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at a credit institution, the claimant shall, in addition to that referred to in the first paragraph of Article 644.24 of this Law, attach a document certifying payment of the costs associated with obtaining the information.

(2) If the claimant's request to obtain information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at a credit institution complies with the requirements referred to in Article 14(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall grant the claimant's request.

(3) In order to obtain the information referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, the court shall send to credit institutions a request to provide information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at the credit institution.

(4) The credit institution shall, without delay but not later than on the third day from the day of receipt of the court's request, send to the court information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at the relevant credit institution.

(5) The court shall send the request to provide information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at a credit institution abroad, referred to in the third paragraph of this Article, to the foreign information authority in the procedure laid down in Article 29 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(6) If the court considers that the claimant's request to obtain information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at a credit institution is not justified, it shall reject the request. An ancillary appeal may be lodged against the decision of the court or judge within the time limit laid down in Article 21(2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(7) If a foreign court, where an application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order has been submitted, requests, pursuant to Article 14(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, to obtain information on the defendant's funds (accounts) at a credit institution, the court shall obtain such information in the procedure laid down in the first, third and fourth paragraphs of this Article, and shall also send it to the relevant foreign court in accordance with Article 14(6) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 644.26. Grounds for refusing to accept an application

(1) The court shall refuse to accept an application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to apply to the court with the application is not attached to the application.

(2) The court shall adopt a reasoned decision on refusal to accept an application. The decision together with the submitted application shall be issued to the potential claimant. The decision is not appealable.

(3) The judge's refusal to accept an application in the cases referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall not be an obstacle to the submission of the same application to the court once the deficiencies committed have been remedied.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.27. Leaving an application without action

(1) If the claimant has not provided all the information required by Article 8 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council or has not attached documents certifying payment of the state fee or costs associated with obtaining information, or if the authorisation of the representative to apply to the court with this application does not follow from the power of attorney or other document attached to the application, the court shall leave the application without action and the consequences provided for in Article 133 of this Law shall ensue.

(2) If the claimant does not remedy the deficiencies within the prescribed time limit and the application is returned to the claimant, the court shall simultaneously adopt a decision on the payment of the amount paid to secure damages from the bailiff's account, if the claimant has provided the security for damages referred to in the first paragraph of Article 644.28 of this Law. The decision shall be immediately enforceable. (08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.28. Securing the defendant's potential damages

(1) The security for damages which the claimant provides in the cases referred to in Article 12 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council in order to secure damages that the defendant may suffer as a result of the issuing of the European Account Preservation Order shall be effected by paying the amount specified by the court or judge into the bailiff's deposit account. In the submission to the bailiff, the claimant shall indicate pursuant to which court decision on securing the defendant's potential damages this amount is being paid and shall also submit to the bailiff the relevant decision.

(2) The court shall adopt a decision on securing damages immediately after submission of the application referred to in Article 644.24 of this Law, but not later than within the time limit referred to in Article 18(4) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The decision is not appealable. The court may adopt a decision on securing damages simultaneously with the decision referred to in Article 644.27 of this Law.

(3) The court shall adopt a decision on the European Account Preservation Order after receipt of the bailiff's notification on the crediting of the amount specified to secure damages to the bailiff's deposit account, except in the cases laid down in the second subparagraph of Article 12(1) and in Article 12(2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council. If the decision referred to in the second paragraph of this Article has been adopted simultaneously with the decision referred to in Article 644.27 of this Law, the decision on the European Account Preservation Order shall be adopted only if the claimant has remedied the deficiencies committed.

(4) In the case referred to in Article 14(7) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall immediately adopt a decision on the payment of the amount paid to secure damages from the bailiff's deposit account. The decision shall be immediately enforceable.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 644.29. Compensation for damages caused by issuing the European Account Preservation Order

(1) In addition to the cases referred to in Article 13(2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the defendant is entitled to claim compensation for damages suffered as a result of the issuing of the European Account Preservation Order also if the claim brought against the defendant has been dismissed or left without examination or the proceedings in the case have been terminated in the cases laid down in points 2 and 4 of Article 223 of this Law.

(2) In the judgment or decision by which the claim has been left without examination or the case has been terminated, the court shall, at the request of the defendant, simultaneously decide the issue of payment of the amount paid to secure damages from the bailiff's deposit account to the defendant. If the request and evidence on the amount of actual damages have not been submitted to the court, the secured damages shall be repaid to the claimant.

(3) When dismissing or partially granting the claim, the court shall, at the request of the defendant, decide the issue of full or partial payment of the security for damages to the defendant. If the request and evidence on the amount of actual damages have not been submitted to the court, the secured damages shall be repaid to the claimant. If the claim has been brought in another country, the defendant shall additionally submit evidence that the claim has been dismissed or partially granted.

(4) The defendant is entitled to bring a claim for compensation of damages not recovered pursuant to the first paragraph of this Article. (08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.30. Decision on issuing a European Account Preservation Order

(1) The court shall adopt a decision on issuing a European Account Preservation Order or a decision wholly or partly rejecting an application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order in the procedure laid down in Article 17 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council in written proceedings, without prior notice to the defendant and other participants in the case.

(2) The court shall draw up the European Account Preservation Order in accordance with Article 19 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council. At the request of the claimant, the court shall perform transliteration or translation of the order referred to in this paragraph on the basis of Article 23(4) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(3) The decision of the court or judge wholly or partly rejecting an application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order may be appealed in the procedure laid down in this Law and in the procedure and within the time limit laid down in Article 21 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.31. Revocation of the European Account Preservation Order if no claim has been brought

(1) If the claimant has submitted an application for issuing a European Account Preservation Order before bringing a claim and has not brought a claim within the time limit laid down in Article 10(1) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court or judge shall, on its own initiative, using the form referred to in Article 10(2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, adopt a decision on revocation of the European Account Preservation Order. The decision shall be immediately enforceable.

(2) After adopting the decision, the court shall immediately send it to the bailiff in whose records the enforcement case is pending or, if the decision is enforceable abroad, in the procedure laid down in Article 29 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council

— to the competent authority of the relevant foreign country.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.32. Enforcement of the decision on the European Account Preservation Order

(1) The decision on the European Account Preservation Order shall be immediately enforceable upon its adoption.

(2) The bailiff shall commence enforcement actions upon the creditor's application, to which Part A of the European Account Preservation Order and the unfilled standard form for notification in accordance with Article 25 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council are attached.

(3) The bailiff, on the basis of Part A of the European Account Preservation Order, shall order the credit institution to preserve the defendant's funds in the amount specified in Part A of the European Account Preservation Order, observing the restriction laid down in point 3 of Annex 1 to this Law with regard to the defendant and the sequence of preservation of the defendant's accounts laid down in Article 24(7) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and to transfer them to the bailiff's deposit account.

(4) After receipt of the credit institution's notification on the results of enforcement of the order referred to in the third paragraph of this Article, the bailiff shall send to the court and the claimant a notification on the preservation of the defendant's funds at the credit institution in the procedure laid down in Article 25(2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council or — where applicable — in the second subparagraph of paragraph 3.

(5) The claimant shall submit a request for the release of excessively preserved funds to the bailiff in the procedure laid down in Article 27(2) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(6) The bailiff, on the basis of the claimant's request referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Article, shall repay the excessively preserved funds by transferring them to the defendant's account from which the funds were received.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.33. Service of the European Account Preservation Order to the defendant

(1) The European Account Preservation Order and the other documents referred to in Article 28(1) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be served to the defendant by the court or, in the case referred to in the fourth paragraph of this Article, by the bailiff.

(2) The court that issued the European Account Preservation Order:

- 1) after receipt of the notification on preservation of funds, within the time limits laid down in Article 28 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, shall serve the documents referred to in the first paragraph of this Article to the defendant:
  - a) if the defendant's place of residence or location is in Latvia,
  - b) by transmitting the documents to the competent authority of the foreign country where the defendant's place of residence or location is located, if the defendant's place of residence or location is in another Member State of the European Union,
  - c) in the procedure laid down in Chapter 82 or 83 of this Law, if the defendant's place of residence or location is not in any of the Member States of the European Union;
- 2) at the request of the claimant, in the case referred to in the second subparagraph of Article 28(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, shall immediately send the documents referred to in Article 28(5) of this Regulation to the competent authority of the country of enforcement.
  - (3) If the European Account Preservation Order has been issued by a foreign court and the defendant's declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is in Latvia, the documents referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall, at the request of the foreign court or a participant in the case, be served by the court in whose territory of operation the defendant's declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is located. The court shall inform the foreign court or the participant in the case, depending on who submitted the request referred to in this paragraph, about the service of documents.
  - (4) The bailiff in whose records there is an enforcement case initiated pursuant to the European Account Preservation Order issued by a foreign court shall, in the case referred to in the second subparagraph of Article 28(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, at the written request of the creditor, send the documents referred to in the first paragraph of this Article to the defendant whose declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is in Latvia. The bailiff shall inform the creditor about the sending of the documents.
  - (5) The court or bailiff, depending on who was responsible for the service of documents in accordance with the provisions of this Article, shall, at the written request of the claimant, in the procedure laid down in the third subparagraph of Article 33(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, re-send the documents referred to in the first paragraph of this Article to the defendant.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 644.34. Revocation, modification of the European Account Preservation Order, refusal of its enforcement or modification of the enforcement procedure

(1) The court that issued the European Account Preservation Order, or the court where the case for consideration on the merits is pending, may revoke or modify the European Account Preservation Order:

- 1) at the request of the defendant in accordance with Article 33 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council;
- 2) at the request of the defendant or claimant in accordance with Article 35(1) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council;
- 3) at the joint request of the defendant or claimant in accordance with Article

655/2014 35(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(2) The court that issued the European Account Preservation Order, or the court where the case for consideration on the merits is pending, may refuse enforcement of the European Account Preservation Order or modify its enforcement procedure:

- 1) at the request of the defendant in accordance with point (a) and points (i) and (iii) of point (b) of Article 34(1) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council;
- 2) at the request of the claimant in accordance with Article 35(4) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
  - (3) Upon receipt of the defendant's request referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of this Article, the court may re-decide on the obligation imposed on the claimant pursuant to Article 644.28 of this Law.
  - (4) The request referred to in the first and second paragraphs of this Article, submitted using the form referred to in Article 36 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, shall be examined in written proceedings with prior notice to the participants in the case. Simultaneously with the notice, the court shall send the request to the participants in the case and set a time limit for submission of explanations, except for requests submitted by the defendant in accordance with point (a) of Article

34(1) or Article 35(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(5) If the request has been submitted in accordance with points (b) and (c) of Article 33(1) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall notify the participants in the case thereof, setting a time limit for the claimant to remedy the deficiencies referred to in these points in the procedure laid down in paragraphs 3 and 4 of Article 33 of this Regulation.

(6) If the claimant does not remedy the deficiencies referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Article, the request shall be examined in the procedure laid down in the fourth paragraph of this Article. If the claimant remedies the deficiencies referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Article, the court shall reject the request.

(7) The court shall adopt the decision referred to in the first and second paragraphs of this Article within the time limit referred to in Article 36(4) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and this decision shall be immediately enforceable.

(8) An ancillary appeal may be lodged against the court's decision using the form referred to in Article 37 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(9) If the European Account Preservation Order is enforceable abroad, the court shall transmit the decision referred to in the first, second and third paragraphs of this Article to the competent authority of the foreign country in the procedure laid down in the second subparagraph of Article 36(5) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.35. Refusal of enforcement of a European Account Preservation Order issued by a foreign court or modification of the enforcement procedure

(1) The district (city) court in whose territory of operation the European Account Preservation Order is enforceable is entitled:

- 1) at the request of the defendant in the cases laid down in Article 34 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council or at the joint request of the claimant and defendant in the case laid down in Article

35(3) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, to refuse enforcement of the European Account Preservation Order or modify its enforcement procedure;

2) at the request of the claimant in the case laid down in Article 35(4) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, to modify its enforcement procedure.

(2) The procedure laid down in Article 644.34 of this Law shall apply to the examination of the request referred to in the first paragraph of this Article.

(3) The court shall adopt the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this Article within the time limit referred to in Article 36(4) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and this decision shall be immediately enforceable.

(4) An ancillary appeal may be lodged against the court's decision using the form referred to in Article 37 of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Article 644.36. Replacement of the European Account Preservation Order

(1) The court that issued the European Account Preservation Order may, at the request of the defendant, on the basis of point (a) of Article 38(1) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, replace the European Account Preservation Order with the means of securing a claim provided for in Article 138 of this Law.

(2) The court in whose territory of operation the European Account Preservation Order issued by a foreign court is enforceable may, at the request of the defendant, on the basis of point (b) of Article 38(1) of Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, replace the European Account Preservation Order with the means of securing a claim provided for in Article 138 of this Law.

(3) The request referred to in the first and second paragraphs of this Article shall be examined in written proceedings with prior notice to the participants in the case. Simultaneously with the notice, the court shall send the request to the participants in the case and set a time limit for submission of explanations.

(4) An ancillary appeal may be lodged against the court's decision.

(5) The decision on replacement of the European Account Preservation Order shall be enforced by the bailiff in whose records the case on enforcement of the relevant European Account Preservation Order is pending, first securing the claim with the substitute means of securing a claim and thereafter cancelling the preservation of funds performed in accordance with the European Account Preservation Order. The bailiff shall repay the amount paid into the bailiff's deposit account in accordance with the European Account Preservation Order only on the basis of a court ruling.

(08.12.2016. in the wording of the law, which enters into force on 04.01.2017. The article enters into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision 121)

Chapter 78

Recognition and enforcement of foreign arbitral awards

#### 645.pants. Foreign Arbitral Tribunal Award

A foreign arbitral tribunal award is a binding award adopted by a foreign arbitral tribunal regardless of its designation.

#### 646.pants. Recognition of a Foreign Arbitral Tribunal Award

A foreign arbitral tribunal award shall be recognised in accordance with this law and international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia.

#### 647.pants. Submission of the Application

(1) An application for recognition and enforcement of a foreign arbitral tribunal award shall be submitted for consideration to the district (city)

court according to the place of enforcement of the award or according to the respondent's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the respondent's place of residence or legal address.

(2) The application shall indicate the information specified in the second part of Section 638 of this law.

(3) The following shall be attached to the application:

- 1) the foreign arbitral tribunal award or a duly certified copy of the award;
- 2) a document certifying the written agreement of the parties to refer the dispute for consideration to an arbitral tribunal;
- 3) a translation into the official language of the application and of the documents specified in Points 1 and 2 of this part, certified in the prescribed manner;
- 4) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021);
- 5) a document confirming the payment of the state fee in the manner and amount prescribed by law, except in cases where the application has been submitted and payment has been made in the online system.
  - (4) The application shall be signed by the applicant or his or her representative. If the application has been signed by a representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to submit the application to the court shall be attached to the application.
  - (5) An unsigned application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.
  - (6) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to submit this application to the court has not been attached to it. The decision is not subject to appeal.

(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 23.04.2015 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 648.pants. Leaving the Application Without Progress

If the application does not comply with the requirements of the second and third parts of Section 647 of this law, or if the authorisation for the representative to submit this application to the court does not follow from the power of attorney or other document attached to the application, the judge shall leave the application without progress and the consequences provided for in Section 133 of this law shall ensue.

(As worded by the law of 23.04.2015, which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

#### 649.pants. Consideration of the Application

(1) An application for recognition and enforcement of a foreign arbitral tribunal award shall be considered in a court session, with prior notice thereof to the parties. The non-appearance of the relevant persons is not an obstacle to the consideration of the application.

(2) The court may request explanations from the parties or additional information from the foreign arbitral tribunal that adopted the award.

(3) Having considered the application for recognition and enforcement of the foreign arbitral tribunal award, the court shall adopt a decision to recognise and enforce the award or to reject the application.

(4) The application may be rejected only in cases provided for in international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia.

(5) An appeal may be submitted regarding the court decision.

#### 650.pants. Securing the Enforcement of a Foreign Arbitral Tribunal Award

(1) Upon the applicant's application, the court, in the decision by which a foreign arbitral tribunal award is recognised, may determine the measures provided for in Section 138 of this law to secure the enforcement of the foreign arbitral tribunal award.

(2) The submission of the appeal referred to in the fifth part of Section 649 of this law does not suspend the execution of the court decision in the part concerning the securing of enforcement of the foreign arbitral tribunal award.

(With amendments made by the law of 07.09.2006, which enters into force on 11.10.2006.)

#### 651.pants. Enforcement of a Foreign Arbitral Tribunal Award

(1) A foreign arbitral tribunal award, following its recognition, shall be enforced in the manner prescribed by this law.

(2) Expenses related to the enforcement of a foreign arbitral tribunal award shall be covered in the general manner, unless otherwise provided for in international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia.

### 78. nodaļa

Adaptation of Rights and Obligations Established in a Foreign Court Decision for Their Implementation in Latvia

(Chapter in the wording of the law of 23.04.2015, which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

651.1 pants. Foreign court decision in which the established rights and obligations are to be adapted for their implementation in Latvia

A foreign court decision within the meaning of this Chapter is such a decision of a foreign court or foreign competent authority that, in accordance with directly applicable European Union law or international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia, is recognisable or enforceable in Latvia, as well as such a decision that is enforceable in the procedure established in this law without requiring recognition of the foreign court decision and declaration of enforcement of the foreign court decision.

651.2 pants. Adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia

(1) If a foreign court decision in its entirety or in any part thereof does not have legal effect in Latvia because it establishes such rights and obligations that are not recognised in Latvian law, adaptation of the rights and obligations established in the foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia shall be carried out. The adaptation referred to in this paragraph shall be carried out only in those cases where it is provided for in European Union law or in international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.

(2) The rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision shall be adapted for implementation in Latvia by adapting them as far as possible to the corresponding legal institutions that are recognised in Latvian law and which have equivalent legal effects, objectives and purposes. The adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision shall not create such legal effects that exceed the legal effects established in the law of the respective foreign country.

(3) If the question of adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for implementation in Latvia is related to the question of recognition of this decision or recognition and enforcement, the questions shall be examined simultaneously, applying the provisions of Chapter 77 and this Chapter of this law. If a foreign court decision is enforceable in the procedure established in this law without requiring recognition of the foreign court decision and declaration of enforcement of the foreign court decision, the question of adaptation of rights and obligations established in the foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia shall be examined as a separate question, applying only the provisions of this Chapter.

651.3 pants. Submission of application

(1) An application for adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for implementation in Latvia shall be submitted for examination to the district (city) court according to the place of enforcement of the decision or according to the respondent's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the respondent's place of residence or registered address.

(2) The application shall indicate the information referred to in the second paragraph of Article 638 of this law, as well as the applicant's request to adapt the rights or obligations established in the foreign court decision that are not recognised in Latvian law to the corresponding legal institutions that are recognised in Latvian law.

(3) If the question of adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for implementation in Latvia is examined as a separate question, the application shall not indicate the applicant's request to recognise or recognise and enforce the foreign court decision in its entirety or in any part thereof.

(4) The following shall be attached to the application:

- 1) the relevant foreign court decision or a duly certified copy of the decision and a translation thereof into the official language certified in the established procedure;
- 2) the text of the relevant foreign law that establishes the rights or obligations established in the foreign court decision that are not recognised in Latvian law, and a translation thereof into the official language certified in the established procedure;
- 3) a document confirming the content of the relevant foreign law that establishes the rights or obligations referred to in the foreign court decision that are not recognised in Latvian law, and a translation thereof into the official language certified in the established procedure;
- 4) a document confirming payment of the state fee in the procedure and amount established by law, except in cases where the application has been submitted and payment made through the online system.
  - (5) In cases concerning the adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia in accordance with Article 11 of Council Regulation No 606/2013, the documents referred to in points 2 and 3 of the fourth paragraph of this Article shall not be attached.
  - (6) The application shall be signed by the applicant or his or her representative. If the application has been signed by a representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to apply to the court with this application shall be attached to the application.
  - (7) An unsigned application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.
  - (8) The judge shall adopt a decision refusing to accept the application if it is not accompanied by a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to apply to the court with this application. The decision is not subject to appeal.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

651.4 pants. Leaving application without movement

If the application does not comply with the requirements of the second and fourth paragraphs of Article 651.3 of this law or if the power of attorney or other document attached to the application does not show authorisation for the representative to apply to the court with this application, the court shall leave the application without movement and the consequences provided for in Article 133 of this law shall occur.

651.5 pants. Resolution of application

(1) A decision on the adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia or a decision on rejection of the application shall be adopted by the judge acting alone on the basis of the submitted application and the documents attached thereto within 10 days after initiation of the case, without summoning the parties.

(2) In cases specified in Article 11 of Council Regulation No 606/2013, the judge shall adopt the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this Article on the next working day after receipt of the application, without summoning the parties. The decision on the adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia in accordance with Article 11 of Council Regulation No 606/2013 shall be notified to the respondent in accordance with point 4 of Article 11 of that Regulation.

(3) If, when assessing the objective circumstances related to the case, in particular the degree of complexity and voluminousness of the case, the judge considers it impossible to adopt the decision referred to in the first paragraph of this Article within 10 days, he or she shall adopt it as soon as possible.

651.6 pants. Entry into force, enforceability and appeal of first instance court and appellate instance court decision

(1) An ancillary complaint to the regional court may be filed against the first instance court decision in a case concerning the adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia, and the regional court decision on the ancillary complaint may be appealed to the Supreme Court by filing an ancillary complaint.

(2) A party whose declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence or registered address is in Latvia, may file the ancillary complaint referred to in the first paragraph of this Article within 30 days from the date of issuance of the decision, but a party whose declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence or registered address is not in Latvia — within 60 days from the date of issuance of the decision.

(3) The first instance court decision and the appellate instance court decision shall enter into legal force after the time limit for appeal thereof has expired, counting from the date of issuance of the later decision, and no ancillary complaint has been filed.

(4) If in the case referred to in the third paragraph of this Article no relevant confirmation of issuance of the decision has been received, the decision shall enter into legal force six months after its proclamation.

(5) The first instance court decision and the appellate instance court decision in a case concerning the adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia in accordance with Article 11 of Council Regulation No 606/2013 shall be enforceable immediately after its adoption.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

651.7 pants. Regional court competence

(1) The regional court, when examining an ancillary complaint, shall have the right to:

- 1) leave the decision unchanged and reject the complaint;
- 2) annul the decision in whole or in part and decide the question of adaptation of rights and obligations established in a foreign court decision for their implementation in Latvia;
- 3) amend the decision.
  - (2) The court may request explanations from the parties or additional information from the foreign court that adopted the decision.

International Legal Cooperation

#### Article 652. Requests for Legal Assistance

(Deleted by the Law of 05.02.2009., which comes into force on 01.03.2009.)

#### Article 653. Communication of Latvian Courts with Foreign Courts and Law Enforcement Authorities

Latvian courts communicate with foreign courts and law enforcement authorities in accordance with laws, international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia, and European Union legal norms.

Article 653.1 Legal Cooperation in Cases of Unlawful Cross-Border Removal or Retention of Children

(1) Unless otherwise provided in this Law, in cases of unlawful cross-border removal or retention of children, Latvian courts communicate with the relevant foreign courts or competent authorities directly or through the intermediary of the Ministry of Justice.

(2) (Deleted by the Law of 12.06.2009.)

(3) The Ministry of Justice shall ensure the translation of court documents into the language specified as the communication language in the application of the relevant legal act, or into the language of the receiving State of the documents, or into the language that the respective State has notified as acceptable for communication.

(4) For the purpose of applying the Hague Convention of 19 October 1996 on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition, Enforcement and Co-operation in Respect of Parental Responsibility and Measures for the Protection of Children, the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, Council Regulation No 2201/2003 or Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, documents of foreign competent authorities, applications of persons or other documents to be submitted to the Ministry of Justice shall, in the relevant cases, be drawn up in the original language with a translation in the official language attached, but if this is not possible, documents may be submitted in English, in which case the Ministry of Justice shall ensure their translation.

(In the wording of the Law of 07.09.2006. with amendments made by the Laws of 12.06.2009. and 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022. The amendment to paragraph four comes into force on 01.08.2022. See point 177 of the transitional provisions) Chapter 80

Application of Foreign Laws in the Adjudication of Civil Cases

#### Article 654. Text of Foreign Law

In cases where foreign law is applicable, the party who refers to foreign law shall submit to the court a translation of its text in the official language, certified in the prescribed manner.

#### Article 655. Clarification of the Content of Foreign Law

(1) The court shall clarify the content of the applicable foreign law in the manner provided for in international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.

(2) In other cases, the court shall, to the extent possible, clarify the content of the applicable foreign law through the intermediary of the Ministry of Justice.

Sixteenth Section

International Civil Procedural Cooperation in Service of Documents

(Section in the wording of the Law of 05.02.2009., which comes into force on 01.03.2009.)

Chapter 81

International Civil Procedural Cooperation in Service of Documents in Accordance with

Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council

(Chapter title with amendments made by the Law of 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### Article 656. Basis of International Civil Procedural Cooperation in Service of Documents

(1) A bailiff shall serve documents on a person whose declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is in Latvia and whose address is known, on the basis of a request from a foreign competent authority for service of judicial or extrajudicial documents (hereinafter – foreign request for service of documents) and an assessment by the Council of Sworn Bailiffs of Latvia on the compliance of the foreign request for service of documents with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(2) If court documents are to be served on a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, the court may submit to a foreign competent authority a request for service of court documents abroad (hereinafter – Latvian request for service of documents) in accordance with Chapter II, Section 1, of Regulation

(EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council, or the court may serve court documents in accordance with Article 18 or 19 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(3) A party to the case may, with the consent of the judge, receive court documents for service on another party to the case whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, in accordance with Article 20(1) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if such direct service is permitted by the laws of the relevant Member State.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 29.11.2012., 30.10.2014. and 31.05.2018. and 16.06.2022., which comes into force on

#### Article 657. Competence of the Ministry of Justice in Service of Documents

(1) (Deleted by the Law of 30.10.2014.)

(2) The Ministry of Justice shall perform the functions referred to in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(3) If necessary, the Ministry of Justice shall:

- 1) transmit a Latvian request for service of documents to a foreign state through the intermediary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, using consular or diplomatic channels, in accordance with Article
  - 16 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council;
- 2) request, through the intermediary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to serve court documents on Latvian diplomatic or consular representatives in accordance with Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 30.10.2014. and 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### Article 658. Language and Form of Foreign Request for Service of Documents

(Deleted from 01.01.2019. by the Law of 31.05.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018. See point 147 of the transitional provisions)

#### Article 659. Language and Form of Latvian Request for Service of Documents

(1) In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall prepare in writing the Latvian request for service of documents, the certificate of service of documents and other forms provided for in Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council in the language of the receiving Member State of the request or in the language that the respective State has notified as acceptable for communication.

(2) The Latvian request for service of documents shall be signed by the judge.

(3) The court shall submit the Latvian request for service of documents or the certificate of service of documents to a foreign state in accordance with the procedure laid down in Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 30.10.2014., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### Article 660. Language of Documents Attached to Latvian Request for Service of Documents

(1) If court documents are served on persons abroad at the request of a party, the court shall, in accordance with Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council, explain to the party that the addressee is entitled to refuse to accept court documents if they have not been drawn up or are not accompanied by a translation in one of the languages referred to in Article 12(1) of Regulation

(EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council. In such a case, the party may, at its discretion, draw up court documents or attach a translation thereof in one of the languages referred to in Article 12(1) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(2) In other cases, including cases where the addressee has refused to accept court documents attached to the Latvian request for service of documents in accordance with Article 12(1) and (3) of Regulation (EU)

2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council, a translation in the language of the receiving Member State of the request or in a language understood by the addressee shall be attached thereto.

(With amendments made by the Law of 16.06.2022., which comes into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### Article 661. Decision on and Execution of Foreign Request for Service of Documents

representatives

In accordance with Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council, service of foreign documents request execution performed by foreign diplomatic or consular representatives by serving documents is permissible only if the documents are served to nationals of the respective foreign state.

### 81. nodaļa

International civil procedural cooperation in service of documents in accordance with

the 1965 Hague Convention

(In the wording of the Law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. The Chapter enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision paragraph 147)

665.1 pants. Basis of international civil procedural cooperation in service of documents

(1) To a person whose declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is in Latvia and whose address is known, the bailiff serves documents on the basis of a foreign service of documents request and the assessment of the Latvian Council of Sworn Bailiffs regarding the compliance of the foreign service of documents request with the requirements of the 1965 Hague Convention.

(2) If court documents are served to a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, the court submits the Latvian service of documents request to the central authority of the receiving state.

(3) In accordance with Article 10(a) of the 1965 Hague Convention, the court may serve court documents to a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, by postal consignment, observing the conditions set by the respective contracting state, if it has not objected to such method of service.

(4) In accordance with Article 10(c) of the 1965 Hague Convention, a party to the case, with the judge's consent, may receive court documents for service to another party to the case whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, directly from judicial authorities, other authorities or other competent persons of the receiving contracting state, observing the conditions set by the respective contracting state, if it has not objected to such method of service.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. The Article enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision paragraph 147)

665.2 pants. Competence of the Ministry of Justice in service of documents

The Ministry of Justice, if necessary:

- 1) transmits the Latvian service of documents request to a foreign state through the intermediary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, using consular or diplomatic channels, in accordance with Article 9 of the 1965 Hague Convention;
- 2) through the intermediary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, requests the Latvian diplomatic or consular representatives to serve court documents in accordance with Article 8 of the 1965 Hague Convention.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. The Article enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision paragraph 147)

665.3 pants. Language of the Latvian service of documents request

(1) The Latvian service of documents request, certificate and summary of documents to be served are prepared in the language of the receiving state of the request or in English or French.

(2) The court documents attached to the Latvian service of documents request are prepared in the official language. A translation in the language of the receiving state of the request may be attached to them.

(3) If the receiving state of the request or the addressee has refused to accept documents in a language that is not the language of that state, a translation in the language of the receiving state of the request is attached to the documents.

(4) If it is not possible to provide a translation in one of the languages referred to in paragraph three of this Article, the competent authorities of Latvia and the foreign state mutually agree on another language in which the documents are to be prepared or in which a translation is to be attached to them.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. The Article enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision paragraph 147)

665.4 pants. Form of the Latvian service of documents request

(1) (Deleted by the Law of 11.11.2021)

(2) The Latvian service of documents request is signed by the judge.

(3) The court submits the Latvian service of documents request and the documents attached to it to a foreign state electronically, but if this is not possible, as a postal consignment.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.05.2018 with amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

665.5 pants. Right of the addressee to refuse to accept documents

(1) The bailiff informs the addressee in writing of their right to refuse to accept documents if they are prepared in or have a translation attached in another language, except the official language or a language understandable to the addressee.

(2) The addressee may refuse to accept the documents at the time of their service or within a week after receiving the documents by submitting or sending back the documents to the bailiff who served them. If the addressee refuses to accept documents that are not in the official language, the addressee notifies the bailiff of the language that they understand.

(3) If the addressee has refused to accept documents in accordance with paragraphs one and two of this Article, the bailiff notifies the Latvian Council of Sworn Bailiffs thereof by sending back the foreign service of documents request and the documents for retranslation.

(4) If, in accordance with Article 10(a) of the 1965 Hague Convention, documents have been sent by post directly to the addressee in Latvia, the addressee may refuse to accept the documents if they are prepared in or have a translation attached in another language, except the official language, or they have been sent by another method, except registered postal consignment with acknowledgment of receipt.

(In the wording of the Law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. The Article enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision paragraph 147)

International civil procedural cooperation in service of documents in accordance with

international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia

#### 666.pants. Basis of international civil procedural cooperation in service of documents

(1) To a person whose declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is in Latvia and whose address is known, the court serves documents on the basis of a foreign service of documents request and the decision of the Ministry of Justice on the admissibility of the foreign service of documents request.

(2) If court documents are served to a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, the court submits the Latvian service of documents request to the Ministry of Justice.

#### 667.pants. Competence of the Ministry of Justice in service of documents

(1) The Ministry of Justice receives and decides on foreign requests for service of documents and forwards Latvian requests for service of documents in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia

(2) In cases provided for in international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia, if necessary, the Ministry of Justice:
