#### 668.pants. Language of the request for service of documents

A request for service of documents shall be prepared and submitted in the language established as the language of communication in the application of international agreements binding on the Republic of

Latvia.

#### 669.pants. Language of documents attached to a Latvian request for service of documents

(1) Court documents attached to a Latvian request for service of documents shall be prepared in the official language. A translation may be attached in the language of the state receiving the request or in another language if international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia allow such possibility.

(2) If, in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia, the state receiving the request or the addressee has refused to accept documents in a language that is not the language of that state, a translation shall be attached to the documents in the language of the state receiving the request or in another language that the state receiving the request has indicated as acceptable for communication.

(3) If it is not possible to provide a translation in any of the languages referred to in paragraph two of this Article, the competent authorities of Latvia and the foreign state shall mutually agree on another language in which documents shall be prepared or in which a translation shall be attached to them.

#### 670.pants. Form of the request for service of documents

(1) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(2) A Latvian request for service of documents shall be signed by a judge and certified with the court seal.

(3) The Ministry of Justice may submit a Latvian request for service of documents and the documents attached to it to a foreign state by other means of communication, also submitting them as a postal item.

(4) A foreign request for service of documents and the documents attached to it shall be accepted prepared as a postal item. A foreign request for service of documents and the documents attached to it may be accepted by other means of communication if they are also submitted as a postal item.

(With amendments made by the laws of 22.06.2017, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 671.pants. Decision on a foreign request for service of documents

(1) A foreign request for service of documents shall be decided by the Ministry of Justice within seven days from the day of its receipt.

(2) The Ministry of Justice shall make one of the following decisions:

- 1) on the admissibility of execution of the request for service of documents, establishing the institution executing the request for service of documents, time limits and other conditions;
- 2) on refusal to accept the request for service of documents or part thereof for execution in cases provided for in international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.
  - (3) The decision of the Ministry of Justice is not appealable.

#### 672.pants. General provisions for execution of a foreign request for service of documents

(1) A foreign request for service of documents shall be executed by the district (city) court in whose territory of operation is located the address of the addressee indicated in the foreign request for service of documents or the declared place of residence of the addressee, but if there is none — the place of residence or legal address of the addressee.

(2) A foreign request for service of documents shall be executed in accordance with Article 56 of this Law, except in cases when, in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia, documents are served in the procedural manner of the state submitting the request or in the manner specifically requested.

(3) Execution of a foreign request for service of documents shall be commenced immediately after a decision has been made on the admissibility of execution of the request for service of documents. If it is not possible to execute the foreign request for service of documents within one month from the day it was received by the Ministry of Justice, or within the time limit specified in the request, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice thereof in writing, indicating the reasons that prevent the execution of the said request.

(4) If execution of a foreign request for service of documents is not possible or it has been executed partially, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice in writing of the reasons for non-execution of the said request, and shall also send the unserved documents.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 673.pants. Rights of the addressee to refuse to accept documents

(1) The court shall inform the addressee in writing of their right to refuse to accept documents if they are prepared or have a translation attached in another language, except the official language or a language comprehensible to the addressee.

(2) The addressee may refuse to accept documents at the time of their service or within one week after receiving the documents, by submitting or sending back the documents to the court that served them. If the addressee refuses to accept documents that are not in the official language, the addressee shall notify the court of the language they understand.

(3) If the addressee has refused to accept documents in accordance with paragraphs one and two of this Article, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice thereof, sending back the foreign request for service of documents and the documents for translation.

(4) (Deleted as of 01.01.2019 by the law of 31.05.2018)

(With amendments made by the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. The amendment on deletion of paragraph four enters into force on 01.01.2019. See transitional provision 147.)

#### 674.pants. Costs of execution of a foreign request for service of documents

(Deleted as of 01.01.2019 by the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. See transitional provision 147.)

83.nodaļa

International civil procedural cooperation in service of documents where there is no agreement with a foreign state providing for cooperation in service of documents

#### 675.pants. Basis for international civil procedural cooperation in service of documents

(1) Documents shall be served by a court to a person whose declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is in Latvia and whose address is known, on the basis of a foreign request for service of documents and a decision of the Ministry of Justice on the admissibility of the foreign request for service of documents.

(2) If court documents are to be served to a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known, the court shall submit a Latvian request for service of documents to the Ministry of Justice.

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 676.pants. Competence of the Ministry of Justice in service of documents

(1) A Latvian request for service of documents shall be submitted and a foreign request for service of documents shall be received and decided by the Ministry of Justice.

(2) The Ministry of Justice may request or issue to a foreign state a confirmation that reciprocity will be observed in cooperation, that is, that in the future the cooperation partner will provide assistance, observing the same principles.

(3) If necessary, the Ministry of Justice:

- 1) forwards a Latvian request for service of documents to a foreign state through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, using consular or diplomatic channels;
- 2) requests, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Latvian diplomatic or consular representatives to serve court documents to Latvian citizens, requesting the consent of the respective state for such manner of service.

#### 677.pants. Content of the request for service of documents

(1) The request for service of documents shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the institution submitting the request for service of documents;
- 2) the subject matter and essence of the request for service of documents;
- 3) information about the addressee: for natural persons — first name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none, other identification data) and place of residence, and for legal persons — name, registration number and legal address, as well as information about the addressee's status in the proceedings;
- 4) the essence of the case and a brief statement of facts;
- 5) other information necessary for the execution of the request for service of documents.
  - (2) In the request for service of documents, it may be requested that documents be served in accordance with the procedural manner provided for by the law of the requesting State.

(As amended by the Law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 678.pants. Language of the request for service of documents and the documents attached thereto

(1) Latvian requests for service of documents and the documents attached thereto shall be prepared and submitted in the official language, attaching a translation in one of the following languages:

- 1) in the language of the receiving State;
- 2) in a language understood by the addressee, if the State in question permits it;
- 3) in another language, by mutual agreement between the competent authorities of Latvia and the foreign State.
  - (2) If the receiving State or the addressee has refused to accept documents in a language other than the language of that State, a translation in the language of the receiving State or in another language indicated by the receiving State as acceptable shall be attached to the documents.
  - (3) Foreign requests for service of documents shall be accepted prepared or with an attached translation in the official language, Russian or English.
  - (4) Documents attached to a foreign request for service of documents shall be accepted prepared or with an attached translation in any language, provided that the addressee accepts them voluntarily (Article 682).
  - (5) If it is not possible to provide a translation in one of the languages referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article or in a language understood by the addressee, the competent authorities of Latvia and the foreign State may agree on another language in which the foreign request for service of documents and the documents attached thereto shall be prepared or in which a translation shall be attached thereto.

#### 679.pants. Form of the request for service of documents

(1) (Deleted by the Law of 11.11.2021)

(2) A Latvian request for service of documents shall be signed by a judge and certified with the seal of the court.

(3) The Ministry of Justice may submit a Latvian request for service of documents and the documents attached thereto to a foreign State by other means of communication, also submitting them as a postal item.

(4) A foreign request for service of documents and the documents attached thereto shall be accepted prepared, as a postal item. A foreign request for service of documents and the documents attached thereto may be accepted by other means of communication if they are also submitted as a postal item.

(As amended by the Law of 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 680.pants. Decision on a foreign request for service of documents

(1) A foreign request for service of documents shall be decided by the Ministry of Justice within 10 days from the date of its receipt.

(2) The Ministry of Justice shall adopt one of the following decisions:

- 1) on the admissibility of the execution of the request for service of documents, determining the institution executing the request, time limits and other conditions;
- 2) on refusal to accept the request for service of documents or part thereof for execution, stating the reasons for refusal.
  - (3) If additional information is required for the decision on the request for service of documents, the Ministry of Justice shall request it from the competent authority of the foreign State concerned.
  - (4) The execution of a foreign request for service of documents may be refused if:
- 1) the execution of the foreign request for service of documents is contrary to the public order of Latvia;
- 2) sufficient information has not been provided and it is not possible to obtain additional information.
  - (5) If the execution of a foreign request for service of documents is refused, the Ministry of Justice shall immediately notify the competent authority of the requesting State thereof.
  - (6) Refusal to execute a foreign request for service of documents or part thereof shall not prevent the competent authority of the foreign State from resubmitting the same request after remedying the deficiencies.
  - (7) The decision of the Ministry of Justice is not subject to appeal.

#### 681.pants. General provisions for the execution of a foreign request for service of documents

(1) A foreign request for service of documents shall be executed by the regional (city) court in whose territory the address of the addressee indicated in the foreign request for service of documents or the declared place of residence of the addressee is located, but if there is none — the place of residence or legal address of the addressee.

(2) A foreign request for service of documents shall be executed in accordance with Article 56 of this Law, except in cases where the competent authority of the foreign State requests that documents be served in accordance with its procedural manner or in a specially requested manner.

(3) The execution of a foreign request for service of documents shall be commenced immediately after a decision on the admissibility of the execution of the request for service of documents has been adopted. If it is not possible to execute the foreign request for service of documents within one month from the date of its receipt by the Ministry of Justice or within the time limit specified in the request, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice thereof in writing, indicating the reasons preventing the execution of the said request.

(4) If the execution of a foreign request for service of documents is not possible or it has been executed partially, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice in writing of the reasons for non-execution of the said request and shall also send the documents not served.

(As amended by the Law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 682.pants. Right of the addressee to refuse to accept documents

(1) The court shall inform the addressee in writing of his or her right to refuse to accept documents if they are prepared or have a translation attached in another language, except for the official language or a language understood by the addressee.

(2) The addressee may refuse to accept documents at the time of their service or within one week after receipt of the documents, by submitting or sending the documents back to the court that served them. If the addressee refuses to accept documents that are not in the official language or in a language understood by the addressee, the addressee shall inform the court of the language he or she understands.

(3) If the addressee has refused to accept documents in accordance with paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice thereof, sending back the foreign request for service of documents and the documents for retranslation.

#### 683.pants. Costs of execution of a foreign request for service of documents

(1) The expenses incurred in executing a foreign request for service of documents shall be covered from the State budget funds, except in the case provided for in paragraph 2 of this Article.

(2) If expenses have been incurred, in cases provided for by law, in executing a foreign request for service of documents in accordance with the procedural manner provided for by the law of the foreign State or in a specially requested manner, the court shall inform the Ministry of Justice of the costs of execution of the said request, and the Ministry of Justice may request the competent authority of the foreign State to cover these costs. Part Seventeen

International civil procedural cooperation in obtaining evidence

(Part adopted in the version of the Law of 05.02.2009, which entered into force on 01.03.2009.)

Chapter 84

International civil procedural cooperation in obtaining evidence in accordance with

Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2020 on cooperation between the courts of the Member States in the taking of evidence in civil and commercial matters (taking of evidence)

(Title of the Chapter as amended by the Law of 16.06.2022, which entered into force on 07.07.2022.)


This excerpt sits under: Publisher: Saeima Published: > Part C > Chapter 81.

#### 684.pants. Basis for international civil procedural cooperation in obtaining evidence

(1) The court obtains evidence in Latvia on the basis of a request from a foreign competent authority for obtaining evidence in Latvia (hereinafter — foreign evidence request) and a decision of the competent authority of Latvia on the admissibility of the foreign evidence request.

(2) The court, in the cases and according to the procedure provided for in this law, on its own initiative or upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, decides on the question of obtaining evidence abroad (hereinafter — Latvian evidence request).

(3) Obtaining evidence within the meaning of this Chapter also includes securing evidence in the procedure established by this law.

#### 685.pants. Competent authorities in obtaining evidence

(1) In accordance with Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2020 on cooperation between the courts of the Member States in the taking of evidence in civil or commercial matters (taking of evidence) (hereinafter — Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council), the court receives and decides on foreign evidence requests, as well as decides on obtaining evidence abroad and submits Latvian evidence requests directly to a foreign state or — in the cases provided for in point (c) of paragraph 1 of Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council — to the Ministry of Justice.

(2) The Ministry of Justice performs the functions referred to in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 16.06.2022. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 07.07.2022.)

#### 686.pants. Language and form of a foreign evidence request

(1) In accordance with Articles 5 and 6 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, a foreign evidence request and the documents attached thereto, as well as communications, shall be accepted if they are prepared in the official language or in English.

(2) (Izslēgta ar 11.11.2021. likumu)

(3) A foreign evidence request and the documents attached thereto, as well as communications, shall be accepted in accordance with the procedure established in Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 11.11.2021. un 16.06.2022. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 07.07.2022.)

#### 687.pants. Language and form of a Latvian evidence request

(1) In accordance with Articles 5 and 6 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall prepare a Latvian evidence request and the documents attached thereto, as well as communications, in writing in the language of the state receiving the request or in the language which the respective state has notified as acceptable for communication.

(2) A Latvian evidence request shall be signed by a judge.

(3) The court or the Ministry of Justice shall submit a Latvian evidence request and the documents attached thereto, as well as communications, to a foreign state in accordance with the procedure established in Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 11.11.2021. un 16.06.2022. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 07.07.2022.)

#### 688.pants. Latvian evidence request for the presence or participation of parties or court representatives

in obtaining evidence abroad

The court, in the cases provided for in this law, on its own initiative or upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, may request in a Latvian evidence request:

- 1) to allow the parties to the case or their representatives to be present at or participate in obtaining evidence in accordance with Article 13 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council;
- 2) to allow court representatives to be present at or participate in obtaining evidence in accordance with Article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 16.06.2022. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 07.07.2022.)

#### 689.pants. Decision on a foreign evidence request

(1) A foreign evidence request shall be decided by the district (city) court in whose area of operation the source of the evidence to be obtained is located, or by the Ministry of Justice in the cases provided for in paragraph 3 of Article 4 and Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, within seven days from the date of its receipt.

(2) If the court to which a foreign evidence request has been submitted in accordance with paragraph one of this Article finds that part of the evidence is located in another city or district, it shall instruct the respective court to perform specific procedural actions in accordance with Articles 102 and 103 of this law.

(3) When examining a foreign evidence request, the court shall take one of the following decisions:

- 1) on the admissibility of execution of the evidence request, accepting it for execution or determining the executing authority of the evidence request, time limits and other conditions;
- 2) on refusal to accept an evidence request or part thereof for execution in accordance with Article 16 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(4) When examining a foreign evidence request in the case provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the Ministry of Justice shall take one of the following decisions:

- 1) on the admissibility of execution of the evidence request, determining that the district (city) court in whose area of operation the source of the evidence to be obtained is located shall participate in the execution of the said request, time limits for execution of the evidence request and other conditions;
- 2) on refusal to accept an evidence request or part thereof for execution in accordance with Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(5) A decision of the competent authority shall not be subject to appeal.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 16.06.2022. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 07.07.2022.)

#### 690.pants. General provisions for execution of a foreign evidence request

(1) A foreign evidence request shall be executed in the procedure established by this law, except in cases where execution of the foreign evidence request is permitted according to foreign procedural procedure at the request of a foreign competent authority.

(2) Execution of a foreign evidence request shall be commenced immediately after a decision on the admissibility of execution of the evidence request has been taken. If it is not possible to execute a foreign evidence request within 90 days from the date of its receipt, the court shall, in accordance with Article

17 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, notify the foreign competent authority thereof in writing, indicating the reasons preventing execution of the said request.

(3) If execution of a foreign evidence request is complicated or impossible, the court shall, in accordance with Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, notify the foreign competent authority in writing of the reasons for non-execution of the said request.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 16.06.2022. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 07.07.2022.)

#### 691.pants. Execution of a foreign evidence request in the presence or with the participation of parties or

representatives of a foreign competent court

(1) The court executing a foreign evidence request in accordance with Article 13 or 14 of Regulation (EU)

2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall notify the representatives of the foreign competent court or the parties or their representatives of the time and place of obtaining evidence, as well as of the conditions for participation.

(2) The court shall ascertain whether an interpreter is necessary for the representatives of the foreign competent court, the parties or their representatives.

(3) If the persons referred to in paragraph one of this Article do not understand the official language and if there are no significant practical difficulties, an interpreter shall participate in obtaining evidence at the request of the representatives of the foreign competent court or the parties or their representatives.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 16.06.2022. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 07.07.2022.)

#### 692.pants. Obtaining evidence using technical means

(1) If execution of a foreign evidence request using technical means has been permitted, such foreign evidence request shall be executed by the district (city) court which has access to the technical means necessary for obtaining evidence.

(2) An interpreter shall participate, if necessary, in obtaining evidence in Latvia or abroad using technical means.

(3) The court shall confirm the identity of the persons involved and ensure the course of obtaining evidence in Latvia.

#### 693.pants. Witnesses' right to refuse to give testimony

(1) When executing a foreign request for taking evidence, the court shall verify whether the obstacles indicated in Article 106 of this law exist, and also explain to witnesses their right to refuse to give testimony in the cases provided for in Article 107 of this law.

(2) When executing a foreign request for taking evidence, the court shall, in accordance with Article 16 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, explain to witnesses their right to refuse to give testimony also in accordance with the law of the requesting state.

(As amended by the law of 16.06.2022, which entered into force on 07.07.2022.)

#### 694.pants. Costs of execution of a foreign request for taking evidence

(1) In the cases provided for in paragraph 3 of Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court may request the competent foreign court to deposit, prior to the execution of the foreign request for taking evidence, the amounts payable to experts.

(2) In the cases provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1783 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court may request the competent foreign court to cover, after execution of the foreign request for taking evidence:

- 1) the amounts of expenses payable to experts and interpreters;
- 2) costs incurred where the foreign request for taking evidence has been executed in accordance with foreign procedural rules at the request of the competent foreign authority;
- 3) costs incurred where the foreign request for taking evidence has been executed using technical means at the request of the competent foreign authority.

(As amended by the law of 16.06.2022, which entered into force on 07.07.2022.)

85.nodaļa

International civil procedural cooperation in taking evidence in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia

#### 695.pants. Basis for international civil procedural cooperation in taking evidence

(1) The court takes evidence in Latvia on the basis of a foreign request for taking evidence and a decision of the Ministry of Justice on the admissibility of the foreign request for taking evidence.

(2) The court, in the cases and manner provided for in this law, on its own initiative or upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, decides the question of a Latvian request for taking evidence.

(3) Taking evidence within the meaning of this chapter also includes securing evidence in the manner prescribed by this law.

#### 696.pants. Competence of the Ministry of Justice in taking evidence

The Ministry of Justice receives and decides on foreign requests for taking evidence and sends Latvian requests for taking evidence in accordance with the Hague Convention of 1970 and other international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.

#### 697.pants. Language of the request for taking evidence and documents attached thereto

The request for taking evidence and the documents attached thereto shall be prepared and submitted in the language designated as the language of communication in the application of international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.

#### 698.pants. Form of the request for taking evidence

(1) The court submits the Latvian request for taking evidence and the documents attached thereto to the Ministry of Justice.

(2) The Latvian request for taking evidence shall be signed by a judge and certified with the seal of the court.

(3) The Ministry of Justice may submit the Latvian request for taking evidence and the documents attached thereto to a foreign state by other means of communication, also submitting them as a postal item.

(4) A foreign request for taking evidence and the documents attached thereto may be received by other means of communication if they are also submitted as a postal item.

(As amended by the law of 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 699.pants. Latvian request for taking evidence regarding the participation of parties or representatives of the court

The court, in the cases provided for in this law, on its own initiative or upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, may in the Latvian request for taking evidence request:

- 1) to allow parties to the case or their representatives to participate in the taking of evidence in accordance with Article 7 of the Hague Convention of 1970;
- 2) to allow representatives of the court to participate in the taking of evidence in accordance with Article 8 of the Hague Convention of 1970.

#### 700.pants. Decision on a foreign request for taking evidence

(1) A foreign request for taking evidence shall be decided on by the Ministry of Justice within seven days from the date of its receipt.

(2) The Ministry of Justice adopts one of the following decisions:

- 1) on the admissibility of execution of the request for taking evidence, determining the authority executing the request for taking evidence, time limits and other conditions; authority, time limits and other conditions;
- 2) on refusal to accept the request for taking evidence or a part thereof for execution in the cases provided for in international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.
  - (3) When considering a foreign request for taking evidence submitted in accordance with Article 16 or 17 of the Hague Convention of 1970, the Ministry of Justice adopts one of the following decisions:
- 1) on the admissibility of execution of the request for taking evidence, determining that the district (city) court within whose jurisdiction the source of the evidence to be taken is located shall participate in the execution of said request, time limits for execution of the request for taking evidence and other conditions;
- 2) on refusal to accept the request for taking evidence or a part thereof for execution.
  - (4) The decision of the Ministry of Justice is not subject to appeal.

#### 701.pants. General provisions for execution of a foreign request for taking evidence

(1) A foreign request for taking evidence shall be executed by the district (city) court within whose jurisdiction the source of the evidence to be taken is located.

(2) If the court to which the foreign request for taking evidence has been submitted in accordance with paragraph one of this Article finds that part of the evidence is located in another city or district, it shall instruct the relevant court to perform certain procedural actions in accordance with Articles 102 and 103 of this law.

(3) A foreign request for taking evidence shall be executed in the manner prescribed by this law, except in cases where execution of the foreign request for taking evidence is permitted in accordance with foreign procedural rules at the request of the competent foreign authority.

(4) Execution of a foreign request for taking evidence shall be commenced immediately after a decision on the admissibility of execution of the request for taking evidence has been adopted. If it is not possible to execute the foreign request for taking evidence within 90 days from the date of its receipt, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice thereof in writing, indicating the reasons that prevent execution of said request.

(5) If execution of the foreign request for taking evidence is difficult or impossible, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice in writing of the reasons for non-execution of said request.

#### 702.pants. Execution of a foreign request for taking evidence with the participation of parties or representatives of the competent foreign court

(1) If execution of the foreign request for taking evidence is permitted, with representatives of the competent foreign court or parties or their representatives being present or participating in the taking of evidence in accordance with Article 7 or 8 of the Hague Convention of 1970, the court executing the foreign request for taking evidence shall notify the competent foreign authority or directly the representatives of the competent foreign court or the parties or their representatives of the time and place of taking evidence, as well as of the conditions of participation.

(2) The court shall ascertain whether representatives of the competent foreign court, parties or their representatives require an interpreter.

(3) If the persons referred to in paragraph one of this Article do not understand the official language and if there are no substantial practical difficulties, an interpreter shall participate in the taking of evidence at the request of representatives of the competent foreign court or the parties or their representatives.

#### 703.pants. Taking evidence using technical means

(1) If execution of the foreign request for taking evidence is permitted using technical means, such foreign request for taking evidence shall be executed by the district (city) court that has access to the technical means necessary for taking evidence.

(2) In taking evidence in Latvia or abroad using technical means, an interpreter shall participate if necessary.

(3) The court shall verify the identity of the persons involved and ensure the course of taking evidence in Latvia.

#### 704.pants. Right of witnesses to refuse to give testimony

(1) When executing a foreign evidence obtaining request, the court ascertains whether the obstacles specified in Article 106 of this law exist, and also explains to witnesses their right to refuse to give testimony in the cases provided for in Article 107 of this law.

(2) When executing a foreign evidence obtaining request in accordance with the 1970 Hague Convention, the court also explains to witnesses their right to refuse to give testimony in accordance with the law of the requesting state.

#### 705.pants. Costs of executing a foreign evidence obtaining request

(1) In accordance with the second part of Article 14 of the 1970 Hague Convention, the court notifies the Ministry of Justice of the costs of executing a foreign evidence obtaining request, if such have arisen.

(2) The Ministry of Justice may request the competent foreign authority to cover the costs of executing a foreign evidence obtaining request that have arisen in accordance with the second part of Article 14 of the 1970 Hague Convention.

86.nodaļa

International civil procedural cooperation in obtaining evidence if there is no treaty with a foreign state providing for cooperation in obtaining evidence

#### 706.pants. Basis for international civil procedural cooperation in obtaining evidence

(1) The court obtains evidence in Latvia based on a foreign evidence obtaining request and the decision of the Ministry of Justice on the admissibility of the foreign evidence obtaining request.

(2) The court, in the cases and manner provided for in this law, on its own initiative or at the reasoned request of a party to the case, decides on the question of a Latvian evidence obtaining request.

(3) Obtaining evidence within the meaning of this chapter is also securing evidence in the manner prescribed by this law.

#### 707.pants. Competence of the Ministry of Justice in obtaining evidence

(1) If there is no treaty with a foreign state providing for cooperation in obtaining evidence, the Ministry of Justice submits Latvian evidence obtaining requests and receives and decides on foreign evidence obtaining requests.

(2) The Ministry of Justice may request or issue to a foreign state a confirmation that reciprocity will be observed in cooperation, that is, that the cooperation partner will provide assistance in the future, observing the same principles.

(3) If necessary, the Ministry of Justice transmits the Latvian evidence obtaining request to a foreign state through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, using consular or diplomatic channels.

#### 708.pants. Content of the evidence obtaining request

(1) The evidence obtaining request shall indicate:

- 1) the name of the court submitting the evidence obtaining request;
- 2) the subject matter and substance of the evidence obtaining request;
- 3) information about the party to the case and its representatives: for natural persons — name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none, other identification data) and place of residence, and for legal persons — name, registration number and legal address;
- 4) the substance of the case and a brief statement of facts;
- 5) information about the evidence to be obtained and its connection with the case;
- 6) information about the cases provided for by law when witnesses may refuse to give testimony;
- 7) other information necessary for the execution of the evidence obtaining request.
  - (2) In a Latvian evidence obtaining request, the court, on its own initiative or at the reasoned request of a party to the case, may request:
- 1) to allow the parties to the case or their representatives to be present or participate in obtaining evidence;
- 2) to allow representatives of the court to be present or participate in obtaining evidence;
- 3) to obtain evidence using technical means;
- 4) to obtain evidence in the procedural manner provided for in this law.

(As amended by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

#### 709.pants. Language of the evidence obtaining request and the documents attached thereto

(1) A Latvian evidence obtaining request and the documents attached thereto shall be prepared and submitted in the official language, with a translation attached in one of the following languages:

- 1) the language of the receiving state of the request;
- 2) another language, as mutually agreed upon by the competent authorities of Latvia and the foreign state.
  - (2) A foreign evidence obtaining request shall be accepted prepared or with an attached translation in the official language, Russian or English.
  - (3) If it is not possible to provide a translation in one of the languages mentioned in the second paragraph of this article, the competent authorities of Latvia and the foreign state may mutually agree on another language in which the foreign evidence obtaining request and the documents attached thereto are to be prepared or in which a translation is to be attached to them.

#### 710.pants. Form of the evidence obtaining request

(1) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(2) A Latvian evidence obtaining request shall be signed by a judge and certified with the seal of the court.

(3) The Ministry of Justice may submit a Latvian evidence obtaining request and the documents attached thereto to a foreign state by other means of communication, also submitting them as a postal item.

(4) A foreign evidence obtaining request and the documents attached thereto may be accepted by other means of communication if they are also submitted as a postal item.

(As amended by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

#### 711.pants. Decision on a foreign evidence obtaining request

(1) The Ministry of Justice shall decide on a foreign evidence obtaining request within 10 days from the date of its receipt.

(2) The Ministry of Justice shall adopt one of the following decisions:

- 1) on the admissibility of the execution of the evidence obtaining request, determining the authority executing the evidence obtaining request, time limits and other conditions;
- 2) on refusal to accept the evidence obtaining request or part thereof for execution, stating the reasons for the refusal.
  - (3) If additional information is necessary for deciding on the evidence obtaining request, the Ministry of Justice shall request it from the competent authority of the foreign state concerned.
  - (4) The execution of a foreign evidence obtaining request may be refused if:
- 1) the execution of the foreign evidence obtaining request is contrary to the public order of Latvia;
- 2) sufficient information has not been submitted and it is not possible to obtain additional information;
- 3) the execution of the foreign evidence obtaining request is impeded.
  - (5) If the execution of a foreign evidence obtaining request is refused, the Ministry of Justice shall immediately notify the competent authority of the requesting state thereof.
  - (6) Refusal to execute a foreign evidence obtaining request or part thereof does not prevent the competent authority of the foreign state from resubmitting the same request after the deficiencies have been remedied.
  - (7) The decision of the Ministry of Justice is not subject to appeal.

#### 712.pants. General provisions for the execution of a foreign evidence obtaining request

(1) A foreign evidence obtaining request shall be executed by the district (city) court in whose area of operation the source of the evidence to be obtained is located.

(2) If the court to which a foreign evidence obtaining request has been submitted in accordance with the first paragraph of this article finds that part of the evidence is located in another city or district, it shall instruct the respective court to perform certain procedural actions in accordance with Articles 102 and 103 of this law.

(3) A foreign evidence obtaining request shall be executed in the manner prescribed by this law, except in cases where the execution of the foreign evidence obtaining request is permitted in the foreign procedural manner at the request of the competent authority of the foreign state.

(4) The execution of a foreign evidence obtaining request shall be commenced immediately after the decision on the admissibility of the execution of the evidence obtaining request has been adopted. If it is not possible to execute the foreign evidence obtaining request within 90 days from the date of its receipt, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice thereof in writing, indicating the reasons that impede the execution of the said request.

(5) If the execution of a foreign evidence obtaining request is impeded or impossible, the court shall notify the Ministry of Justice in writing of the reasons for non-execution of the said request.

#### 713.pants. Execution of a foreign request for obtaining evidence in the presence of or with the participation of parties or representatives of a foreign competent court

(1) If the execution of a foreign request for obtaining evidence is permitted, with parties or their representatives, or representatives of a foreign competent court being present or participating in obtaining evidence, the court executing the foreign request for obtaining evidence notifies the foreign competent authority or directly the representatives of the foreign competent court or the parties, or their representatives, of the time and place for obtaining evidence, as well as the conditions for participation.

(2) The court ascertains whether an interpreter is necessary for the representatives of the foreign competent court, the parties or their representatives.

(3) If the persons referred to in the first paragraph of this Section do not understand the state language and if there are no significant practical difficulties, at the request of the representatives of the foreign competent court or the parties, or their representatives, an interpreter shall participate in obtaining evidence.

#### 714.pants. Obtaining evidence using technical means

(1) If the execution of a foreign request for obtaining evidence using technical means is permitted, such foreign request for obtaining evidence shall be executed by the district (city) court that has access to the technical means necessary for obtaining evidence.

(2) In obtaining evidence in Latvia or abroad using technical means, if necessary, an interpreter shall participate.

(3) The court verifies the identity of the persons involved and ensures the proceedings for obtaining evidence in Latvia.

#### 715.pants. Rights of witnesses to refuse to testify

(1) When executing a foreign request for obtaining evidence, the court verifies whether there are no obstacles specified in Section 106 of this Law, and also explains to witnesses their rights to refuse to testify in the cases provided for in Section 107 of this Law.

(2) When executing a foreign request for obtaining evidence, witnesses may also refuse to testify in accordance with the law of the requesting state, if such rights are indicated in the foreign request for obtaining evidence or otherwise confirmed by the foreign competent authority.

#### 716.pants. Costs of Execution of Foreign Evidence Collection Requests

(1) Expenses incurred in executing a foreign evidence collection request shall be covered from state budget funds, except in the case provided for in paragraph two of this Article.

(2) The court executing a foreign evidence collection request shall notify the Ministry of Justice of the following costs of executing the said request:

- 1) amounts of expenses payable to experts and interpreters;
- 2) expenses incurred in executing a foreign evidence collection request in foreign procedural order in cases provided for by law;
- 3) costs incurred if a foreign evidence collection request has been executed at the request of a foreign competent authority using technical means.

- (3) The Ministry of Justice may request a foreign competent authority to cover the costs provided for in paragraph two of this Article.

- Annex 1 List of property not subject to enforcement under enforcement documents

(Annex with amendments made by the Law of 17.06.2004, which came into force on 01.07.2004.)

The following types of property and items belonging to the debtor or being his or her share in joint ownership are not subject to enforcement under enforcement documents:

- 1. Household furnishings and household items, clothing necessary for the debtor, members of his or her family, as well as persons who are his or her dependants:
  - 1) necessary everyday clothing, footwear and underwear;
  - 2) bedding accessories, bedclothes and towels;
  - 3) kitchen and table accessories necessary for everyday use;
  - 4) furniture — one bed and one chair per person, as well as one table and one cupboard per family;
  - 5) all children's items.
- 2. Food products in the home in such quantity as necessary for the maintenance of the debtor and his or her family members for three months.
- 3. Money in the amount of the minimum monthly wage for the debtor, each member of his or her family and dependent person, but in cases of collection of maintenance for a minor child or in favour of the Administration of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund — money in the amount of 50 percent of the minimum monthly wage for the debtor, each member of his or her family and dependent person.
- 4. Per family, one cow or goat and one pig, as well as animal feed in such quantity as necessary until new animal feed is harvested or until animals are driven to pasture.
- 5. Fuel necessary for the family for food preparation and heating of living quarters during the heating season.
- 6. Books, instruments and tools necessary for the debtor in his or her personal daily work to provide the means necessary for subsistence.
- 7. Agricultural inventory, that is, agricultural implements, machinery, livestock and seed necessary for a farm, together with the amount of feed necessary for the maintenance of the livestock of the respective farm until the new harvest. What agricultural implements, how many livestock and what amounts of feed are considered necessary shall be determined by an instruction of the Minister of Agriculture.
- 8. Movable property that is recognised as an appurtenance to immovable property under the Civil Law — separately from such immovable property.
- 9. Houses of worship and ritual objects.

- Annex 2

Procedures for Restoring Lost Court Proceedings or Enforcement Records

(Annex with amendments made by the Law of 11.11.2021, which came into force on 01.12.2021.)

1. The court may restore lost court proceedings or enforcement records in a civil case at the request of a party to the case, at the submission of a bailiff or prosecutor, as well as on its own initiative.

2. Lost court proceedings records shall be restored completely or in the part that is necessary to restore in the court's opinion. If there was a court judgment or decision to discontinue the proceedings in the case, it must be restored.

3. A request for restoration of lost court proceedings records or a writ of execution shall be submitted to the court that heard the case, but a request for restoration of lost enforcement records (except a writ of execution) — to the district (city) court according to the place of execution.

4. The request shall indicate precise information about the case. Documents that have been preserved by the applicant and that relate to the case shall be attached to the request, even if they have not been certified in the prescribed manner.

5. When examining the case, the court shall use the preserved parts of the court proceedings records, request documents from the parties to the case or other persons that were issued to them before the loss of the court proceedings records, as well as other materials relating to the case. The parties to the case are entitled to submit for consideration a draft of the judgment or decision to be restored prepared by them.

6. The court may interrogate as witnesses persons who were present during the execution of procedural actions and, if necessary, — persons who were in the composition of the court when hearing the case whose court proceedings records have been lost, as well as persons who executed the court judgment.

7. If the collected materials are insufficient to accurately restore the lost court proceedings records, the court shall by decision discontinue the examination of the request for restoration of court proceedings records. In this case, the applicant is entitled to re-submit the claim or request in the general order. Expenses related to the examination of such a case shall be covered by the state.

8. Expenses incurred by the court in examining a case for restoration of lost records shall be covered by the state. If a knowingly false request is submitted, court expenses shall be recovered from the applicant.

- Transitional Provisions

1. The procedure for examination of cases arising from administrative legal relations, until the day the administrative procedure law enters into force, shall be governed by the general provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and the provisions of chapters twenty-two, twenty-three, twenty-three-A, twenty-four, twenty-four-A and twenty-five of the Latvian Civil Procedure Code.

2. The provisions of paragraph two of Article 548, Articles 550 and 632 of this Law shall be applicable after the respective amendments to the Law "On Judicial Power" enter into force.

3. Until the day the amendments to the Law "On Judicial Power" referred to in paragraph 2 of the transitional provisions enter into force:

- 1) the correct and timely execution of court judgments shall be supervised by the Bailiffs Department of the Ministry of Justice;
- 2) a decision of the senior bailiff by which a request for disqualification of a bailiff has been left without satisfaction may be appealed to the Bailiffs Department of the Ministry of Justice. The submission of a complaint shall not suspend enforcement actions;
- 3) complaints about actions of bailiffs or their refusal to perform such actions may be submitted by the creditor or debtor to the court only after the complaint has been examined by the Bailiffs Department of the Ministry of Justice. A complaint may be submitted to the court within 10 days from the day the complainant received a reply from the Bailiffs Department, or from the day when a one-month period has expired after the submission of the complaint and the applicant has not received a reply thereto.

4. If immovable property is not registered in the Land Register (apartment property in cases provided for by law — in the Cadastre Register), when securing a claim with it or enforcing against it, the immovable property shall be described and transferred to administration in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs two to four of Article 603 and Article 605 of this Law. Before describing the immovable property, the bailiff shall ascertain its ownership or its possessor by requesting information from the State Land Service or the respective municipality. The bailiff shall notify the State Land Service or municipality respectively of the description of immovable property to secure a claim or to collect a debt.

5. If on the date this Law enters into force the procedural time limits regarding judgment enforcement actions established in the Latvian Civil Procedure Code have not expired and this Law establishes a longer time limit, the longer time limit shall apply, including the elapsed time.

6. If property was transferred to a commission until the date this Law enters into force in accordance with Article 390 of the Latvian Civil Procedure Code, its realisation shall be made in accordance with the terms of the commission contract.

7. If capital shares or closed-issue shares of a commercial company have been transferred to the executive institution of the respective commercial company until the date this Law enters into force in accordance with the provisions of paragraph three of Article 389 of the Latvian Civil Procedure Code, the executive institution shall carry out the sale within the prescribed one-month period from the date of transfer.

8. If an auction of described property belonging to the debtor was announced until the date this Law enters into force, it shall be held according to the announced terms.

9. If a calculation prepared by a bailiff for judgment execution expenses was submitted to the court until the date this Law enters into force, the court shall adopt a decision on the calculation previously prepared by the bailiff.

10. If a bailiff has adopted a decision to suspend enforcement proceedings, then in the case where suspension of enforcement proceedings is not provided for by the Civil Procedure Law, enforcement proceedings shall be immediately resumed after this Law enters into force. The bailiff shall adopt a respective decision thereon and send it to the interested persons.

11. With the entry into force of this Law, the Latvian Civil Procedure Code shall cease to be effective, except for its chapters twenty-two, twenty-three, twenty-three-A, twenty-four, twenty-four-A and twenty-five.

12. Amendments to the Civil Procedure Law regarding points 1 and 2 of paragraph two and the first sentence of paragraph three of Article 34, point 8 of Article 39, point 9 of Article 43, and the deletion of chapters 40, 41, 42, 43, 44 and paragraph two of Article 566 shall enter into force on 1 January 2012. (In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the Laws of 01.12.2005 and 11.12.2008, which entered into force

13. Cases regarding inheritance rights that were accepted for examination in special proceedings until 31 December 2002 shall be examined by the court in the procedure established by the Civil Procedure Law as it was in force until 31 December 2011 (the norms referred to in paragraph 12 of the transitional provisions that cease to be effective on 31 December 2011). (In the wording of the Law of 04.08.2011, which entered into force on 01.10.2011.)

14. The court shall examine requests for the establishment of guardianship over an inheritance in inheritance cases in notarial proceedings by applying Article 323 of this Law and Article 660 of the Civil Law. (In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, which entered into force on 01.01.2003.)

15. The court shall examine a request for the ascertainment of an oral will that is necessary for submission to a notary in an inheritance case in the procedure established in Article 309 of this Law, inviting the heirs as interested persons. (In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, which entered into force on 01.01.2003.)

16. Until the establishment of the state fee for the transfer of property to heirs on the basis of an inheritance certificate issued by a notary, the state fee shall be payable in the amount of 50 percent of the rate established in Article 34 of the Civil Procedure Law in cases of confirmation of inheritance rights or entry into legal force of an act of last will. The state fee established in the said cases shall be collected in relation to immovable property before the consolidation of property rights in the Land Register, but in relation to movable things it shall be paid before the issuance of the inheritance certificate, and the notary shall make a certification thereof in the inheritance certificate. Keepers of registers of movable things, as well as persons with whom the inheritable property is located (credit institutions, etc.), are not entitled to re-register or issue the inherited property to the heirs if the property is not indicated in the inheritance certificate and the state fee has not been paid. (In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, which entered into force on 01.01.2003.)

17. Point 2 of paragraph one of Article 346 of this Law regarding that a copy of the judge's decision on the initiation of an insolvency case shall be sent to the Financial and Capital Market Commission, and paragraph 2.1 of Article 378 shall enter into force by a special law. (In the wording of the Law of 12.02.2004, which entered into force on 10.03.2004.)

18. All requests for recognition and enforcement of foreign court judgments (except foreign arbitral awards) that were submitted to a district (city) court and have not been examined until 1 May 2004 shall be examined by a first instance court in the procedure that was in force before 1 May 2004. At the applicant's request, the judge may decide such requests in the procedure established in this Law, and the 10-day time limit for deciding the request shall be calculated from the date of submission of the applicant's request. (In the wording of the Law of 07.04.2004, which entered into force on 01.05.2004.)

19. If a district (city) court has adopted a decision on the recognition and enforcement of a foreign court judgment (except a foreign arbitral award) or a decision on the rejection of a request and the time limit for submitting an appeal has not expired on 1 May 2004, the time limits for submitting an appeal established in paragraph two of Article 641 of this Law shall apply, including the elapsed time. (In the wording of the Law of 07.04.2004, which entered into force on 01.05.2004.)

An arbitral tribunal that was established and whose establishment was notified to the Ministry of Justice until 31 March 2005 shall submit a request to the Register of Enterprises for registration of the arbitral tribunal no later than 15 August 2005, observing the procedure established in this Law and other regulatory enactments. (In the wording of the Law of 17.02.2005, which entered into force on 10.03.2005.)

If the parties have agreed to submit a dispute for resolution to a permanent arbitral tribunal and this arbitral tribunal has not registered in the prescribed manner by 30 September 2005 or has ceased its operations, the parties shall agree on submitting the dispute for resolution to another arbitral tribunal. If no agreement is reached, the dispute shall be examined in court. (In the wording of the Law of 17.02.2005, which entered into force on 10.03.2005.)

Priority for the arbitral tribunal name in the register of arbitral tribunals shall belong to the arbitral tribunal that was first entered in the Ministry of Justice list with such a name. If arbitral tribunal proceedings have been initiated until 10 March 2005 in disputes referred to in points 6 and 7 of Article 487 of this Law (regarding eviction of a person from residential premises and individual labour law disputes), their resolution shall be completed in the respective arbitral tribunal. Cases on insolvency of enterprises and commercial companies initiated until 30 June 2006 shall be examined by the respective regional court. The new wording of Article 447 of this Law, which establishes the examination of appeals against decisions of judges and decisions of Land Register division judges in written proceedings, shall enter into force on 1 July 2006 and shall apply to the examination of appeals against decisions adopted from 1 July 2006. 28. Amendments to paragraph three of Article 238, paragraph two of Article 239, paragraph four of Article 246, paragraph one of Article 250.5, paragraph one of Article 266, paragraph three of Article 267, paragraph two of Article 268, paragraphs one and three of Article 270, paragraph two of Article 275, paragraph two of Article 276, paragraph two of Article 277, paragraph two of Article 280, paragraph four of Article 286, Article 323 (regarding the deletion of the word "parish court") and paragraph three of Article 329 (regarding the replacement of the word "parish court" with the word "orphan's court") of this Law shall enter into force on 1 January 2007. Cases in which the insolvency of an enterprise (commercial company), as well as a merchant registered in the Commercial Register, was declared until 31 December 2007 shall be examined by the court that declared the insolvency. The new wording of Article 434 of this Law (on the procedure by which a judgment of a court of appeal enters into legal force and is enforceable), Article 439.1, the new wording of Article 464 (on a hearing of the Supreme Court), as well as Articles 464.1 and 477.1 shall enter into force on 1 July 2008. Judgments of a court of appeal that were pronounced by the court until 30 June 2008 shall enter into legal force at the moment of their pronouncement, and the enforcement of these judgments of a court of appeal shall be initiated, continued and completed in the procedure established in Part E of this Law. In insolvency proceedings in which the insolvency petition was submitted to the court until 31 December 2007 and in which issues are to be decided in court in accordance with the regulatory enactments that regulated the insolvency of enterprises and commercial companies until 31 December 2007, the appointed administrator shall submit to the court until the hearing of the case or until the time limit set in the judge's decision:

- 2) a list of property belonging to third parties and in the possession or holding of the debtor;

- 4) a report on the debtor's funds in bank accounts and cash, the value of the debtor's fixed assets and current assets;
