50. The new wording of paragraph six of Article 587 of this Law (which provides that the person who has bid for the item to be sold shall pay the full bid amount and value added tax, if the auction price is subject to value added tax, no later than the next working day after the auction) shall enter into force on 1 February 2011. (In the wording of the Law of 20.12.2010, which entered into force on 01.01.2011.)

51. In relation to auctions of movable property and immovable property that were announced until 31 December 2010, the norms of the Civil Procedure Law that were in force until 31 December 2010 shall be applied. (In the wording of the Law of 20.12.2010, which entered into force on 01.01.2011.)

52. Point 3 of paragraph one of Article 133 of this Law, chapter 30.3, as well as amendments to paragraph one of Article 37, paragraphs two and four of Article 406.4, paragraphs two and three of Article 406.6, paragraphs two and three of Article 406.8, paragraphs one and three of Article 450 and paragraph five of Article 486 of this Law shall enter into force on 1 October 2011. (In the wording of the Law of 08.09.2011, which entered into force on 30.09.2011.)

53. The provisions of chapter 30.3 of this Law shall not apply to the examination of claim applications received by the court until 30 September 2011. (In the wording of the Law of 08.09.2011, which entered into force on 30.09.2011.)

54. State fees paid until 30 September 2011 in cases of compulsory enforcement of obligations by warning procedure shall be refunded in the procedure established by the Civil Procedure Law as it was in force until 30 September 2011. (In the wording of the Law of 08.09.2011, which entered into force on 30.09.2011.)

55. The amendment to paragraph five of Article 486 of this Law on the distinguishability of arbitral tribunal names shall not apply to an arbitral tribunal name that was entered in the register of arbitral tribunals until 30 September 2011. (In the wording of the Law of 08.09.2011, which entered into force on 30.09.2011.)

56. The second sentence of Article 24 of this Law [on the competence of the Land Register division of a district (city) court in examining requests for undisputed compulsory enforcement and compulsory enforcement of obligations by warning procedure] and paragraph three of Article 566, as well as the amendment that provides for deletion of the introductory part of paragraph two of Article 34, and amendments to Article 403 and paragraph two of Article 406.2 [on submission of requests to the Land Register division of a district (city) court] shall enter into force on 1 January 2012. (In the wording of the Law of 04.08.2011, which entered into force on 01.10.2011.)

57. An administrator whom the court has dismissed from the performance of his or her duties by decision in the period from 1 November 2010 to 1 July 2012 on the basis of point 7 of paragraph two of Article 22 of the Insolvency Law may appeal this court decision in the procedure established in paragraph seven of Article 341.8, paragraph twelve of Article 363.14 or paragraph nine of Article 363.28 of this Law until 11 July 2012. The decision of a regional court shall not be grounds for reinstatement of the administrator in the insolvency proceedings or legal protection proceedings from which he or she was dismissed. (In the wording of the Law of 21.06.2012, which entered into force on 01.07.2012.)

58. (Deleted by the Law of 19.12.2013, which entered into force on 04.01.2014.)

59. If the court has established temporary guardianship on the basis of point 1 of Article 21 of the Law "On the Time of Entry into Force and Procedure of the Family Law Part of the Renewed Civil Law of the Republic of Latvia of 1937" and within one month after the date these amendments enter into force a request for restriction of a person's active legal capacity and establishment of guardianship has not been submitted, the judge shall adopt a decision to discontinue temporary guardianship. The decision on discontinuation of temporary guardianship shall be sent to the orphan's court for execution, to the prosecutor, the guardian and the person whose active legal capacity has been restricted. (In the wording of the Law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

60. If the court has suspended proceedings on the basis of points 2 and 3 of Article 21 of the Law "On the Time of Entry into Force and Procedure of the Family Law Part of the Renewed Civil Law of the Republic of Latvia of 1937", it shall resume proceedings on its own initiative, at the request of a party to the case or the guardian. If the person who is the applicant in the suspended case has lost claim rights in cases on establishment of guardianship or review of a restriction of active legal capacity in accordance with amendments to the Civil Law and Civil Procedure Law that entered into force on 1 January 2013, the court shall notify the prosecutor's office thereof and the prosecutor shall replace the applicant. When resuming proceedings, the court shall explain to the applicant his or her rights to amend the subject matter and grounds of the request. Such cases shall be examined in court in the procedure established by the Civil Procedure Law as it is in force from the date these amendments enter into force. (In the wording of the Law of 29.11.2012 with amendments made by the Law of 23.05.2013, which entered into force on 01.11.2013.)

61. A person whom the court recognised until 31 December 2011 as incapable due to mental illness or dementia and established guardianship due to its wasteful or extravagant life, as well as due to consumption of alcohol or other intoxicants, shall henceforth be considered a person with restriction of active legal capacity without restriction of personal non-property rights. Until the respective amendments to other regulatory enactments enter into force, the legal regulation in relation to an incapable person and the person for whom guardianship has been established due to its wasteful or extravagant life, as well as due to consumption of alcohol or other intoxicants, shall be interpreted and applied in accordance with what is established in this Law and the Civil Law. (In the wording of the Law of 29.11.2012, which entered into force on 01.01.2013.)

62. The incapacity of the person referred to in paragraph 61 of these transitional provisions shall be reviewed according to the same provisions as for a person with restriction of active legal capacity. The guardian has a duty to submit to the court a request for review of restriction of active legal capacity for the person referred to in paragraph 61 of these transitional provisions within four years after these amendments enter into force if a request for review of restriction of active legal capacity has not been submitted to the court or a judgment has not entered into force in relation thereto. If after the said time limit a request for review of a person's restriction of active legal capacity has not been submitted to the court or a judgment has not entered into force in relation thereto, the orphan's court shall within one year from the expiration of the aforementioned time limit for the duty imposed on the guardian inform the prosecutor's office of such incapable persons for whom it is necessary to review the restriction of active legal capacity.The court informs the Population Register that it has received an application for review of capacity restrictions for an incapacitated person, which was submitted after four years from the date when the respective amendments entered into force. The Population Register informs the prosecutor's office which person, after four years from the date when these amendments entered into force, does not have a judgment in force regarding the review of capacity restrictions and for which person mentioned in point 61 of these transitional provisions a review of capacity restrictions has been initiated in court. The prosecutor's office submits an application to the court for review of the said person's capacity restrictions within seven years from the date when these amendments enter into force. (Wording of 29.11.2012. law, which enters into force 01.01.2013.)

63. Until the date of entry into force of the amendments to Section 483 of this law, a complaint submitted to the relevant official shall be examined in accordance with the provisions that were in force on the date of submission of the complaint. (Wording of 29.11.2012. law, which enters into force 01.01.2013.)

64. The amendments made to point 4.2 of the first paragraph of Section 11 of this law, point 3.1 of Section 251 and Chapter 34.1 "Suspension of Rights of Future Attorney" in connection with future power of attorney enter into force simultaneously with subsection III1 "Future Power of Attorney" of the first sub-chapter of Chapter 18 of the fourth part of the Civil Law. (Wording of 29.11.2012. law, which enters into force 01.01.2013. See 29.11.2012. law)

65. The founder of a permanent arbitration tribunal registered in the Arbitration Tribunal Register shall submit to the Enterprise Register by 1 April 2013 a confirmation that the arbitrator meets the requirements of the second paragraph of Section 497 of this law, attaching documents substantiating the arbitrator's qualifications. (Wording of 29.11.2012. law, which enters into force 01.01.2013.)

66. If the parties have agreed to submit a dispute to a permanent arbitration tribunal and the founder of this arbitration tribunal has not submitted, in the manner prescribed by regulatory enactments by 1 April 2013, a confirmation of the compliance of the arbitrator in the permanent arbitration tribunal with the requirements of the second paragraph of Section 497 of this law, the parties agree on submitting the dispute for resolution to another arbitration tribunal. If an agreement is not reached, the dispute shall be examined in court. (Wording of 29.11.2012. law, which enters into force 01.01.2013.)

67. An arbitrator who does not meet the requirements of the second paragraph of Section 497 of this law shall complete arbitration proceedings initiated before the entry into force of these amendments in the relevant arbitration tribunal. (Wording of 29.11.2012. law, which enters into force 01.01.2013.)

68. The provisions of Chapter 30.4 of this law are not applicable to the examination of claims received by the court before 30 June 2013. (Wording of 18.04.2013. law, which enters into force 22.05.2013.)

69. The amendment to Section 400 of this law regarding its supplementation with paragraph 1.1, which provides that the first paragraph of the section is not applicable to notarial acts drawn up in the manner prescribed in Section D1 of the Notary Law, applies to those notarial acts that were drawn up after 31 October 2013. (Wording of 23.05.2013. law, which enters into force 01.11.2013.)

70. Cases concerning undisputed compulsory enforcement of obligations, based on obligations according to which undisputed compulsory enforcement was admissible before 31 October 2013, shall be examined in the manner prescribed in this law that was in force until 31 October 2013. (Wording of 23.05.2013. law, which enters into force 01.11.2013.)

71. Point 5 of the second paragraph of Section 539 of this law and point 15 of Section 540 apply to those notarial acts that were drawn up after 31 October 2013. (Wording of 23.05.2013. law, which enters into force 01.11.2013.)

72. The amendments to the first paragraph of Section 551 of this law and the first and second paragraphs of Section 594, which provide that the debtor shall retain wages and payments equated thereto not less than the amount of the minimum monthly wage and for each dependent minor child funds in the amount of the state social security benefit, enter into force on 1 January 2014. In enforcement cases that have been entered into the proceedings of a sworn bailiff and have not been completed before the entry into force of the amendments to the first and second paragraphs of Section 594 of this law and in which the enforcement measure is applied

— recovery against wages or payments equated thereto payable to the debtor —, the amount of funds to be retained by the debtor specified in the first and second paragraphs of Section 594 of this law during the period from the entry into force of the amendments mentioned in the first and second paragraphs of Section 594 of this law until the debt amount to be recovered specified in the order of the sworn bailiff has been extinguished or the enforcement measure applied has been revoked, shall be calculated by the employer or the relevant legal person at the moment when the deduction is made from the debtor's wages or payments equated thereto. (Wording of 23.05.2013. law with amendments made by 19.12.2013. law, which enters into force 04.01.2014.)

73. (Deleted by 10.12.2020. law, which enters into force 31.12.2020.)

74. The amendments to Section 250.27 of this law regarding the appeal in the order of appeal of court judgments rendered in cases concerning small claims enter into force on 1 April 2014. (Wording of 19.12.2013. law, which enters into force 04.01.2014.)

75. The amendments to Section 250.27 of this law regarding the appeal in the order of appeal of court judgments rendered in cases concerning small claims apply to judgments that were pronounced or — if the judgments were rendered in written proceedings — drawn up after 1 April 2014. (Wording of 19.12.2013. law, which enters into force 04.01.2014.)

76. The provisions of point 10 of the second paragraph of Section 406.3 of this law regarding the inclusion of a confirmation in the application are not applicable to the examination of applications submitted to the court before 1 July 2014. (Wording of 19.12.2013. law, which enters into force 04.01.2014.)

77. The founder of a permanent arbitration tribunal registered in the Arbitration Tribunal Register shall submit to the Enterprise Register by 15 July 2014 amendments to the regulation in accordance with the amendments to Section 486.1 of this law. (Wording of 22.05.2014. law, which enters into force 05.06.2014.)

78. If the founder of a permanent arbitration tribunal registered in the Arbitration Tribunal Register has not submitted the said documents to the Enterprise Register within the time period specified in point 77 of these transitional provisions, the Enterprise Register shall, by 15 September 2014, in accordance with Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 204 of 29 March 2005 "Regulations on the Arbitration Tribunal Register", decide on the deletion of the permanent arbitration tribunal from the Arbitration Tribunal Register. (Wording of 22.05.2014. law, which enters into force 05.06.2014.)

79. If the parties have agreed to submit a civil dispute for resolution to a permanent arbitration tribunal that has been deleted from the permanent arbitration tribunal register in accordance with point 78 of these transitional provisions, the parties agree on submitting the civil dispute for resolution to another arbitration tribunal. If an agreement is not reached, the dispute shall be examined by a district (city) court. (Wording of 22.05.2014. law, which enters into force 05.06.2014.)

80. A permanent arbitration tribunal that has been deleted from the permanent arbitration tribunal register in accordance with point 78 of these transitional provisions may complete the examination of initiated cases, but not longer than until 31 December 2014. (Wording of 22.05.2014. law, which enters into force 05.06.2014.)

81. The founder of a permanent arbitration tribunal deleted from the Arbitration Tribunal Register shall, by 1 October 2014, transfer procedural documents for storage to the National Archives of Latvia, covering the expenses for the storage of procedural documents. (Wording of 22.05.2014. law, which enters into force 05.06.2014.)

82. An application for compulsory enforcement of a permanent arbitration tribunal award or for refusal to issue a writ of execution for compulsory enforcement of a permanent arbitration tribunal award, which was received before 31 December 2014, shall be examined by the court in the manner that was in force at the time of rendering the permanent arbitration tribunal award. (Wording of 11.09.2014. law, which enters into force 01.11.2014.)

83. The amendments to Part D of this law regarding the procedure for enforcement of permanent arbitration tribunal awards and regarding the deletion of Chapters 61, 62, 63, 64 and 65 enter into force on 1 January 2015. (Wording of 11.09.2014. law, which enters into force 01.11.2014.)

84. The third paragraph of Section 611 of this law regarding electronic submission of an application for registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer, the third paragraph of Section 613 of this law regarding access to the Enforcement Cases Register and the fifth paragraph of Section 615 of this law regarding electronic submission of an application for registration of immovable property in the name of the successful bidder, co-owner or creditor and for deletion of debts registered in the land register shall be applied upon availability of the respective technical support, but not later than 1 January 2015. (Wording of 11.09.2014. law, which enters into force 01.11.2014.)

85. Cases concerning registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer (person who has taken over the immovable property, or successful bidder), which were accepted for examination by a regional court before 31 October 2014, shall be examined in the manner prescribed in the Civil Procedure Law that was in force until 31 October 2014. (Wording of 11.09.2014. law, which enters into force 01.11.2014.)

86. The Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court shall examine complaints regarding decisions adopted by a regional court when examining cases concerning registration of immovable property in the name of the acquirer (person who has taken over the immovable property, or successful bidder), if they were accepted for examination by a regional court before 31 October 2014. A decision of the Civil Chamber of the Supreme Court, which was adopted after 1 November 2014 when examining a complaint and by which a decision of a regional court was revoked and the matter was referred for re-examination, shall be referred for re-examination to the land register of a district (city) court

### division according to the location of the immovable property. (As worded by the law of 11.09.2014, which enters into force on 01.11.2014.)

87. Cases which have been examined in a regional court as a court of first instance and in which the date for pronouncement of the judgment has been set after 31 December 2014, as well as interlocutory appeals against decisions of a regional court as a court of first instance which have been pronounced after 31 December 2014, shall be examined in appellate proceedings by the same regional court as a court of appellate instance, but in a new composition of the court. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

88. Cases in respect of which appellate proceedings have been instituted in the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court, and interlocutory appeals against decisions pronounced by a regional court as a court of first instance, but which have not been examined by 31 December 2016, including cases in which a decision has been taken to suspend proceedings, shall be transferred for examination to a regional court as a court of appellate instance, but in a new composition of the court. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, with amendments made by the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015.)

89. Cases which have been instituted for examination in a regional court as a court of first instance by 31 December 2014, but the examination of which on the merits has not been commenced by 30 June 2015, shall be transferred for examination to a district (city) court as a court of first instance. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

90. Cases which a regional court as a court of first instance has commenced to examine on the merits shall be examined in the same court in which they have been submitted. Cases which a regional court as a court of first instance has commenced to examine on the merits, but which have not been examined by 31 December 2015 due to a decision having been taken to suspend proceedings in them, shall be transferred for examination to a district (city) court as a court of first instance. (As worded by the law of 10.12.2015, which enters into force on 01.01.2016.)

91. After 1 January 2015, a court of cassation instance, upon setting aside a ruling of the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court as an appellate instance, shall transfer the case for new examination to a regional court as a court of appellate instance or to a city (district) court as a court of first instance (Article 474, paragraph 2). An appellate instance court, upon setting aside a judgment of a regional court as a court of first instance (Article 427), a decision on termination of proceedings, a decision on leaving a claim without examination, as well as a decision on refusal to accept a statement of claim (Article 132) and a decision on leaving a statement of claim without progress (Article 133), shall transfer the case for new examination to a district (city) court as a court of first instance. In such a case, the case shall be transferred to a court in accordance with the rules of jurisdiction of civil disputes. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, with amendments made by the law of 10.12.2015, which enters into force on 01.01.2016.)

92. If after 1 January 2015, in a case which has been examined in a regional court as a court of first instance, issues related to the execution of the ruling are to be decided, they shall be decided by the regional court which adopted the ruling. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

93. If after 1 January 2016, in a case which has been examined in the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court in appellate proceedings, issues related to the execution of the ruling are to be decided, they shall be sent for decision to a regional court as a court of appellate instance. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

94. A court which has commenced to hear a civil case by 1 January 2015, the materials of which include a state secret object, shall complete its examination. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

95. Cases examined in the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court concerning decisions and actions of a land register division judge, in which after 1 January 2015 a cassation instance has set aside a ruling of the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court, shall be transferred for new examination to a regional court in whose territory of operation the land register division of the district (city) court is located. Complaints concerning decisions and actions of a land register division judge which have not been examined by the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court by 31 December 2016, including complaints in which a decision has been taken to suspend proceedings, shall be transferred for examination to a regional court in whose territory of operation the land register division of the district (city) court is located. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

96. Interlocutory appeals which have been submitted against decisions adopted by a regional court as a court of first instance, the time limit for appealing which expires by 31 December 2014, shall be examined in appellate proceedings in the manner which was in force until 31 December 2014. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

97. Amendments to Articles 540, 541.1, 555, 559, 644, 644.2 and 644.3 of this law in relation to Council Regulation No 44/2001 and Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council enter into force on 10 January 2015. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

98. Amendments to Articles 541.1, 543.1, 545.1 and 644.3 of this law in relation to Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council enter into force on 11 January 2015. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

99. To proceedings which have been commenced, public acts which have been officially drawn up and registered, and court settlements which have been approved or concluded in the period from 1 May 2004 to 9 January 2015, Article 541.1, paragraph three, and Article 644, paragraph two, of this law shall apply in the wording which was in force until 9 January 2015. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

100. Applications to be examined in the procedure specified in Chapters 77.1 and 77.2 of this law, which have been submitted to a district (city) court by 28 February 2015, but examination of the case on the merits has not been commenced, shall be transferred for examination to Riga City Ziemeļu District Court. Applications to be examined in the procedure specified in Chapters 77.1 and 77.2 of this law, which have been submitted to a district (city) court by 28 February 2015 and examination of the case on the merits has been commenced, shall be completed for examination by the court in which the application has been submitted. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

101. If after 1 March 2015, in a case concerning the wrongful removal of a child across the border to a foreign state or retention in a foreign state, if the child's habitual residence is in Latvia, and wrongful removal across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia, if the child's habitual residence is in another state, issues related to the execution of the ruling are to be decided, they shall be examined by Riga City Ziemeļu District Court. (As worded by the law of 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

102. A court shall adopt a decision on termination of a legal person's insolvency proceedings if an

application has been received from the Insolvency Control Service for revocation of an administrator and termination of a legal person's insolvency proceedings in the case specified in paragraph 27 of the transitional provisions of the Insolvency Law. (As worded by the law of 12.02.2015, with amendments made by the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

103. A court which adopts the decision referred to in paragraph 102 of the transitional provisions of this law shall, at the request of the Insolvency Control Service, instruct the administrator revoked from the insolvency proceedings to carry out the actions related to the deletion of the debtor from the Enterprise Register. If the administrator does not submit to the court an application for termination of the insolvency proceedings due to the fact that the sale of assets has not been commenced or has not been completed or the satisfaction of creditors' claims has not been commenced or has not been completed, at the request of the Insolvency Control Service, the court shall, in addition to the obligation specified in this paragraph, instruct the administrator revoked from the insolvency proceedings to carry out the actions related to the completion of the insolvency proceedings. (As worded by the law of 12.02.2015, with amendments made by the law of 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

104. In legal protection proceedings, legal person insolvency proceedings and natural person insolvency proceedings commenced by 30 June 2012, complaints shall be examined by the court in the procedure specified in Chapters 45.1, 46.1 and 46.2 of this law. (As worded by the law of 12.02.2015, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

(As worded by the law of 12.02.2015, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

105. If a natural person insolvency proceedings application has been submitted by 1 March 2015, then Articles 363.25 and 363.27 of this law shall apply in the wording which was in force on the day of submission of the natural person insolvency proceedings application. (As worded by the law of 12.02.2015, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

106. Amendments to Chapter 73 of this law, which are related to the organisation of auctions of immovable property on an electronic auction website, enter into force on 1 July 2015. Insolvency proceedings administrators, when organising an auction of immovable property, shall apply the said amendments from 1 January 2016. Auctions which a bailiff has announced by 30 June 2015 shall take place in accordance with the procedure which was in force until 30 June 2015. Auctions which an insolvency proceedings administrator has announced by 31 December 2015 shall take place in accordance with the procedure which was in force until 31 December 2015. (As worded by the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015.)

107. Amendments to Article 594, paragraph one, paragraph 2 of this law, which provide for retention for the debtor of wages and equivalent payments in the amount of 50 per cent of the minimum monthly salary, enter into force on 1 July 2015. In enforcement cases referred to in Article 594, paragraph one, paragraph 2 of this law, which have been entered into a bailiff's proceedings and have not been completed by 30 June 2015 and in which the enforcement measure of levying execution on wages or equivalent payments payable to the debtor is applied, from 1 July 2015 until such time as the amount of debt to be recovered specified in the bailiff's order has been extinguished or the enforcement measure applied has been revoked, the amount of funds to be retained for the debtor shall be calculated independently by the employer or the relevant legal person (the addressee of the bailiff's order) at the time when the deduction is made from the debtor's wages or equivalent payments in accordance with the amendments to Article 594, paragraph one, of this law, which entered into force on 1 July 2015. (As worded by the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015.)

108. Amendments to Article 250.2, paragraph three, Article 401, paragraph 3 and Article 644, paragraph two of this law in relation to the European Certificate of Succession and Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council enter into force on 17 August 2015. (As worded by the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015.)

109. At the proposal of the President of the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court, the President of the Supreme Court shall decide the question of transfer of a case pending in the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court to another court of appellate instance, if it is not possible to ensure the examination of the case by 31 December 2016. The decision shall be adopted in the form of a resolution and it is not subject to appeal. The case shall be transferred to another court of appellate instance in observance of the conditions of Article 32.1, paragraphs five and six of this law. (As worded by the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015.)

110. The Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court, upon setting aside a judgment of a regional court as a court of first instance in the cases specified in Article 427 of this law, shall send the case for new examination to a court of first instance in accordance with the rules of jurisdiction of civil disputes. (As worded by the law of 28.05.2015, which enters into force on 02.07.2015.)

111. In enforcement cases concerning the enforcement of a ruling arising from guardianship or contact rights, which have been entered before the date of entry into force of Chapters 74.4 and 74.5 of this law, a bailiff shall, after the entry into force of the said chapters, send the notice specified in Article 620.17 or Article 620.23 of this law and carry out the further enforcement of the ruling in the procedure specified in the relevant chapter. If in an enforcement case concerning the enforcement of a ruling arising from guardianship or contact rights the court has imposed a fine in accordance with Article 620 of this law, it shall be counted towards the fine imposed in accordance with Article 620.18 or 620.25 of this law. (As worded by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

112. Article 33, paragraph three, paragraph 4 and Article 44.1 of this law shall apply to cases which have been instituted after 1 March 2016. (As worded by the law of 10.12.2015, which enters into force on 01.01.2016.)

113. Amendments concerning the deletion of Article 539, paragraph three, Article 540, paragraph 9 and Article 567, paragraph five of this law shall enter into force simultaneously with the International and National Sanctions Law of the Republic of Latvia. Enforcement proceedings in cases concerning the enforcement of a decision of the responsible institution on the enforcement of sanctions imposed by international organisations, which have been entered into a bailiff's proceedings before the date of entry into force of the International and National Sanctions Law of the Republic of Latvia, shall be terminated by the bailiff, revoking all enforcement measures adopted in connection with the enforcement of such a decision. Judgment enforcement costs incurred in an enforcement case shall be reimbursed to the bailiff in accordance with the requirements of those regulatory enactments which were in force until the date of entry into force of the International and National Sanctions Law of the Republic of Latvia. (As worded by the law of 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016.)

114. Amendments made in relation to interpreters in Article 13, paragraph four, Article 33, paragraph three, supplementing it with paragraph 5, Article 44, paragraph one, paragraph 4 and supplementing it with paragraph 5, as well as supplementing the article with paragraph six, Article 54, paragraph three, Article 55, supplementing it with paragraph 8, Article 74, paragraph seven, supplementing it with paragraph 2.1, Article 210, paragraph one, paragraph 3 and supplementing the paragraph with paragraph 6 of this law, enter into force on 31 July 2016. (As worded by the law of 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016.)

115. Article 540, paragraph 18, Article 560, paragraph 2.2, Article 562, paragraph one, paragraph 15 and Article 563, paragraph one, paragraph 12 of this law enter into force on 18 June 2016. (As worded by the law of 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016.)

116. A court which has commenced by 1 August 2016 to examine applications for retrial of a case due to newly discovered circumstances shall complete the examination thereof. The examination of those applications which have been transferred for examination to the Civil Cases Chamber of the Supreme Court shall be decided in accordance with paragraph 109 of these transitional provisions. (As worded by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

117. Orders of a bailiff issued by 30 June 2017 concerning the attachment and transfer to a bailiff's deposit account of funds deposited in a credit institution or with another payment service provider shall be enforced by applying the provisions of this law which were in force until 30 June 2017. (As worded by the law of 23.11.2016, which enters into force on 01.01.2017.)

118. From 1 July 2019, orders referred to in Article 599.1 of this law shall be issued, enforced and information on their enforcement shall be provided, using the State Information System Connector under the supervision of the State Regional Development Agency. (As worded by the law of 23.11.2016, which enters into force on 01.01.2017.)

Until the day when document circulation in civil proceedings has completely transitioned to electronic form, documents prepared in paper form shall be converted to electronic form by certifying them with an electronic signature within the meaning of point 10 of Article 3 of Regulation No. 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council and observing the following provisions:

- 1) the representation and compliance of the content of the original document with it during the prescribed data storage period is ensured;
- 2) the reading of the content electronically and, if necessary, the creation of a derivative in paper form is ensured;
- 3) the converted document is protected against additions, changes or unauthorised access or destruction. Informative reference to European Union directives

(In the version of the 14.12.2006. law with amendments made by the 20.12.2010., 15.03.2012., 19.12.2013., 04.02.2016., 19.10.2017., 28.02.2019., 16.06.2022. and 16.03.2023. laws, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

The Law incorporates legal norms arising from:

- 1) (deleted by the 19.12.2013. law);
- 2) Directive 2004/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 April 2004 on the enforcement of intellectual property rights;
- 3) Directive 2008/52/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2008 on certain aspects of mediation in civil and commercial matters;
- 4) Council Directive 2010/24/EU of 16 March 2010 concerning mutual assistance for the recovery of claims relating to taxes, duties and other measures;
- 5) Directive 2011/7/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 February 2011 on combating late payment in commercial transactions;
- 6) Directive 2014/67/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014 on the enforcement of Directive 96/71/EC concerning the posting of workers in the framework of the provision of services and amending Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012 on administrative cooperation through the Internal Market Information System ('the IMI Regulation');
- 7) Directive 2014/104/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2014 on certain rules governing actions for damages under national law for infringements of the competition law provisions of the Member States and of the European Union;
- 8) Directive (EU) 2016/943 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 June 2016 on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (trade secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure;
- 9) Directive (EU) 2019/1 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 to empower the competition authorities of the Member States to be more effective enforcers and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market;
- 10) Directive (EU) 2019/1023 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 on preventive restructuring frameworks, on discharge of debt and disqualifications, and on measures to increase the efficiency of procedures concerning restructuring, insolvency and discharge of debt, and amending Directive (EU) 2017/1132 (Directive on restructuring and insolvency).

The Law enters into force on 1 March 1999.

The Law was adopted by the Saeima on 14 October 1998.

President of the State G.Ulmanis
